content: -[Revealing the Truth] - Author: Muhammad Rahmatullah bin Khalil al-Rahman al-Kiranawi al-Uthmani al-Hindi al-Hanafi (deceased: 1308 AH)
Study, investigation and commentary: Dr. Muhammad Ahmed Muhammad Abdul Qadir Khalil Malkawi, Assistant Professor at the College of Education, King Saud University - Riyadh
Publisher: General Presidency of Scientific Research, Fatwa, Da’wah and Guidance Departments - Saudi Arabia
Edition: First, 1410 AH - 1989 AD (the first edition issued corresponding to the author’s two golden manuscript and printed copies)
Number of parts: 4 parts in one serial numbering
[Book numbering corresponds to the printed version] In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful

[Introduction] Praise be to God, who has not taken a son, and has never had a partner in His kingdom. Glory be to Him who sent down the Book to His servant, and made it an insight and a reminder for those with understanding, and revealed the veil of the truth with certainty with the evidence of His verses, and erected on His platform flags of guidance to establish the truth with His words, until without his argument the arguments of peoples pretending to appear similar to them, while they {want to extinguish the light of God) ceased. with their mouths, and God refuses except to perfect His light, even if the disbelievers hate it.} And prayers and peace be upon him whose miracles of prophecy were revealed with the best revelations, and whose symbols of law appeared, abolishing the features of religions and laws. His master sent him with guidance and the religion of truth to make it prevail over all religions, and supported him with a decisive book that rhetoricians are unable to express. They bring a surah like him, our master Muhammad, who

With his appearance, the Torah and the Gospel were heralded, and with his presence the call of his father Ibrahim Al-Khalil, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him and his family, who were victorious in following his law, who followed the path of righteousness in following his path, was fulfilled with his presence, and his companions, among whom God brought Islam, until they became harsh against the infidels and merciful among them.

(As for what follows) the servant who is hoping for the gracious mercy of his Lord, the mercy of God, son of Khalil Al-Rahman, says, may God forgive him and his parents, and be kind to them and to him: When the English state took strong control over the Kingdom of India, and they spread the carpet of security and order satisfactorily, and from the beginning of their sultanate until forty-three years, the call from their scholars to their doctrine did not appear, and after that they began to call and were gradually increasing in it, until they wrote letters and books in response to the people of Islam, and distributed them in the regions among the common people, and they began to preach in the markets, people’s gatherings, and the public streets, and the common people were the people of Islam. For a while, we refrained from listening to their preaching and reading their letters. None of the Indian scholars bothered to respond to those letters, but weakness set in after a while, in the alienation of some of the common people, and there was a fear of slipping on the feet of some ignorant people who are like cattle. Then some of the scholars of the people of Islam went to respond to them. Although I was isolated in a corner of idleness, and I was not counted among the group of distinguished scholars, and I was not worthy of this great speech, but when I looked at their reports, And their edits, and letters reached me

Many of their writings, I decided to also strive to the best of my ability and ability. I first wrote books and letters, so that the situation would become clear to those with understanding, and secondly I summoned the priest who was brilliant and the most powerful of the Christian scholars who were in India busy attacking and attacking the Islamic religion, in writing and reporting. I mean the author of (Mizan al-Haqq) to have a debate between me and him, in the general council, so that it becomes truly clear that the Islamic scholars’ lack of direction is not due to their inability to respond to the letters. priests, as some Christians claim, so it was decided to debate the five issues that are the main issues in dispute between Christians and Muslims, namely: distortion, abrogation, trinity, and the truth of

The Qur’an, and the prophecy of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace; The General Council was held in the month of Rajab in the year one thousand two hundred and seventy of the Hijra of the Master of the Ancients and the Others, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the town of Akbarabad.

Some of the honorable beloved, may God prolong his life, were appointed for me in this council, and some of the priests were appointed for the described priest, so we prevailed, thanks to God, in the two issues of abrogation and distortion, which were among the most accurate and oldest issues in the priest’s claim, as indicated by his statement in the book Solution to Problems. When he saw that, he closed the door to debate in the remaining three issues. Then it was agreed that I arrived in Mecca, honored by God Almighty, and attended the threshold of the eminent scholar and narrator, the eye of knowledge and know-how, the fountain of wisdom and narration, the sun of writers, the crown of eloquent people, the bravest of investigators, the support of auditors, the imam of hadith scholars, the role model of jurists and theologians, the delight of the virgin’s liver, named the accepted messenger, my master, my support, and my master, Mr. Ahmed bin Zaini Dahlan, may God continue his abundance until the day Standing up, he ordered me to translate with my tongue
These five topics are among the books that were written in this section, because they were either in the language of the Persians, or in the language of the Muslims of India.

The reason for my writing on these two tongues was that the first tongue is familiar to the Muslims in that kingdom, and the second tongue is theirs, and that the preaching priests residing in that kingdom are certainly skilled in the second tongue, and are also a little familiar with the first tongue, especially the priest who debated with me, for his skill in the first was greater than the second, and I saw obedience to the command of my master as being in the status of a duty, and I rolled up my feet to be diligent in obeying his command. He conceals my mistakes and draws the pen of correction over my lapses. I ask God, the Easeer of all difficulties, to bestow upon me what guides me to the truth and correctness, and to make this book acceptable to people, benefiting from it privately and publicly, and to protect it from the suspicions of the invalids and the delusions of the deniers. He is the protector of reconciliation, and in His hand is the crisis of investigation, and He is capable of all things, and deserving of the answer. It is called (manifesting the truth) and it is arranged in an introduction and six chapters.

content: [Introduction to explaining matters that should be taken into account]

sections.heading: the first
content: (The first) If I say anything in this book in one place, it is quoted from the books of (Protestant) scholars by force and argument. If the observer sees it as contradicting the doctrine of the people of Islam, he should not fall into doubt. If I quote from Islamic books, I will often refer to it unless it is well-known.

sections.heading: the second
content: (Second) That the quotation in this book is mostly from the books of the Protestant sect, whether they are biographies, interpretations, or histories, because this sect is in control of the Kingdom of India, and from its scholars the debate and discussion took place, and it reached its books, and it is rarely from the books of the Catholic sect as well.

sections.heading: the third
content: (Third) that changing and reforming is like a natural matter for the Protestant sect, and therefore you see that if one of their books is printed again, it often undergoes a lot of change compared to the first time, either by changing some of the contents or by adding or subtracting them, or by introducing or delaying the topics. If what is copied from their books is matched by the books from which it was copied, then if those books are printed of the same type as the books from which the transmitter copied them, then the transfer comes out conforming, otherwise it comes out mostly inconsistent, so whoever did not adhere to their custom. He thinks that the carrier made a mistake, but he is right, and this happened

The customs of these priests, and I also fell into the fallacy twice before learning about their customs, so the observer in this matter must be completely alert; So that he does not make a mistake or cause someone to make it, and so that the carrier is not accused. I will explain the books that I am quoting, and I will say: The books mentioned are these:

[1] Translation of the Five Books of Moses, peace be upon him, in the Arabic language, printed by William Watts in London in the year 1848 AD, based on the copy printed in the Great Romans in the year 1264.

[2] The translation of all the books of the Old Testament and the New Testament in the Arabic language, which was printed by the also mentioned William Watts in the year 1844, and he made in this translation the ninth and tenth Psalms into one Psalm, and he divided the one hundred and forty-seventh Psalms into two parts and made them two Psalms, so the number of Psalms between the tenth and the one hundred and forty-seventh became one less compared to the other translations, and everything else is in agreement. If the examiner finds a difference in this matter in relation to the other translations It must be based on what you mentioned
[3] The translation of the New Testament into the Arabic language, printed in Beirut in 1860, and the phrase “New Testament” was often quoted from this translation because its phrase is not
Poor as the first translation phrase
[4] Adam Clarke’s Commentary on the Old and New Testament, printed in London in 1851
[5] Horne’s interpretation, which was printed in London in 1882 for the third time
[6] Henry Wascott's interpretation, printed in London
[7] Lardner's interpretation, printed in London in 1717 in ten volumes
[8] Tafsir Dawali Warrardment, printed in London in 1848
[9] Harsley's interpretation [10] Watson's book
[11] Translation of the Protestant group in the English language with the seal affixed to it, printed in 1819, 1830, 1821, and 1836.
[12] A translation of the Roman Catholic Old and New Testaments in the English language and printed in Dublin in the year

1840, and other books as well, which will be mentioned in their appropriate places. These books are in countries dominated by the English, and they are abundant. So whoever doubts, let him match the transmission with its original.

sections.heading: Fourth
content: (Fourth) If, in any place, a statement comes out of my pen that suggests bad etiquette in relation to one of their books that has been accepted by them, or to one of the prophets, peace be upon them, then the observer should not blame me for my bad belief in relation to the divine books and the prophets, peace be upon them; Because insulting one of the books of God or one of the prophets, peace be upon them, is one of the ugliest things that is forbidden to me. May God protect me and all the people of Islam from it. However, since it has not been proven that the Muslim books attributed to them, according to their claim, are divine books, but rather the opposite has been proven, and it has been proven that some of the contents of these books must be strongly denied by every Muslim, and it has been proven that error, disagreement, contradiction, and distortion have definitely occurred in them, then I am excused for saying: These books are not divine books and for denying some stories, such as: That Lot drank wine and committed adultery with his two daughters and they became pregnant by adultery, or that David, peace be upon him, committed adultery with the wife of Uriah and she became pregnant by adultery by him, and he referred to the military commander to plan something by which he would be killed.

Uriah destroyed him by trickery, and disposed of his wife, and that Aaron made a calf and built an altar for it, and Aaron worshiped it with the children of Israel and bowed down to him and sacrificed sacrifices before him, and that Solomon apostatized at the end of his life and worshiped idols and built temples to them,

It is not proven from their holy books that he repented, but rather it appears that he died as an apostate and polytheist. We must deny these stories and others like them and say that they are absolutely untrue, and we believe with certainty that the arena of prophecy is free from such ugly matters.

I am also excused for saying that it is a mistake, and thus it is not appropriate for Protestant scholars to doubt this matter. Do they not see for themselves how they are going beyond the limit in their attacks on the Glorious Qur’an, the Prophetic hadiths, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace? How do their pens produce inappropriate words? But a person does not see his own fault, even if it is great, and is exposed to the fault of others, even if it is small, except for those whose insight God has opened. Yes, what Christ, peace be upon him, said: (Why do you look at the speck that is in your brother’s eye, but do not pay attention to the plank that is in your own eye? Or how can you say to your brother, “Let me remove the speck from your eye,” when the plank is in your own eye, you hypocrite? First remove the plank from your own eye, and then
See carefully to remove the speck from your brother's eye) as stated in the seventh chapter of the Gospel of Matthew.

sections.heading: Fifth
content: (Fifth) A word may come out that weighs heavy on the violator. Do you not see that Christ, peace be upon him, addressed the scribes and Pharisees verbally with these words (Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, and woe to you, you blind leaders, and you blind ignorants, and you blind Pharisee, and you serpents and serpents, how do you escape from the judgment of hell) and made their ugliness public so that some of them complained that you You insult us, as is stated in the twenty-third chapter of the Gospel of Matthew, and the eleventh chapter of the Gospel of Luke, and how dogs were used to call the Canaanites who were infidels, as is stated in the fifteenth chapter of the Gospel of Matthew, and how Yahya, peace be upon him, addressed the Jews by saying: “You generation of vipers, who advises you to flee from the wrath to come,” as is stated in the third chapter of the Gospel of Matthew, especially in the apparent debates of scholars, such words fall under the same meaning. Humanity, don't you see?

Muqtada of the Protestant sect and leader of the reformers, Janaab Lothar. How do you say about the one who was the Muqtada of the Christians during his time, I mean the Pope, his contemporary? And how do you say about the greatest sultan and the most magnificent king, Henry VIII, King of London? And I quote some of his sayings by way of translation from page 277 of the ninth volume of (The Catholic Herald), and its author claimed that he quoted these sayings from the second and seventh volumes of the seven volumes of Janaab, the leader of the reformers.

The praised president said on page 274 of the seventh volume printed in 1558 regarding the Pope: “Thus I am the first whom God has asked to reveal the things that He preaches among you, and I know that the holy word of God is with you. Walk smoothly, my little Paul, and protect yourself, my donkey, from falling. Save yourself, my donkey, the Pope, and do not advance, lest you fall and break your leg, because the air this year is so thin that there is a lot of thick snow in it, and you slip in it.” The feet, if they fall, the creation will mock. What devilish matter is this? Away from me, you wicked, indifferent, foolish, humiliated donkeys. Do you imagine yourselves that you are better than donkeys? You, O Pope, are a donkey, indeed a foolish donkey, and you will always remain a donkey. Then he said on page 474 of the written volume like this: (If I were a ruler...

I would have decided that the wicked should surround the Pope and his companions and then drown them in Istia, which is three miles from the Romans, and there is a great stream (meaning the sea) because it is a good bath for healing the Pope and all those attached to him from all diseases and weaknesses, and I give my word, rather I give Christ as guarantor, that if I drowned them gently for half an hour, they would be cured of all diseases. And he said on page 451 of the aforementioned volume: (The Pope And those who cling to him are a group of evildoers, corrupters, deceivers, and liars, and the kennel of the wicked is filled with the greatest hellish devils, and it is so full that the devils come out of their spit and snot.) And he said on page 109 of the second volume printed in the year 1562 (I first said that some of the issues of Jan Hus are the issues of the evangelists, and now I retract this statement and say: Not some, but all of his questions that the antichrist and his disciples rejected in the forum of the universe, and I tell you verbally, O representative. Sacred to God: All matters
Jan Hus, the return is obligatory, and every one of your issues is satanic
It is disbelief, so I accept the rejected issues of Jan Hus and am prepared to support them, by the grace of God.)

One of the issues of Jan Hus was (that if a sultan or a priest commits one of the major sins, he no longer remains a sultan or a priest). Since all of his issues were accepted by the head of the reformers, this issue was also accepted. Accordingly, none of his followers will be considered worthy of the sultanate or the priesthood, because there is not one of them who does not commit one of the major sins. What is surprising is that infallibility is not a condition for the prophets, and they were not infallible according to the ruler, and it is required for the sultan. And the priest. Perhaps the position of prophethood is more important to him than the position of priesthood.
As for the words of the aforementioned president regarding the Supreme Sultan Henry VIII, these are: He said on page 277 of the seventh volume, printed in the year 1558, thus:

[1] There is no doubt that Lotar would be afraid if the Sultan spent this much of his saliva on lies and idle talk [2] I am speaking to the cuckolded liar, and since he, for his foolishness, did not respect his sultan’s position, why did I not want him to lie in his throat [3] O ignorant wooden basin, you are lying and the Sultan is a fool who stole the shroud [4] This is how they reached this foolish and persistent Sultan).

It seems that it is permissible for Protestant scholars to use such expressions at an opponent unless they say that they came from them due to human nature. So I say that, God willing, I do not intentionally mention a word that is equivalent to one of the words of their imitators regarding the Christian scholars. However, if a word was issued unintentionally that is not appropriate for their situation in their claim, I ask them for forgiveness and supplication. Christ, peace be upon him, said: (Bless those who curse you, do good to those who hate you, and pray for those who despitefully use you and persecute you) as stated in the fifth chapter of the Gospel of Matthew.

sections.heading: Sixth
content: (Sixth) There are many people in Europe who are described by Protestant scholars as atheists, who deny prophecy and inspiration, and especially mock sects.

According to the Christian doctrine, they misbehave with regard to the prophets, especially with regard to Christ, peace be upon him, and they increase in the mentioned lands day by day, and their books are famous throughout the world, so their sayings will also be quoted as a few in this book, so let no one think from this quotation that I approve of their words and actions, God forbid, no, for the denier of a prophet is among the prophets whose prophethood has been proven to us, especially the one who denies Christ, peace be upon him, is like the denier of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Rather, the transmission is to alert Protestant scholars to know that what they reported regarding the Islamic religion is nothing by comparison with what the people of their homes reported and classified them according to the Christian religion.

sections.heading: Seventh
content: (Seventh) The habit of most Protestant scholars in writing down the answer to the dissenter is that they examine his book with the eyes of stubbornness and arrogance. If they find in the entire book the few weak sayings, they seize them and quote them to mislead the common people. Then they say: All of his books are like this. In fact, for the purpose of their examination, they found nothing but the written amount. Then after that, they take the dissenter’s sayings where they are able to interpret and answer, and they leave out the strong statements altogether and do not indicate. To her too,

They do not transmit all the words of his book in response to make it clear to the observer the state of the words of both sides. Rather, betrayal comes out of them, sometimes in the transmission, so they distort his words, and their original purpose is to make the observer fall into the error of thinking by observing some of the sayings that they transmitted that the words of the opponent are all as they said. This practice is not recommended, and whoever was aware of it would be certain that they did not find in the book of the opponent except this amount, and it is clear that it does not necessitate from him, in assessing the validity of the transmission, that the entire book of the opponent is weak, especially if it is large, because if the book is not Inspirational, there are usually weak sayings in it, because human speech is difficult to be free from this, just as it was said that every strict person has a prophethood, and every horse has a fate, and the first people are the first people, and infallibility from error, oversight, and weakness among us is especially the inspired speech and the inspired book and nothing else. Do they not see that there is not one of their investigators from the time of the imam of the group, Janaab (Lottar) until this present time, such that there is no error or weakness in his words in any of the places in their classifications? Otherwise, they should
The statement and we have the answer.

Is it permissible, in the form mentioned by them, to quote some of the weak sayings that were issued by their imam, Al-Mamduh, or by their other imam (Kalon), or by a famous investigator from among their investigators, and say: All of his remaining words are false and nonsense of this kind, and he did not have accurate consideration? God forbid! We do not say that, but it is contrary to fairness, and if this much was sufficient for them, we would have great comfort, so we quote sayings from the sayings of their imams and scholars in the places that their followers and their people also admitted were weak or wrong, and then we say after that that all of their remaining words are like this, and that they were like that, so what is expected of them is that if they write the answer to this book of mine, they must quote all of my statements in the response, and take into account the matters that are mentioned in Introduction: Even if they apologize for not having the opportunity, this excuse is unacceptable. Because the author of the guide to the seekers stated this on page 310 of his book published in 1840, in the twelfth chapter

From the second part (that about a thousand Protestant pilgrims continue to spread the Gospel, and they have as many as a hundred helpers in this regard, including preachers, teachers, and others who have converted to Christianity). All of these people left their country and have nothing important to do other than preaching and calling to their religion, so how can the excuse of not having the opportunity be accepted from this huge crowd?

I mention something to clarify what I said, regarding the status of the translation of the imam of the group, Janab (Lotar), the status of the book Mizan al-Haqq by the noble priest (Fandar), and the book Solution to Problems and the Key to Secrets by the praised priest as well. Ward Catholic said in his book printed in the year 1841 regarding the aforementioned translation that was in Lisan Dejah (Zonklis, who is one of the greatest Protestant scholars, said, addressing Luther): O Luther, you are destroying the word of God. You are a great destroyer and distorter.

The Holy Books, and we are ashamed of you because we used to venerate you to the end, and now you appear to be such and such.” Loter responded to the translation of Zonclis and called him a fool, a donkey, a charlatan, and a deceiver. The priest (Karman) said regarding the aforementioned translation: (The translation of the books of the Old Testament, especially the Book of Job and the books of the Prophets, is flawed and its defect is not a little, and the translation of the New Testament is also flawed and its defect is not a small one). Psroa and Cyander said to Loter: Your translation is wrong, and six phils found In the translation of the New Testament alone, Emseres recorded one thousand four hundred (1,400 corruptions that are heresies). If the corruption in the translation of the New Testament was one thousand and four hundred, then most likely there is no less than four thousand corruptions in the entire translation, and ignorance and lack of investigation should not be attributed to their glorified Imam despite the presence of these corruptions. How can fair people attribute them to someone whose words were offensive in five or six places, according to the violator’s claim?

And when I have finished explaining the translation of their imam, I will turn to Al-Mizan Al-Haqq and others. Know, brother, that this book has two versions, an old version that had been in circulation for a period of time among the preaching priests before the inquiry was written. When the eminent Zaki Al-Hassan wrote the inquiry, the first and third chapters of the aforementioned copy were returned, and the state of his book was revealed to the noble priest (Fender) after observing the inquiry. He decided to edit it and correct it again, adding something to it and subtracting something from it. So he did this, and produced a new copy. He changed it after complete reform, and printed this new one in the Persian tongue in the year 1849 in the town of Akbarabad and in the Urdu tongue in the year 1850. So that old copy with this new copy became like the abrogated law among them, and they do not care about it. I only quote one saying about it, even though there is a wide scope to talk about it, and I quote twenty-four sayings from this new Persian by way of model, and nine sayings from the book Solving Problems printed in 1847, and two sayings about the old Key of Secrets. What is new is by way of translation in the Arabic language, with reference to the chapter, chapter, and page, so I say, by God, success.
(The first statement) in the second chapter of the first chapter of Mizan al-Haqq on page 17: “The Qur’an and the commentators in this section claim” i.e. abrogation “that as

The Torah was abrogated with the revelation of the Psalms, and the Psalms were abrogated with the appearance of the Gospel. Likewise, the Gospel was abrogated because of the Qur’an.” End quote. His saying: “The Torah was abrogated with the revelation of the Psalms, and the Psalms were abrogated with the appearance of the Gospel” is a slander that has no trace in the Qur’an or in the interpretations. Rather, it has no trace in a book of the books considered by the people of Islam, and the Psalms in our view are not an abrogation of the Torah, nor abrogated by the Gospel. David, peace be upon him, followed the law of Moses, peace be upon him, and the Psalms were supplications that he might have heard from some. The common people thought that it would be in the Qur’an and interpretations and attributed it to it. This is the case of this investigator in stating the case in the appeal, which is the first and greatest of the appeals.
(The second statement) in the chapter mentioned on page 24 is as follows: “There is no basis for the claim of the Muhammadan person that the Psalms abrogated the Torah and the Gospel abrogated them.”

This is also not as true as the first; When I learned that the Psalms were not abrogated by the Torah nor abrogated by the Gospel, and when I asked him to correct the transmission of these two statements in the debate that took place between me and him in the general assembly, he had no recourse but to admit that he had made a mistake, as stated in the debate letters, which were printed repeatedly in Akbarabad and Dehli in Persian and Urdu, so whoever wishes may return to them.

(The third statement) in the chapter mentioned on page 25: “The law of abrogation requires this concept: that God intentionally wanted, in view of His interest and will, to give something incomplete that does not reach or explain what is desired, but how can anyone imagine such incomplete and false concepts in the ancient essence of God, perfect in attributes?”

You will know in the third chapter, God willing, yes, he responds to their sanctifier, Paul, because this sanctified person was afflicted with this incomplete and false conception that the priest had, and it is not possible. He quoted his words from the Arabic translation printed in the year 1860. He said in the seventh chapter of the Hebrew Epistle thus: “18 For the previous commandment would be nullified on account of its weakness and uselessness [19] since the law did not complete anything,” etc., and in the eighth chapter of the aforementioned epistle thus: “[7] For if it were That first one (16) was without blemish when a place was sought for the second” [13] “So if he said new, he freed the first.

As for what is old and old, it is close to disappearing.” And in the ninth verse of the tenth chapter of the aforementioned letter, “The first will be removed until the second is established.” So their sanctifier called the Torah invalid and removed, and it was weak and useless, and did not complete anything and defective, and made it more deserving of decay and invalidation. Rather, he responds to this priest’s claim that God was first afflicted with this false and incomplete conception, and God forbid, because he said through Ezekiel is like this: “Then I gave them not good commandments and judgments to live by,” as stated in the twenty-fifth verse of the twentieth chapter of the Book of Ezekiel. What is most astonishing is the fairness of this investigator that he attributes to the people of Islam what is required according to his doctrine and not theirs.

(The fourth statement) in the chapter mentioned on page 26: “The provisions of the Gospel and the books of the Old Testament must remain in effect as long as the heavens and the earth exist in accordance with these verses,” and this is wrong. Because if what it requires is the continuation of the provisions of the two covenants, then all the priests must be obligated to kill, because they do not glorify the Sabbath, and its glorification contradicts the ruling of the Torah, the obligation of killing. However, he acknowledged in this chapter on page 19: “The apparent rulings” of the Torah “were perfected by the appearance of the Messiah, and abrogated in the sense that as long as their observance remained necessary.” These apparent rulings, according to his confession, remained current as long as the heavens and the earth existed, and they were perfected and abrogated in the aforementioned sense.

According to them, it is the abrogation of the rulings that are termed by us, and Jesus, peace be upon him, said to the disciples when he sent them on the way to the Gentiles: “Do not go, nor enter into the city of the Samaritans,” and “He said, ‘I have not been sent except to the lost sheep of the House of Israel.’” So he neglected to call on the Gentiles and the Samaritans, and devoted his message to the children of Israel. Then he said at the time of their ascension to heaven: “Go into the whole world and preach the Gospel to the whole creation.” So he ordered the whole world to be invited, and he circulated his message, so he abrogated His first rule.

After consultation, the disciples abrogated all the practical rulings included in the Torah except four rulings: the prohibition of idol sacrifice, the prohibition of blood, the prohibition of strangled meat, and the prohibition of adultery, and they wrote a letter on this subject to the churches, as stated in chapter fifteen of the Book of Acts.

Then their sanctifier Paul abrogated the first three from these four also with a fatwa of general permissibility included in the fourteenth verse of the fourteenth chapter of his letter to the Romans, and in the fifteenth verse of the first chapter of his letter to Titus. The disciples abrogated the provisions of the Torah, and their sanctifier abrogated the provisions of the apostles. It appears from what I mentioned that abrogation as occurred in the provisions of the Torah also occurred in the provisions of the Gospel. (As for the first section of the Old Testament) it consists of thirty-eight books:

[1] The Book of Genesis, also called the Book of Creation. [2] The Book of Exodus. [3] The Book of the Rabbis. [4] The Book of Numbers. As for the second part of the New Testament, it consists of seven books and some paragraphs from the first letter of John:

Likewise, the Fourth Book of Ezra is attributed to Ezra, the Book of Isaiah’s Ascension, and the Book of Isaiah’s Observations are attributed to Isaiah, peace be upon him. Another book attributed to him is the famous book of Jeremiah, peace be upon him, and several manuscripts are attributed to Hakkuk, peace be upon him, and several Psalms are attributed to Solomon, peace be upon him.

Of the books of the New Testament, other than the books mentioned, there are more than seventy books attributed to Jesus, Mary, the disciples and their followers. You learned in the first chapter that the Book of Baruch, the Book of Tobit, the Book of Judith, the Book of Zoddam, the Book of Ecclesiastical Styx, the two books of the Macabians, and part of the Book of Esther are obligatory for Catholics to accept and for Protestants to reject.

Joseph Bess stated in the third chapter of the third book of his history: “The first letter of Peter is authentic, except that his second letter was not included in the holy books at any time, but the fourteen letters of Paul were read, except that some people took out the Hebrew letter.” Then he stated in the twenty-fifth chapter of the aforementioned book: “They disagreed that the Epistle of James, the Epistle of Judea, the Second Epistle of Peter, and the Second and Third Epistle of John were written by the Evangelists or other people, whose names were these. And let him understand that the Acts of Paul and (Bachter) and the observations of Peter, and the Epistle of Berniah, and the book called (Anas te Toshin) of the Apostles are fictitious books, and if it is proven, then let him consider the observations of John also as such.” In chapter twenty-five of the sixth book of his history, he quoted (Argen) saying in relation to the Hebrew Epistle as follows: “The situation that was on the tongues of the people was that

Some of them said that this letter was written by Clement, who was (47) the Romans, and some of them said that Luke translated it and denied it outright (Arnis Bishop Lys), who was in the year 178, (Wahb Politus), who was in the year 220, and (Nuites Preceptor, the Romans), who was in the year 251, and (Naztulin Preceptor Carthage), who was in the year 300, said: It is the letter of Berniaukes, the Preceptor of the Romans. In the year 212, he counted thirteen letters of Paul, and he did not prepare this letter. (Wasi Bern Basheb Carthage) who was in the year 248, did not mention this letter, and the Syriac Church to this day does not hand over the second letter of Peter, and the second and third letters of John, and (Schalger) said that whoever wrote the second letter to Peter wasted his time, and (Jose Bess) said in the twenty-third chapter of the second book of his history regarding the letter of James: “They thought that This message is fictitious, but many of the ancients mentioned it, and it was also thought that the message of Judea was true, but it was
It is used in many churches.
In the History of the Bible, published in 1850, Crotis said: “This letter is the letter of the bishop Yehuda, who was the fifteenth bishop of Jerusalem during the reign of the Sultanate of Aydarin.”

And Yossi Bess wrote in the twenty-fifth chapter of the sixth book of his history: “Argen said in the fifth volume of the Commentary on the Gospel of John that Paul did not write anything to all the churches, and what he wrote to some of them is two or four lines.” According to Argen, the letters attributed to Paul are not his classification, but rather they are a metaphor attributed to him, and perhaps as much as two or four lines are found in some of Paul’s words as well, and if you contemplate the aforementioned sayings, it will appear to you that what Fastus said: “This New Testament was not compiled by Christ nor the Apostles, but rather by an unknown man

He attributed to the Apostles and their companions "an undoubted truth, and he was correct in this matter. I learned in the first chapter that the six letters and the Book of Observations were doubtful and were rejected in the year 363, and they were not handed over by the (Nasi) assembly, which was held in the year 325. Then the six letters were accepted in the Ludisia forum in the year 364, and the Book of Observations remained doubtful and rejected in this forum as well, so it was accepted in the (Carthage) assembly in the year 397, and the acceptance of these two jurors is not an argument.

As for the first: Because the scholars of all six forums handed down the Book of Judith, and that the scholars of the Ludisia forum handed down ten verses from the tenth chapter, and six chapters after the tenth chapter of the Book of (Esther), and that the scholars of the (Carthage) forum handed down the Book of (Zadham), the Book of (Tobiah), the Book of (Baruch), the Book of (Ecclesiastyx), and the Book of the Macabians, and their ruling on these books was handed down by the scholars of the three subsequent forums, so if their ruling was with evidence and proof, it would be necessary. Rejecting all, even if it is without proof, as is the truth, requires rejecting all. It is surprising that the Protestant group accepts their ruling in the Six Epistles and the Book of Observations, and rejects it in others, especially in the Book of Judith, which the six assemblies agreed to hand over. Their lame excuse does not match the books rejected by them other than the Book of Esther, that their origins have been lost, because Jerome says: He obtained the origin of Judith and the origin of Tobiah in the tongue of the cock, and the origin of the first book of the Macabites.

The origin of the book Ecclesiastyx was in the Hebrew tongue, and these books were translated from their originals, so they are obliged to hand over these books, the origins of which were obtained by Jerome, but they are obligated not to hand over the Gospel of Matthew as well, because its original is lost.

Secondly: Because it has been proven by (Horn’s) admission that the narrations were not adhered to among their ancients, and they believed the weak narrations and wrote them down, and those who came after them followed their sayings, it is most likely that some weak narrations in the chapter of these books reached the scholars of the forums as well, and they handed them over after they had been rejected for centuries.

And thirdly: Because the state of the Holy Books among them is like the state of regulations and laws, do you not see: [1] that the Greek translation was considered by their predecessors from the time of the Apostles to the fifteenth century, and they believed that the Hebrew version was distorted and the correct one was this one, and after that the matter was reversed, and the distorted version became correct, and the correct one was wrong and distorted, so it was necessary for all their predecessors to be ignorant [2] and that the Book of Daniel was considered by their predecessors according to the Greek translation, When Argen ruled that it was not authentic, they left it and took it from the translation of (Theodosian) [3] and that the Epistle (Ars Tis) was Muslim until the sixteenth century, then they spoke about it in the seventeenth century, so it became false according to the majority of Protestant scholars [4] and that the Latin translation is considered by (the Catholics) and is a corruption that is not considered by the Protestants.

[5] And that the Little Book of Genesis was considered authentic until the fifth century, as you will know in the second chapter, and then in the sixteenth century it became incorrect and seminal [6] and that the Third Book of Ezra is handed down by the Church of (Creek) (48) until now, and the Catholic and Protestant factions reject it, and that the Psalms of Solomon were handed down by their ancients and it was written in their holy books and is found until now in a copy (Codex Alexandrianus) and now it is considered seminal, and we hope that they will gradually They will acknowledge the creation of all, God willing.

From what I mentioned, it appears to the discerning observer that there is no continuous support for them, neither for the books of the Old Testament, nor for the books of the New Testament, and if they are restricted in this regard, they sometimes cling to the fact that Christ testified to the truth of the books of the Old Testament, and you will know the status of this testimony in detail in the answer to the second fallacy from the second chapter, so wait for it.

content: [Chapter Three: Explaining that these books are full of differences and errors]
I divide this chapter into two sections and provide examples in each section:
[Part One: Explaining the Differences]

The difference [1] The first one who contrasted chapters forty-five and forty-six of the Book of Ezekiel with chapters twenty-eight and twenty-ninth of the Book of Numbers found a clear difference in the rulings.

The difference [2] between the thirteenth chapter of the Book of Joshua and the second chapter of the Book of Exception in explaining the inheritance of the Children of Gad is a clear difference, and one of the two statements is definitely wrong, as I learned in the second chapter regarding the Book of Joshua.

[The difference [3]] There is a difference between the seventh and eighth chapters of the first book of the Chronicles in explaining the children of Benjamin, and likewise between them and the forty-sixth chapter of the Book of Genesis, and the scholars of the People of the Book, both Jews and Christians, acknowledged that what occurred in the first book of the Chronicles was wrong, as you will know in the first purpose of the second chapter.

The difference [4] There is a difference between the names in the eighth chapter of the first book of Chronicles from the twenty-ninth to the thirty-eighth verse, and in the ninth chapter of the aforementioned book from the thirty-fifth to the forty-fourth verse, and (Adam Clark) said in the second volume of his interpretation: “The Jewish scholars say that Ezra found two books in which these passages are found with different names, and he could not distinguish which of them was better, so he copied them.”

The difference [5] The ninth verse of the twenty-fourth chapter of the Second Book of Samuel is thus: “And Joab 2 brought the number and account of the people to the king, and the number of the children of Israel was eight hundred thousand men who were valiant and might use the sword, and the men of Judah were numbered five hundred thousand fighting men.” And the fifth verse of the twenty-first chapter of the first book of the Chronicles is thus: “And the census of the people was delivered to David, and the number of the children of Israel was one thousand one hundred thousand men who drew the sword, and the Jews were four hundred thousand and seventy thousand.” A fighting man.” There was a difference between them in the number of the children of Israel by three hundred thousand, and in the number of the Jews by the amount of thirty thousand
The difference [6] The thirteenth verse of the twenty-fourth chapter of the Second Book of Samuel is thus: “And Gad came to David and told him, saying: Either there will be seven

Years of famine for you in your land,” etc., and in the twelfth verse of the twenty-first chapter of the first book of the Chronicles, it is as follows: (Either three years of famine), etc. In the first, there are seven years, and in the second, three years. Their commentators have acknowledged that the first is wrong.

The difference [7] The twenty-sixth verse of the eighth chapter of the Second Book of Kings is thus: “And Ahaziah had ruled twenty-two years when he reigned,” etc. And the second verse of the twenty-second chapter of the Second Book of Chronicles is thus: “Ahaziah was forty-two years old” etc. So there is a difference between them, and the second was definitely a mistake, as their commentators acknowledged, and how could it not be a mistake, since his father (Joram) was forty years old when he died and sat down? He is on the Sultanate’s bed after his father’s death, as is evident from the previous chapter, even if it was not a mistake
He must be two years older than his father

The difference [8] The eighth verse of the twenty-fourth chapter of the Second Book of Kings is like this: “And Joachin was eighteen years old on the day he reigned,” etc. And the ninth verse of the thirty-sixth chapter of the thirty-second book of Chronicles is like this: “Joachin was eight years old as king,” etc. There is a difference between them, and the second is definitely wrong, as their commentators have acknowledged, and you will know in the first purpose of the second chapter.

The difference [9] between the eighth verse of the twenty-third chapter of the Second Book of Samuel and the eleventh verse of the eleventh chapter of the Book of Kings of the Chronicles is a difference, and (Adam Clarke) said at the end of the explanation of Samuel’s phrase: (Daktarkni Kat said): “There are three gross distortions in this verse.”
There are three mistakes in this one verse

The difference [10] It was stated in the fifth and sixth chapters of the Second Book of Samuel that David, peace be upon him, brought the ark of God after fighting the Philistines, and it was stated in the thirteenth and fourteenth chapters of the first book of the Chronicles that he brought the ark before fighting them, and the incident is the same, as is not hidden from anyone who sees it.
The mentioned chapters, then one of them is wrong

The difference [11] It is known from verses 19 and 20 of the sixth chapter, and from verses 8 and 6 of the seventh chapter of the Book of Genesis, that God commanded Noah, peace be upon him, to take from every bird, animal, and insects of the earth two by two, male and female, and it is known from verse 2 and 3 of the seventh chapter that he was commanded to take from every clean animal, and from every bird, pure or unclean, seven pairs, and from every impure animal two by two.

The difference [12] It is known from the thirty-first chapter of the Book of Numbers that the children of Israel annihilated the Midianites during the reign of Moses, peace be upon him, and that they did not leave any male among them at all, neither mature nor immature, even an infant boy as well, and likewise they did not leave among them a woman.
And they took non-adult female slave girls for themselves.

It is known from the sixth chapter of the Book of Judges that the Midianites during the reign of the Judges were of such great power that the children of Israel were defeated and helpless by them, and there was no period between the two covenants except for the duration of two hundred years. (So I say) If the Midianites perished during the reign of Moses, how did they become so powerful during this period of time that they defeated the children of Israel or incapacitated them for seven years?

The difference [13] in the ninth chapter of the Book of Exodus is as follows: “So the Lord did this word on the next day, and all the livestock of the Egyptians died, and not one of the livestock of the children of Israel died.” So it is known from it that all the livestock of the Egyptians died. Then in this section: “Whoever fears the word of the Lord among the servants of Pharaoh will flee with his servants
And his animals go to the houses, and whoever does not think of the word of the Lord leaves his servants and his animals in the fields.” There is a difference between them.

The difference [14] in the eighth chapter of the Book of Genesis is as follows: “4 And the ark rested on the twenty-seventh day of the seventh month on the Armenian mountains, 5 and the waters went and decreased until the tenth month, for in the tenth month, on the first of the month, the tops of the mountains became visible.” So there is a difference between the two verses because if the tops of the mountains appeared in the tenth month, how did the ark rest in the seventh month on the Armenian mountains?

The fifteenth difference to the twenty-sixth difference: There is a large discrepancy between the eighth chapter of the Second Book of Samuel and the eighteenth chapter of the First Book of Chronicles in the Hebrew original, although the translators corrected it in some places and quoted it from the words of (Adam Clarke), the interpreter, from the second volume of his interpretation, the footer of the phrase Samuel.

Adam Clarke, the commentator, quoted the differences in translations and explanations at the end of the phrase in the Book of Kings first, then said: “It is better to acknowledge that there has been a distortion in the number due to these differences.”

The difference [34] between the twenty-fourth verse of the seventh chapter of the first book of Kings, and the third verse of the fourth chapter of the second book of the chronicles is a difference. Adam Clarke said in the second volume of his interpretation, following the explanation of the phrase of the chronicles: “The senior scholars thought that it would be better to include the phrase in the book of kings here as well, and it is possible that the word 2 bakrim occurred in the place of the bak’im.”

The meaning of the Beqrim is the bull and the meaning of the Buqaym is the necklace. This commentator admitted that there had been a distortion in the Chronicles, so the phrase “Chronicles” was a mistake in his view. The compilers of Henry Wascat’s interpretation said: “The difference occurred here because of the change of letters.”

The difference [35] The second verse of the sixteenth chapter of the Second Book of Kings is thus: “And Ahaz was twenty years old on the day he began to reign, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem,” etc. And in the case of his son Ezekiel, it occurred in the second verse of the eighteenth chapter of the aforementioned book thus: “And the day that he reigned twenty-five years had come upon him,” so Ezekiel must have been born to Ahaz in the eleventh year of his age.

This is contrary to custom, as it appears that one of them is wrong, and the commentators have acknowledged that the first is wrong. The compilers of Henry Wascott’s interpretation said at the end of the explanation of chapter sixteen: “Most likely the word twenty was written in the place of thirty. See the second verse of chapter eighteen of this book.”

The difference [36] in the first verse of the twenty-eighth chapter of the second book of the Chronicles is like this: “When Ahaz reigned he was twenty years old, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem” and in the first verse of the twenty-ninth chapter of the aforementioned book like this: “So Hezekiah reigned twenty-five years old.” Here also one of them is wrong and it seems that the first one is as you know.

The difference [37] between the thirty-first verse of the twelfth chapter of the Second Book of Samuel and the third verse of the twentieth chapter of the first book of the Chronicles is a difference, and (Horne) said in the first volume of his interpretation: “The phrase of the Book of Samuel is correct, so let the phrase of the Book of Chronicles be made like it.” When the phrase of the Book of Chronicles is wrong, see how he orders correction and distortion. It is surprising that the translator of the Arabic translation printed in 1844 made
The phrase of the book of Samuel is like the phrase of the book of Chronicles and justice, that it is no wonder this is their upper room.

The difference [38] The thirty-third verse of the fifteenth chapter of the First Book of Kings is thus: “In the third year of Asamalch of Judah, Baasha the son of Ahijah reigned over all Israel in Tirzah twenty-four years.” And the first verse of the sixteenth chapter of the Second Book of Chronicles is thus: “And in the thirty-sixth year of the reign of Asaa, king of Israel, Baasha ascended over Judah,” etc. There is a difference between them, and one of them is definitely wrong, because Baasha, according to the rule of the first, died in

The twenty-sixth year of Asa, and in the thirty-sixth year of Asa, ten years had passed since the death of Baasha, so how did he go up against Judah in this year? The compilers of Henry and Scott's interpretation of the end of the phrase of the Book of Chronicles said: “It appears that this date is wrong.” And Usher, who is one of the most prominent Christian scholars, said: This is the thirty-sixth year of (the division that occurred during the reign of Ur in the year of the Sultanate, not of the Sultanate of Asa). These scholars accepted that the phrase of the Chronicles is wrong. Either the word “thirty-six” occurred in the place of the word “twenty-six,” or the word “King Asa” occurred in place of the word “the division of the Sultanate.”

The difference [39] The nineteenth verse of the fifteenth chapter of the second book of the Chronicles is like this: “And there was no war, that is, between Asa and Baasha, until the thirty-fifth year of the reign of Asa.” This also contradicts the thirty-third verse of the fifteenth chapter of the first book of Kings, as it was known in the previous difference.

The difference [40] In the sixteenth verse of the First Book of Kings, the number of those appointed was three thousand and three hundred, and in the second verse of the second chapter of the Second Book of Chronicles, three thousand and six hundred, and the translators of the Greek translation distorted the Book of Kings and wrote three thousand and six hundred.

The difference [41] in the twenty-sixth verse of the seventh chapter of the First Book of Kings: “And the sea 2 contained two thousand divisions” and in the fifth verse of the fourth chapter of the second book of the Chronicles thus: “It contained three thousand divisions.” And the first sentence in the Persian translation printed in 1838 is thus: “Dohzarbet Daran Knjid” and in the Persian translation of 1845 thus: (Dohzarkham ab Mycraft) and the second sentence is thus in a Persian translation in the year 1838: (Waseh Hazarbet Duran Kangid) Persian translation in 1845: (Wasah Hazarakham Ab Karfateh Nikah Midasht) There is a thousand differences and disparities between them.

The Book of Nehemiah found a great difference between them in most places, and if we ignore the difference, there is another mistake in them, which is that they agreed on the sum of the summation and said: Those who came from Babylon to Jerusalem after they had been released from the captivity of Babylon were forty-two thousand three hundred and sixty persons. The sum does not come out to this extent if we sum it up, neither in the words of Ezra nor in the words of Nehemiah, but rather the sum of the summation in the first is 29,818 and in the second, 31,089, and the wonder is that This agreed combination is also an error in the historians’ statement. In the rest, the Greek translation is used to explain the Hebrew text.

If they are unable, they attribute it to the writers who are innocent of this, and whoever looks now at these two chapters will find the differences and errors more than twenty, and I do not know how they will do it tomorrow and how they will distort it.

The difference [43] in the second verse of the thirteenth chapter of the second book of Chronicles: “The mother of Abijah was Miciah, the daughter of Uriel of Gibeah.” It is known from the twentieth verse of the eleventh chapter of the aforementioned book that his mother was (Maachah the daughter of Abi Shalom), and it is known from the twenty-seventh verse of the fourteenth chapter of the second book of Samuel that Abu Shalom had only one daughter named Tamar.

The difference [44] is known from the tenth chapter of the Book of Joshua that when the children of Israel killed the ruler of Jerusalem, they ruled over his kingdom: And from the sixty-third verse of the fifteenth chapter of the aforementioned book, they did not rule over the kingdom of Jerusalem.

The difference [45] is known from the first verse of the twenty-fourth chapter of the Second Book of Samuel that God put it into the heart of David to number the children of Israel, and it is known from the first verse of the twenty-first chapter [p. 96] of the first book of the Chronicles that the one who cast it was Satan, and since God was not the creator of evil according to them, a strong disagreement is necessary.

The forty-sixth difference to the fifty-first difference: Whoever compares the statement of Christ’s lineage in the Gospel of Matthew with the statement in the Gospel of Luke will find six differences:

[1] It is known from Matthew that he is Joseph, the son of Jacob, and from Luke, that he is the son of Heli. [2] It is known from Matthew that Jesus was one of the sons of Suleiman bin David, peace be upon them, and who

Luke is one of the sons of Nathan, son of David. [3] It is learned from Matthew that all of Christ’s fathers, from David to the deportation to Babylon, were famous sultans, and from Luke that they were neither sultans nor famous except David and Nathan. [4] It is known from Matthew that Shealtiel was the son of Johaniah, and it is known from Luke that he was the son of Neri. [5] It is known from Matthew that the name of the son of Zor Babylon is Abihud, and from Luke that his name is Rez. What is surprising is that the names of the son of Zor Babylon are written in the third chapter of the first book of the Chronicles, and neither Abihud nor Rez is in it, so the truth is that both of them are wrong.

[6] From David to Christ, peace be upon them, twenty-six generations, according to what Matthew explained, and forty-one generations, according to what Luke explained, and since there was a period of a thousand years between David and Christ, then in the first there are forty years in each generation, and in the second there are twenty-five, and since the difference between the two statements was apparent upon contemplation, Christian scholars were confused about them from the time of the popularity of these two Gospels until today, and were given weak instructions, and for this reason a group of investigators such as (Eckharn) admitted (Keyser, Hess, Diot, Wey Norfresh), and others, that they are morally different, and this is right and fair, because just as the evangelists issued errors and differences in other places, so there was confusion here. They had two different papers in explaining the lineage of Yusuf al-Najjar, and they could not distinguish between what is true and what is wrong, so one of them chose, according to his opinion, one of the two papers, and the other the other, and the aforementioned commentator’s hope that time does it like this is a hopeless hope, because if it does not describe for a period of one thousand eight hundred, especially in these last three centuries in which the rational and traditional sciences became widespread in the lands of Europe, and they headed to achieving everything, even to realizing the religion as well, so they reformed the religion somewhat first, so they ruled on At first glance, the general doctrine was false, and the pope, who was an imitator of the religion, was accused of being ignorant and treacherous. The well-known guidance now is that it is possible for Matthew to have written the genealogy of Joseph, and Luke to have written the genealogy of Mary, and Joseph would have circumcised Heli, and Heli would not have a son, so the circumcision was attributed to him, and he was included in the genealogy, and this guidance is rejected for several reasons: First: Christ, according to this estimation, would be one of the children of Nathan, not one of the children of Solomon, because his true lineage is on his mother’s side, and the lineage of Joseph the carpenter is not considered in his right, so it is necessary that not

The second: This guidance is not valid unless it is proven from reliable histories that Mary is the daughter of Heli, and one of the children of Nathan, and mere possibility is not enough for this, especially in the form in which the investigators, such as Adam Clarke the interpreter and others, reject it, and their imitator (Kalwyn) rejects it.
