Edom, and Adam Clarke, the commentator, first ruled that it was definitely a mistake, then said: It was most likely the writer’s mistake.

(The fourteenth witness) occurred in the seventh verse of the aforementioned chapter: “Abu Salum said to the Sultan after forty years.” The wording of forty is certainly wrong, but the correct wording of four is correct. Adam Clarke said in the second volume of his interpretation: “There is no doubt that this phrase is distorted,” and then he said: “The majority of scholars are of the opinion that the forty occurred in the place of the four due to the writer’s error.”

(Fifteenth Witness) Adam Clarke said in the second volume of his interpretation at the end of the eighth verse of the twenty-third chapter of the Second Book of Samuel: “He said, ‘Keni Kat,’ in this verse in the Hebrew text, there are three great distortions,” so here he acknowledged three gross distortions.

(The sixteenth verse) The sixth verse of the seventh chapter of the first book of the Chronicles is thus: “The sons of Benjamin, Bela, Bakr, and Jediba Bel, three persons,” and in the eighth chapter of the aforementioned book thus: [1] “Benjamin begat his eldest son Bela, the second Ishbal, and the third Aharah” [2] “And the fourth was Noah, and the fifth was Rephah,” and in the twenty-first verse of the forty-sixth chapter of the Book of Genesis thus: “The version of the year 1848: The sons of Benjamin, Bala, Bachur, Ashbal, Gera, Naaman, Ahi, Rosh, Mavim, and Hupim, is mentioned.” In the three phrases, there is a difference in their first meaning in the names, and the second in number, where it is understood from the first that Benjamin’s sons are three, and from the second it is understood that they are five, and from the third it is understood that they are ten, and since the first and second phrases are from one book, a contradiction is necessary in the words of one author, which is Ezra the Prophet, peace be upon him, and there is no doubt that one of their phrases is true. The remaining two are false, and the scholars of the People of the Book were confused about it and were forced to attribute the error to Ezra, peace be upon him. Adam Clarke said at the end of the first phrase: “It was written here for the sake of not distinguishing the son of the son from the place of the son and vice versa, and the application in such differences is not

Mufid, and Jewish scholars say that Ezra, peace be upon him, who wrote this book, had no knowledge that some of these people were sons or sons of sons, and they also say that the lineage papers that Ezra, peace be upon him, quoted were mostly incomplete, and we must leave such transactions.”

So look, O wise man, here how the People of the Book were forced to flee, whether they were Jews or Christians, and they found no recourse but to acknowledge that what Ezra, peace be upon him, wrote was wrong, and what happened to him was the distinction between sons and sons’ sons, so he wrote what he wrote, and the interpreter of why he despaired of application said firstly: “Application in such differences is useless” and secondly said: “We must abandon such transactions.”

(A great benefit) that must be noted. Know, may God Almighty guide you, that the majority of the People of the Book say: The first and second books of the Chronicles were compiled by Ezra, peace be upon him, with the help of Haggai and Zechariah, the two messengers, peace be upon them. Accordingly, the two books mentioned were agreed upon by the three prophets, peace be upon them, and the books of history bear witness that the condition of the books of the Old Testament before the incident of Bukhnezzar was incomplete, and after his incident, nothing remained of them except the name. And if Ezra, peace be upon him, had not written down these books again, they would not have existed in his time, let alone time. The other, and this matter is accepted by the People of the Book also in the book that is attributed to Ezra, and the group of Protestants do not acknowledge that it is
Heavenly, but with that belief it does not degrade its rank from the books of Christian historians.

To them, it happened like this: “The Torah was burned, and no one knew it, and it was said that Ezra collected what was in it again with the help of the Holy Spirit.” Clemens Alexander Janus said: “The heavenly books were lost, so he inspired Ezra to write them again.” Tertulline said: “It is well-known that Ezra wrote the collection of books after the Babylonians raided Jerusalem.” And Hugh Felket said: “The Holy Books were completely lost, so Ezra created them.” Once again with inspiration.” End quote. Jean Melz Catholic said on page 115 of his book, which was printed in the town of Derby in 1842: “The scholars have agreed that the original copy of the Torah, as well as the copies of the books of the Old Testament, were lost at the hands of the army of Bukhnezzar, and when their authentic sayings appeared through Ezra, those sayings were lost, also in the Antiochus Incident.” As much as necessary, if you know these sayings, refer to the words of the aforementioned commentator, and I say it appears.

The scholar here has seven matters: (The first matter) is that this Torah that is currently being circulated is not the Torah that was first inspired by Moses, peace be upon him, and then after it ceased to exist, Ezra, peace be upon him, wrote it with inspiration again. Otherwise, Ezra, peace be upon him, would have returned to it, and he would not have disagreed with it, and he quoted according to his own will and did not rely on the incomplete papers from which he was unable to distinguish between the wrong and the correct ones, even if they said it was him, but it was also copied from the incomplete copies that came to him, and he was not able to distinguish between them when editing, as It was not estimated here among the missing papers, so I said that based on this assessment, the Torah is not reliable, even if its transmitter was Ezra, peace be upon him.

(The second matter) is that if Ezra made a mistake in this book even though the other two messengers were appointed to compose this book, then it is permissible for the mistake to be made by him in the other books as well. There is no harm if someone denies something from these books if that thing is contrary to definitive proof or contradicts intuition, such as denying what happened in the nineteenth chapter of the Book of Genesis, that Lot, peace be upon him, committed adultery with his two daughters, God Almighty forbid, and they became pregnant by their father. Two sons were born to them, the father of the Moabites and the Omanites, and what happened

In the twenty-first chapter of the first book of Samuel, it is mentioned that David, peace be upon him, committed adultery with the wife of Uriah, and she became pregnant by his adultery, so he killed her husband by trickery and disposed of it. And what happened in the eleventh chapter of the first book of Kings is that Solomon, peace be upon him, apostatized at the end of his life at the urging of his wives, and worshiped idols and built temples to them, and fell from the sight of God, and such stories that make people of faith shiver from the skin and are denied by evidence.

(The third matter) is that if a thing becomes distorted, it is not necessary for that distortion to disappear with the direction of the Prophet after him, and for him to inform God Almighty about the distorted places at all, nor did the divine custom apply to him.

(The fourth matter) is that the Protestant scholars claimed that the prophets and disciples, even if they were not infallible from sins, error, and forgetfulness, were infallible in conveying and writing, so everything they conveyed or edited was protected from error, oversight, and forgetfulness. I say that what they claimed has no basis in their books, otherwise why did the liberation of Ezra, peace be upon him, with the two messengers, peace be upon him, being his appointees, not be protected from error?

(The fifth matter) is that the Prophet was not sometimes inspired in some matters even though he was in need of inspiration, because Ezra, peace be upon him, was not inspired even though he was in need of inspiration in that matter.

(Sixth matter) It has become apparent that the claim of the people of Islam is true, that we do not accept that everything included in these books is inspired and on the part of God, because the error does not fit to be inspired and on the part of God, and it is found in these books without a doubt, as I knew above, and in the previous evidence, and it will be known in the subsequent evidence as well, God willing.

(The seventh matter) If Ezra, peace be upon him, was not immune from error in editing, then how could Mark and Luke the Evangelists, who were not also among the Apostles, be immune from error in editing? Because according to the People of the Book, Ezra, peace be upon him, was a prophet with inspiration, and the two prophets were inspired and appointed to him in liberation, and Mark and Luke are not prophets with inspiration, but for us Matthew and John are not like that, even if the claim of the Christians from the Protestant sect is contrary to him, and the words of these four evangelists are full of errors and outrageous differences.
(The seventeenth witness) Adam Clarke said in the second volume of his interpretation, the tail of the verse

The twenty-ninth of the eighth chapter of the first book of the Chronicles: “In this chapter, from this verse to the thirty-eighth verse, and in the ninth chapter, from the thirty-fifth verse to the forty-fourth verse, there are different names, and the Jewish scholars said that Ezra found two books in which these passages were found, with some difference in names, and he could not distinguish which of them was better, so he quoted them.” And you can say here as mentioned in the previous witness.

(The eighteenth witness) In the thirteenth chapter of the second book of the Chronicles, in the third verse, the word “four hundred thousand” is mentioned in the number of Abiah’s army, and the word is “eight hundred thousand” in the number of the army of Jeroboam, and in the seventeenth verse the word is “five hundred thousand” in the number of those killed from the army of Jeroboam, and since these numbers for these kings were inconsistent with analogy, they were changed in most copies of the Latin translation to forty thousand in the first place, and eighty One thousand in the second place, and fifty thousand in the third place, and the commentators were satisfied with this change. Horn said in the first volume of his interpretation: “It is most likely that the number of these copies is.”

That is, the copies of the Latin translation are “authentic,” and Adam Clarke said in the second volume of his interpretation: “It is known that the small number” that is, what is found in the copies of the Latin translation, “are extremely correct, and we have been greatly distressed by the occurrence of distortion in the numbers of these history books.” He ended his words, and this commentator, after acknowledging the distortion here, stated that it occurred frequently in the numbers.

(Nineteenth witness) In the ninth verse of the thirty-sixth chapter of the Second Book of Chronicles: “Joachin was eight years old when he became a ruler.” He pronounced eight years incorrectly, and contradicts what occurred in the eighth verse of the twenty-fourth chapter of the Second Book of Kings: “And Joachim was eighteen years old when he sat on the throne.” Adam Clarke said in the second volume of his interpretation at the end of the phrase in the Book of Kings: “It occurred in the ninth verse of the thirty-sixth chapter.” From the second book of the Chronicles, the word “eight” is completely wrong, because his rule lasted for three months, then he went to Babylon as a prisoner, and he was in prison with his wives with him, and it is most likely that he did not have a son.
Eight or nine years in pairs, and it is also a mistake to say to such a young child that he did something that was disgraceful to God, as this place in the book is distorted.”

(The Twentieth Witness) In the seventeenth verse of the twenty-first Psalms, according to what is in some versions, or in the sixteenth verse of the twenty-second Psalms, this sentence occurred in the Hebrew version: “And both of my hands are like a lion.” And the Christians from the Catholic and Protestant sect in their biographies convey it like this: “And they pierced my hands and my feet.” These people agree on distorting the Hebrew here.

(Twenty-one Witness) Adam Clarke said in the fourth volume of his interpretation, the footer of the second verse of the sixty-fourth chapter of the Book of Isaiah: “The Hebrew text is greatly distorted here, and it is correct for it to be like this: “As wax melts from fire.”

(Twenty-second Witness) The fourth verse of the aforementioned chapter is thus: “For from of old man has not heard nor reached anyone’s ear, nor has anyone’s eyes seen a God other than You who does such things to those who wait for Him.” Paul quoted this verse in the ninth verse of the second chapter of his first letter to

The people of Corinthians are like this: “But as it is written, ‘The things which God has prepared for those who love Him are things that no eye has seen, nor any ear heard, nor have entered into the mind of man.’” So how much difference is there between them? One of them is distorted. In Henry Wascat's interpretation. “The good opinion is that the Hebrew text is distorted,” and Adam Clark, following the statement of Isaiah, peace be upon him, first quoted many sayings, which he rejected and criticized, then he said: “I am confused about what to do in these problems other than to place in the hands of the observer one of two things: Either it is believed that the Jews intentionally distorted this place in the Hebrew text and the Greek translation, as is the strong belief in other places transmitted in the New Testament from the Old Testament, see the book of On from chapter six to chapter nine regarding the Greek translation, or it is believed that Paul did not quote from that book, but rather he quoted from one or two books of the Biblical books, I mean the Ascension of Isaiah, and the sightings of Elijah, from which this passage was found. In both of them, some thought that the disciple quoted from the books of jurisprudence, and perhaps people do not accept the first possibility easily, so he eloquently alerted the onlookers that Jerome considered the second possibility worse than atheism.” End of his words.
(Witness Twenty-Three to Witness Twenty-Eight) Horn said in the second volume of his interpretation: “It is known that the Hebrew text in the detailed paragraphs at the end is distorted.”

1 - The first verse of the third chapter of the Book of Malachia” 2 - “The second verse of the fifth chapter of the Book of Micah” 3 - “From the eighth verse to the eleventh verse of the sixteenth Psalms” 4 - “The eleventh and twelfth verses of the ninth chapter of the Book of Amos” 5 - “From the sixth to the eighth verse of the fortieth Psalms” 6 - “The fourth verse of the one hundred and tenth Psalms” Their investigator acknowledged the distortion in these places in the verses, and directed His confirmation: The first place was quoted by Matthew in the tenth verse of the eleventh chapter of his Gospel, and what he quoted contradicts the words of Malachiah that are quoted in the Hebrew text and the ancient biographies in two ways: (The first) that the word “before your face” in this sentence: Here I am, I send my King before your face” is an addition to Matthew’s quote, which is not found in the words of Malachiah (and the second) is that it occurred in his quote, “to tread the path before you,” and in the words of Malachiah, “to tread the path.” before me,” and Horne said in a footnote: “The reason for the discrepancy cannot be easily explained except that some distortion occurred in the ancient copies.” The second place was also quoted by Matthew in the sixth verse of the second chapter of

His Gospel, and there is a discrepancy between them, and that the third place was quoted by Luke in the twenty-fifth to twenty-eighth verse of the second chapter of the Book of Acts of the Apostles, and there is a discrepancy between them, and that the fourth place was transmitted by Luke in the sixteenth and seventeenth verses of the fifteenth chapter of the Book of Acts of the Apostles, and between them there is a discrepancy, and that the fifth place was transmitted by Paul in the fifth to seventh verse in his letter to the Hebrews, and between them is a discrepancy.
As for the status of the sixth place, it was not really clear to me, but Horn, since it was from
The investigators are considered to have acknowledged it as sufficient evidence against them.

(The twenty-ninth witness) In the eighth verse of the twenty-first chapter of the Book of Exodus in the Hebrew text, the original in the issue of the slave girl was denied, and in the footnote phrase, confirmation was found.

(The Thirteenth Witness) In the twenty-first verse of the eleventh chapter of the Book of News regarding the ruling on birds that walk on the ground, in the Hebrew text there is a negation, and in the footnote phrase there is an affirmation. �

(The Thirty-One Witness) In the thirtieth verse of the twenty-fifth chapter of the Book of News regarding the rule of the verse, in the text there is a negation and in the footnote phrase there is an affirmation.

In these three places in their biographies, the Protestant scholars chose proof, and the footnote phrase, and left the original text. For them, the original in these places is distorted, and since the distortion occurred in them, the three rulings included in them are suspected, so it is not known with certainty that the correct ruling is the ruling that is restricted by negation, or the ruling that is supported by proof, and it appears from this that what they said, that no ruling from the rulings of the heavenly books has stated that the distortion occurred in them, is incorrect.

(Witness Thirty-Two) In the twenty-eighth verse of the twentieth chapter of the Book of Acts: “Until they forsook the church of God, which He obtained with His blood.” Krebach said: “The word God is wrong, but the correct word is the word of the Lord,” so according to him, the word God is distorted.

(Witness Thirty-Three) In the sixteenth verse of the third chapter of Paul’s first letter to Timothy, “God appeared in the flesh,” Krebach said, “The word ‘God’ is incorrect, but the correct word is the third person,” meaning that it is said “he.”
(Witness Thirty-Four) In the thirteenth verse of Chapter Eight of Observations: “Then I saw a flying angel.”
Krebach and Schulz said: “The word ‘king’ is incorrect, but the correct word is ‘qaab’.”

(Thirty-fifth witness) In the twenty-first verse of the fifth chapter of Paul’s letter to the Ephesians: “And let them submit to one another in the fear of God.” Krebach and Schulz said: “The wording of God is wrong, but the correct wording is the wording of Christ,” and I will suffice with the evidence of the first purpose for fear of prolonging it.

sections.heading: The second purpose: to prove distortion by addition
content: [The second purpose: to prove the distortion by adding]

(The first witness) Know that eight books from the Old Testament were questionable and unacceptable to Christians until three hundred and twenty-four years ago, and they are these: [1] The Book of Esther. [2] The Book of Baruch. [3] The Book of Tobit. [4] The Book of Judith. [5] Book and Zam. [6] Eccles Yastics book. [7] The first book of Macabians. [8] The second book of Macabians.

In the year three hundred and twenty-five of the Christian years, a council of Christian scholars was held under the rule of Sultan Constantine in the town of Naas, to consult and investigate the matter regarding these questionable books. After consultation and investigation, they ruled that the book of Judith was obligatory to submit, and they left the rest of the books questionable as they were. This matter appears from the introduction that Jerome wrote to that book. Then after that, the Council of Ludisia was held in the year three hundred and sixty-four, and the scholars of this council accepted the ruling of the scholars of the first council in the book Judith, and they added to it from the books mentioned the Book of Esther, and confirmed their ruling with the general letter. Then after that, the Council of Carthage was held in the year three hundred and ninety-seven, and the people of that council were one hundred and twenty-seven famous scholars, including the famous and well-known eminent one, who was accepted by them, Eckstein. These scholars accepted the rulings of the first two councils, and handed over the remaining [p. 237] books, but they made the Book of Baruch the status of a part.

From the Book of Jeremiah, because Baruch, peace be upon him, was in the position of a representative of Jeremiah, peace be upon him. Therefore, they did not write the name of the Book of Baruch separately in the names of the books. Then three other councils were held after that, meaning the Council of Trullo, the Council of Florence, and the Council of Trent. The scholars of these three councils handed over the rulings of the three previous councils. After the convening of these councils, the aforementioned books became Muslim among the majority of Christians, and remained for a period of one thousand and two hundred years, and then the Protestant sect appeared, and they rejected the ruling of their predecessors. In the Book of Baruch, the Book of Tobit, the Book of Judith, the Book of Zoddam, the Book of Ecclesiastes, and the two Books of the Macabites, they said: These books are not an inspired revelation, but rather must be rejected. They returned their ruling in part of the Book of Esther and accepted in a part.
Because this book had sixteen chapters, they left the first nine chapters, three verses from the tenth chapter, and rejected ten verses from

This chapter, and six remaining chapters, and they cling to aspects of it: that the historian Yossi Bes stated in the twenty-second chapter of the fourth book that these books distorted, especially the second book of the Macabians, and among them is that the Jews do not say that they are inspired.

The Roman Church, which is followed to this day by more than the Protestant sect, has received these books to this day, and they believe that they are inspirational and must be delivered, and they are included in their Latin translation, which is Muslim and highly regarded by them, and the foundation of their religion and religions. If you know this, then I say: What distortion with addition can be more than this? According to the Protestants and Jews, the books that were unacceptable until three hundred and twenty-four years ago and were distorted and uninspired were made by the Christian ancestors in the various councils obligatory, and they included them in the inspired books, and thousands of their scholars unanimously agreed on their truth and inspiration, and the Roman Church until [p. 238] this time insists on them being inspired, so it appears from this that there is no consideration for the consensus of their predecessors, and this consensus is not weak evidence of the dissent, let alone being strong. Just as they agreed upon these distorted, uninspired books, it is possible for their consensus to be on these promoted Gospels even though they were distorted, uninspired. Don’t you see that these predecessors were unanimous in the authenticity of the Greek version, and they believed that the Hebrew version was distorted, and they used to say that the Jews distorted it in the year one hundred and thirty of the Christian years, as you know in the second witness of the first purpose.

The Greek Church, as well as the Eastern churches to this day, are also unanimous in its validity and belief, like the belief of the ancestors. The majority of Protestant scholars have proven that the consensus of the ancestors, as well as the disagreement of those who follow them, is wrong. They reversed the matter and believed and said about Hebrew what their predecessors said about it.

The Greek Church, as well as the Roman Church, unanimously agreed on the validity of the Latin translation, and Protestant scholars proved that it was distorted, and indeed no translation like it was distorted. Horne said in the fourth volume of his interpretation of the 1822 edition, page 463: “Many distortions and additions occurred in this translation from the fifth century to the fifteenth century,” and then he said on page 467: “You must have this in mind that no translation of the biographies has been distorted like the Latin one.

The transmitters of it, indifferently, inserted passages from some books of the New Testament into another book, and also inserted phrases of footnotes into the text, and if what they did in relation to their accepted and circulated translation was the goal of circulation, how can they be expected to have not distorted the original text, which was certainly not circulated among them? Rather, what is more apparent is that whoever among them initiated to distort the translation hastened to distort the original, so that his action would be covered by his people. What is surprising about the Protestant sect is that they did not deny these books when they denied them. Why did they keep part of the Book of Esther, and why did they not deny it completely?? Because this book does not contain [p. 239] from beginning to end any of the names of God, let alone an explanation of His attributes or one of His rulings, and the condition of its author is not known, and the commentators of the Old Testament do not attribute it to one person as a matter of certainty based on evidence, but rather by conjecture and conjecture, based on the unseen. Some of them attributed it to the scholars of the temple who were from the time of Ezra, peace be upon him, to the time of Simon, and Philo the Jew was attributed to Jehochin.

“Who is the son of Jesus who came from Babylon after the release of the Isra’, and attributed Ishtian to Ezra, peace be upon him, and some attributed it to Mard Ki, and some to him and to Esther.” And on page 347 of the second volume of the Catalc Hurald: “The Honorable Melitoma wrote the name of this book at the end of the names of the Muslim books, as Yossi Bess stated in the History of Clisia in the twenty-sixth chapter of the fourth book, and Kiri Nazin Zen in the poems recorded the names of the correct books, and the name of the books was not written.” This book is in it, and Im in Lukis showed his suspicion of this book in the poems he wrote to Seleucus and insulted Sich in his thirty-ninth letter, “Replying this book and its ugliness.”

(Second Witness) The thirty-first verse of the thirty-sixth chapter of the Book of Creation is thus: “And these are the kings who reigned in the land of Edom before the children of Israel reigned.” This verse cannot be from the words of Moses, peace be upon him, because it indicates that it was spoken after a time in which the sultanate of the children of Israel was established, and their first king was Saul, and he was three hundred and fifty-six years after Moses, peace be upon him.

Adam Clarke said in the first volume of his interpretation at the end of this verse: “My most likely belief is that Moses, peace be upon him, did not write this verse and the verses that follow it up to the thirty-nine verse. Rather, these verses are the verses of the first chapter of the first book of the Book of Chronicles, and I have a strong suspicion close to certainty that these verses were written on the footnote of an authentic copy of the Torah, so the transmitter thought that they were part of the text and included them in it.” This commentator admitted that the nine verses were appended, and he agreed with his confession. It is necessary that their books were subject to corruption, because these nine verses, despite not being from the Torah, were included in it and were subsequently widespread in all copies.
(Third Witness) The fourteenth verse of the third chapter of the Book of Exceptions: “Fe’er

Ibn Mansaba (99) inherited all the land of Arghub up to the borders of Jasur and Macakani (100) and named Basan after him, Jaloth Jaber, which are the villages of Jaber to this day.” This verse also cannot be from the words of Moses, peace be upon him, because the speaker of it must have been much later than Jaber (101), as is evident from his saying to this day, because such pronunciation is only used in more distant time, according to what the investigators of their scholars have verified. As you will soon know, the famous eminent Horne said in explanation of these two paragraphs that I quoted in the second and third witnesses in the first volume of his interpretation: “These two paragraphs cannot be

They consist of the words of Moses, peace be upon him, because the first paragraph indicates that he wrote this book after a time when the Sultanate of the Children of Israel was established, and the second paragraph indicates that he wrote it after the time of the Jews’ residence in Palestine. However, if we impose them as two appendices, the defect in the truth of the book will not be addressed, and whoever looks carefully will know that these two paragraphs are not only useless, but they are heavy on the body of the book, especially the second paragraph because Moses or someone else who wrote it did not say a word to this day, so most likely it was in In the books, Jair the son of Mansaw inherited all the land of Arghub up to the borders of Jasur and Maakatha, and Basan named Goliath Jair by his name. Then, after centuries, this word was added in the footnote to make it known that the name by which Jair called it is its name until now. Then this phrase was transferred from the footnote to the text in the later copies. Whoever doubts this matter should look at the Greek copies and find in them that the appendages that are found in the text of some copies are found in the other copies at Footnote.

So he admitted that these two paragraphs could not have been from the words of Moses, peace be upon him, and his saying: Most likely, etc., indicates that he has no support for this matter other than his claim, and that this book, after centuries of its writing, was valid for the distortion of the distorters, because this word, according to his confession, was added after a century, and despite that it became part of the book, and was widespread in all later copies, and his saying: “If we impose them as appendices, the flaw in the authenticity of the book will not be addressed” indicates fanaticism, which is It is apparent.

The compilers said regarding Henry’s interpretation and silence at the end of the second paragraph: “The last sentence is an appendix that was added by someone after Moses, peace be upon him, and if it were left out, there would be no corruption in the content.” I say: The specification of the last sentence is redundant because the entire second paragraph cannot be from the words of Moses, as Horne admitted.

(Warning) Another thing remains in the second paragraph, which is that Jair is not the son of Mansa, but rather he is the son of Sagheb, as stated in the twenty-eighth verse of the second chapter of the first book of the Chronicles.

(Fourth Witness) The fortieth verse of the thirty-second chapter of the Book of Numbers: “As for Jair the son of Mansa, he deliberately took its settlements and called them Goliath of Jair, which are the towns of Jair.” The context of this verse is the same as the verse in the Book of Exceptions, and it was taught in the third verse and in the Book of Bible (102) which was printed in America and the territory of the English and India.

Calment began writing it, and Zabit and Taylor completed it thus: “Some of the sentences found in the books of Moses clearly indicate that they are not his words, such as verse 40 of chapter 22 of the Book of Numbers, and verse 14 of chapter 2 of the Book of Exceptions, and also some of the phrases of this book that are not in dialogue with the words of Moses, and we cannot say with certainty that anyone appended these sentences and phrases, but we say with the most likely belief that the prophet Ezra appended them as he predicts. From the ninth and tenth chapters of his book and the eighth chapter of the Book of Nehemiah. These scholars asserted that some of the sentences and phrases were not from the words of Moses, peace be upon him, but they were not able to indicate the name of the appendix by way of specification. Rather, they were attributed as a matter of suspicion to Ezra, peace be upon him. This suspicion is nothing, and it does not appear from the aforementioned chapters that Ezra added anything to the Torah because it is understood from the chapter of the Book of Ezra that he regretted the actions of the children of Israel and confessed the sins. It is understood from the chapter of the Book of Nehemiah that Ezra He read the Torah to them.
(The fifth witness) occurred in the fourteenth verse of the twenty-second chapter of

The Book of Creation: “As it is said on this day in the mountain of God, people must appear.” This mountain was not called the Mountain of God until after the construction of the temple that Solomon, peace be upon him, was built, four hundred and fifty (450) years after the death of Moses, peace be upon him. Adam Clarke ruled in the preamble to the interpretation of the Book of Ezra that this sentence was appendix, then he said: “And this mountain was not given that name unless the temple was indicated on it.”

(Sixth Witness) The twelfth verse of the second chapter of the Book of Exceptions is thus: “But before the Apostles dwelt in Seir, and the sons of Esau drove them out and destroyed them, and they settled in it as the children of Israel did with the land of their inheritance which he gave them.”

In the preamble to the interpretation of the Book of Ezra, Adam Clarke ruled that this verse is an appendix, and he made this statement, “as the children of Israel did,” etc., evidence of the appendix.

(Seventh Witness) The eleventh verse of the third chapter of the Book of Exceptions is thus: “Because only Og, king of Basan, was left of the descendants of the giants. This has a bed of iron, and it is in Rabath of the sons of Ammon. Its length is nine cubits, and its breadth is four cubits, the size of the cubit of a hand.”

Adam Clarke said in the preamble to the interpretation of the Book of Ezra: The dialogue, especially the last phrase, indicates that this verse was written long after the death of that sultan, and Moses did not write it because he died within a period of five months.

(Eighth Witness) The third verse of the twenty-first chapter of the Book of Numbers is thus: “So God heard the supplication of the family of Israel, and delivered the Canaanites into their hands. They made them and their villages deserts, and called that place a sanctuary.” Adam Clarke said in the first volume of his interpretation on page 697: “I know that this verse was added after the death of Joshua, peace be upon him, because all the Canaanites did not perish during the reign of Moses, but after his death.”

content: Chapter Three: On Proof of Copying.

Abrogation in the language is removal, and in the terminology of the people of Islam it is an explanation of the period of expiration of the practical ruling that brings together the conditions, because abrogation does not occur with us to stories, nor to definite matters of reason such as that the Maker of the world exists, nor to sensory matters such as the light of day and the darkness of night, nor to supplications, nor to rulings that are obligatory in and of themselves, such as believe and do not associate, nor to eternal rulings such as {And accept no testimony for them ever}, nor to temporary rulings before their appointed time such as {So pardon and pardon until God will bring His command.

Rather, it occurs in rulings that are a possible process of existence and non-existence, non-perpetual and non-temporary, and they are called absolute rulings, and it is stipulated that the time, the person responsible, and the aspect are not the same, but rather there must be a difference in all or some of these three. The meaning of the term abrogation does not mean that God commanded or forbade first and did not know its outcome, then an opinion appeared to him and he abrogated the first ruling to require ignorance, or he commanded or forbade and then abrogated with the union in the written matters to require heinousness with reason.

And if we say that he knew the outcome, then this abrogation is not permissible according to us, God is far above that. Rather, what it means is that God knew that this ruling would remain on those in charge until such-and-such a time and then it would be abrogated. Then when the time came, he sent another ruling from which the addition, subtraction, or removal appeared absolutely. In fact, this is a statement of the end of the first ruling, but since the time was not mentioned in the first ruling, when the second came, it is imagined, due to the shortcomings of our apparent knowledge, that it was changed, and its counterpart is Without any analogy, you can order your servant, whose condition you know, to perform one of the services, and it is your intention that he will be in this service for a year, for example, and after the year he will be in another service, but as long as you have demonstrated your intention and intention for it, then if the period of time passes and you appoint him to another service, then this is according to what appears to the servant, and likewise to others whom you did not inform of your intention to change, but in reality and to you there is no change, and there is no impossibility in this meaning, neither with regard to the essence of God nor to His attributes, as

In changing the seasons such as spring, summer, fall and winter, as well as in changing the night and day and changing people’s conditions such as poverty, wealth, health, illness and others, there is wisdom and interests for God Almighty whether they appear to us or not. Likewise, in abrogating rulings there is wisdom and interests for Him in view of the condition of those in charge, the time and the place. Do you not see that the wise doctor changes medicines and foods by observing the patient’s conditions and others according to the interest that he sees, and no one blames his action for frivolity, foolishness and ignorance, so how can a rational person think of these matters in The Absolutely Wise One who knows things through ancient, eternal, and everlasting knowledge. If I knew this, I would say that none of the stories included in the Old and New Testaments are abrogated by us.

Yes, some of them are false, such as that Lot, peace be upon him, committed adultery with his two daughters and they became pregnant through adultery through the father, as stated in the nineteenth chapter of the Book of Genesis, or that Yehud ibn Jacob, peace be upon him, committed adultery with Tamar, his son’s wife, and she became pregnant through adultery with him and gave birth to twins, Perez and Zerah, as stated in the thirty-eighth chapter of the aforementioned book, and David, Solomon, and Jesus, peace be upon them, are all children of the mentioned Pharez, as stated in the first chapter of the Gospel of Matthew.

Or that David, peace be upon him, committed adultery with the wife of Uriah, and she became pregnant by adultery with him, so he destroyed her husband through deception and took her as his wife, as is stated in the eleventh chapter of the Second Book of Samuel, or that Solomon, peace be upon him, apostatized at the end of his life and worshiped idols after the apostasy and built temples to them, as is stated in the eleventh chapter of the First Book of Kings, or that Aaron, peace be upon him, built a temple for the calf and worshiped it, and commanded the children of Israel to worship it as is stated in Chapter Thirty-Two of the Book of Exodus, we say: These stories and others like them are false and void in our view, and we do not say that they are abrogated. The definite matters of reason and sense, the obligatory rulings, the eternal rulings, the temporary rulings before their appointed times, and the absolute rulings in which the time, the person responsible, and the purpose are imposed together. All of these things are not abrogated, so that the reprehensible thing is necessary. Likewise, the supplications are not abrogated, so the Psalms, which are supplications, are not abrogated in our terminological sense. We do not definitely say that they abrogated the Torah and abrogated from the Gospel, as this person fabricated. The matter is up to the people of Islam, the author of Mizan al-Haqq, and he said that this is stated in the Qur’an and the interpretations. Rather, we were prevented from using the Psalms and other books from the Old and New Testaments because they are certainly doubtful due to the lack of continuous chains of transmission and the proven occurrence of verbal distortion in them in all its parts, as I learned in the second chapter.

It is permissible to abrogate in matters other than the absolute rulings mentioned that are valid for abrogation. We acknowledge that some of the rulings of the Torah and the Gospel are of the type that are valid for abrogation, and they are abrogated in the Sharia of Muhammad. We do not say that every ruling of their rulings is abrogated. How can it be that some of the rulings of the Torah were not abrogated with certainty, such as: the prohibition of false oaths, murder, adultery, sodomy, theft, false testimony, betrayal of a neighbor’s wealth and honor, the obligation of honoring one’s parents, and the prohibition of marrying fathers and sons, mothers and daughters? And paternal uncles and aunts and uncles and aunts, and the plural of two sisters, and many other rulings, as well as some of the rulings of the Gospel were not abrogated with certainty. For example, it occurred in the twelfth chapter of the Gospel of Mark like this: 29 “Then Jesus said to him while he was conversing with him: The first of the rulings is his saying, “Listen, O Israel, for the Lord our God is one Lord.” 30 “And to love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, with all your understanding, and with all your strength. This is the first rule.” 31 “And the second is like it, which is to love your neighbor as yourself, and there is no other rule greater than these.” These two rulings remain in our law in the most certain way, and they are not abrogated, and abrogation is not specific to our law. Rather, it was found in the previous laws also in abundance, in both parts of it. I mean the abrogation that There is in the law of a later prophet a ruling that was in the law of a previous prophet, and the abrogation that is in the law of a prophet of another ruling from the law
This Prophet, and the examples of the two sections in the Old and New Testaments are not limited, but I will suffice here with some of them and say:

sections.heading: Examples of the first section
content: Examples of the first section: These (the first) brothers married sisters during the era of Adam, peace be upon him, and Sarah, the wife of Abraham, peace be upon him, was also his open sister, as can be understood from his statement regarding her right included in the twelfth verse of the twentieth chapter of the Book of Genesis, an Arabic translation in the year 1625 and 1648: “She is my sister in reality, my father’s daughter, not my mother’s daughter, and I married her.” Marriage with a sister is absolutely forbidden in Sharia law.
Al-Mawsawiyya is in person, whether the sister, openly or secretly, and is equivalent to adultery. The one who marries is cursed, and killing both spouses is obligatory.

The ninth verse of the eighteenth chapter of the Book of Chronicles is like this: “You shall not uncover the nakedness of your sister, whether of your father or of your mother who was born in the house or outside the house.” And in the interpretation of Dawali Wargardment at the end of the explanation of this verse: “Such a marriage is equivalent to adultery.” And the seventeenth verse of the twentieth chapter of the aforementioned book is like this: “Any man who marries his sister, his father’s daughter, or his sister, his mother’s daughter, and sees her nakedness and she sees his nakedness, this is a severe disgrace, and they will be killed in the presence of their people, and that Because he uncovered the nakedness of his sister, and their sin will be on their heads.” The twenty-second verse of the twenty-seventh chapter of the Book of Exceptions is thus: “Cursed shall be the one who lies with his sister, whether by his father or by his mother.” If this marriage was not permissible in the law of Adam and Abraham, peace be upon them, it would be necessary for all people to be children of fornication, and those who marry are adulterers, obligated to kill, and cursed. How can this be thought regarding the prophets, peace be upon them? It must be recognized that it was. Permissible in their law, then abrogated.

(Interest) The author of the Arabic translation printed in 1811 translated the twelfth verse of the twentieth chapter of the Book of Genesis as follows: “She is my relative by my father, not by my mother.” It appears that he intentionally distorted it so that abrogation would not be necessary with regard to Sarah’s marriage, because the father’s relative includes the daughter of a paternal uncle, aunt, and others.

(The second) God’s statement in the speech of Noah and his children in the third verse of the ninth chapter of the Book of Genesis, thus an Arabic translation in the years 1625 and 1648, “And whenever it moves on the earth while it is alive, it will be for you to eat, like green herbs.” Thus, all animals were lawful in the law of Noah, like legumes, and many animals were forbidden in the Mosaic law, including pigs as well, as stated in the eleventh chapter of the Book of News and the fourteenth chapter of the Book of Exceptions.

(Benefit) The author of the Arabic translation printed in 1811 also distorted this word and translated the third verse mentioned as follows: “Every clean, living creeping thing will be for you to eat, like the green grass.” He added the word “clean” on his part so as not to include the animals forbidden in the law of Moses, because it was said about them in the Torah that they are unclean.

(Third) Jacob brought together the two sisters Leah and Rachel, his cousins, as stated in the twenty-ninth chapter of the Book of Genesis, and this combination is forbidden in the Mosaic Law, verse eighteen of the eighteenth chapter of the Book of Chronicles, thus: And you shall not marry your wife’s sister while she is alive, lest she grieve her, nor uncover their nakedness at all, lest you grieve them. If the union between the two sisters was not permissible in the law of Jacob, it is necessary for their children to be the children of adultery, and it is forbidden. By God and most of the Israeli prophets in their children.

(Fourth) I learned in the first verse of the third purpose that Imran’s wife, Jochabeth, was his aunt. The translators of the Arabic translation printed in 1635 and 1648 intentionally distorted it to hide the defect, so Abu Musa married his aunt, and this marriage was forbidden in the Mosaic law. The twelfth verse of the eighteenth chapter of the Book of News is like this:

“You shall not uncover the private parts of your paternal aunt, for she is a relative of your father.” The same applies to the nineteenth verse of the twentieth chapter of the aforementioned book. If this marriage had not been permissible before the Law of Moses, Moses, Aaron, and their sister Miriam would have to be children of adultery, God forbid. They would not have entered the congregation of the Lord for ten years, as stated in the third verse of the twenty-third chapter of the Book of Exceptions. And if they were capable of being removed from the congregation of the Lord, who would be fit to enter it?

(Fifth) In the thirty-first chapter of the Book of Jeremiah as follows: 31 “Behold, the days are coming - says the Lord - when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and the house of Judah.” 32 “It is not like the covenant that I made with their fathers on the day that I took them by the hand to bring them out of the land of Egypt, a covenant that they broke, and I ruled over them by the word of the Lord.” What is meant by the new covenant is the new law, so it is understood that this new law is an abrogation of the Mosaic law, and he claimed. Paul sanctified them in the eighth chapter of his letter to the Hebrews that this law is the law of Jesus. According to his confession, the law of Jesus, peace be upon him, abrogates the law of Moses, peace be upon him. These five examples are binding on all Jews and Christians, and other examples are binding on Christians.

(Sixth) It is permissible in the Mosaic law for a man to divorce his wife for any reason, and for another man to marry that divorced woman after she has left the house of the first, as stated in the twenty-fourth chapter of the Book of Exceptions. Divorce is not permissible in the Jesus law except on the ground of adultery. Likewise, it is not permissible for another man to marry a divorced woman. Rather, it is tantamount to adultery, as stated in the nineteenth chapter of the Gospel of Matthew. When the Pharisees objected to Jesus, peace be upon him, in this matter, he said in their answer. Moses did not permit you to divorce your wives except because of the hardness of your hearts, but as for before, he did not

It will not be so, and I say to you that whoever divorces his wife for other than the reason of adultery and marries another has committed adultery, and whoever marries that divorced woman commits adultery.” He learned from his answer that abrogation of this ruling was proven twice, once in the Mosaic law and once in His law, and that the ruling may be sent down sometimes in accordance with the condition of those charged, even if it is not good in the same matter.

(Seventh) Many animals were forbidden in the Mosaic law, and their prohibition was abrogated in the Jesus law, and the general permissibility was confirmed by Paul’s fatwa. The fourteenth verse of the fourteenth chapter of Paul’s letter to the Romans is thus: “For I know and believe in the Lord Jesus that nothing is unclean to the eye. Rather, everything is unclean to him who considers it unclean.” And the fifteenth verse of the first chapter of his letter to Titus is thus: “For all things are pure.” For the pure, and nothing is pure for the impure and the hypocrites, because they are all impure, even their mind and conscience.”

These two universals: Everything is impure to those who consider it impure, and all things are pure to those who are pure. They are apparently strange. Perhaps the children of Israel were not pure and this general permissibility did not occur to them. And since the Christians were pure, general permissibility occurred to them and everything became pure for them. Their sanctuary was striving to spread the rule of general permissibility. Therefore, he wrote to Timothy in the fourth chapter of his first letter [4] “For everything that God created is good and it is not permissible to reject it.” Something that if we eat it we are thankful [5] because it is sanctified by the word of God and by supplication [6]. If you remind the brothers of this, then you have become a good servant of Christ, educated in the words of faith and the correct teaching, whose footsteps you have followed.”

(Eighth) The rulings on holidays that were detailed in the twenty-third chapter of the Book of News were obligatory and eternal in the Mosaic law, and in verse 14, 21, 31, and 41 of the aforementioned chapter, words were applied to them indicating their being eternal.
(Ninth) The glorification of the Sabbath was an eternal rule in the Mosaic law.

No one was allowed to do the slightest work in it, and whoever did anything in it and whoever did not maintain it was obligated to kill, and this ruling and emphasis was repeatedly stated in the books of the Old Testament in many places, for example in the third verse of the second chapter of the Book of Genesis, and in the twentieth chapter of the Book of Exodus from the eighth to the eleventh verse, and in the twelfth verse of the twenty-third chapter of the Book of Exodus, and in the twenty-first verse of the thirty-fourth chapter of the Book of Exodus, and in the third verse of the nineteenth chapter, as well as in the twenty-third chapter of the Book of News, and in the fifth chapter. From the Book of Exceptions from verses twelve to fifteen, and in the seventeenth chapter of the Book of Jeremiah, and in the fifty-sixth and fifty-eighth chapters of the Book of Isaiah, and in the ninth chapter of the Book of Nehemiah, and in the twentieth chapter of the Book of Ezekiel, and it occurred in the thirty-first chapter of the Book of Exodus as follows: [13] “Speak to the children of Israel and tell them to keep my day the Sabbath, because it is a sign between me and you throughout your generations, so that you may know that I am the Lord who purifies you. [14] So keep my day, the Sabbath, for it has been purified for you, and whoever does not keep it must surely be put to death. Whoever does it, that person will be destroyed.”

The soul is from its people (15) Do your work for six days, and the seventh day is a sabbath day of rest, purified to the Lord. And whoever does any work on this day let him be put to death. [16] And let the children of Israel keep the Sabbath and make it a festival throughout their generations for a covenant forever. [17] Between me and the children of Israel is a sign forever. For the Lord created heaven and earth in six days, and on the seventh day he rested from his work. It will be a holy sabbath and rest for you from the Lord whoever works in it

Let him be put to death [3] Do not set fire to all your dwellings on the Sabbath.” And it occurred in the fifteenth chapter of the Book of Numbers thus: [32] “And when the children of Israel were in the wilderness, they found a man gathering wood on the Sabbath [33] and they brought him to Moses and Aaron and all the company [34] and they threw him into prison, because they did not know what to do with him. [35] Then the Lord said to Moses, “Let this man be killed, and let all the people stone him with stones outside the camp.” [36] So they took him out and stoned him, and he died as the Lord had commanded. The Jews who were contemporary with Christ, peace be upon him, were harming him and wanted to kill him for not honoring the Sabbath, and this was also evidence of their denial.” Verse sixteen of the fifth chapter of the Gospel of John is like this: “And for that reason the Jews expelled Jesus and sought to kill him because he had done those things on the Sabbath.” Verse sixteen of the ninth chapter of the Gospel of John is like this: “Then some of the Pharisees said that this man is not from God because he does not keep the Sabbath,” etc.

And if I know this, I say: Their saint, Paul, abrogated these rulings that were mentioned in the seventh, eighth, and ninth example, and made clear that all of these things were misleading, in the eighth chapter of his letter to the people of Cola Sais 16: “So let no one condemn you by food or drink or by looking at the feasts or the new moon or the Sabbaths. 17 For these things are shadows of the things planned for the coming, but the body is Christ’s.” In the interpretation of Dawali and Rajrad Mint, the tail of the explanation of the sixteenth verse is like this: He said: Berkat and Daktrot, “The Jewish feasts were divided into three parts: in each year, a year, in each month, a month, and in each week, a week. So all of these were abrogated, and even the Sabbath as well, and the Christian Sabbath was established in its place.” Bashar Harsley said at the end of the explanation of the aforementioned verse: “The Sabbath of the Jewish Church disappeared, and the Christians did not follow the childish patterns of the Pharisees in keeping their Sabbath.”

In Henry Waskat’s interpretation: “If Jesus abrogated the law of drawings, no one has the right to oblige foreign sayings because of their lack of observance. Yasuper and Leah said: For if observing the Sabbath had been obligatory for all people, and for all the peoples of the world, it would never have been possible to abrogate it, as it has now been abrogated in reality, and it would have been necessary for Christians to observe it layer by layer, as they did in the beginning, for the sake of honoring and pleasing the Jews.” What their sanctifier Paul claimed about the aforementioned things being a delusion does not fit the statement of the Torah, because God He explained the reason for the prohibition of animals because they are “unclean, so you must be holy, for I am holy” as stated in the eleventh chapter of the Book of Chronicles, and he explained the reason for the Feast of Unleavened Bread “that I will bring your armies out of the land of Egypt, so observe this day for your generations as a law forever” as stated in the twelfth chapter of the Book of Exodus, and he explained the reason for the Feast of Tabernacles thus: “So that your generations may know that I seated the children of Israel in tents when I brought them out of the land of Egypt,” as stated in

Chapter twenty-three of the Book of News, and he explained in several places the reason for glorifying the Sabbath: “That the Lord created the heaven and the earth in six days and rested from His work on the seventh day.”

(Tenth) The ruling on circumcision was eternal in the law of Abraham, peace be upon him, as stated in the seventeenth chapter of the Book of Genesis, and therefore this ruling remained in the children of Ishmael and Isaac, peace be upon them, and it remained in the law of Moses, peace be upon them as well. The third verse of the twelfth chapter of the Book of News is like this: “And on the eighth day the boy shall be circumcised.” And Jesus, peace be upon him, was also circumcised, as stated in the twenty-first verse of the second chapter of the Gospel of Luke, and Christians up to this time have a specific prayer that they perform. On the day of the circumcision of Jesus, peace be upon him, as a reminder of this day, and this ruling remained until the ascension of Jesus, peace be upon him, and it was not abrogated, but rather abrogated by the Apostles during their time, as explained in the fifteenth chapter of the works of the Apostles, and you will know in the thirteenth example as well, and their saint, Paul, gives great emphasis in abrogating this ruling in the fifth chapter of his letter to the Galatians, thus: “And here I, Paul, say to you that if you are circumcised, Christ will be of no benefit to you. 3 For I bear witness that every circumcised person is obligated to perform all the works of the law. 4 If you are purified by the law, you have no benefit from Christ and have fallen short of receiving grace. 6 For circumcision has no benefit in Christ or for the foreskin, but

Faith that works through love” and the fifteenth verse of the sixth chapter of the aforementioned message is thus: “There is no benefit to circumcision in Jesus Christ, nor to the foreskin, but to the new creation.”
(Eleventh) The provisions for sacrifices were many and eternal in the Law of Moses, and they were all abrogated in the Isawi Law.
(Twelfth) The many rulings pertaining to the family of Aaron, such as priesthood, dress at the time of attending service, and others, were eternal and were all abrogated in the Isawiya law.

(Thirteenth) The disciples, after full consultation, abrogated all the practical rulings of the Torah except four: idol sacrifice, blood, strangled meat, and adultery. They kept them forbidden and sent a letter to the churches. It is quoted in the fifteenth chapter of the works of the disciples, and some of its verses are like this: 24 “Then we have heard that some of those who have gone out from us are disturbing you with their words and disturbing your souls, and saying that you must be circumcised. And keep the law, and we did not command them to do that, 28 because it seemed good to the Holy Spirit and to us not to burden you with anything other than these necessary things, 29 which are that you abstain from idol offerings, blood, things strangled, and fornication, which if you abstain from them, you will

“Well done and peace.” Rather, they preserved the sanctity of these four so that the Jews who had soon entered the Christian religion would not become alienated, and they loved the provisions of the Torah and its decrees with complete aversion. Then, when their saint, Paul, saw after this time that this care was not necessary, they abrogated the sanctity of the first three with a fatwa of general permissibility that was quoted in the seventh example, and upon this the majority of Protestants agreed, for what remained of the practical provisions of the Torah was adultery, and since there was no limit to it in the Isawi law, it was abrogated from In this respect also, the void in this law has been achieved by abrogating all the practical rulings that were in the Mosaic law, whether eternal or non-eternal.

(XIV) In the second chapter of Paul’s letter to the Galatians 30 “And I was crucified with Christ and now I live, but I am not alive, but Christ is the one who lives in me, and what I have now received of physical life is related to faith in the Son of God who loved me and made himself a ransom for me.” 21 “And I do not nullify the grace of God, for if justice is by the law, then Christ died in vain.” Doctor Hammand said at the end of the explanation of verse 20: “He saved me by giving his Spirit for me in exchange for the law.” Moses,” and he said in the explanation of verse twenty-one: “He used this emancipation for that purpose. I do not depend for salvation on the law of Moses, nor do I understand that the provisions of Moses are necessary because it makes the Gospel of Christ seem useless.”

Doctor WP said at the end of the explanation of verse twenty-one: “And if such and such had been, and he had purchased salvation through his death, it would not have been necessary, and there would have been no meaning in his death.” And Yael said, “If the law of the Jews had protected us and saved us, what necessity would there have been for the death of Christ, and if the law had been a part of our salvation, then the death of Christ would not have been sufficient for it.” All of these statements speak of the occurrence of emptiness of the law of Moses and its abrogation.

(Fifteenth) In the third chapter of the aforementioned letter, this is how: “All those who do the works of the law are cursed. No one is approved of people by God, for the law is not related to faith, and Christ has redeemed us from the curse of the law when it became a curse for us.” Ending with a summary, Lard said on page 478 of the ninth volume of his interpretation after quoting these verses: “It is suspected that what the disciple means here is the meaning that many know, meaning that the law was abrogated or became useless. By the death and crucifixion of Christ.” Then he said on page 487 of the aforementioned volume: “Al-Hawari clearly stated in these places that the abrogation of the formal provisions of Sharia law was a result of the death of Jesus.”

(Sixteenth) In the third chapter mentioned thus: 23: “We were confined before the coming of faith by the law and restricted in waiting for the faith that was about to appear.” 24 “So the law was our instructor who guides us to Christ so that we may be purified by faith.” 25 “And when faith came, no

Nabaq under the discipline.” Their sanctity declared, “There is no obedience to the provisions of the Torah after believing in Jesus, peace be upon him.” In the interpretation of Dawali and Rijrd Mint, the religion of Istan Hope says thus: “The drawings of the Sharia were abrogated with the death of Jesus and the spread of his Gospel.”
(Seventeenth) In the fifteenth verse of the second chapter of Paul’s letter to the Ephesians, this is how: “And he abolished in his flesh the enmity, that is, the law of the statutes.”

(Eighteen) The twelfth verse of the seventh chapter of the Hebrew Epistle is thus: “For the soothsaying did not necessarily replace the law as well.” In this verse, there is proof of the connection between the change of the imamate and the change of the law. If the Muslims also say, in view of this connection, that the Jesus law was abrogated, then they are correct in saying that they are not wrong. In the interpretation of Dawali and Rijrd Mint, following the explanation of this verse, Dr. Sikanait said thus: “The law was definitely changed with regard to the rulings.” “Sacrifices, purity, etc.” means raised.
(Nineteen) The eighteenth verse of the aforementioned seventh chapter is thus: “Because the previous versions of the ruling have been presented due to their weakness and uselessness.”

In this verse, there is a statement that abrogating the provisions of the Torah because they were weak was useless in Henry Waskat’s interpretation: “The law and soothsaying, from which no completion is possible, were removed, and a new priest and pardon arose from which the true believers were perfected.”

(Twenty) in the eighth chapter of the Hebrews: “If the first covenant had not been objected to, there would have been no place for the second. 13 So by saying a new covenant, the first is made obsolete, and the old and obsolete thing is close to annihilation.” In this statement is a statement that the provisions of the Torah were flawed and capable of being abrogated because they were obsolete and obsolete. In the Tafsir Dawali and Rijrd Mint at the end of the explanation of the thirteenth verse, Yael said thus: “This is very clear that God Almighty wants to abrogate the ancient ones. The new, beautiful message is diminished, and therefore the Jewish graphic doctrine is removed and the Christian doctrine takes its place.”

(Twenty-one) In the ninth verse of the tenth chapter of the Hebrews, “So he abolishes the first with a right that confirms the second.” In the interpretation of Dawali and Rijrd Mint in the explanation of the eighth and ninth verses, Yael’s statement is thus: “The disciple inferred in these two verses, which contain notice, that the sacrifices of the Jews were insufficient, and therefore Christ bore death upon himself to make up for their deficiency, and by the action of one of them abrogated the use of the other.”

From the examples mentioned, things became clear to the discerning person: (the first) that the abrogation of some rulings in the later Sharia is not specific to our Sharia, but rather it was found in the previous Sharia as well (and the second) that all the practical rulings of the Torah, whether eternal or non-eternal, were abrogated in the Isawi Sharia (and the third) that the word abrogation is also present in the words of their sanctifier regarding the Torah and its rulings (and the fourth) that their sanctifier proved the connection between the change of the Imamate and the change of the Sharia (and the fifth) that their sanctifier claims that the thing The ancient and obsolete is close to extinction, so I say that since the Isawiya law was ancient in relation to the Muhammadan law, there is no exclusion in abrogating it, but rather it is necessary in accordance with the fourth command, and I learned in the eighteenth and sixth example that their sanctifiers and interpreters used inappropriate words in relation to the Torah and its rulings, even though they acknowledge that it is the word of God (the seventh), that there is no problem in abrogating the rulings of the Torah in our terminological sense except in the rulings in which it was declared that they are eternal or that they must always be observed, layer after layer, but this is The problem does not answer us because we do not accept, firstly, that this Torah is the revealed Torah or the classification of Moses, as taught in the first chapter, and we do not accept, secondly, that it is not protected from distortion, as it was known and proven in the second chapter.

And thirdly, we say obligatory that God may appear to him with a beginning and remorse for what he commanded or did, so he will retract it, and likewise he makes a permanent promise and then breaks his promise, and this third matter I say obligatory only because it is understood from the books of the Old Testament in this way from places as you will soon know, and I and all Sunni scholars are innocent and disavow this corrupt doctrine. Yes, this problem arises from the Christians who acknowledge that this Torah is the word of God and was written by Moses and was not distorted, and remorse and initiation. Far from fair and very weak with these words in everything, it is in the meaning that suits it. And if a great people is said to remain until the end of the world, even if his personalities change in each layer after layer, that they must always do such and such, layer after layer, or forever, or until the end of time, then it means permanence until the end of the world. There is no doubt, and comparing one to the other is very unlikely, and therefore Jewish scholars rule out their interpretation of the predecessor and successor and attribute tampering and temptation to them.
