content: Examples of the second section) are:

(The first) that God commanded Abraham, peace be upon him, to slaughter Isaac, peace be upon him, and then abrogated this ruling before acting, as stated in the twenty-second chapter of the Book of Genesis.

(The second) is that he quoted the words of one of the prophets regarding Eli the priest in the second chapter of the first book of Samuel as follows: 30 “For God, the God of Israel, says: ‘I said, ‘Your house and your father’s house will always serve before me.’ But God says now, ‘Far be it from me. It will not be so. Rather, I will honor him who honors me, and he who despises me will be humiliated. 34 And I will appoint for myself a devout priest, etc.’” So God’s promise was that the position of priesthood would remain in the house of Eli the priest and the house of Eli. His son, then he broke his promise and abrogated it and appointed another priest. In the interpretation of Dawali and Regardment, the virtuous Patrik said thus: “God here abrogates the decree which He promised and confirmed by it, that the High Priest will be among you forever. He gave

This position belonged to Lazarus, the eldest son of Aaron. Then he gave Tamar, the younger son to Aaron, and now, because of the sin of the children of Eli the priest, it passed to the children of Eleazar. So the successor occurred in God’s promise twice until the time of the continuation of the Mosaic Law. As for the succession that occurred in this section when the Isawi Law appeared a third time, there was no trace of this position left, neither in the children of Eleazar, nor in the children of Tamara. The promise that Lazarus had was stated in the twenty-fifth chapter of the Book of Numbers thus: “Indeed, I have given him my covenant of peace, so he will have the covenant of the Haburah and the caliphate after him for all eternity.” And the observer should not be puzzled about the successor to God’s promise according to the taste of the People of the Book, because the books of the Old Testament speak of it, and that God does something and then regrets it. In the thirty-ninth verse of the eighty-eighth Psalms, or the eighty-ninth, depending on the different translations, David, peace be upon him, said in the speech of God Almighty like this: “You have broken the covenant of your servant.”

And you have despised His sanctuary in the land.” David, peace be upon him, says, “You have broken the covenant with your servant.” And in the sixth chapter of the Book of Genesis it is as follows: 6 “And he regretted that he had made man on the earth, and he was deeply sorry in his heart. 7 And he said, ‘Erase the human beings that I have created from the face of the earth, from human beings to the beasts, from creeping things to the birds of the sky, for I regret that I have made them.’” The entire sixth verse, and this saying - “Because I regret that I made them” - indicate that God regretted and was sorry for creating man, and in the fifth Psalm after The hundred are like this: 44 “Then the Lord looked upon their sorrows, when He heard the voice of their supplications, 45 and remembered their covenant, and regretted His great mercy.” In the eleventh verse of the fifteenth chapter of the first book of Samuel, God says thus: “I repented that I had made Saul king, because he had returned from following me and had not done what I commanded,” and then in the thirty-fifth verse of the aforementioned chapter thus: “Samuel grieved for Saul because the Lord regretted that he had made Saul king over me.” "Israel."

Here is a scratch that we may only mention obligatorily. It is that, since remorse was proven against God and it was proven that he regretted creating man and making Saul king, it is possible that he regretted sending Christ, peace be upon him, after he demonstrated the claim of divinity, as is claimed by the Trinitarians, because this claim from mankind that occurred is a greater crime than Saul’s disobedience to the Lord’s command, and just as God was not standing on the fact that Saul disobeyed His command, so it is possible that he was standing on the fact that Christ, peace be upon him, claimed divinity. I only said this obligatory because we do not believe it. By the grace of God, there is no repentance from God, nor does Christ, peace be upon him, claim divinity. Rather, we have the arena of divinity, as well as the arena of prophecy of Christ, peace be upon him, clear of the rubbish of these depravities and abominations.

(Third) In the fourth chapter of the Book of Ezekiel, this is an Arabic translation in the year 1844 [verse] 10: “And the food that you shall eat shall be by weight twenty shekels. Every day you shall eat from time to time. 12 And you shall eat like bread of barley and smear it with dung that comes out of men in their eyes. 14 Then I said, Ah, ah, ah, O Lord God, behold, my soul has not been defiled, and the dead and the prey of the seven I have not eaten of since my youth until now, and I have not eaten of it since my youth until now. Every unclean meat shall enter my mouth. 15 And he said to me, “Behold, I will give you cow dung instead of people’s dung, and you shall make your bread with it.” God first commanded that “you smear it with dung that comes out of man.” Then, when Ezekiel, peace be upon him, asked for help, he copied this ruling before acting and said: “I will give you cow’s dung instead of people’s dung.”

(Fourth) In the seventeenth chapter of the Book of Chronicles this is how: 3 “If any man of the children of Israel slaughters an ox or a sheep or a goat in the camp or outside the camp, 4 and does not bring his offering to the door of the Dome of Time to offer it as an offering to the Lord, then let it be counted against that man for shedding of blood because he has shed blood, and that man shall be destroyed from among his people” and in the twelfth chapter of the Book of Exceptions thus: 15 “But if you are willing to eat and enjoy eating Kill the meat and eat with the blessing that the Lord your God has given you in your villages, etc. 20 And if the Lord your God enlarges your borders according to what he said to you, and you want to eat meat whatever your soul desires, 21 and the place that the Lord your God has chosen to be named there is far away, then slaughter of the herds and sheep that are yours, as I have commanded you, and eat in your villages as you wish. 22 As the gazelles and camels are eaten, so shall you eat of them all, whether clean or unclean.” So the ruling of the Book of Chronicles was abrogated by the ruling of the Book of Deuteronomy.

Horne said on page 619 of the first volume of his interpretation after quoting these verses like this: “In these two places there is an apparent contradiction, but if it is noted that the Mosaic law was increased and decreased according to the condition of the children of Israel and was not such that it could not be changed, then the guidance is very easy.” Then he said: “Moses in the fortieth year of their migration before entering Palestine abrogated that ruling” i.e. the ruling of the Book of News “by explicitly abrogating the rule of the Book of Exceptions, and he commanded that it was permissible for them after entering Palestine to They slaughter cows and sheep in any place they wish and eat.” He concluded with a summary, so he admitted that the aforementioned ruling was abrogated and that the Mosaic law was increased and decreased according to the condition of the Children of Israel. What is surprising about the People of the Book is that they object to such an increase and decrease in another law and say that it entails ignorance of God.

(Fifth) In verse 3, 23, 30, 35, 39, 43, and 46 of the fourth chapter of the Book of Numbers, the servants of the Dome of the Covenant must not be less than thirty and more than fifty, and in verse 24 and 25 of the eighth chapter of the aforementioned book, they must not be less than thirty.
From twenty-five to more than fifty.

(Sixth) In the fourth chapter of the Book of News, the redemption for the group’s mistake is one bull, and in the fifteenth chapter of the Book of Numbers, it says that it must be a bull with its accessories and a kid, so the first was abrogated.

(Seventh) God’s command is known from the sixth chapter of the Book of Genesis to enter the ark, two by two of every kind of animal, whether bird or animal, with Noah, peace be upon him, and it is known from the seventh chapter of the aforementioned book to enter seven males and two females of pure animals, and of birds in general, and of unclean animals two by two. Then it is known from the aforementioned chapter that two by two of each kind entered, so this ruling was abrogated twice.

(Eighth) In the twentieth chapter of the Book of Kings, it is as follows: “And in those days Hezekiah fell sick and was about to die, and the prophet Isaiah the son of Amos came to him and said to him, ‘Thus says the Lord God, ‘Take charge of your house, for you are dead and not living.’ 2 Then Hezekiah turned with his face to the wall and prayed before the Lord and said, 3 ‘O Lord, remember that I have walked before you in justice and in a sound heart and have done good deeds before you.’ And Hezekiah wept bitterly. 4 “And when Isaiah came out, the Lord inspired him. Before he reached the center of the court, he said, 5 Return to Hezekiah, the ruler of my people, and say to him, Thus says the Lord, the God of your father David: I have heard your prayer and seen your tears, and, behold, I will heal you quickly, so that on the third day you may go up to the house of the Lord, 6 and I will add to your age fifteen years. Ten years.

(Ninth) In the tenth chapter of the Gospel of Matthew, this is how: “These twelve Jesus sent and commanded them, saying, ‘Do not go into the way of the Gentiles, and do not enter into a city of the Samaritans, 6 but go especially to the sheep of the children of Israel that perished.’” And in the fifteenth chapter of the Gospel of Matthew, Christ, peace be upon him, said regarding him thus: “I was not sent except to the lost sheep of the house of Israel.”

According to these verses, Jesus, peace be upon him, was devoting his message to the children of Israel, and his saying was quoted in the fifteenth verse of the sixteenth chapter of the Gospel of Mark as follows: “Go into the whole world and preach the Gospel to the whole creation,” so the first ruling has been abrogated.

(The tenth) in the twenty-third chapter of the Gospel of Matthew as follows: 1 “Then Jesus addressed the crowds and his disciples, 2 saying, “The scribes and Pharisees sat on the seat of Moses. 3 So whatever they told you to observe, observe and do.” So he ruled that everything they said to you, do, and there is no doubt that they are saying to preserve all the practical provisions of the Torah, especially the eternal one, according to their claim, and all of them are abrogated in the Jesus law, as I taught in detail in the examples of the first section, so this ruling is completely abrogated, and it is amazing. Among the Protestant scholars, they mention these verses in their letters to mislead the common people of Islam, using them as evidence for the invalidity of the abrogation in the Torah, so they must be obligated to kill because they do not venerate the Sabbath, and its glorification contradicts the ruling of the Torah and the obligation to kill, as I learned in the ninth example of the examples of the first section.

(Eleventh) You learned in the thirteenth example that the disciples, after consultation, abrogated all the practical provisions of the Torah other than the four, and then Paul abrogated the prohibition of three of them.

(Twelfth) In the fifty-sixth verse of the ninth chapter of the Gospel of Luke, Christ, peace be upon him, said thus: “The Son of Man did not come to destroy the lives of men, but to save them.” And the same is true in the Gospel of John, in the seventeenth verse of the third chapter, and in the forty-seventh verse of the twelfth chapter, and it occurred in the eighth verse of the second chapter of the second letter to the Thessalonians. We remain like this: “And then the wicked one will be revealed, whom the Lord will destroy with the breath of his mouth and will abolish him with his appearing.” The second saying abrogates the first, and it is known from these last four examples, I mean from the ninth to the twelve, that abrogating the rulings of the Gospel is an actual reality as well as a possibility, as Jesus, peace be upon him, abrogated some of its rulings with another ruling, and the disciples abrogated some of its rulings with their rulings, and Paul abrogated some of the rulings of the disciples, and even some of the sayings of Jesus, peace be upon him, with his rulings and words, and it appears to you that what was quoted from Christ, peace be upon him, In the thirty-fifth verse of the twenty-fourth chapter of the Gospel of Matthew, and the thirty-third verse of the twenty-first chapter of the Gospel of Luke, what is meant is not one of my sayings or a ruling.

Of my rulings, it is not to be abrogated, nor is it necessary to deny their Gospel. Rather, what is meant by his saying “my words” is the usual words that he told about the events that occur after him, and they are mentioned before this statement in the two Gospels. The addition in his saying is my words for the covenant, not for generalization. Their commentators also interpreted this saying on what I said in the interpretation of Dawali and Jared Mint at the end of the explanation of the phrase of the Gospel of Matthew, like this: “The priest Pyrrhus said: What he means is that the things that I was told will happen with certainty,” Dean Estyn. Hope: Although the heavens and the earth are not interchangeable with respect to other things, they are not as decisive as the rulings of my informing of the things that I was informed of, for all of these will pass away, and my informing of the things that I was informed of will not disappear. Rather, the saying

“What I have said now, none of it exceeds his requirement.” The inference for this saying is very weak, and the aforementioned saying is like this: “The heavens and the earth will pass away, but my words will not pass away.”

If you know the examples of the two sections, you will have no doubt about the occurrence of abrogation of both parts in the Mosaic and Isawi law, and it appears that what the People of the Book claim regarding the abstention from abrogation is unquestionably false. How can it not be, since interests may differ depending on time and place?

And those who are charged, some rulings are possible for those who are charged at some times and are not at other times, and some are appropriate for some of those who are charged but not for others. Do you not see that Christ, peace be upon him, said, addressing the disciples: “I have many things to say to you that you cannot bear now, but when He, the Spirit of truth, comes, he will guide you into all the truth,” as stated in the sixteenth chapter of the Gospel of John, and he said to the leper whom he healed: Do not tell about this situation to anyone, just as It is stated in the eighth chapter of the Gospel of Matthew, and he said to the blind men whose eyes he opened: Do not tell anyone about this situation, as stated in the ninth chapter of the Gospel of Matthew, and he said to the parents of the girl whom he revived, “Do not tell anyone about what happened, as is stated in the eighth chapter of the Gospel of Luke.” He commanded the one who cast out the demons from it to “return to your house and tell what God has done to you,” as stated in the aforementioned chapter. You learned in the sixth and thirteenth example of the examples of the first section, and in the fourth example of the examples of the second section, what is appropriate for this situation, and also what he commanded the children of Israel to wage jihad against the infidels. As long as they were in Egypt and ordered after they left.

content: The introduction contains a statement of twelve matters that provide insight into the chapters.

(The first matter) is that the books of the Old Testament speak that God is one, eternal, eternal, undying, able to do whatever He wills, and there is nothing like Him, neither in essence nor in attributes, free of body and form, and this matter, due to its fame and abundance in those books, does not need to transmit evidence.

(The second matter) is that worshiping other than God is forbidden, and its prohibition is stated in various places in the Torah, such as chapters twentieth and thirty-four of the Book of Exodus, and it was stated in chapter thirteen of the Book of Exceptions that if a prophet or someone who claims inspiration calls in a dream to worship other than God, this caller will be killed, even if he performs great miracles. Likewise, if he tempts one of his relatives or friends to it, this tempter will be stoned and not stoned, and in the seventeenth chapter of the written book. If anyone is proven to worship other than God, he or she will be stoned.

(The third matter) In the many verses that are not limited to the Old Testament, there is a notification of the physicality, form, and organs of God Almighty, for example in verse 26 and 27 of the first chapter of the Book of Genesis and verse 6 of the ninth chapter of the aforementioned book, proving the form and form of God.

And in verse 17 of the fifty-ninth chapter of the Book of Isaiah, the head is confirmed, and in verse 9 of the seventh chapter of the Book of Daniel, the head and hair are confirmed, and in verse 3 of the forty-third Psalms, the face, hand, and upper arm are confirmed, and in verse 22 and 23 of the thirty-third chapter of the Book of Exodus, the face and neck are confirmed, and in verse 15 of the thirty-third chapter of the eye and ear, and similarly in verse 18 of the ninth chapter of the Book of Daniel, there is evidence of the eye and ear, and in verse 29 and 52 from chapter eight of the first book of Kings, and in verse 17 of chapter sixteen, and verse 19 of chapter thirty-two of the book of Jeremiah, and verse 21 of chapter thirty-four of the book of Job, and verse 21

In Chapter Five and Verse 3 of Chapter Fifteen of the Book of Proverbs, there is evidence of the eye. In Verse 4 of the Tenth Psalm, there is evidence of the eye and eyelids. In Verse 6, 8, 9, and 15 of the Seventeenth Psalm, there is evidence of the ear, foot, nose, soul, and mouth. In Verse 27 of Chapter Thirty of the Book of Isaiah, there is evidence of the lip and tongue. In Chapter Thirty-Three of the Book of Exceptions, there is evidence of the hand and foot. And in Verse 18 of Chapter Thirty-One of the Book of Exodus, evidence of the fingers. And in verse 7 of the Second Psalms there is proof of the private parts, and in verse 28 of the twentieth chapter of the works of the disciples there is proof of blood, and for purification in the Torah there are two verses:

The twelfth verse and the fifteenth verse of the fourth chapter of the Book of Exceptions are as follows: 12 “So the Lord spoke to you from the belly of the fire, and you heard the voice of His words, but you did not see the resemblance at all.” 15 “So guard yourselves carefully, for you have never seen anything similar to it. The Lord spoke to you at Horeb from the belly of the fire.” Since the content of these two verses is consistent with the rational proof, it is necessary to interpret the non-limited verses, not [lack of] interpreting them, and the People of the Book here also agree with us and do not give preference to the non-limited verses to these two. The two verses, and just as there is a notification of the physicality of God Almighty, so there is proof of the place of God Almighty in the non-exclusive verses of the Old and New Testaments, such as verse 8, chapter 25, and verses 45 and 46 of chapter 29 of the Book of Exodus, and in verse 3, chapter 5 and 34, chapter 35 of the Book of Numbers, and in verse 15 of the twenty-sixth chapter of the Book of Exceptions, and in verses 5 and 6 of the seventh chapter of the Second Book of Samuel, and in the verse 30, 32, 34, 36, 39, 45 and 49 of Chapter Eight of the First Book of Kings.

And in verse 11 of the ninth Psalms, and in verse 4 of the tenth Psalms, and in verse 8 of the twenty-fifth Psalms, and in verse 16 of the sixty-seventh Psalms, and in verse 2 of the seventy-third Psalms, and in verse 2 of the seventy-fifth Psalms, and in verse 1 of the ninety-eighth Psalms, and in verse 21 of the hundred and thirty-fourth Psalms, and in verses 17 and 21 of the third chapter of the book of Yotil, and in verse 2 of the eighth chapter of the book Zechariah, in verse 45 and 48, chapter 5, 1, 9, 14, and 26, chapter 6, 11, and 21, chapter 7, 32, and 33, chapter 10 and 50, chapter 2 and 13, chapter 15 and 17, chapter 16, 10, 14, 19, and 35, chapter 18, 19, and 22, chapter 23 of the Gospel of Matthew. There are no verses in the Old and New Testaments that indicate God’s transcendence of the place except Few as verse

1 and 2 of the sixty-sixth chapter of the Book of Isaiah, and verse 48 of the seventh chapter of the works of the disciples. However, since the content of these few verses was consistent with the proofs, the many verses that were not limited and felt the place were attributed to God Almighty, not these few verses, and the People of the Book also agree with us in this interpretation.

It has become clear from this third matter that if a lot is in contradiction to the proof, it must be attributed to a small amount that agrees with it, and its abundance is not taken into account. So, if a lot is in agreement and a small amount is in contradiction, then interpretation in it is necessary according to the intuition of reason.

(The fourth matter) I learned in the third matter that God has no likeness or image, and it was also stated in the New Testament in many places that seeing God in this world is not a reality, in the eighteenth verse of the first chapter of the Gospel of John thus: “No one has ever seen God,” and in the sixteenth verse of the sixth chapter of the first letter to Timothy: “No man has seen him, nor is he able to see him,” and in the twelfth verse of the fourth chapter of the first epistle of John: “God has never been seen by anyone.” It is proven from these verses that whoever is visible is never a god, even if the word God or the like is given to him in the words of God or the prophets or the disciples. No one should be deceived by simply using the word God, and should not claim that the interpretation is metaphorical. How can it be committed? Because turning to metaphor must be based on the presumption that prevents the desire for truth, especially if the definitive proof indicates prevention. Yes, using such terms to describe other than God has an appropriate meaning for every situation. For example, in the five books attributed to Moses, peace be upon him, it is applied to some angels because the majesty of God appears in them more than in others.

And in the twenty-third chapter of the Book of Exodus, God Almighty says thus: 20 “I am sending my angel before you to guard you on the way and to bring you to the place where you are prepared, 21 so guard him and obey his command and do not oppose him. He will not forgive you if you sin, for my name is with him. 23 And my angel will go before you and bring you in to the Amorites, the Hittites, the Parzanites, the Canaanites, the Hivites, and the Janusites, whom I will bring out.”

So his saying: I send my angel before you, and similarly to his saying, my angel will go, are two texts that indicate that the one who walked with the children of Israel in a pillar of cloud by day and a pillar of fire by night was an angel among the angels, and he was given such terms as you will learn about him for what I said, as appears from his saying, “My name is with him,” and their application came in

Places that are not limited to the king and the perfect human being, but rather to individual people, but to the accursed Satan, and even to non-minded people as well. The interpretation of some of these words has been learned from some places, and in some places the simplicity of speech is indicated in such a way that the observer is not suspicious at first. And here I am presenting to you the evidence for this section and in this section I quote the phrase of the books of the Old Testament from the Arabic translation that was printed in London in the year 1844 AD, and the phrase from the New Testament, either from the aforementioned translation or from the Arabic translation that was printed. In Beirut in the year 1860, and I do not copy the entire phrase of the place cited, but rather I copy the verses that relate to the purpose in this place, and I leave out the verses that are not intended, in the seventeenth chapter of the Book of Genesis, like this: 1 “And when Abram was ninety-nine years old, the Lord appeared to him and said, ‘I am God Almighty, go forward before me and be perfect.’” 4 “And God said to him, ‘I am he, and my covenant is with you, and you will be the father of many nations.’” 7 “And I will raise up

My covenant between me and you and your descendants after you throughout their generations is an everlasting covenant, that I will be God to you and to your descendants after you.” 8 “And I will give to you and to your descendants the land by which you are a stranger, all the land of Canaan, for a possession forever, and I will be their God.” 9 “And God said to Abraham a second time,” 15 “And God also said to Abraham.” This visible speaker is a king according to what you know, and for his saying that he ascended from Abraham, in this phrase he was called God, the Lord, and the God, and he called himself, “I am God Almighty, to be your God and to your offspring after you, and to be their God.” Likewise, he used similar words in the eighteenth chapter of the Book of Genesis to the king who appeared to Abraham, peace be upon him, with the other two kings, and gave him good news of the birth of Isaac and told that the villages of Lot would be destroyed.
In more than fourteen places, and in the section

The twenty-eighth of the book mentioned in the case of Jacob, peace be upon him, when he traveled to a country whose situation was like this: 10 “And Jacob departed from Beersheba and proceeded to Harran.” 11 “And he came to a place and spent the night there, and he took a stone from the stones of that place and put it under his head and slept there.” 12 “And he saw in a dream a ladder standing on the earth and its top reaching to heaven, and the angels of God ascending and descending on it.” 13 “And the Lord was standing at the top of the ladder, and said, ‘I am God, the God of Abraham. Your father and the God of Isaac, the land on which you sleep I give it to you and to your descendants.” 14 “And your descendants will be like the sand of the earth, and will expand to the west and the east, and will flourish, and all the families of the earth will be blessed by you and by your seed.” 15 “And I will guard you wherever you go, and I will return you to this land and will not leave you until I do what I have said to you.” 16 “Then Jacob awoke from his sleep and said, ‘Indeed, the Lord is in this place, and I did not know it.’” 17 “And he was afraid, and said, ‘How frightening is this?’ This place is nothing but the house of God and the gate of heaven.” 18 “And Jacob arose in the morning, and took the stone with which he had cushioned himself, and set it up as a pillar, and poured oil upon it.” 19 “And he called the name of the city Ben-El, which was first almonds.” 20 “And he vowed a vow.

Saying, “If God will be with me and keep me in the way that I am going and provide me with bread to eat and clothing to wear.” 21 “And I return in peace to my father’s house, then the Lord will be my God.” 22 “And this stone that I have set up as a pillar will be called the house of God, and of everything you have given me I will give you a tithe.”

And in the thirty-first chapter of the aforementioned book, Jacob, peace be upon him, said in a speech to his wife, Leah, and Rachel, like this: 11 “Then the angel of God said to me in a dream, ‘Jacob,’ and I said, ‘Here I am.’” 12 “And he said to me, etc.” 13 “I am the God of Bethel, where you anointed the stone pillar and vowed to me a vow. On him in the expressions mentioned in more than eighteen places, and this king said: “I am the Lord, the God of Abraham your father and the God of Isaac,” and Jacob, peace be upon him, said regarding him, “O God of my father Abraham and the God of my father Isaac, O Lord, and

From Genesis like this: 9 “Then God appeared to Jacob again after he had returned from between the rivers of Syria and blessed him,” 10 “saying, ‘Your name will no longer be called Jacob, but your name will be Israel,’ and he called his name Israel.” 11 “And he said to him, ‘I am God the Ruler of all things. “I am God Almighty,” and in the third chapter of Exodus 2, “And the Lord appeared to him in a flame of fire from the midst of a bush. He looked at the bush in which the fire was kindling, but it was not consumed. 4 And he saw God.

And in the thirteenth chapter of the Book of Exodus, this is the following: 21 “And the Lord went before them to show them the way by day with a pillar of cloud and by night with a pillar of fire, to guide them the way by day and by night. 22 The pillar of cloud by day nor the pillar of fire by night never departed from before the people.” Then in the fourteenth chapter of the book.

The interpretation that occurs in verse 38 of the first chapter of the Gospel of John is thus: “And my Lord said, ‘Interpret it, Master.’” If you know what I mentioned, you have attained complete insight that it is not permissible for a rational person to infer by using some of these words to some events whose occurrence, change, or inability to occur from the senses that he is a God or the Son of God, and rejects all definitive rational proofs, as well as the textual proofs behind him.

(The fifth command) The occurrence of the metaphor in places other than those mentioned in the third and fourth command is frequent: For example, God promised Abraham, peace be upon him, to multiply his children, like this, verse sixteen of the thirteenth chapter of the Book of Genesis: “And I will make your descendants like the dust of the earth. And the seventeenth verse of the twenty-second chapter of the aforementioned book: “I will bless you and multiply your offspring as the stars of the sky and as the sand that is on the seashore, etc.” Thus, Jacob, peace be upon him, promised that your offspring would be like the sand of the earth, as I knew in the fourth command, and their children did not reach the amount of a pound of sand in the world at any time, let alone the amount of sand on the seashore or the sand of the earth, and he fell in praise of the land that God promised to give in the eighth verse of the third chapter of the Book of Exodus and other verses that milk and honey flowed into it and no A land in this world as well, and it was written in the first chapter of the Book of Exceptions like this: “And the cities are great and fortified to the sky.” And it was written in the ninth chapter of the aforementioned book like this: “And more powerful than you are large and fortified cities built up to the sky” and in the Seventy-Seventh Psalms like this: 65: “And the Lord awoke like a sleeper, like a mighty man awakened from wine, 66 and he struck back his enemies and made them a disgrace for eternity.” The third verse of the hundred and third Psalms describes God thus: “And He who covers the waters with His high places, Who has made the clouds His chariot, who walks on the wings of the winds.”

John’s words are full of metaphors. There is rarely a paragraph in which there is no need for interpretation, as is well known to anyone who reads his Gospel, his letters, and his observations. The Christians explained it literally, and for this reason we present some examples to show that interpreting the metaphors literally is not correct, such as Christ saying about Herod, “Go and tell that fox.” It is known that what is meant by the word “fox” in this phrase is a tyrant and an oppressor, because that animal called like this is known for trickery and treachery as well. Our Lord said to the Jews: I am the living bread that came down from heaven. Everyone who eats of this bread will live forever, and the bread that I will give him is my body. I give it for the life of the world, John, p. 6, verse 15. The lustful Jews understood this phrase in the literal sense

They said: How can this man give us his body to eat? Verse 52, and they did not notice that by this he meant his sacrifice, which he gave as an atonement for the sins of the world. Our Savior also said about the bread when appointing the Last Supper: This is my body, and about the wine, this is my blood, Matthew, p. 26, verse 26. Since the twelfth century, the Roman Catholics have given this saying another meaning, opposite and different from other evidence in the Holy Books and the correct evidence, and they were bound to result from this in their teaching about transubstantiation, that is, the transformation of bread and wine into the body and blood of Christ. The two essences are when the priest utters the words of imaginary sanctification, even though it may appear to all five senses that the bread and wine remain in their essence and have not changed.

As for the correct interpretation of our Lord’s saying, it is that the bread is like his body and the wine is like his blood.” His words ended with his wording. His confession is clear, but it is necessary to look at his saying. Since the twelfth century until the end of it, he responded to the Romans who believed that bread and wine were transformed into the body and blood of Christ, peace be upon him, according to the testimony of sense. He began the saying of Christ, peace be upon him, by deleting the genitive, even if it is apparent from the statement as they understood it, because it is like this: 26 “And while they were eating, Jesus took the bread, blessed him, and broke it.” And he gave to the disciples, saying, “Take, eat, this is my body.” 27 And he took the cup, and gave thanks, and gave it to them, saying, “Drink from it, all of you.” 28 For this is my blood of the new covenant, which is shed for many for the remission of sins.” They said: The wording of this indicates the essence of the entire present thing, and if the essence of the bread had remained, this statement would not have been correct, and they were before the emergence of a sect.
Protestants are the most Christians in the world, and many of them are from this group to this day as well.

Just as this doctrine is wrong according to the testimony of sense according to this sect, so the doctrine of the Trinity is wrong, even if we assume the significance of some similar statements according to their apparent meaning, rather it is impossible with conclusive evidence. If they say, “Aren’t we among the possessed of minds,” then how can we acknowledge it if it is impossible? We said: Aren't the Romans people of intellects like you, and more in stature than you to this day, let alone in the past? So how did they acknowledge and agree on what is not true according to you and whose invalidity is also evidenced by sense? It is also false in the same respect for the following reasons:

(The first) is that the Roman Church claims that the bread alone transforms the body and blood of Christ and becomes a complete Christ. So I say that if it transforms into a complete Christ alive with his divinity and humanity that he took from Mary, peace be upon them, then the symptoms of the human body must be seen in it, and there is skin, bones, blood, and other organs in it, but they are not found in it. Rather, all the symptoms of the bread remain now as they were, so if anyone looks at it, touches it, or tastes it, he will not feel anything other than the bread, and if he preserves it, the corruption that It occurs in bread, not the corruption that occurs in the human body. If transmutation was proven, then the transmutation of Christ would be bread, not the transmutation of bread into Christ. If they had said that Christ transmuted into bread, it would have been less far-fetched than this, even if it was also false and contrary to self-evidentity.

(Second) The presence of Christ in his divinity in multiple places at the same time, although it is possible according to their claim, but considering his humanity it is not possible because in this regard he was like us to the point that he was hungry, eating, drinking, sleeping, afraid of the Jews, fleeing, and so on. So how can his multiplicity be possible with this consideration in one body in places that are not limited to one time in reality? What is astonishing is that what existed before his ascension to heaven with this consideration in two places also, in addition to infinite places, and also after his ascension to heaven, so how can he exist after centuries after the invention of this corrupt belief with the aforementioned consideration in places that are not confined at the same time?

(Third) If we assume that millions of priests in the world were sanctified at the same time and that it was impossible for each to offer Christ who was born of the Virgin, then it is not impossible that either each of these new Christians was the same as the other or someone else, and the second is invalid according to their claim and the first is invalid in the same matter because the substance of each is different from the substance of the other.

(Fourth) If the bread turns into a whole Christ under the hand of the priest, and this priest breaks this bread into many pieces and small parts, then either Christ will be broken up piece by piece according to the number of pieces and parts, or each piece and part will turn into a whole Christ as well. In the first case, what is received is not the reach of a whole Christ, and in the second case, where did these Christs come from, because what happened with the offering is the one Christ?
(Fifth) If the Lord’s Supper that occurred before his crucifixion were as simple as the same sacrifice that occurred on the cross, it would have to be sufficient to save the world.

There is no need for him to be crucified on the tree again by the Jews, because according to their claim, Christ did not come into the world except to save people through a sacrifice once, and he did not have to suffer repeatedly, as the phrase at the end of the ninth chapter of the Hebrew Epistle clearly indicates.

(Sixth) If what I claim is true, then Christians must be more vile than the Jews, because the Jews only harmed him once, so they abstained and did not eat his flesh. These people torture him and slaughter him every day in unlimited places. If the killer was an infidel and cursed once, then what is the matter with those who slaughter him countless times and eat his flesh and drink his blood? We seek refuge in God from those who eat their god and drink his blood in reality. If their poor, weak god is not saved from the hands of these people, then who will be saved? May God keep us away from their arena. And yes, what was said, “Dosti nadan sarasar dashmni sett” (placed in the margin:) includes the meaning of the Arabic proverb: A wise enemy is better than an ignorant friend, and the literal translation: An ignorant friend is like an enemy. .

(Seventh) It occurred in the twenty-second chapter of Luke that Christ said in the Lord’s Supper thus: “Do this in remembrance of me.” If this supper were the same sacrifice, it would not be valid for it to be a remembrance, because a thing is not a remembrance of itself. The rational people, whose sound minds judge such illusions in the sensible, if they were delusional in the essence of God or in the rational, then what is the exclusion from them? But I abandon this and say in an interview with Protestant scholars: It is just as these rational people among you gathered on this doctrine that is contrary to sense and reason, in imitation of the fathers or for another purpose.

Likewise, they and yours joined together in the doctrine of the Trinity, which is contrary to common sense and evidence, and the many people whom you call atheists, and their number in this time is greater than the size of your sect, and even of the Roman sect, and they are rational like you, and of your kind, and of your people, and they were Christians like you, so they left this doctrine because it included matters like these, mocking it with eloquent mockery, and they do not mock anything else like it, as it is not hidden from anyone who looks at it. Their books, and the Uni Niren band, also among the Christian groups, deny it, while Muslims and Jews, both past and present, understand it as a kind of pipe dream.

(Sixth matter) There was a lot of generality in the sayings of Christ, peace be upon him, such that his contemporaries and disciples often did not understand them unless he explained them himself. The sayings that he explained among these general sayings were understood by them, and some of them he did not explain, some of them were understood after a long period of time, and some of them remained vague to them until the end of life, and their counterparts are many, and I will suffice here with some of them.

In the second chapter of the Gospel of John, Christ’s call, peace be upon him, to the Jews who were asking for a miracle occurred in this way: 19 “Jesus answered and said to them, ‘Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up.’ 20 “And the Jews said, ‘In forty-six years has this temple been built, and in three days will you raise it up?’” 21 “But he was talking about the temple of his body.” 22 “And when he rose from the dead, his disciples remembered that he had said this, and they believed the Scripture and the words that Jesus had spoken.” Here the disciples did not understand. In addition to the Jews, but the disciples understood after He rose from the dead,

Christ said to be led by a razor from the Jewish scholars: If one is not born from above, he cannot see the kingdom of God, so he did not understand his meaning. He said, “How can a man be born when he is old? Can he enter into his mother’s womb again and be born?” Christ understood him again, but he did not understand his meaning this time either. He said, “How is this possible?” Christ said, “Don’t you understand, since you are the teacher of Israel?” And this story is detailed in the third chapter of the Gospel of John. And Christ said in addressing the Jews: “I am the bread of life. If anyone eats of this bread, he will live forever.” And the bread that I will give is my flesh.” Then the Jews argued among themselves, saying, “How can this man give us his flesh to eat?” Then Christ said to them: “Unless you eat the flesh of the Son of Man and drink his blood, you have no life. Whoever among you eats my flesh and drinks my blood has eternal life. For my flesh is true food and my blood is true drink. Whoever eats my flesh and drinks my blood abides in me and I in him. Just as the living Father has sent me and I live through the Father, whoever eats me will live because of me.” And many of his disciples said, “Who can hear these words?” Many of them left his company, and this story is detailed in the sixth chapter of the Gospel of John. Here the Jews did not understand the words of Christ, and the disciples found it difficult, and many of them apostatized.
And in the eighth chapter of the Gospel of John, this is how: 21 “Jesus also said to them, ‘I am going away, and you will seek me and die in your conversation. Where I go, you cannot go.

They came 22 and the Jews said: Perhaps he will kill himself so that he may say, “Where I am going, you cannot come.” 51 Truly, truly, I say to you, if anyone keeps my words, he will never see death. 52 Then the Jews said to him, “Now we know that you have a demon. Abraham and the prophets are dead, and you say, ‘If anyone keeps my words, he will never taste death.’” Here too, the Jews did not understand his meaning in the two places, but rather attributed it to madness in the second place.

And in the eleventh chapter of the Gospel of John, this is the following: 11 “He said to them, ‘Our beloved Father has fallen asleep, but I go to wake him.’ 12 And his disciples said, ‘Master, if he has slept, he will be healed.’ 13 And Jesus was speaking about his death, but they thought he was talking about falling asleep. 14 Then Jesus said to them publicly, ‘Our beloved Father has fallen asleep.’” Here, the disciples of Christ, peace be upon him, did not understand his words until he declared it, and in the sixteenth chapter of the Gospel of Matthew, thus: 6 “And Jesus said to them, ‘Look. And they guarded themselves against the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees, and they thought within themselves, “We have not taken bread.” 8 Then Jesus knew and said to them, “Why are you thinking within yourselves, O you of little faith, that you have not received bread?” 11 How can you not understand that I did not tell you about bread to guard against the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees? Intended before warning,.

And in the eighth chapter of the Gospel of Luke, in the case of the girl whom Christ, peace be upon him, revived, God willing, is like this: 52 “And everyone was weeping and stroking her, and he said, ‘Do not weep; she is not dead, but sleeping.’” 53 “Then they laughed at him, knowing that she was dead.” And here not everyone understood the meaning of Christ, peace be upon him, and so they laughed at him. And in the ninth chapter of the Gospel of Luke, Christ said in addressing the disciples like this: 44 “Put these words in your ears, for the Son of Man will He will be delivered into the hands of men.” 25 “But they did not understand this saying, and it was hidden from them so that they would not understand it, and they were afraid to ask him about this saying.” And here the apostles did not understand and did not ask him for fear of him, and in the eighteenth chapter of the Gospel of Luke, thus: 31 “And he took the Twelve and said to them, ‘See, we are going up to Jerusalem, and everything that is written by the prophets concerning the Son of Man will be fulfilled.’” 32 “For he will be handed over to the Gentiles, and he will be mocked and reviled.” And he will spit on it” 33

“And they will flog him and kill him, and on the third day he will rise.” 34 “But they did not understand anything of that, and this matter was hidden from them, and they did not know what was said.” And here also the disciples did not understand, even though this explanation was the second time, and there was no generality in the speech either, according to what appears. Perhaps the reason for the lack of understanding is that they had heard from the Jews that the Messiah would be a great authority, so when they believed in Jesus, peace be upon him, and believed him.

With Christianity, they thought that he would sit on the bed of power, and we also sit on the bed of power, because Jesus, peace be upon him, had promised them that they would sit on twelve beds and each of them would rule over one of the groups of the children of Israel, and they carried this worldly power as it appears, and this bread was contrary to what they thought and what they hoped for, so they did not understand, and you will soon know that they were hoping for this, and it was also compared to the disciples. There are two things about Jesus, peace be upon him, from some Christian sayings, and this suspicion has not disappeared from most or all of them until death. (The first) is that they believed that John would not die until the resurrection. (The second) is that they believed that the resurrection would occur during their time, as I knew in detail in the first chapter. This matter is certain for me, because the exact words of Jesus, peace be upon him, are not preserved in any of the Gospels. Rather, in each of them there is a translation in Greek according to what the narrators understood, and I knew in detail in the eighteenth verse of the Gospel. The third purpose of the second chapter is that the Gospel of Matthew did not remain, but rather the rest is a translation, and the name of its translator is not known with certainty until now, and it is not proven with a connected chain of transmission that the remaining books are from the people attributed to them, and it has been proven that distortion occurred in these books with certainty and it has been proven that the people of religion and religion were distorting it with the intention of supporting an acceptable issue or to ward off an objection, and it was known in the thirty-first witness of the second purpose with evidence.

What is strong is that their distortion in this matter was proven, so they added this phrase in the fifth chapter of the First Epistle to John: “There are three in heaven, the Father, the Word, and the Holy Spirit, and these three are one, and those who bear witness on earth.” They added some words to the first chapter of the Gospel of Luke and dropped some words from the first chapter of the Gospel of Matthew, and they omitted the eighth verse of the twenty-second chapter of the Gospel of Luke. In this case, if there were some similar Christian sayings indicating the Trinity, there is no reliance. It is, although it is not explicit, as you will know in the twelfth matter of the introduction.

(Seventh matter) The mind may not comprehend the essence of some things and their essence as they are, but nevertheless it judges their possibility and their existence does not necessitate to it an impossibility, and therefore these things are considered possible, and it may judge a priori or with conclusive evidence that some things are impossible.

Things, and for him it is necessary for their existence to be impossible, and between the two forms there is a clear difference, and from the second category is the meeting of the two true opposites and their elevation, as well as the meeting of true unity and multiplicity in one time from one side, as well as the meeting of evenness and individuality, as well as the meeting of different individuals, as well as the meeting of opposites such as light and darkness, blackness and whiteness, heat and cold, wetness and dryness, blindness and sight, and stillness and movement in personal matter. With the unity of time and direction, and the impossibility of these things is self-evident and ruled by the mind of every rational person, and also from the second section, the necessity of period and sequence and the like, the mind judges their invalidity with conclusive evidence.

(Eighth matter) If the two statements contradict each other, then they must be omitted if the interpretation is not possible, or they must be interpreted if possible, and the interpretation must be such that it does not entail the impossible or falsehood. For example, the verses that indicate physicality and form are contradicted by some verses that indicate exaltation, so they must be interpreted as I knew in the third matter, but the interpretation must not be that God is characterized by two attributes, meaning physicality and exaltation, and if our minds do not understand this matter, then this interpretation is invalid. The mere duty to respond does not remove the contradiction.

(The Ninth Order) Number, when it is a part of quantity, does not exist by itself, but rather by something else, and every existent must be exposed to unity or multiplicity. The entities that exist with the real distinction and are personified by personification are exposed to real multiplicity, so if they become exposed to it, they are not exposed to real unity, otherwise the two real opposites would be required to come together as you knew in the seventh matter. Yes, it is permissible for them to be exposed to legal unity if the sum is real many and one legal.

(The tenth matter) The dispute between us and the people of the Trinity and monotheism is both real, and if they say that the trinity is real and monotheism is legal, there is no dispute between us and them, but they say that each of them is real as stated in the books of Protestant scholars. The author of Mizan al-Haqq said in the first chapter of his book called The Solution to the Problem like this: “The Christians hold both monotheism and the Trinity to have the real meaning.”

(The eleventh matter) The scholar Al-Maqrizi said in his book called Al-Khattab in explaining the Christian sects that existed in his time: “The Christians are many sects: the Melkite, the Nestorian, the Jacobite, the Budhaani, and the Marquliyyah, and they are the Rahawis who were in the regions of Harran and other than these.” Then he said, “The Melkite, the Jacobite, and the Nestorian are all agreed on

Their deity is three hypostases, and these three hypostases are one, and it is an ancient essence, meaning father, son, and the Holy Spirit, one God. Then they said, “The Son united with a created human being, so he and what he was united with became one Christ, and that Christ is the God of the servants and their Lord.” Then they disagreed about the character of the union, and some of them claimed that he fell between a divinity essence and a human essence, a union, and the union did not deprive each one of them of its essence and element, and that Christ is a worshiped God and that he is the son of Mary whom she bore. And she gave birth to him, and that he was killed and crucified. Some people claimed that Christ after the union was two essences, one of which was divine and the other was human, and that the killing and crucifixion occurred in relation to his humanity, not in terms of his divinity, and that Mary conceived Christ and gave birth to him in terms of his humanity, and this is the saying of the Nestorians. Then they say that Christ, in all his perfection, is a worshiped god and that he is the son of God Almighty, according to their saying.

Some people claimed that the union occurred between two essences, the divine and the human, as the theological essence is simple, undivided and indivisible. Some people claimed that the union is in terms of the son’s indwelling in the body and his mingling with it. Some of them claimed that the union is in terms of appearance, such as the appearance of the writing of a seal and an inscription, if it is signed on clay or wax, or the appearance of a human being’s image in a mirror, and other differences that are not found in others. Kingship is attributed to the king of the Romans, and they say that God is a name with three meanings, so it is one, three, and three, one. The Jacobites say that He is one, ancient, and that He was neither a body nor a human being, then He became flesh and became human. And the Marquliyyah say that God is One, and His knowledge of others is eternal with Him.
Christ is his son on the side of mercy, just as it is said that Abraham is the friend of God.” His words ended with his words,

It has become clear to you that their opinions regarding explaining the sign of the union between the hypostasis of the Son and the body of Christ were very different, and therefore you see the proofs provided in the ancient Islamic books are different, and we have no dispute in this doctrine with Marqulism except by considering the use of the misleading word, and the group of Protestants, when they saw that explaining the relationship of the union was not devoid of obvious corruption, abandoned the opinions of the ancestors, and were incapable of themselves and chose to remain silent about explaining it and explaining the relationship between the three hypostases.

(The Twelfth Order) The doctrine of the Trinity was not present in any of the previous nations from the time of Adam to the time of Moses, peace be upon him, and the obsessions of the people of the Trinity in their adherence to some verses of the Book of Genesis do not apply to us because they are in fact a distortion of their meanings, and the meaning of their adherence is such that the meaning is in the poet’s stomach, and I do not claim that they are

They do not cling to their claim to any of the verses of the aforementioned book. Rather, I claim that it has not been proven in the text that this belief belonged to one of the previous nations, and as for it not being established in the law of Moses and his nation, there is no need for clarification, because whoever reads this used Torah will not be hidden from him, and Yahya, peace be upon him, was there until the end of his life.

Doubting whether Christ, peace be upon him, is the promised Messiah or not, as he stated in the eleventh chapter of the Gospel of Matthew, that he sent two of his disciples and said to him, “Are you the one who is coming, or should we wait for another?” If Jesus, peace be upon him, was a god, then it would be necessary to disbelieve in God. Doubting God is disbelief, and how can one imagine that he does not know his God when he is his prophet? Rather, he is the best of the prophets according to Christ’s testimony as stated in this chapter, and if he did not know the best despite being a contemporary, then not knowing the other prophets who preceded Jesus is more deserving. Considering that, the Jewish scholars from the time of Moses, peace be upon him, to this time do not acknowledge it, and it appears that the essence of God and His perfect attributes are ancient, unchangeable, existing forever and ever. If the trinity were inevitable, then it would have been obligatory for Moses, peace be upon him, and the prophets of the children of Israel to explain it properly. It is very surprising that the Mosaic law, which was obligatory to obey for all the prophets until the era of Jesus, peace be upon him, was devoid of explaining this doctrine, which is the source of salvation according to the claim of the people of the Trinitarians. It is not possible for anyone to be saved without it, whether a prophet or not, and neither Moses nor any of the Israeli prophets explained this doctrine with a clear statement.

So that this doctrine can be clearly understood from him, and no doubt remains, and Moses, peace be upon him, clarifies the rulings that according to the sacred people of the Trinity are weak and very incomplete with a complete explanation, and he repeats them time after time and time after time, and emphasizes the

Maintaining it is an eloquent confirmation, and it requires death for those who abandon some of it. And what is even more astonishing is that Jesus, peace be upon him, also clarified this belief until his ascension with a clear statement, for example, by saying that God is three hypostases, the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit, and the son’s hypostasis is attached to my body through a so-and-so relationship or a relationship whose understanding is beyond the comprehension of your minds, so know that I am God and nothing else, for the sake of the aforementioned relationship, or he says another statement similar to it in stating this meaning explicitly, and it is not in the hands of the people of the Trinity to His sayings, except for some similar sayings: The author of Mizan al-Haqq said in his book called Miftah al-Asrar: “If you say, why did Christ not explain his divinity with a clearer statement than what he mentioned, and why did he not say clearly and concisely that I am God and nothing else? He answered first with an unacceptable answer, which our purpose is not related to conveying in this place. Then he answered secondly, “that no one was able to understand this relationship and oneness before his resurrection,” meaning from the dead, “and his ascension. If he had said it explicitly, they would have understood that he is a god according to the human body, and this matter was absolutely false. He also realized this demand from the demands in which he said to his disciples, ‘I have many things as well.

I tell you, but you cannot bear it now, but when he, the Spirit of truth, comes, he will guide you into all the truth, for he will not speak on his own authority, but rather what he hears will speak, and he will tell you things to come.” Then he said, “The elders of the Jewish sect repeatedly wanted to seize him and stone him, but the situation is that he did not explain his divinity in their hands except through riddles.” So two excuses were learned from his words: (the first) the inability of anyone to understand before the Ascension (and the second) the fear of the Jews, and both of them. They are extremely weak

Weakness. As for the first, this amount was sufficient to remove the suspicion: that the relationship of the union between my body and the hypostasis of the Son is beyond your power to understand, so abandon its investigation and believe that I am not a god with regard to the body, but rather with the relationship of the aforementioned union. As for the same inability to understand it, it also remains after the ascension, to the point that none of their scholars have known until now the nature of this relationship and unity, and whoever said what he said, his statement is stoning the unseen and is not without great corruption, and so the scholars left The Protestant sect has explained it directly, and this priest admits in places in his books that this matter is a secret that is beyond the comprehension of reason. As for the second, it is because Christ, peace be upon him, did not come to them except to be an atonement for the sins of creation, and for the Jews to crucify him, and he knew with certainty that they would crucify him, and when they would crucify him, what place was there for fear of the Jews in explaining the doctrine? And the wonder is that the Creator

The earth and the sky, and He who is capable of doing what He wills, fears His servants who are among the most humble people in the world, and because of their fear, He does not explain the doctrine that is the source of salvation.

His servants of the prophets, such as Jeremiah, Isaiah, and Yahya, peace be upon them, were not afraid of them in explaining the truth, but they were severely harmed and some of them were killed. And what is more astonishing than that is that Christ, peace be upon him, is afraid of them in explaining this great issue, and he puts great stress on them in enjoining good and forbidding evil until the shift reaches the point of cursing, and he addresses the scribes and Pharisees verbally with these words: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, and woe to you, you blind leaders. Oh, blind ignorant people, and you blind Pharisee, and you serpents and serpents, how do you escape from the judgment of hell, and your ugliness is revealed on the evidence, to the point that some of them complained that you are cursing us, as stated in the twenty-third chapter of the Gospel of Matthew and the first chapter of the Gospel of Matthew?

Ten from the Gospel of Luke, and things like this are mentioned in other places in the Gospel as well. How can one think that Christ, peace be upon him, would abandon the explanation of the doctrine that is the source of salvation for the sake of their fear? God forbid, God forbid, for his honor to be like this, and it was known from his words that Christ, peace be upon him, never explained this issue to the Jews except through riddles, and that they denied this doctrine so vehemently that they wanted to stone him repeatedly for the riddles.

sections.heading: Chapter One: On invalidating the Trinity with rational proofs
content: [Chapter One: On invalidating the Trinity with rational proofs]

(The first proof) Since trinity and monotheism are true for Christians by virtue of the tenth command of the introduction, if true trinity exists, then true multiplicity must also exist by virtue of the ninth command of the introduction, and true monotheism cannot be proven after it. Otherwise, the meeting of the two true opposites is necessary by virtue of the seventh command of the introduction, which is impossible, so the multiplicity of the necessary matters is necessary and monotheism is definitely absent. So the one who says the Trinity cannot be united to God Almighty through true monotheism, and to say that the true Trinity and the true monotheism, even if they are true opposites in something other than obligatory, yet they are not, is pure sophistry because if it is proven that the two things, in view of themselves, are true opposites or opposites in the same matter, then it is not possible for them to come together in one personal matter in one time from one aspect, whether that matter is obligatory or not. How can it be that the true one does not have a true third and the three have a true third, which is one? The three are the sum of three ones, and the real one is not the sum of three ones.

The true One is a part of the three, so if they were to come together in one place, it would be necessary for the part to be a whole and the whole to be a part, and this meeting would require that God be composed of infinite parts in the act due to the union of the reality of the whole and the part according to this estimation, and the whole is composite, so each of its parts is also a composite of the parts that constitute the same part, and so on, and the fact that the thing is composed of infinite parts in the act is absolutely false, and that this combination entails the one being a third of itself and the three being three times the same, and the one being three times the same. All three.

(The second proof) If there were to be found in the essence of God three excellent persons with true excellence, as they said, then without regard to the multiplicity of obligations, it would be necessary for God not to be a summed reality, but rather a theoretical compound, for the true composition must include lack between the parts. To some other things that the singular essence is not composed of, given that God in the aforementioned form is a composite, and every composite lacks in its realization the realization of each one of its parts, and the part is not the whole by definition, so every composite lacks something else, and every thing lacking something else is possible for its own sake, so it is necessary for God to be possible for its own sake, and this is false.

(The third proof) If the true privilege between the hypostases is proven, then the matter by which this privilege occurred is either one of the attributes of perfection or it is not. On the first part, not all the attributes of perfection are shared between them, which is contrary to what was established by them that each of these hypostases is characterized by all the attributes of perfection, and on the second part, then what is described by it is described by an attribute that is not one of the attributes of perfection, and this is a deficiency from which God must be removed.

(The fourth proof) The union between the divine and human essence, if it were real, then the hypostasis of the Son would be limited and infinite, and everything that was like that would be possible for it to accept increase and decrease, and everything that was like that would be its specification to the specified extent for the specification of an allocation and a decreed estimate, and everything that was like that would be created, so it is necessary for the hypostasis of the Son to be created, and its occurrence requires the occurrence of God.

(The fifth proof) If the three hypostases were truly excellent, the distinguishing entity must be other than the intrinsic necessity, because it is shared between them, and what is shared is other than what is the excellence, so each one of them is composed of two parts, and each composite is possible for its own sake, so it is necessary for each one of them to be possible for its own sake.

(Sixth proof) The doctrine of the Jacobites is clearly false because it requires the overturning of the ancient by the accidental and the abstract by the material. As for the doctrine of others, it is said in its invalidation: This union is either by solution or by something else. If it is the first, it is invalid in three ways, according to the number of trinity.

Firstly, because that solution is not without either being like the solution of rose water in roses, fat in sesame, and fire in coal, and this is false because it would only be true if the hypostasis of the Son were a body, and they agreed with us that it is not a body, or it could be like the occurrence of color in the body, and this is also false because what is reasonable from this dependency is the occurrence of color in space due to the occurrence of its place in this space, and this also is only imagined in bodies, or it is like the occurrence of additional attributes. For essences, and this is also false because what is reasonable from this dependency is need. If it were proven that the son’s hypostasis in this sense was present in something that was in need, then it would be possible and lack an effector, and that is impossible, and if all reports are proven to be false, it is impossible to prove it.

And secondly, if we abandon consideration of the meaning of subrogation, we say: If the hypostasis of the Son were to inhabit the body, then that subsumption would either be by way of obligation or permissibility, and there is no way to the former because His essence is either sufficient in requiring this subsumption or not sufficient in that. If the former is impossible for that requirement to depend on the fulfillment of a condition, then it is necessary for either God to occur or the place to come, and both of them are invalid. Solutions: Something happens in it, so it is susceptible to accidents, and that is impossible, because if it were so, then that ability would be a requisite.

His essence, and it existed eternally, and that is impossible because the existence of events in eternity is impossible, and there is no way to the second according to this estimation. That solution is in addition to the essence of the hypostasis, so if it is dissolved in the body, a created quality must be dissolved in it, and its occurrence requires that it be subject to occurrences, and it is false as you know.

As for the third, if the hypostasis of the Son resides in the body of Jesus, peace be upon him, it is not devoid of either that he also remains in God’s essence or not. If the first is necessary, the personal state must exist in two places, and if the second is necessary, God’s essence must be devoid of Him, then it is nullified, because the absence of the part requires the absence of the whole. And if that union is without substitution, then we say that if the hypostasis of the Son is united with Christ, peace be upon him, then in a state of union, if they exist, then they are two, not one, then there is no union, and if they are absent and a third occurs, then it is also not. It is a union, rather the non-existence of two things and the occurrence of a third thing, and if one of them remains and the other is non-existent, then the non-existent is impossible to unite with the existing because it is impossible to say that the non-existent itself is the existing, so it appears that the union is impossible, and whoever says that the union is in terms of appearance, like the appearance of the writing of a ring if it falls on clay or wax, or like the appearance of the image of a human being in a mirror, his statement does not prove true union, but rather proves heterogeneity. The hypostasis of the Son is other than Christ, peace be upon him. Rather, what is necessary is that the effect of the attribute of the hypostasis be more apparent in him

Of its appearance in other places, just as the appearance of the effect of the sun’s rays in Badakhshan on some of the stones from which known gems are generated is greater than its effect on stones that are not those stones, and yes what was said:
Impossible is not equal to impossible * And what is said in truth is not said
False thought and false talk * started from them and originated from imagination
God Almighty, what they said is blasphemy * and sin in the consequences is not said.

(Seventh Proof) The Protestant sect responds to the Catholic sect regarding the transformation of bread into Christ in the Lord’s Supper with the testimony of sense, and mocks it. This response and mockery also goes back to them, because the one who saw Christ saw only one person of Him, a human being. Denying the truest of senses, which is sight, opens the door to sophistry regarding necessities, so saying it is as invalid as saying it is impossible, and the ignorant Christians from any of the Trinitarian sects have gone astray in this doctrine. A clear error, and they do not distinguish between the theological and human essence as their scholars apparently distinguish. Rather, they believe in the divinity of Christ, peace be upon him, considering the human essence, and they are greatly mistaken.

It was reported that three people converted to Christianity and some priests taught them the necessary doctrines, especially the doctrine of the Trinity, and they were in his service, so a loved one of this priest came and asked him who had converted to Christianity? He said: Three people became Christians. He asked this lover: Did they learn any of the necessary doctrines? He said: Yes. He asked one of them to see his lover and asked him about the doctrine of the Trinity. He said: You taught me that the gods are three, one of whom is in heaven, the second was born from the womb of the Virgin Mary, and the third was descended in the form of a dove on the second god after he became thirty years old. The priest became angry and expelled him, and said: This is unknown. Then he asked the other of them and asked him, and he said: You taught me that the gods were three.

And one of them was crucified, so the rest were two gods. The priest also became angry with him and expelled him. Then he asked for the third, and he was intelligent compared to the first two and keen to memorize the doctrines. He asked him and said: Oh, my lord, you have memorized what you taught me well, and I fully understood, thanks to the Lord Christ, that one is three and three are one. One of them was crucified and died, so all died for the sake of the union. There is no god now, otherwise the union must be denied. (I say) There is no negligence on the part of those responsible, for this doctrine is misleading.

In it, the ignorant people are like this, and their scholars are confused, and they admit that we believe but do not understand, and they are unable to depict and explain it, and for this reason Al-Fakhr Al-Razi said in his interpretation following the interpretation of Surat An-Nisa: “And know that the doctrine of the Christians is very unknown.” Then he said: “We do not see a doctrine in this world that is more weak and more distant from reason than the doctrine of the Christians.” And he said in the interpretation of Surat Al-Ma’idah: “And we do not see in this world a speech more corrupt and more apparent of invalidity than the doctrine of the Christians.” So if you know With definitive rational proofs that true trinity is impossible in the essence of God, if a Christian saying is found to indicate, apparently, the trinity, it must be interpreted, because each one of us is not devoid of the significance of the evidence and the significance of the statement.
Either we leave them, or we give priority to transmission over reason, or we give priority to reason over transmission,

The first is absolutely invalid, and it is not necessary for the one thing to be impossible and not impossible in the same matter. The second is also impossible, otherwise the two extremes must be removed. The third is also not permissible because the mind is the origin of transmission. The proof of transmission depends on the existence of the maker, his knowledge, and his ability, and his being sent to the messengers, and proving it with rational evidence. An insult to the mind is an insult to reason and transmission together. So what remains is for us to be certain of the validity of reason and work with the interpretation of transmission, and interpretation according to the People of the Book is neither rare nor small for what I learned in the third matter from the introduction. They interpret the non-limiting verses that indicate the physicality and form of God for the sake of the two verses whose content is consistent with the rational proof. Likewise, they interpret the many non-limiting verses that indicate the place of God Almighty for the sake of the few verses that agree with the proof. I also knew in the fourth and fifth matter something like it explained, but what is surprising about the rational Catholics and those who followed them is that they sometimes invalidate the ruling of both sense and reason, and they rule that the bread and wine that occurred between... Our eyes, after a period of more than one thousand and eight hundred years since the ascension of Christ, peace be upon him, are transformed in the Lord’s Supper into his true flesh and blood, and they worship them and prostrate to them, and at times they nullify the rule of reason and intuition and throw away the rational proofs behind their backs, and they say:

True Trinitarianism and true monotheism can be combined in one personal matter at one time from one perspective, and what is surprising about the Protestant sect is that they differed from them in the first matter rather than the second. If acting on the apparent meaning of the transmission was necessary, even if it contradicted sense and reason, then it is fair that the Catholic sect is better than their sect because they went to extremes in obeying the apparent meaning of the words of Christ, peace be upon him, until they acknowledged the worship of that which conflicts with sense and intuition, and just as the people of the Trinitarianism

They exaggerate about Christ, peace be upon him, and bring him to the rank of divinity. They also exaggerate about him and his fathers, and they believe that he was cursed, and after he died, he descended into Hell and resided there for three days, as you will know, and that David and Solomon, peace be upon them, as well as the other fathers of Christ, peace be upon him, were among the children of Farez, whom Tamara gave birth to through adultery from Judah, and that David, peace be upon him, committed adultery with the wife of Uriah, and that Solomon, peace be upon them, apostatized at the end of his life, as you know.

He was a Christian scholar, and he had acquired some Islamic sciences as well. He translated the glorious Qur’an in his own language and its translation was accepted by Christians. He advised his people on some matters, and he copied his will from his printed translation in the year 1836 AD: The first: “Do not impose any coercion on the part of Muslims, and the second: Do not teach them matters that are contrary to reason, because they are not fools. We can overcome them in these matters, such as worshiping idols and the Lord’s Supper, because they stumble over many of these matters.”
