Issues, and every church that has these issues is not able to attract them to itself.” So look at how he commanded and demonstrated that the likes of idol worship and the issue of the Lord’s Supper are contrary to fair reason. The people of these issues are definitely polytheists, whom God has guided to the straight path.

sections.heading: Chapter Two: On invalidating the Trinity through the sayings of Christ, peace be upon him
content: [Chapter Two: On invalidating the Trinity through the sayings of Christ, peace be upon him.]

In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful (the first statement): In the third verse of the seventeenth chapter of the Gospel of John, Jesus, peace be upon him, said in God’s speech thus: (And this is eternal life, that they know you, the only true God, and Jesus Christ whom you have sent.) So Jesus, peace be upon him, explained that eternal life means that people know that God is one true and that Jesus, peace be upon him, is His Messenger. And what he said is eternal life

To know that Yourself is three distinct persons with true excellence, and that Jesus is a human being and a God, or that Jesus is an anthropomorphic God, and since this statement was in God’s speech in supplication, there is no possibility here for fear of the Jews. If the belief in the Trinity were the source of salvation, it would be clear. And since it has been proven that eternal life is the belief in the true monotheism of God and the belief in the message of Christ, the opposite of them is eternal death and clear error, and true monotheism is against the true Trinity, as I explained in detail in the chapter. First, Christ being a messenger is the opposite of being a god, because the difference between the messenger and the sent is necessary, and this eternal life exists among the people of Islam thanks to God. As for others, the Magians and polytheists of India and China are deprived of it due to the absence of both beliefs in them, and the Christians of the Trinitarians are deprived of it due to the absence of the first belief, and all Jews are deprived of it due to the absence of the second belief.

(The second saying): In the twelfth chapter of the Gospel of Mark, this is how 28: (Then one of the scribes came and heard them discussing, and when he saw that he had answered them well, he asked him: Which commandment is the first of all?) 29: (Then Jesus answered him, “The first of all commandments: Hear, O Israel, the Lord our God is one Lord. [30]: And you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, and with all your soul, and with all your mind, and with all your strength. This is the first commandment [31].

And the second like it is, “Love your neighbor as yourself. There is no other commandment greater than these [32].” And the scribe said to him, “Well, Master, you have truly said, ‘For (that is, God) is one, and there is no other besides Him.’” 33 “And to love Him with all the heart, and with all the understanding, and with all the soul, and with all strength, and to love one’s neighbor as oneself is better than all burnt offerings and sacrifices.” 34 (And when Jesus saw that he answered wisely, he said to him, “You are not far from the kingdom of God.”) And in the twenty-second chapter of the Gospel of Matthew, in his saying, peace be upon him, after explaining the two aforementioned rulings, thus: (On these two commandments depend the law and the prophets). He knew that the first commandment, which is declared in the Torah and in all the books of the prophets, and it is the truth and is the reason for the nearness of the kingdom, is to believe that God is one and there is no god other than Him. If the belief in the Trinity were the source of salvation, it would have been made clear in the Torah and all the books of the prophets because it is the first of the commandments, and Jesus, peace be upon him, would have said: The first of the commandments is that the Lord is one and has three excellent persons with true distinction, but it was not explicitly stated in any of the books of the prophets, and Jesus, peace be upon him, did not say so, so he was not the focus of salvation.

It has been proven that its focus is the belief of true monotheism, not the belief of the Trinity, and the Trinitarians’ obsession with deducing it from some of the books of the prophets is not valid for the dissenter, because this deduction is very hidden and rejected by contrast with the text. The goal of the dissenter is that the belief of the Trinity, if it had any bearing on salvation, would have been clearly explained by the Israeli prophets.

Clearly, as they explained monotheism in the fourth chapter of the Book of Exceptions - 35 (so that you may know that the Lord is God and there is no other) 39 (so know today and accept with your heart that the Lord is God in the heaven above and on the earth below and there is no other). And in the sixth chapter of the aforementioned book, 4 (Hear, O Israel, the Lord is our God, for He is one Lord) 5 (Love the Lord your God with all your heart, and with all your soul, and with all your strength) and in the forty-fifth chapter of the book of Isaiah 5 (I am the Lord, and there is no other, and there is no god beside me. I have strengthened you, and you have not known me) 6 (So that those who are from the rising of the sun and those from the west may know that there is none other than me. I am the Lord, and there is no other). It is necessary for the people of the East and West to know that there is no god but God alone, not to know that God is the third of three. And in the ninth verse of the forty-sixth chapter of the book of Isaiah 2 (I am God, and there is no god other than Me, and I have no likeness).

(Warning) The author of the Arabic translation printed in 1811 AD distorted the words of Christ, peace be upon him, by replacing the first-person pronoun with the directive pronoun, and translated it as follows: (The Lord your God is one God). The greater intended distortion was lost because the first-person pronoun here indicates that Jesus is not a Lord, but rather a servant to be loved, unlike the directive pronoun, and it appears that this distortion is intentional.

(The third statement) In the thirty-second verse of the thirteenth chapter of the Gospel of Mark, Christ, peace be upon him, said thus: (But as for that day and that hour, no one knows, neither the angels in heaven, nor the Son, except the Father.) This statement calls for the invalidity of the Trinity because Christ, peace be upon him, assigned knowledge of the resurrection to God and denied Himself as He denied the other servants of God, and equated Himself with them in this. This is not possible in the form of His being God, especially if we note that the Word and the Son’s hypostasis are expressions of God knew, and we imposed their union with Christ, and we took this union according to the doctrine of those who advocated substitution or the doctrine of the Jacobites who advocated inversion, for it requires that the matter be the opposite, and nothing less than that the son knows as the father knows, and since knowledge is not an attribute of the body, it does not apply to their well-known excuse that he denied himself on the basis of his corporeality, so it appeared that he is not a god, neither on account of corporeality nor on account of anything else.

(The fourth statement): In the twentieth chapter of the Gospel of Matthew, like this: 20 (The mother of my son Zaydi came up to him with her two sons and bowed down and asked him for something) 21 (And he said to her, “What do you want?” She said to him, “Tell these two sons of mine to sit, one on your right and the other on your left, in your kingdom.” 22 (And Jesus answered) etc. 23 (Sitting on my right and on my left is not mine to give except to those who are more just than my father.) He ended with a summary, so Jesus, peace be upon him, denied himself here. Power and attributed it to God, just as he denied knowledge of the Hour and attributed it to God, and if he were a god, this would not be true.

(The fifth statement): In the nineteenth chapter of the Gospel of Matthew, like this: 16 (And if someone came forward and said to him, “O good teacher, what good thing should I do that I may have eternal life?” 17 (And he said to him, “Why do you call me good? No one is good but one, and He is God.”) This saying takes away the principle of the Trinity, and he did not accept in humility to be called the word “good” also. If he were a god, his statement would not have had meaning, and he would have had to make it clear that there is no good but the Father, I, and the Holy Spirit. He did not delay the statement until the time of need, and if he did not agree to With his good saying, how can he be satisfied with the sayings of the people of the Trinity that they utter during their times of prayer (O our Lord and our God Jesus, do not waste whom You have created with your hand)? Far be it from him to be satisfied with them.

(The sixth statement): In the twenty-seventh chapter of the Gospel of Matthew, this is how: 46 (And about the ninth hour Jesus cried out with a loud voice, saying, Eli, Eli, lama sabachthani, that is, my God, my God, why have you forsaken me?) 50 (Then Jesus cried out again with a loud voice and gave up his spirit.) And in the forty-sixth verse of the twenty-third chapter of the Gospel of Luke, it is as follows: (And Jesus called out with a loud voice and said, “Father, into your hands I commit my spirit.”) This [p.

He said, O Father, into your hand I commit my spirit, and incapacity and death will not be withheld from it.. The twenty-eighth verse of the fortieth chapter of the Book of Isaiah is thus: (Have I not known or heard of an eternal God? The Lord, who created the ends of the earth, will not grow weak or weary, and his wisdom will not be tested.) The sixth verse of the forty-fourth chapter of the aforementioned book is thus: (Thus says the Lord, the King of Israel and his Redeemer, the Lord of hosts: I am the first and I am the last, and there is no god besides me.) The tenth verse of the tenth chapter of the Book of Arsiah is thus: (But the Lord is a true God, a living God and an eternal King) etc. And in the twelfth verse of the first chapter of the Book of Huqoq, it is as follows: (O Lord, my holy God, and do not die.) And in the seventeenth verse of the first chapter of the first letter to Timothy, it says: (And the King of the ages, who is immortal, will not see the wise God alone.) So how can He who is an eternal God, innocent of weakness and fatigue, living, holy, and undying, and there is no god other than Him, become powerless and die? Would a helpless mortal be a God? No, no. Rather, the true God is the one whom Jesus, peace be upon him, was calling for help at this time, according to their claim. The surprising thing is that they are not satisfied with the death of God, but they believe that after He died, He also entered Hell.
Jawad Ibn Sabat transferred this doctrine from the prayer book printed in the year 1506 as follows: (Just as Christ died for us and was buried, so we must believe that he entered Hell.) End quote.

(And Philip Quadnolls) The monk wrote, in response to the letter of Ahmad al-Sharif Ibn Zain al-Abidin al-Isfahani, a book in the Arabic language that he called Philip’s Fictions. This book was printed in the year 1669 in the Great Roman City in Basluqit. An old copy of this book was obtained for me by way of bare land from an English bookstore in the town of Dehli. The hidden monk wrote in his aforementioned book thus: (He who suffered for our salvation and descended into hell, and then on the third day rose from the dead.) End quote. There is a statement in Brierbok in explaining the doctrine of Athanish that Christians believe in

(Does) exist and it means hell. Jawad bin Sabat said that the priest Martiros told me in directing this doctrine that when Christ accepted the human body, he must bear all the human symptoms, so he entered Hell and was also tortured, and when he came out of Hell, everyone who had been tortured in it before he entered was taken out of it.

So I asked him whether there is any textual evidence for this doctrine. He said that it does not need evidence. A Christian man from the people of that forum said in a funny way that the father was hard-hearted, otherwise he would not have left the son in Hell. The priest became angry and expelled him from the forum. This man came to me and converted to Islam, but he took a covenant from me not to reveal his state of conversion as long as he lived. Joseph and Wolf entered the town of Lucknow in the year 1248 AH and 1833 AD. He was one of the famous priests and he claimed inspiration for himself and he claimed that Christ would come down. It will be in the year 1847 AD, and the debate took place between him and the Shiite mujtahid, writing and reporting on this topic. The Shiite mujtahid asked him about this doctrine as well, and he said, yes, Christ entered hell and was tortured, but

There is nothing wrong with him because this entry was for the salvation of his nation, and some of their groups believe it to be the most horrific situation, Bell said in his history in a statement by the Marcioni group. This group believed that after Jesus, peace be upon him, died, he entered Hell and saved the souls of Cain and the people of Sodom because they had come to him and were disobedient to the God who created evil. He kept the souls of Abel, Noah, Abraham, and the other righteous people of the ancients in Hell because they disobeyed the first group. (This group believed that the Creator of the world was not limited to the God who sent Jesus, and therefore it did not accept that the books of the Old Testament were inspirational.) End quote.
The doctrine of this sect included matters:
1- All souls, whether they were the souls of the prophets, the righteous, or the wretched, were tormented in Hell before the entry of Jesus, peace be upon him.
2- That Jesus, peace be upon him, entered Hell.
3- Jesus, peace be upon him, saved the souls of the wretched from torment and preserved the souls of the prophets and the righteous in it.
4- These righteous people contradict Jesus, while the wretched people agree with him.

5- The creator of the world is two gods, the creator of good and the creator of evil, and Jesus, peace be upon him, is the messenger of the first and the other famous prophets are messengers of the second.
6-The books of the Old Testament are not inspired.

The author of Mizan al-Haqq said in his book called Solution to the Problem in the Answer to Unveiling the Curtains thus: (The truth is that it is found in the Christian belief that Christ entered Hell and rose on the third day and ascended to heaven, but what is meant here by Hell is a house, which is a place between Hell and the original ark. The meaning is that he entered a house so that its people could see his majesty and warn them that I am the possessor of life and that I was given the atonement for sin through death on the Crusader and I made Satan and Hell defeated and the believers as non-existent.) End quote. Summary.

(I say) Firstly: It is proven from the apparent meaning of the Book of Prayer and the words of Philip Quadlonus, and it is explicitly proven from the statement of Martirus and Joseph Wolf, and from the doctrine of Ethany Sesh, that Hell is in its meaning, and he also admitted that this is found in the doctrine. Then first, his interpretation without evidence is not acceptable, and he must prove from his books that what is between Hell and the original ark is a place called Haus. Then it is proven from these books that Christ’s entry into Hell was for the sake of the aforementioned clarification and warning that it is not The celestial bodies existed among the sages of Europe, and recent Protestant scholars followed them in this opinion, so how is this guidance correct according to their claim?

(Then I say) Secondly: This abode is the place of pleasure and reward or the place of tribulations and punishment. If it is the first, then there is no need to warn its people because before this they were in a happy and contented life. If it is the second, then there is no benefit in interpretation because the Hell of souls is only the place of their torment.

(Then I say) Thirdly: The fact that death on the Crusader is an atonement for sin is certainly unreasonable because what is meant by this sin, according to their claim, is the original sin that came from Adam, peace be upon him, not the sin that comes from his children, and it is not permissible for his children to be punished for this original sin because the children are not held accountable for the sins of the fathers, nor vice versa. Rather, it is contrary to justice.. The twentieth verse of the eighteenth chapter of the Book of Ezekiel is thus: (The soul that sins will die, and the son will not bear the sin of the father, and the father will not bear it. The sin of the son and the justice of the just will be upon him, and the hypocrisy of the hypocrite will be upon him.)

(Then I say) Fourth: What is the meaning of making Satan defeated by death because, according to the rule of their Gospel, he is bound by eternal restrictions before the birth of Jesus, peace be upon him? The sixth verse of the Epistle of Judea is thus: (And the angels who did not keep their government, but forsook their dwelling place, are kept under eternal chains under darkness until the judgment of the great day.) Then what is astonishing is that they are not satisfied with the death of their alleged god and his entry into hell, but rather they add to it that he has also become cursed, and God forbid, and his curse is accepted by Christians, and the author of the Mizan al-Haqq also accepts it with complete satisfaction of thought and declares it in his books, and their saint, Paul, also declared it. The thirteenth verse of the third chapter of his letter to the Galatians is thus: (Christ has redeemed us from the curse of the law, having become a curse for us. For it is written, “Cursed is everyone who hangs on a tree.”) And in our view, using such a word is very heinous. Indeed, cursing God is obligatory by stoning according to the Torah, and one person was stoned for this error during the time of Moses, peace be upon him, as

It is stated in the twenty-fourth chapter of the Book of News. Indeed, cursing one’s parents is also obligatory to kill, in addition to cursing God, as stated in the twentieth chapter of the aforementioned book.

(Seventh saying): In the seventeenth verse of the twentieth chapter of the Gospel of John, Christ, peace be upon him, said in a speech to Mary Magdalene like this: (Do not touch me, for I have not yet ascended to my Father, but go to my brothers and tell them, I am ascending to my Father and your Father, and my God and your God.) So he equated himself with the people in this saying (My Father and your Father and my God and your God) so that they do not speak falsehood against him and say that he is a god or the son of a god, just as his disciples are servants of God. They are not the sons of God in reality, but rather in a metaphorical sense. Likewise, he is the servant of God and not the son of God in reality. And since this statement was made after Jesus, peace be upon him, rose from the dead, as they claim, shortly before the Ascension, it is proven that he was declaring that I am the servant of God until the time of Ascension, and this saying matches what God spoke about in the Glorious Qur’an: {I did not say to them except what you commanded me to do: Worship God, my Lord and your Lord}.

(The eighth statement): In the twenty-eighth verse of the fourteenth chapter of the Gospel of John, Christ, peace be upon him, said thus: (Indeed, my father is greater than I), which also includes a denial of his divinity, because God is nothing like him, let alone being greater than him.

(Ninth statement): In the twenty-fourth verse of the fourteenth chapter of the Gospel of John, Christ, peace be upon him, said thus: (The words that you hear are not mine, but those of the Father who sent me). It also contains a statement of the message and that the words that you hear are revelation from God.

(The tenth statement): In the twenty-third chapter of the Gospel of Matthew, Christ, peace be upon him, said in a speech to his disciples like this: 9 (And do not call you a father on earth, for there is one father who is in heaven) 10 (And do not call you teachers, for your teacher is one, the Christ). Here he also stated (that God is one, and I am your teacher).

(The eleventh saying): In the twenty-sixth chapter of the Gospel of Matthew, this is the following: 36 (Then Jesus came with them to a place called Gesemane, and said to the disciples, “Sit here while I go and pray there.” 37 (Then he took with him Peter and my son Zaidi and began to be sad and distressed.) 38 (And he said to them, “My soul is very sad, even to death. Stay here and watch with me.”) 39 (Then he went forward a little and fell on his face and was praying. Saying, “O My Father, if it is possible, let this cup pass from me, not as I will, but as You will.” 40 (Then he came to the disciples, etc.) 42 (And he went away a second time and prayed, saying, “O My Father, if it is not that this cup should pass from me, that I should not drink it, let your will be done.”) 43 (Then he came, etc.) 44 (So he left them and went away again and prayed a third time, saying the same words.) His sayings and conditions included in these expressions indicate his servitude. He denied his divinity. Does the god become sad, depressed, die, pray to another god, and pray with utmost supplication?

No, I swear. When His Noble Majesty came into the world and was incarnated to save the world with His noble blood from the torment of hell, what is the meaning of sadness and depression, and what is the meaning of supplication: If possible, let this cup pass from me.

(The twelfth statement): It was his honorable habit that when he expressed himself, he would often express himself as the Son of Man, as is well known to the observer of this popularized Gospel as well: For example, in verse 20, chapter 8 and 6, chapter 9, 13, and 27, chapter 16, 9, 12, and 22, chapter 17 and 11, chapter 18 and 28, chapter 19, 18, and 28, chapter 20 and 27, chapter 24, 24, 45, and 64, chapter 26 of The Gospel of Matthew, and so on in others, and it appears that the Son of Man is only a human.

sections.heading: Chapter Three: On invalidating the transmissional evidence of the divinity of Christ
content: [Chapter Three: On invalidating the transmissional evidence of the divinity of Christ]

You learned in the fifth matter of the introduction that John’s words are full of metaphors. You rarely find a paragraph that does not need interpretation. You learned in the sixth matter that summary is found in many of the sayings of Jesus, peace be upon him, such that his contemporaries and disciples did not understand them in many cases unless he interpreted them himself. You learned in the twelfth matter that Jesus, peace be upon him, explained his divinity to ascension with a statement in which no doubt remains, and from which this meaning is clearly understood. The sayings that Christians cling to are often summaries copied from the Gospel of John. And in three sections

-Some of them do not indicate, according to their true meanings, what they intended, so deducing divinity from them is merely their claim, and this deduction and claim are neither valid nor permissible in contrast to the definitive rational proofs and the Isawiya texts, as I have known in the two aforementioned chapters.
-And some of them are sayings whose interpretation can be understood from other Christian sayings and from some places in the Bible, in which also their opinion is not taken into consideration.

Some of them are statements that must be interpreted according to them as well. If interpretation is required, then we say that this interpretation must be such that it does not contradict the proofs and texts, and how can they be interpreted?
that?! There is no need to quote the whole thing, but rather I will quote most of it so that the observer will be clear about their reasoning and measure the rest against it.
Evidence (first): From applying the word “Son of God” to Christ, peace be upon him: I say this evidence is extremely weak in two ways:

Firstly, because this term is contradicted by the term “Son of Man” as you know, and by the term “Ibn David”, it must be applied in such a way that it does not prove to be contrary to rational proofs and there is no impossibility from it. Secondly, because it is not correct for the term “son” to be in its true meaning, because its true meaning, according to the language of the people of the world, is “one who is born from the sperm of the parents,” and this is impossible here. Therefore, it is necessary to adopt the appropriate metaphorical meaning regarding Christ, and it is known from the Bible that this term in his right means the good. Verse thirty-nine of the fifteenth chapter of the Gospel of Mark is as follows: (And when the centurion standing opposite him saw that he had thus declared and given up the spirit, he said, “Truly this man was the Son of God.”) Luke quoted the commander’s words in the forty-seventh verse.

From the twenty-third chapter of his Gospel, thus: (Indeed, this man was righteous). In the Gospel of Mark, the word “Son of God” is used, and in the Gospel of Luke, he replaced it with the word “righteous,” and such a word was used in relation to the righteous other than Christ as well. Likewise, the parable of the son of Satan was used against the righteous in the fifth chapter of the Gospel of Matthew, thus: (And) (Blessed are the peacemakers, for they will be called the sons of God.) 44 (But I say to you, love your enemies, bless your eyes, do good to those who hate you, and pray. For the sake of those who take you captives) 54 (so that you may be the sons of your Father who is in the heavens). Then Jesus, peace be upon him, used the term “sons of God” to those who make peace and reconciliation, to those who do the aforementioned works, and to God the term “father” in relation to them.

And in the eighth chapter of the Gospel of John, in the conversation that took place between the Jews and Christ, it is as follows: 41 (You are doing the works of your father. They said to him, “We were not born of fornication. We have one father, which is God.” 42 (And Jesus said to them, “If God were your Father, you would love me.”) etc. 44 (You are of a father who is the devil, and you want to do the desires of your father. He was a murderer from the beginning and did not abide in the truth, because there is no truth in him. When he speaks a lie, he speaks from his own because he is a lie.) And the father of lies. The Jews claimed that we have one father, which is God. Christ, peace be upon him, said, “No, your father is Satan.” It is apparent that God and Satan are not their fathers in the real sense, so the metaphorical meaning must be taken. The purpose of the Jews is that we are righteous and obedient to the command of God, and the purpose of Christ, peace be upon him, is that you are not like that, but rather you are bad and obedient to Satan.

And in the third chapter of the First Epistle to John, this is the following: 9 (Everyone who is born of God does not commit sin, because his seed remains in him and he cannot sin because he is born of God) 10 (By this the children of God are evident, and the children of the devil) etc. And in the seventh verse of the fourth chapter of the aforementioned epistle: (And everyone who loves is born of God) and in the fifth chapter of the aforementioned epistle: (Everyone who believes that Jesus is the Christ has been born of God, and everyone who loves the father loves the child born of him) 2 (By this we know that we love the children of him.) God, if we love God and keep His commandments) and the fourteenth verse of the eighth chapter of the Epistle to the Romans is thus: (For all who are led by the Spirit of God are the sons of God) and in the second chapter of Paul’s Epistle to the Philippians thus: 14 (Do everything without murmuring or disputing) 15 (So that you may be blameless and simple, children of God without blemish). The evidence of these sayings on what I said is not hidden, and if the use of the word God and its likeness is not understood as divinity as

I learned in the fourth matter of the introduction, how to understand the word “Son of God” and its like, especially if we notice the frequent occurrence of the metaphor in the books of the Old and New Testaments, as I learned in the introduction, especially if we notice that the use of father and son in the books of the two Testaments came in non-exclusive places, and some of them were quoted by way of example:

-[1] Luke said in the third chapter of his Gospel in explaining the lineage of Christ, peace be upon him, that he is the son of Joseph and Adam, the son of God. It appears that Adam, peace be upon him, was not

He is a son of God in the true sense and is not a god, but when he was born without parents, he was attributed to God. By God, Luke did well here because when Christ, peace be upon him, was only born without a father, he attributed it to Joseph the carpenter, and when Adam, peace be upon him, was born without parents, he attributed it to God.

-[2] In the fourth chapter of the Book of Exodus, God says like this: 22 (And you say to him, “This is what the Lord says, ‘My son, my firstborn Israel.’) 33 (And I said to him, ‘Let my son go, that he may worship me. But if you refuse to let him go, behold, I will kill your son, your firstborn son.’) So he called Israel the Son of God in both places, and even called him the firstborn son.

- [3] In the eighty-eighth Psalms, David, peace be upon him, said in his speech to God as follows: 19 (Then I spoke to your prophet by revelation and said, “I have put help on the strong and have exalted a chosen one among my people.”) 20 (I found David my servant, and I anointed him with my holy oil) 26 (He calls me, “You are my Father and my God and the Supporter of my salvation.”) 27 (And I also make him a firstborn, higher than all the kings of the earth.) So he gave God the word “Father” and David the word “Father.” The strong one
The Elect, the Messiah, the firstborn Son of God, and higher than all the kings of the earth.

- [4] The ninth verse of the thirty-first chapter of the Book of Arsa says God says thus: (I have become the father of Israel, and Ephrem is my firstborn.) So Ephrem was given the term the firstborn son of God. If using such terms meant divinity, then Israel, David, and Ephrem would be entitled to divinity, because the firstborn son is more deserving of honor than others according to the previous laws and according to common marriage as well. And if they said that the term only son was applied to Jesus, peace be upon him, we would say that the only son is not It could be in its meaning because God confirmed that he had many brothers and said that the three of them were the firstborn son. Rather, he must be in the figurative sense like a son.

-[5] In the seventh chapter of the Second Book of Samuel, God Almighty said regarding Solomon thus: (And I will be his father, and he shall be my son.) If using this word was a reason for divinity, Solomon, peace be upon him, would have been more deserving of Christ, peace be upon him, because he preceded him and was one of the fathers of Christ, peace be upon him.
-[6] In the first verse of Chapter Fourteen and the nineteenth verse of Chapter Thirty-two of the Book of Exceptions, and the second verse of Chapter One and the first verse

From the thirtieth chapter, the eighth verse of the sixty-third chapter of the Book of Isaiah, and the tenth verse of the first chapter of the Book of Hosea, the designation of the sons of God came to all the children of Israel.

-[7] In the sixteenth verse of the sixty-third chapter of the Book of Isaiah, Isaiah’s statement in God’s speech is thus: (For you are our father, and Abraham did not know us, and Israel is our ignorance. You, O Lord, are our father, so save us from eternity in your name). The eighth verse of the sixty-fourth chapter of the aforementioned book is thus: (And now, O Lord, you are our father), etc. So Isaiah, peace be upon him, declared in his right and in the right of other children of Israel: that God is our father.
-[8] The seventh verse of the thirty-eighth chapter of the Book of Job is thus: (If all the morning stars praise me and all the children of God rejoice).

-[9] You knew at the beginning of the answer that the sons of God were applied to the righteous, to the believers in Christ, to those who love, to those who are obedient to God’s command, and to those who do good deeds.
-[10] The fifth verse of the sixty-seventh Psalms is like this: (Father of orphans and Judge of widows, God is in His holy place). So he called God the father of orphans.

-[11] In the sixth chapter of the Book of Creation, this is how 2: (Then the sons of God saw the daughters of men that they were beautiful, and took to themselves wives of all they chose) 4: (And as for the giants in those days, they were on the earth; for after the sons of God had come in unto the daughters of men, and they had given birth, these are powerful of old, and famous.)

What is meant by the sons of God is the sons of the nobles and the daughters of the people are the daughters of the common people. Therefore, the translator of the Arabic translation printed in 1811 AD translated the first verse as follows: (The sons of the nobles saw the goodness of the daughters of the common people and took them as wives.) So the sons of God were used to refer to the sons of the nobles in general, and it is understood from this that God’s use of the nobles was also correct.
-[12] In many places in the Bible, the word “your father” was used to refer to God in the speech of the disciples and others.

-[13] The word son and father may be added to something that has a certain occasion, in its true meaning, such as calling the father of lies to Satan, as you know, and like calling the sons of Hell and the sons of Jerusalem to the Jews in the words of Christ, peace be upon him, in the twenty-third chapter of the Gospel of Matthew. The sons of eternity were called the people of this world, and the sons of God and the sons of the resurrection were called the people of Paradise, in the words of Christ, peace be upon him, in the twentieth chapter of Luke. In the fifth verse of the fifth chapter of the First Epistle to the Thessalonians, the term “sons of light” and “sons of the day” came
On the Thessalonians.

The second evidence is in the twenty-third verse of the eighth chapter of the Gospel of John, like this: (And he said to them, “You are from below, but I am from above. You are of this world, but I am not of this world”) meaning that I am a god who came down from heaven and was incarnated.

(I say): Since this statement contradicts what is apparent, because Jesus, peace be upon him, was from this world, they gave this interpretation, and it is incorrect in two ways: (First): It contradicts rational proofs and texts. (The second): Jesus, peace be upon him, also said something like this about his disciples in the nineteenth verse of the fifteenth chapter of the Gospel of John, thus: (If you were of the world, the world would love its own, but you are not of the world. Rather, I chose you from the world, and therefore the world hates you.) And in the seventh chapter of the Gospel of John, this is 14: (For they are not of the world, just as I am not of the world) [16] (They are not of the world, just as I am not of the world) and he said regarding his disciples: They are not of the world, and he equated him with them in not being of this world. If this necessitates divinity as they claimed, then it would be necessary for them all to be gods, God forbid. Rather, the correct interpretation is: You are seeking this worldly world, and I am not. Rather, you are seeking the afterlife and the satisfaction of God. This metaphor is common in tongues. It is said to ascetics and righteous people that they are not of this world.

The third evidence: In the thirtieth verse of the tenth chapter of the Gospel of John, this is how: (I and the Father are one) This indicates the union of Christ with God. I say this inference is incorrect in two ways: (First): According to them, Christ, peace be upon him, is also a human being with a rational soul, and he is not united by this consideration. They need an interpretation and say: Just as He is a perfect human being, so He is also a perfect God, so according to the first consideration, He is different, and according to the second consideration, He is united. I knew that this interpretation was false. (And the second): Something like this happened to the Apostles in the seventeenth chapter of the Gospel of John, thus 21: (That they may all be one, just as you, Father, are in me and I in you, so that they also may be one in us, so that the world may believe that you sent me) 22 (And I have given them the glory which you gave me, that they may be one, just as we are one) 33 (I in them and you in me, that they may be perfected into one). So he said that they should all be one, and he said [p. 20] that they should be one just as we are one. And his saying that they are complementary to one indicates their union. In the second statement, he equated his union with God with his union among themselves. It seems that his union with each other is not real, and neither is his union with God. Rather, the truth is that union with God means obeying His rulings and doing good deeds, and in this same union Christ, the disciples, and all people of faith are equal. The difference is based on strength and weakness, so Christ’s union in this sense is stronger and stronger than the union of others. The evidence that the union expresses this meaning is John’s words in the first chapter of his first epistle, which is like this: 5: (And this is the report that we heard from him and we declare to you, that God is light.

And there is no darkness in Him at all. 6 If we say that we have fellowship with Him and walk in darkness, we lie and do not do the truth. 7 But if we walk in the light as He is in the light, we have fellowship with one another.

The sixth and seventh verses in the Persian biographies are like this: 6 (Ikr kunyim ke pawi matahdim wa darzalmat rafta renmayim dor and ghkuyim wa dar rasti ma’am ntammayim). 7 (And akerdur ro shenai rfta ranmayyim jannah oder roshnai mi bashid baikd ikr mutahtahid hastim), so he used in it, instead of the word “communion,” the word union, so he knew that union with God or fellowship with God is an expression of what we said.

The fourth evidence: In the fourteenth chapter of the Gospel of John, this is the following: 9 (He who has seen me has seen the Father, so how can you say, “Show us the Father?” 10 Do you not believe that I am in the Father and the Father is in me? The words that I speak to you I do not speak on my own authority, but the Father residing in me does the works.) So his saying: He who has seen me has seen the Father, and his saying I am in the Father and the Father is in me, and his saying the Father residing in me indicates Christ’s union with God, and this inference is also weak in two aspects: (But The first: Because seeing God in this world is impossible for them, as was known in the fourth matter of the introduction, so they interpret it with knowledge, and knowing Christ with regard to physicality also does not benefit union, so they say that what is meant by knowledge is with regard to divinity, and the solution that occurred in the second and third statement is obligatory for interpretation according to the majority of Trinitarians, so they say that what is meant is inner union. After these interpretations

They say that because He was a perfect human being and a working God. His three statements are correct with the second consideration, and I have repeatedly known that they are false because the interpretation must not contradict the evidence and texts. (As for the second): Because the twentieth verse of the aforementioned chapter is like this: (On that day you will know that I am in my Father and you are in me and I am in you) and you knew in the answer to the third evidence that Christ said regarding the disciples: (I am in them and you are in me) and it is obvious that the adverb of adverb is adverb in the case of adverb. The nineteenth verse of the sixth chapter of the First Epistle to the Corinthians is thus: (Or do you not know that your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit who is in you, which you have from God, and that you are not your own?) And the sixteenth verse of the sixth chapter of the second letter to Corinthians is thus: (And a sign that the temple of God agrees with idols, for you are the temple of the living God) etc.
The sixth verse of the fourth chapter of the Epistle to the Ephesians is thus: (One God and Father of all, who is over all and through all and in you all).

If the solution was a feeling of unity and a confirmation of divinity, then it would be necessary for the disciples, and indeed all the people of Corinthians, as well as all the people of Ephesus, to be gods. Indeed, if the lowest is one of the followers of the highest, then he would be his messenger, his servant, his student, or a close relative of his. The matter attributed to the lowest, such as veneration, contempt, love, etc., is attributed to the highest metaphorically. That is why Christ, peace be upon him, said regarding the disciples: (Whoever accepts you accepts me, and whoever accepts me accepts the One who sent me). It also occurred in the fortieth verse of the tenth chapter of the Gospel of Matthew and said regarding the little boy: (Whoever welcomes this child in my name receives me, and whoever receives me receives the one who sent me) as stated in the verse in the forty-eighth verse of the ninth chapter of the Gospel of Luke. He said regarding the seventy whom he sent two by two into the country (He who hears you hears me, and he who rejects you will reject me, and he who rejects me rejects him who sent me) as stated in the sixteenth verse in the tenth chapter of the Gospel of Luke. And this is what happened with regard to those on the right and those on the left in the twenty-fifth chapter of the Gospel of Matthew. For this reason, God said through Jeremiah: (He ate me up, swallowed me up, and the king of Babylon made me as an empty vessel. He filled his belly with my ease and cast me out) as stated in Chapter fifty-one of the Book of Jeremiah

A similar matter occurred in the Glorious Qur’an as well: “Indeed, those who pledge allegiance to you only pledge allegiance to God; the hand of God is above their hands.” Mawlana Al-Ma'awani, may his secret be sanctified, said in his Mathnawi:
Kartu khawahi hamanshiti bakhda * ronshin toder presence olia

Knowing Christ in this regard is in the same position as knowing God, and as for the abiding of others in God or the abiding of God in him, as well as the abiding of others in Christ or the abiding of Christ in him, it is an expression of obedience to their command. In the third chapter of the First Epistle to John, it is as follows: (Whoever keeps His commandments abides in Him and He in Him. And by this we know that He abides in us by the Spirit that He gave us).

They may cling to his divinity in some of his cases, and sometimes they infer that he was born without a father, and this inference is very weak, because the entire world is an event, and six thousand years have passed since its occurrence to this time, according to their claim. And every creature, from the sky, the earth, inanimate objects, plants, animals, and Adam, was created for them in one week. All animals are created without a father and a mother. Each of these shares with Christ in being a creature without a father, and surpasses him in being without a mother. Types of insects are born every year in the rainy season without a father and a mother. So how can this matter be a reason for divinity? (If we look at the type of human being, Adam, peace be upon him, is superior to him, and likewise Melchite Zadok the priest, who is a contemporary of Abraham, peace be upon him). In the third verse of the seventh chapter of the Hebrew Epistle, it is stated as follows: (Without a father, without a mother, without a lineage, with no beginning of days and no end of life) He surpasses Christ in being without a mother and in the fact that he has no beginning, and they sometimes cite his miracles as evidence, and this is also weak because one of his greatest miracles is reviving the dead, regardless of his reliability, and that it is understood from this well-known Gospel that it is false.

I say that Jesus, peace be upon him, according to this Gospel, only three people were revived until the time of the crucifixion, as I knew in the first chapter. Ezekiel, peace be upon him, revived thousands as stated in the thirty-seventh chapter of his book, so he is more worthy of being a god. Elijah, peace be upon him, revived a dead person as stated in the seventeenth chapter of the First Book of Kings. Elisha, peace be upon him, also revived a dead person as stated in the fourth chapter of the Second Book of Kings. This miracle occurred after Elisha. His death, that a dead person was thrown into his grave and he was revived, God willing, as stated in the thirteenth chapter of the aforementioned book, and the leper was cured of his leprosy, as stated in the fifth chapter of the aforementioned book. They may cling to some verses of the Old Testament books and some sayings
The disciples.

I have quoted these assertions, along with their answers, in the book Removing Illusions, so whoever wants to learn about them should refer to it. I left out mentioning them in this book because the primary assertions are very weak, and regardless of the weakness, divinity cannot be proven from them, according to their claim either, unless it is acknowledged that Christ is a perfect man and a perfect God. This interpretation is false, as I have repeatedly known, and the secondary assertions are the same as adherences to the Christian situations in most cases, so they are treated the same as Christ’s statements from the three instances, as I knew at the beginning of this chapter. If we assume that some of their statements stipulate this matter, then it is assumed that it is according to their ijtihad. I learned in the first chapter that all of their writings were not inspired, and that errors, differences, and contradictions had certainly occurred from them, and the statement of their saint, Paul, is not accepted by us because it is not a dialogue and is not obligatory for us to accept. Rather, we do not accept its reliability. And know, God Almighty, I ask you, I only quoted the Christian sayings and interpreted them in order to fulfill the obligation and prove that their adherence to them is weak. Likewise, what I said about the sayings of the disciples is based on the assumption that they are their sayings, and it is not proven in our view that they are the sayings of Christ, peace be upon him, and the disciples because of the loss of the chain of transmission of these books, as I knew in the first chapter, and because of the distortion in them in general and in this issue in particular, as I learned in the second chapter that their custom in such matters was like that, and my belief is that Christ The disciples were absolutely innocent of this infidel doctrine, and I bear witness that there is no god but God, that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger, that Jesus is the servant of God and His Messenger, and that the disciples are messengers of the Messenger of God.

A debate occurred between Imam Al-Hammam Al-Fakhr Al-Razi, may God have mercy on him, and some priests in Khwarezm, and since its narration was not without benefit, I narrate it: He said, sanctified his secret, in the second volume of his interpretation of Surat Al-Imran, under the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: {And whoever disputes with you concerning it after the knowledge that has come to you} the verse. It happened that when I was in Khwarazm, I was told that a Christian had come claiming to investigate and delve into their doctrine, so I went to him and we started talking, and he said to me, “What is the evidence for the prophethood of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace?” So I said to him: Just as the appearance of the supernatural was transmitted to us at the hands of Moses, Jesus, and other prophets, peace be upon them, the appearance of the supernatural was transmitted to us at the hands of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. If we reject the frequency or accept it, but say that the miracle does not indicate truthfulness, then the prophecy of all the prophets, peace be upon them, is invalid, and if we acknowledge the validity of the frequency and acknowledge its evidence.

The miracle is based on honesty, and since they occurred against Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, the prophethood of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, must be definitely recognized as a necessity. When the evidence is equal, the meaning must be equal.. The Christian said, “I do not say about Jesus, peace be upon him, that he was a prophet, but rather I say that he was a god.” So I told him that speech about prophecy must be preceded by knowledge of God, and this speech that you say is false and is indicated by the fact that God is an entity that must exist for its own sake, and must not be a body, nor biased, nor an accident, and Jesus is an expression of this physical human person who existed after he was non-existent, and was killed after he was alive, as you say, and he was a child first, then he became an adult, then he became a young man. He was eating, drinking, talking, sleeping and waking up. It has been decided intuitively by minds that something new is not old. The needy is not rich, the possible is not obligatory, and the variable is not permanent.

(And the second aspect) in invalidating this article is that you admit that the Jews took him, crucified him, and left him alive on the stake, and they tore out his ribs, and that he was deceitful in escaping from them and hiding from them, and when they treated him in these ways, he showed extreme alarm. If he was a god, or the god was present in him, or a part of the god was present in him, then why did he not push them away from himself, and why did he not destroy them completely, and what need did he have to show fear of them and deceive them in fleeing from them? By God, I am very surprised that it is appropriate for a rational person to say this and believe that it is true. The intuition of the mind is almost a witness to its corruption.

(The third aspect) is that it can either be said that God is this bodily, visible person, or it can be said that God is completely dissolved. Or part of God is dissolved and part of it is in it, and the three sections are invalid: As for the first, because if the God of the world were that body, then when the Jews killed him, that would be a statement that the Jews killed the God of the world, so how could the world remain after that without a God? Then the most humiliated and basest people are the Jews, so the God whom the Jews kill is a God of utmost helplessness. As for the second, which is that God, in its entirety, resides in this body, then it is also corrupt, because if God is neither a body nor an accident, His presence in the body is impossible, and if He is a body, then His presence in another body is a result of the mixing of its parts with the parts of that body, and that necessitates the occurrence of separation in the parts of that God. If it was an accident, it needed a place, and God needed something else. And it's all ridiculous. As for the third, which is that some of God’s elements and part of His parts were included in it, that is also impossible, because if that part is considered in divinity, then upon its separation from God, God must not remain a god, and if it is not considered in achieving divinity, then it is not a part of God. The corruption of these sections was proven, so the Christians’ statement was false.

(The fourth aspect) regarding the invalidity of the Christians’ statement is what has been proven by frequent transmission that Jesus, peace be upon him, had a great desire for worship and obedience, and if he were a god, this would be impossible, because God does not worship Himself. These are very clear and evident aspects that indicate the corruption of their words.
Then I said to the Christian, what indicated to you that he was a god?

He said that what was indicated by the appearance of miracles on him, such as reviving the dead and healing the blind and the lepers, is that this cannot be achieved except by the power of God Almighty. So I asked him: Do you accept that the absence of evidence does not necessitate the absence of the meaning or not? If you do not accept that by denying the world in eternity you must deny the Maker, and if you accept that the lack of evidence does not necessitate the absence of the signified, then I say, since it was permissible for God to reside in the body of Jesus, peace be upon him, how did you know that God did not enter my body and your body and the body of every animal, plant, and inanimate object? He said, “The difference is apparent, and that is because I only ruled that the solutions are because those strange actions appeared on him, and the strange actions did not appear on my hand or on yours, so we know that that solution is missing here.” So I said to him, it turns out that you did not know the meaning of my statement that the absence of evidence does not necessitate the absence of meaning, because the appearance of those supernatural things indicates the presence of God in the body of Jesus, peace be upon him, so the non-appearance of those supernatural things from me and from you is not in him except that that evidence did not exist, so if it is proven that the lack of evidence does not necessitate the absence of meaning, then the absence of those supernatural phenomena from me and from you does not necessitate the non-appearance of those supernatural things from me and from you, and even in the right of the dog, the feline, and the mouse. Then I said that it is a doctrine that saying it leads to The permissibility of the presence of God in the body of dogs and flies is extremely vile and low. Moreover, turning the stick alive is farther in the mind than bringing back the dead

Alive, because the problem between the body of the living and the body of the dead is greater than the problem between the piece of wood and the body of the snake. If turning the stick did not necessitate the fact that Moses, peace be upon him, was a god and the son of God, then reviving the dead does not indicate divinity, that would have been better, and upon this the Christian was cut off and there was no speech left for him, and God knows best. He ended his speech with his noble words.
