content: Chapter Five: On proving that the Qur’an is the word of God and a miracle and removing the suspicions of the priests. I have added to the topic of the Qur’an the topic of proving the authenticity of the prophetic hadiths narrated in the books of authentic books by: Ahlus-Sunnah wal-Jama’ah.
This section consists of four chapters:

sections.heading: Chapter One: Things that indicate that the Qur’an is the word of God
content: [Chapter One: Matters that indicate that the Qur’an is the word of God]

In proving that the Qur’an is the word of God, the matters that indicate that the Qur’an is the word of God are many. I will suffice with twelve matters according to the number of Christ’s disciples and leave the rest, such as it being said that the disappointed person who disagrees when explaining a matter of worldly or religious matters is also noticeable in the Qur’an, and that explaining everything, whether by encouragement or intimidation, whether by compassion or reproach, is to the degree of moderation, not excessive or negligent, and these two matters do not exist in human speech because he speaks in explaining every situation. As appropriate to that situation, one does not notice in reproach the condition of those who are amenable to compassion and vice versa, and one does not notice when mentioning this world the state of the hereafter and vice versa. He says that anger is more than a mistake and so on other things.

(The first matter): It is at a high level of eloquence, the likes of which is not known in their compositions and their levels of eloquence fall short of it. It is the expression in admirable language of the meaning appropriate to the position in which the speech was mentioned, without any addition or decrement in the explanation and indication of it. Accordingly, the more honorable the words, the splendor of the meanings, and the matching of the connotation, the more eloquent the speech is, and the fact that it is at this level is indicated by the following aspects:

(The first) is that the most eloquent Arabs describe sightings, such as describing a camel, a horse, a slave girl, a king, a blow, a stab, a description of a war, or a description of a raid. Likewise, the eloquence of the non-Arabs, whether they are poets or writers, is greatest in things like these

Things. The scope of eloquence and eloquence is very wide because the natures of most people are inclined to it. From ancient times, at every time and in every region, a poet or writer appeared with a new content and a nice joke in an explanation of any of these things mentioned, and the latecomer, the follower, often stands on the scrutiny of the earlier one. If a man were of sound mind and aimed to acquire the ability to describe them, he would obtain, after practice and work, the ability to explain in describing any of these things to the extent of the soundness of his thought and the quality of his mind. The Qur’an does not explain the specifics of these things, so the eloquent words that the Arabs agreed upon in their speech should not be obtained in it.

(Second) That God Almighty took into account the method of honesty and abstained from lying in all of it, and every poet who abandoned lying and adhered to honesty, his poetry was revealed and it was not good, and for this reason it is said that the best poetry is the most untruthful. You see that when Labid bin Rabia and Hassan bin Thabit, may God be pleased with them, converted to Islam, their poetry was revealed, and their Islamic poetry was not like their pre-Islamic poetry, and the Qur’an was eloquent while abstaining from lying and taking risks.
(Third) that eloquent speech is only consistent in the poem in the verse and two verses, but the rest is not like that, unlike the Qur’an, which, despite its length, is entirely eloquent.
So that creation is incapable of it. Whoever reflects on the story of Joseph, peace be upon him, will know that, despite its length, it attained a high level of eloquence.

(Fourth) that if the poet or writer repeats a content or a story, his second statement will not be the same as the first. The stories of the prophets, the conditions of the beginning and the resurrection, the rulings, and the divine attributes were repeated, and the expressions differed in brevity, redundancy, and artistry in their explanation, backbiting, and rhetoric, and yet each one of them is at the end of eloquence, and the discrepancy does not appear at all.

(Fifth) It was limited to obligating acts of worship, prohibiting obscene acts, urging good morals, abandoning this world, and choosing the afterlife, and such matters necessitate reducing eloquence. Therefore, if an eloquent poet or an eloquent writer is told to write nine or ten issues of jurisprudence or beliefs in an eloquent phrase that includes eloquent similes and precise metaphors, he will be unable.
(Sixth) Every poet whose speech is good in one art is weak in his speech in other art, as they said about the Arab poets: The poetry of Imru’ al-Qais is good.

When feeling happy, mentioning women and describing horses, Al-Nabigha’s poetry when fearful, Al-A’sha’s poetry when seeking, describing wine, and Zuhair’s poetry when wanting and hoping. They said in Persian Poets that Al-Nazami and Ferdowsi are alone in their statement

War, Al-Saadi Farid in poetry, Al-Anwari in poems... And the Qur’an was eloquent with the utmost eloquence in every art, be it encouragement or intimidation, be it rebuke, admonition, or anything else. (And here I cite verse by verse as an example of every art.) In the encouragement is His saying, “No soul knows what has been hidden from them of the comfort of their eyes,” and in the intimidation, His saying, “And every tyrant who is stubborn will fail. Behind him is Hell, and he will be made to drink of purulent water. He swallows it and can hardly swallow it, and death comes to him from everywhere, but he is not dead. And behind it is a severe punishment.

And in rebuking and rebuking, he said: “And each of us took responsibility for his sin, and among them were those whom We sent as a judge against him.” Some of them were taken by the trend. And among them are those whom We caused the earth to swallow. Some of them drowned us. And God would not wrong them, but they wronged themselves. And in the exhortation, His saying, “Have you considered that We gave them enjoyment for years, then came to them what they were promised, and what they used to enjoy availed them of no avail.” And in the divine, His saying, “God knows what every female bears, and what the wombs bear, and what they increase, and everything is with Him in measure. The Great and Transcendent Knower of the Unseen and the Witness}.

(Seventh) Most likely, if the speech moves from one content to another content, and includes explaining different things, the good linking of the speech does not remain and it falls below the high level of eloquence. In the Qur’an, there is a transition from one story to another, going from one chapter to another, including a command and a prohibition, information and intelligence, a promise and a feast, proof of prophecy, unification of the essence, singling out attributes, encouraging and intimidating, setting an example, and explaining a situation. However, there is a perfection of connection and a high degree of eloquence that is out of the ordinary, astonishing the minds of Arab eloquent people.

(Eighth) The Qur’an, in most places, comes with a simple word containing a lot of meaning, and the wording is sweeter, and whoever meditates on Surah (may God bless him and grant him peace) will know what I said, how it was published, and the news of the infidels, their disagreement, and their censure of destroying the centuries before them, and their denial of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and their astonishment at what he brought, and the news.

About the consensus of their people on disbelief, the appearance of envy in their words, their inability and contempt and their threat of disgrace in this world and the hereafter, the denial of the nations before them and God’s destruction of them, and the threat of the Quraysh and their likes similar to their affliction. He encouraged the Prophet to be patient with their harm and to entertain him in the stories of prophets such as David, Solomon, Job, Abraham, Jacob, and others, peace be upon them. All of this was mentioned from beginning to end in simple words containing many meanings, as well as the Almighty’s saying: “And for you there is life in retaliation,” for this saying has a short pronunciation and has a lot of meaning. Although it is eloquent and includes the correspondence between the two opposite meanings, which are retribution and life. Strangely enough, killing, which is the loss of life, is considered a condition for it and more important than all the well-known sayings of the Arabs on this subject, because they expressed this meaning by saying: (Killing some is the life of all) and saying: (Murder more so that killing will decrease) and saying: (Killing is negated by killing). The best sayings transmitted about the last saying and the wording of the Qur’an are more eloquent than it in six ways: (One of them): That it is shorter than all, because his saying {and for you} does not fall into this section because it must be estimated in all, because the saying of the one who killed some in order to revive all must be evaluated like it, and likewise in their saying killing is negated by killing. (Secondly): Their saying that killing negated the apparent meaning of killing requires that the thing be a cause

Because it does not exist, contrary to the wording of the Qur’an, it implies that a type of killing, which is retaliation, is a reason for a type of life. (Thirdly): Their saying is better than repeating the word “killing” in contrast to the word “killing” in the Qur’an.
(And fourthly): Their best words only benefit deterrence from killing, unlike the words of the Qur’an, which help deterrence from killing and wounding, which is more useful.

(Fifthly): Their better statement indicates what is required by consequence, unlike the wording of the Qur’an, which indicates what is originally intended, because denying killing is required by consequence in that it includes the attainment of life, which is originally required. (And sixth): Unjust killing is also killing, although it does not negate killing, unlike retaliation, so the apparent meaning of their statement is false, but as for the wording of the Qur’an, it is correct, both apparent and hidden. Likewise, God Almighty says: {While obeying God} in His obligations {and His Messenger} in His Sunnahs or in all that they command and forbid {and fearing God} that is, fearing His disagreement, His punishment, and His reckoning {and fearing Him} for the remainder of his life in all His affairs {for those are the ones who will be successful} in what is meant in the beginning and the future. This saying, despite the brevity of its wording, encompasses all the necessities (it was narrated) that Omar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, was one day sleeping in the mosque.

He was standing with his head bearing witness to the truth, so I informed him that he was one of the Romans’ patriarchs and among those who were good at understanding the tongues of the Arabs and others, and that he heard a man from among the Muslim captives reciting a verse from your book. He pondered it and saw that it included everything that God had revealed to Jesus, son of Mary, regarding the conditions of this world and the hereafter, which is his saying {And whoever obeys God and His Messenger} the verse. It was said that a clever Christian doctor asked Al-Hussein bin Ali Al-Waqidi: Why did you not...

Something is mentioned in your book about the science of medicine... and science is two sciences, the science of bodies and the science of religions. Al-Hussein said: God explained all the knowledge of medicine in half a verse, so he asked the Christian doctor about this verse. He said: It is his saying: {Eat and drink} what God has made lawful for you of foods and drinks {and do not be extravagant} meaning, do not transgress into what is forbidden, do not increase in shameful spending, and do not consume a large amount that will harm you and you do not need it.

Then he asked the doctor: Did your Prophet also say anything about this matter? Al-Hussein said: Our Prophet also collected medicine in simple words, so he asked the doctor about it, and Al-Hussein said: It is this: “The stomach is the house of disease, and diet is the head of all medicine, and give each body what it requires.” The doctor said: It is fair that your book and your Prophet did not leave any need for Galen.
That is to say, we have explained the matter which is the basis of preserving health and removing disease, their origin and their harms.

(Ninth): Magnificence and sweetness are like two opposite qualities, and their combination is as it should be in every part of a long speech, contrary to the usual habit of eloquent people. Their combination in every place in the entire Qur’an is evidence of its perfect eloquence and eloquence, which are outside the norm.

(Tenth): It includes all the arts of rhetoric, including forms of emphasis, types of similes and representations, types of metaphor, good readings and syllables, good breaks, introduction, delay, separation and connection appropriate to the position, and it is free from prosaic and irregular pronunciation that deviates from analogy and is unusable, and other types of rhetoric. None of the eloquent and perfect Arabs is capable of speaking except one or two of the types mentioned, and if he were to mention something else in his speech, it would not come to him, and he would be negligent. The Qur’an contains all of them, so that is a complete ten, and these ten aspects indicate that the Qur’an is at a high level of eloquence that is outside the norm. The eloquent Arabs know it by their eloquence, and the scholars of the sects by their skill in the art of eloquence and their familiarity with the methods of speech, and whoever knows the language of the Arabs and the arts of its eloquence knows the miracle of the Qur’an.

(The second matter): His wondrous composition and his strange style of readings, passages, and breaks, while containing subtleties of explanation, truths of knowledge, good expression, gentleness of reference, sound structure, and sound arrangement, so minds were perplexed by it.

Arab Arabs, and the concept of classical people. The wisdom behind this violation is that the stubborn, arbitrariness does not have the suspicion of theft, and this speech is distinguished from their words and shows its superiority, because the eloquent speaker, whether he is a narrator or a proselytizer, exerts complete diligence in these matters, and is often praised and criticized in these matters, just as he disgraced Imru’ al-Qais:
Stand up and cry at the memory of a lover and a home.. The bone fell between entering and I was pregnant

That the beginning of the verse combined sweetness of pronunciation, ease of expression, and abundance of meanings, as he stopped and paused and wept and lamented and mentioned the beloved and the home, and that the second part does not contain any of that... And shame on the beginning of Abu Al-Najm, the famous poet, because he entered upon Hisham bin Abdul Malik, and he recited it:
It was almost yellow, but it did not.. as if it were on the horizon in any case
Hisham was cross-eyed, so he took him out and ordered his imprisonment.
Shame on Jarir's introduction, for he entered upon Abd al-Malik and praised him with a Ha'i poem. The first is:
Are you awake or is your heart not awake? Abdul Malik said to him: Rather, your heart, O son of the doer.
A defect in Al-Buhtari’s beginning is that Yusuf bin Muhammad recited his poem, the beginning of which is:

Woe to you from a night whose end is short, and he said: Nay, woe and disgrace to you... Shame on the beginning of Ishaq al-Mawsili, the clever writer, for he entered upon al-Mu’tasim after he had finished building his palace in the square and recited to him his poem which
Its beginning:
Oh someone else's home, wear and tear. * I wish my hair had done to you!!

Al-Mu'tasim fled from this place and ordered the palace to be demolished immediately. Thus, most of the famous poets made mistakes in the mentioned places. The Arab nobles, despite their perfect skill in the secrets of speech and their intense hostility to Islam, did not find any scope in the eloquence of the Qur’an and its good organization and style. They did not mention any criticism in the slightest. Rather, they admitted that it was not of the same type as the sermons of preachers and the poetry of poets, and they sometimes attributed it to

They marveled at his eloquence and good organization, and they said at times that it was a lie he had fabricated and the myths of the ancients, and at times they said to their friends and loved ones, “Do not listen to this Qur’an, and distort it, perhaps you will prevail.” These are all the habit of the dazzled Mahjuj. It has been proven that the Qur’an is miraculous due to its eloquence, eloquence, and good organization. How can it be imagined that the eloquent and eloquent Arabs would be as numerous as the sands of Dahna and the pebbles of Batha, and known for their extreme fanaticism and pre-Islamic fever, and their addiction to competition, ostentation, and defending the most eminent. So they abandon the easiest matter, which is the Etan, in proportion to the shortest surah, and choose the more difficult one, such as evacuation and the sacrifice of sacrifice and lives, and they are afflicted with the captivity of descendants and the plundering of wealth, and their defiant opponent knocks them down over the heads of public for a while with the likes of these sayings: {Then bring a surah like it, and call on whomever you can besides Allah, if you are truthful.}

{And if you are in doubt about what We have sent down to Our servant, then produce a surah like it, and call your witnesses instead of God if you are truthful. If you do not do it and you will not do it, then fear the Fire whose fuel is people and stones. {Say: If mankind and the jinn were to gather together to produce the like of this Qur’an, they would not produce the like of it, even if they were to support each other.}

If they had thought that Muhammad, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, sought help from others, they would also have been able to seek help from others, because he is like those who deny knowledge of the language and the ability to seek help. So when they did not do that and preferred conflict over opposition and fighting over agreement, it was proven that the eloquence of the Qur’an was a given to them and they were incapable of opposing it. The point of the matter is that they became separated between someone who believed in it and the one to whom it was revealed, and someone who was confused about something wonderful. His eloquence. It was narrated that he heard Al-Walid bin Al-Mughirah from the Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, “Indeed, God commands justice and goodness and giving to relatives, and forbids indecency, evil, and transgression. He exhorts you that you may remember.” So he said: By God, he has sweetness, and there is paint upon him, and even the lowest.

It is blessed and the highest is fruitful. What he says is human.. It was also narrated that when he heard the Qur’an his heart softened, so Abu Jahl came to him and his nephew was disapproving of him. He said: By God, there is no one among you who knows poetry more than me, and by God there is nothing like the one who says any of this. It was also narrated that he gathered the Quraysh at the arrival of the season and said: The Arab delegations are repelling the Arabs, so agree on an opinion in which you do not lie to one another. They said: We say a soothsayer. He said: By God, he is not a soothsayer with his flute or his sajda. They said: He is crazy. He said: He is not crazy, nor is he angry or obsessed. They said: So we say he is a poet. He said: He is not a poet.

We have known all poetry, its rajaz and hazj, qaridh, simplified and qasat. They said: So we say a sorcerer. He said: He is not a sorcerer, nor does he spit or contract. They said: So what do we say? He said: You are not saying any of this unless I know that it is false and that the most likely statement is that he is a magician. Then he said: It is magic by which a person and his son separate, a person and his brother, a person and his wife, and a person and his clan. So they dispersed and sat on the roads warning people not to follow the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, so God Almighty revealed about the newborn: {Leave me and whomever I have created alone}... the verses.
It was narrated that Utbah spoke to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding what he had brought regarding the disagreement with his people, and he recited to him:

{father-in-law. Download from the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Book Fussilat..} to his saying: {I warn you of a thunderbolt like the thunderbolt of Ad and Thamud}. So Utbah held his hand over his mouth and the relative implored him to desist. According to a narration, the Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, began reading while Utbah was holding his hands behind his back, relying on them until he finished prostrating. So the Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, prostrated, and Utbah stood up, not knowing what he was reviewing. He returned to his family and did not go out to his people until they came to him. He apologized to them and said, “By God, he spoke to me words the likes of which my ears had never heard, so I did not know what to say to him.” Abu mentioned. Ubaida said that a Bedouin heard a man reading

{So proclaim what you are commanded} So he prostrated and said, I prostrated because of his eloquence, and another man of the polytheists heard a Muslim man reciting: {And from which they despaired, they would be saved free} and he said: I bear witness that no creature is capable of such speech.. Al-Asma’i related that he heard a slave girl speaking with an eloquent phrase and an eloquent gesture, which was pentathlon or hexagram, and she said, “I seek forgiveness from God for all my sins,” so he said: Why do you seek forgiveness and did not Does he drag a pen on you? She said:
I ask God for forgiveness for all my sins. * I killed a person without permission
Like a soft gazelle in a dallah * The night has reached midnight and I have not arrived

He said to her: May God fight you for your eloquence, and she said: Or after this, eloquence after the Almighty’s saying: {And We revealed to the mother of Moses, “Suckling him; but if you fear for him, then throw him into the sea, and do not be afraid and do not grieve.” Indeed, they have returned him to you and made him one of the messengers.} So he combined in one verse two commands, two prohibitions, two pieces of news and two good tidings... And in the hadith of Abu Dharr’s conversion to Islam, he described his brother Anis and said: By God, I have not heard anything more poetic than my brother Anis. He contradicted twelve poets in the pre-Islamic era, of which I am one of them, and that he set off for Mecca and came to me. I said: So what do the people say? He said: They say a poet, a soothsayer, then he said: I heard what the priests said, so what is their saying, and I put it down. On reciting poetry, it did not come together, and it did not come together on the tongue of anyone after me

He felt that he was telling the truth and that they were liars. It was narrated in the two Sahihs on the authority of Jubair bin Mutim, may God be pleased with him, who said: I heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, reciting in the sunset at At-Tur, when he reached this verse: {Or were they created from nothing, or are they the creators, or did they create the heavens and the earth, but they are not certain, or do they have the treasures of your Lord, or are they the ones in control?} My heart almost flew to Islam.

It was reported that Ibn al-Muqaffa asked to oppose the Qur’an and began to do so. He passed by a boy reciting: “And it was said, ‘O earth, swallow your water.’” So he returned and erased what he had done and said: “I bear witness that this is not contradicted and that it is not the words of humans.” Yahya bin Hakam Al-Ghazali was an eloquent speaker in Andalusia in his time. He said that he saw something of this, so he looked at Surat Al-Ikhlas to find its style and organize the speech in its style. He said: Then I was overcome by fear of him and a piety that led me to repent and repent.
The system of the Mu'tazilites said: The miracle of the Qur'an through morphology, in the sense that the Arabs

It was able to speak words like the Qur’an before the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sent, but God diverted them from opposing it due to reasons after the resurrection. This transformation is extraordinary and therefore miraculous. He also acknowledges that the Qur’an is miraculous for the sake of the transmission, and something like it is not possible for them after the resurrection. Rather, his dispute is that it was empowered before the resurrection and his statement is incorrect in several aspects: (The first): If it had been such and such, they would have opposed the Qur’an with the words that were issued by them before the resurrection and it would be like the Qur’an. (The second): The eloquent Arabs were amazed at his good organization, his eloquence, and his generosity in his greatness, not because opposition did not come with ease in itself. (Third): If he had intended to be miraculous with morphology, it would have been more appropriate to neglect paying attention to its eloquence and the highness of its class, because according to this estimate, the more the Qur’an was revealed in eloquence and entered into rarity, the greater the lack of possibility of opposition becomes in violating custom. (And the fourth): He rejects the Almighty’s saying: {Say: If mankind and the jinn gathered together to produce the like of this Qur’an, they would not produce the like of it, even if they were one another’s helpers.}

If it is said: When the eloquent Arabs were able to speak the words of the surah and its short components, they would be able to come up with something like it (I say) This conjunction is forbidden because the rule of the sentence may contradict the rule of the parts. Do you not see that every hair by hair is not suitable for an elephant or a ship to be tied to, and if it is not

One of the poems is a strong rope that can be used to tie an elephant or a ship with this rope, and because if it were authentic, all the Arabs would be able to come up with poems like Imru’ al-Qais and others like him.
(The third matter): The fact that the Qur’an contains information about the following events, and they were found in the following days in the manner in which it was reported.

1- As God Almighty said: {You will enter the Sacred Mosque, God willing, safe, with your heads shaved and shortened, and not afraid.} So it happened as he was told, and the Companions entered the Sacred Mosque safely, with their heads shaved and shortened, and not afraid. 2- And as the Almighty says: {God promised those of you who believe and do righteous deeds that He will certainly appoint them as successors in the land just as He appointed those before them as successors, and that He will establish for them their religion which He has chosen for them, and that He will replace them with security after their fear. They will worship Me, not associating anything with Me.} So God had promised the believers to make caliphs from among them, to empower the religion that was acceptable to them, and to replace their fear with security. He fulfilled his promise in a short period of time when it appeared in the life of the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, that the people of Islam had gained control over Mecca, Khaybar, Bahrain, the Kingdom of Yemen, and most of the lands.

The Arabs, and that the territory of Abyssinia became the abode of Islam through the faith of the King Negus, and that people from the Hijras and some Christians from the regions of the Levant accepted obedience and paid tribute, and that this dominion increased in the caliphate of the Greatest Siddiq, may God be pleased with him, by the people of Islam dominating some of the lands of Persia and Busra and Damascus, and some other lands of the Levant as well. Then this dominion increased in the caliphate of Al-Faruq, may God be pleased with him, by having dominion over the rest of the lands of the Levant and all of the kingdom of Egypt, and more The lands of Persia as well. Then this domination increased during the caliphate of Dhul-Nourin, may God be pleased with him, when they gained dominion

On the western side as far as Andalusia and Kairouan, and on the eastern side as far as China, for a period of thirty years the people of Islam had complete control over these kingdoms, and the acceptable religion of God prevailed over all other religions in these kingdoms, so they worshiped God in security and without fear. In the succession of the Commander of the Faithful, Ali bin Abi Talib, may God honor his face, even if the people of Islam did not dominate the new kingdoms, there is no doubt about the advancement of the Islamic religion during his noble era as well.

4- And as God Almighty says: {You will be called against a people of mighty might; you will fight them or they will submit}. It occurred as it was reported, because what is meant by a people of power in the clearest and most famous sense is the Banu Hanifa, the people of Musaylimah, the liar and the preacher, Al-Siddiq Al-Akbar, may God be pleased with him.

About him. 5- And as the Almighty says: {It is He who sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth that He might make it prevail over all religions}. This statement is the same as the second statement, and the full fulfillment of this promise will appear soon as is hoped for, God willing. He is powerful over everything. 5- And as the Almighty says: {God was pleased with the believers when they pledged allegiance to you under the tree. So He knew what was in their hearts, so He sent down tranquility upon them and rewarded them with an imminent victory. And they take many spoils, and God is Mighty, Wise. God promised you many spoils that you would take, so He hastened these for you and restrained the hands of people from you. That it may be a sign for the believers and that it may guide you to a straight path. And others that you could not do, God has encompassed them, and God is over everything

Almighty}. What is meant by the near conquest is the conquest of Khaybar, and by the many spoils in the first place are the spoils of Khaybar or Hajar, and by the many spoils in the second place is the spoils that will accrue to the Muslims from the Day of Promise until the Day of Resurrection, and in another place is the spoils of Hawazin, Persia, or the Romans, and it occurred as he was told. 6- And as the Almighty says: {And others that you love: victory from God and a near conquest}. So his saying “another” means he will give you another quality, and his saying “victory from God” explains the other, and his saying “conquest is near,” meaning “urgent,” which is the conquest of Mecca. Al-Hasan said: It is the conquest of Persia and the Romans, and it took place as he was told. 7- And as God Almighty says: {When God’s victory and conquest come and you see people entering God’s religion in crowds}.

What is meant by conquest is the conquest of Mecca, because what is more correct is that this Surah was revealed before the conquest of Mecca because {if} requires reception and it is not said about what happened when it came and if it happened, so the conquest of Mecca took place and the people entered Islam, group after group of the people of Mecca and Taif.

وغيرها في حياته صلى الله عليه وسلم. ٨- وكقوله تعالى: {قل للذين كفروا ستغلبون} . وقد وقع كما أخبر فصاروا مغلوبين. 9- And as God Almighty says: {And when He promised you} meaning, remember when He promised you {God is one of the two groups} the caravan returning from the Levant and the caravan coming from the Sacred House of God {that it is yours and you wish that the other than the one with a thorn} meaning the returning caravan {would be yours and God desires to establish the truth with His words and cut off the traces of the disbelievers} so it occurred as he was told.
10- And as God Almighty says: {Indeed, We have sufficed you with mockers}.

When this verse was revealed, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave good tidings to his companions that God had protected him from their evil and harm. The mockers were a group in Mecca who alienated people from him and harmed him, so they perished in various types of affliction and hardships, so his light was complete and his appearance was complete. 11- And as God Almighty says: {And God will protect you from people}. It happened, as he reported, with a large number of people intending to harm him, so God Almighty protected him, until he moved from the worldly abode to the most beautiful homes in the afterlife. 12- And as God Almighty says: {Have you not defeated the Romans in the lowest part of the earth} i.e. the land of the Arabs {while they} i.e. the Romans {after their defeat they will prevail} i.e. the Persians {in a few years} i.e. between three and ten years {and on that day the believers will rejoice in the victory of God. He helps whomever He wills, and He is the Mighty, the Merciful. a promise

God does not break His promise, but most people do not know. They know what is apparent from the life of this world, but they are heedless of the Hereafter. The Persians were Magians and the Romans were Christians. When the news of the Persians’ victory over them came to Mecca, the polytheists rejoiced and said, “You and the Christians are people of the Book, and we and the Persians are illiterate and have no Book. Our brothers have prevailed over your brothers, and we will prevail over you.” فنزلت هذه الآيات. Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, said: May God not close your eyes, for by God the Romans will prevail over Persia in a few years. Ubayy ibn Khalaf said: You lied. Set a term between us and you, so he bet it on ten qalais from each of them and they made the term three years. Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, informed the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: The amount is between three and nine, so add it to the camels and add it to the term, so he made it one hundred qalas to nine years. My father died after he returned from Uhud, and the Romans defeated Persia in the seventh year of their defeat, and he was captured
Abu Bakr Al-Qalais is one of my father’s heirs. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Give it in charity.

The author of Mizan al-Haqq said in the fourth chapter of the third chapter: (If we assume the truth of the claim of the commentators that this verse was revealed before the Romans conquered the Persians, then we say that Muhammad, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, said according to his opinion or his correct thought in order to calm the hearts of his companions, and he heard such sayings from people of reason and opinion at all times.) End quote. If we assume the commentators’ claim to be true, his statement indicates that this matter is not accepted by him, and this is strange because the Almighty’s saying, “They will be victorious in a few years,” states that this matter will happen in the time of the near future, in a time of less than ten years, as is implied by the word “years” and a few years. Likewise, his saying, “And on that day the believers will rejoice,” and his saying, “God’s promise. God does not break His promise,” because they indicate the occurrence of joy in the time to come. And this matter occurred in him, and there is no meaning to the promise and not to break the matter after it happened, and his saying that Muhammad, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, said according to his suspicion or his correct thought is rejected in two ways: (The first): Muhammad, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, was one of the wisest among Christians as well, and this noble priest is recognized here and in other places in his books. It is not the business of a rational person claiming to be a prophet to make a definitive claim that such-and-such matter will be like this at all during a short period of time and command his believers to bet on this, especially when confronting seeker deniers.

Because of his humiliation, those who examine his misstep in a matter whose occurrence is not of any significant benefit, and whose non-occurrence is a reason for his humiliation and lie to them, and they obtain great support for his disbelief.

(The second): Even though rational people say about some matters with their minds and their thoughts are sometimes correct and sometimes wrong, it is the divine custom that if the one who claims to be a prophet is a liar and tells about the coming event, and slanders God by attributing this news to God, then this news is not true, but rather comes out as a mistake and a mistake at all, as you will know at the end of this topic, God willing. 13- And as God Almighty says: {Or do they say, “We are all victorious?” The crowd will be defeated and they will turn back.} On the authority of Omar, may God Almighty be pleased with him, that he said when it was revealed: I did not know what it was until it was on the day of Badr that I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, as he was putting on his armor and saying: {The crowd will be defeated}. So I taught him.
14- And as the Almighty says: {Fight them; God will punish them by your hands, and disgrace them, and grant you victory over them, and heal the breasts of a believing people}.

These circumstances occurred as he reported. 15- And as God Almighty says: {They will not harm you except harm} either by criticizing Muhammad and Jesus, peace be upon them, or by intimidating the weak among the Muslims {And if they fight you, they will turn back to you, then they will not be helped.} So He told about three things that are not hidden: (The first): That the believers will be safe from the harm of the Jews. (The second): If they fight the believers, they will be defeated. (And the third): They do not gain strength or strength after defeat, and all of them have occurred. 16- And as God Almighty says: {Humility has been struck upon them wherever they find themselves, except with a rope from God and a rope from mankind. They have incurred the wrath of God, and misery has struck them.} It happened as he reported, and the Jews did not have a government in any place, and in every region they were found to be subjects subject to humiliation.

17- And as God Almighty says: {We will cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieve} and it happened on the Day of Uhud in two ways, as he told us. (The first): When the polytheists took control of the Muslims on the Day of Uhud and defeated them, God struck terror in their hearts, so they abandoned them and fled from them without any reason. (And the second): When they went to Mecca, when they were part way through, they regretted it and said, “What a miserable thing you have done. You killed them until, if nothing remained but the fugitive, you left them. Go back and eradicate them before they found strength and thorns.” Then God cast terror into their hearts, so they went to Mecca.

18- And as God Almighty says: {Indeed, it is We who sent down the Remembrance, and indeed We will preserve it} that is, from the distortion, addition, and subtraction, which has been frequently reported by notable scholars among the readers of the time, and it occurred as he reported, so none of the atheists, scholars, and Qarmatians were able to say that.

He distorts any of it, not one of the letters of its constructions, nor of the letters of its meanings, nor one of its parsings until this period that we are in, I mean one thousand two hundred and eighty of the Hijra, in contrast to the Torah, the Gospel, and others, as I learned in the first and second chapters, and praise be to God for the completion of this blessing.

19- And as the Almighty says: {Falsehood will not come to it}, meaning distortion by addition or subtraction {from before it or behind it, a revelation from the Wise, the Praiseworthy}, and the status of this saying is the same as the previous saying. 20- And as God Almighty says: {Indeed, He who imposed upon you the Qur’an} i.e. its rulings and obligations {will bring you back to a resurrection}. It was narrated that when he, peace be upon him, came out of the cave and walked on a different path for fear of being sought, then when he was safe, he returned to the road and descended in Al-Juhfa between Mecca and Medina. He knew the way to Mecca and longed for it, and mentioned his birth and the birth of his father. Then Gabriel, peace be upon him, came down and said: Do you miss your country and your birth? He, peace be upon him, said: Yes.

Gabriel, peace be upon him, said: God Almighty says: {Indeed, the one who imposed the Qur’an on you will return you to Ma’ad} meaning to Mecca, appearing over them. 21- And as God Almighty says: {Say, “If the Hereafter is for you,” O Jews, “the abode of the Hereafter with God, exclusive to other people, then wish for death if you are truthful, and they will never wish for it,” meaning as long as they live, “for what their hands have put forward. And God is All-Knowing of the wrongdoers.” What is meant by wishing is wishing by saying, and there is no doubt that, peace and blessings be upon him, despite his progress in opinion, firmness, and good consideration of the outcome, as is accepted by the one who opposes and agrees, and reaching the position he has reached in the two worlds, and attaining great leadership, it is not permissible for him - while he is not confident about the Lord’s revelation - to challenge the most enemy of his enemies with a matter in which he is not sure of the outcome of the situation, nor is he safe from his opponent vanquishing him with evidence and argument, because a rational person who has not tried matters is hardly He is satisfied with that, so what is the situation among the most rational people? It was proven that he did not undertake this challenge until after the revelation and his complete approval.

Likewise, there is no doubt that they were among his most vehement enemies, and they were the most keen people in disbelieving him, and they were thinking about the matters by which Islam would be erased or its people would be humiliated, and what was required of them was an easy matter, not a difficult one. If the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, had not been truthful in his claim to them, they would hastened to claim it in order to disbelieve him. Rather, they declared this wish by saying it repeatedly and made it known that he was a liar, slandering God for saying such-and-such, and claiming on his own behalf. A claim, and sometimes he says: By the One in whose hand is my soul, not one of them says it except that his luster is lost, meaning he died in his place, and he sometimes says: If the Jews had wished for death, they would have died, and we wished repeatedly, and we would not have died in our place, so it appeared that they turned away from their wish, despite the fact that they were in denying it. The people were keenest on his miracle and his proof was clear, and in this verse there are two reports about the unseen: (The first) that his saying {they will not wish for it} indicates a clear indication that this will not happen in the future from any of them. It is beneficial to all people.

(The second) is that His saying “never” indicates that there is nothing in the future tenses that indicates the generality of the times, so considering the two generalities they are unseen 22 - And as the Almighty says: {And if you are in doubt about what We have sent down to Our servant, then produce a chapter like it and call your witnesses besides God if you are truthful. But if you do not and you will not do it, then fear the Fire whose fuel is people and stones, prepared for the disbelievers} So he informed that they would not do it at all. And it happened as he told me,

This verse indicates the miraculous in four ways: (The first of them) We know with frequent transmission that the Arabs were extremely hostile to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and extremely keen to nullify his command, because separation from homelands and clans and sacrifice of souls and paths are among the strongest evidence for that. If such rebuke is added to it, which is his saying: {And if you do not do it, and you will never do it}, their eagerness becomes more intense. If they were able to come up with something like the Qur’an or a surah from it, They brought it, and wherever they brought it, the miracle appeared. (The second) is that the Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, was accused by them regarding the matter of prophecy, but he was known to be in a state of abundant reason, virtue, and knowledge of the consequences. If he were a liar, he would not have challenged them so seriously to the end. Rather, he had to be afraid of what he expected of a scandal that would affect all his affairs. If he had not known about the revelation of their inability to oppose, it would not have been permissible for him to force them to do so with this rebuke.

(Thirdly) if he had not been decisive in his matter, he would not have been decisive in saying that they would not produce something like it, because the forger is not decisive in his words, so his being decisive indicates that he is decisive in his matter.

(And fourthly) that the one who reported this news was found to be in that manner, because from his time, peace be upon him, until our era, there has never been a time when someone was hostile to religion and Islam, and they were harsh on him in attacking it, and then, with this extreme care, opposition never existed. These four aspects of the miracle are included in this verse.

These reports and others like them indicate that the Qur’an is the word of God, because God’s custom is that if a claimant of prophethood tells about something and attributes a lie to God, his report will not come out as authentic. In the eighteenth chapter of the Book of Exceptions, it is as follows: (Then if you love and say in your heart, “How can I discern the words that the Lord has not spoken?”) 22- This will be a sign to you, that what that prophet said in the name of the Lord and did not happen, the Lord did not speak, but rather that prophet portrayed it in his self-exaltation, and therefore do not fear him.)

(The fourth matter) What he told of the news of past centuries and perishing nations, and it was known that he was illiterate. He did not read or write, nor did he study with the scholars or sit with the virtuous. Rather, he was raised among a people who worshiped idols and did not know the Book, and were devoid of rational sciences as well. He was not absent from his people for an absence in which he could learn from others, and the places in which he contradicted the Qur’an in explaining the stories and cases mentioned [in] the books of the People of the Book, such as the story of the crucifixion of Christ, peace be upon him, and others. This is an intentional violation: either because some of these books are not original, like the famous Torah and Gospel, or because they are not inspired, and what you mentioned is indicated by the Almighty’s saying: {Indeed, this Qur’an relates to the Children of Israel most of what they differ about}.

(The fifth matter) is the revelation of the secrets of the hypocrites, as they secretly conspired in many types of deception and plotting, and God used to inform His Messenger of those conditions, time and time again, and told him about them in detail, so they found nothing in all of that except honesty, as well as the revelation of the state of the Jews and their consciences.

(The sixth matter) His collection of partial knowledge and comprehensive sciences that neither the Arabs in general nor Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, knew, especially the knowledge of laws, warnings about the methods of rational arguments, conduct, sermons, wisdom, news of the afterlife, and good manners and character. The truth of what is said in this section is that the sciences are either religious or other, and there is no doubt that the first is the greatest in importance and the highest in status, as it is either the science of beliefs and religions, or the science of deeds. As for the knowledge of beliefs and religions, it is knowledge of God, His angels, His books, His messengers, and the Last Day. As for knowledge of God Almighty, it is knowledge of Himself, knowledge of the attributes of His majesty, knowledge of the attributes of His honor and actions, knowledge of His rulings, and knowledge of His names. The Qur’an includes the evidence of these issues, their branches, and details in a way that is not equal to any other book, or even comes close to it. As for the knowledge of deeds, it is either the knowledge of costs related to phenomena, which is the science of jurisprudence. It is known that all jurists derived their arguments from...

The Qur’an, or it is the science of Sufism related to purifying the interior and exercising the hearts, and some discussions of this science have occurred in the Qur’an that are not found in others, such as His saying: {Take pardon and enjoin custom and turn away from the ignorant} and His saying: {Indeed, God enjoins justice and benevolence and giving to relatives and forbids immorality, wrongdoing and transgression} and His saying: {And good and bad are not equal. Repel with what is better. Then, behold, there is enmity between you and Him. As if he were a close friend.} So his saying: {Repel with what is best} means remove their foolishness and ignorance with the quality that is better, which is patience and responding to evil with good. And His saying, “So that” etc. means that if their evil deeds are met with good deeds and their evil deeds are met with good deeds, they will abandon their evil deeds and turn from enmity to love, and from hatred to affection.
There are many sayings like these.

So it has been proven that it brings together all the transmission sciences, their origins and branches, and it contains a warning about the types of rational connotations and a response to the masters of misguidance with compelling proofs and dazzling proofs that are easy to establish and concise meanings, such as the Almighty’s saying: {Is not He who created the heavens and the earth able to create the like of them?} and His Almighty’s saying: {He who created them the first time gives life to them} and His Almighty’s saying: {If there were in them gods other than Allah, they would certainly be corrupted} And how wonderful is what was said: All knowledge is in the Qur’an, but men’s understandings fall short of it.

(The seventh matter) is that it is free from difference and discrepancy, even though it is a large book that includes many types of knowledge. If that had been from someone other than God, then there would have been types of contradictory words in it, because the large, long book does not deviate from that. And since that was not found in it, we knew that it is not from anyone other than God, as God Almighty said: {Will they not contemplate the Qur’an? And if it had been from other than God, they would have found in it much discrepancy.} And to these seven matters mentioned, God Almighty referred by saying: {It was sent down by Him who knows the secret in the heavens and the earth} because such eloquence, wondrous style, and information

About the unseen, including all kinds of sciences, and abstaining from difference and disparity, despite the fact that the book is large and includes all kinds of sciences. It only comes from the world, from whose knowledge not the weight of an atom of what is in the heavens and the earth is absent.

(The eighth matter) It is an enduring miracle that is repeated everywhere, with God taking care of its preservation. Unlike the miracles of the prophets, they have passed with the expiration of their times, and this miracle remains as it was from the time of its revelation to our time. A period of one thousand two hundred and eighty has passed, and its evidence is compelling, and opposition to it is impossible. In all times, villages and regions are filled with people of the tongue and imams of eloquence, and the atheist is many among them, and the stubborn opponent is present. And prepared, and, God willing, it will remain like this as long as the world and its people remain in good health and well-being. Since the miracle of it is the size of the shortest surah, every part of it is of this size a miracle, so the Qur’an contains more than two thousand miracles.
(The ninth command) is that the reader does not get bored of it and the listener does not get bored with it, but rather repeating it necessitates an increase in his love, as it was said:
The best companion never gets tired of talking, and his repetition increases his beauty

And other speech, even if it is eloquent in purpose, becomes boring with hesitation in the hearing and dislikes in nature, but this matter applies to someone who has a healthy heart, not to someone who has a weak nature.

(The tenth matter) is that it combines the evidence with its meaning. What follows is that if he is one of those who understand its meanings, he understands the points of argument and obligation together in one speech, considering its utterance.
And its meaning, because through the eloquence of speech it infers the miraculous, and in the meanings it stands for God’s commands, prohibitions, promises, and threats.

(The eleventh command) is to memorize it with ease for those who learn it, as God Almighty said: {And We have certainly made the Qur’an easy for remembrance}, so memorizing it is easy for young children at the earliest. And in this nation, in this time also, despite the weakness of Islam in most countries, there are more than a hundred thousand memorizers of the Qur’an, so that the Qur’an can be written from the memorization of each of them from first to last, so that no error occurs in parsing, let alone words, and the number of memorizers of the Gospel is not equal to the number of memorizers in all European lands. In one of the villages of Egypt, Christians lost their minds and turned to sciences and crafts for three hundred years, and this is the obvious merit of the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and their writers.

(The Twelfth Order) The fear that afflicts the hearts and ears of its listeners when they hear the Qur’an, and the awe that afflicts it following it. This fear may afflict those who do not understand its meanings or know its interpretation. Some of them submitted to it at first glance, and some of them continued in their disbelief, and some of them disbelieved at that time and then returned to their Lord after that.

It was narrated that a Christian man passed by a reciter, and he stopped crying and was asked about the reason for the crying. He said that he was afraid because of the effect of the word of the Lord, and that when Ja’far al-Tayyar, may God be pleased with him, recited the Qur’an to the Negus and his companions, they were still crying until Ja’far, may God be pleased with him, finished reading, and that the Negus sent seventy Christian scholars to the Messenger of God, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, and he recited to them Surah (Yasin), so they wept and believed, and then God Almighty revealed regarding both groups or one of them: {And when they hear what was revealed to the Messenger, you will see their eyes overflowing with tears because of the truth they recognized. They say, “Our Lord, we have believed, so record us with the witnesses.” The case of Jubair bin Mut’im, may God be pleased with him, Utbah, Ibn al-Muqaffa, and Yahya bin Hakam al-Ghazali was known.

Nour Allah Al-Shustri said in his interpretation: When the scholar Ali Al-Qushji went from across the river to the Romans, a Jewish rabbi came to him to establish Islam and looked over it for a month, and he did not hand over any of the scholar’s evidence until that time. Then he came one day in the morning and the scholar was busy reciting the Qur’an on the roof of the house, and his voice was extremely unpleasant. When he entered the door and heard the Qur’an, the Qur’an had a profound effect on his heart. When he reached the scholar, he said: I am entering Islam, so the scholar introduced him. In Islam, then he was asked about the reason, and he said: I have never heard, in my entire life, a voice as foul as you. When I arrived at the door, I heard the Qur’an from you, and it had an eloquent effect on me, so I knew that it was a revelation. It is proven from the matters mentioned that the Qur’an is miraculous and the word of God. How could it not be? And good speech is due to three things: that its words be eloquent, that its arrangement be desirable, and that its content be good. These three matters are undoubtedly fulfilled in the Qur’an, and we conclude this chapter by stating three benefits:

(The first benefit) The reason why the miracle of our Prophet is also of the type of eloquence is that some miracles appear in every era of the type that prevails in its people as well, because they reach the highest level in it and stand on the limit that humans can reach. If they see what is outside the mentioned limit, they know that it is from God, and that is like magic in the time of Moses, peace be upon him, for it was prevalent among its people and they were perfect in it. His staff turned into a snake, catching their magic, which they were turning from the established truth to the false imagination without increasing its size. They knew that it was beyond magic and a miracle from God, so they believed in it. As for Pharaoh, when he was a minor in this craft, he thought that it was magic as well, even if it was greater than the magic of his magicians. Likewise, medicine was prevalent among the people of the time of Jesus, peace be upon him, and they were perfect in it. When they saw the resurrection of the dead and the healing of the blind, they knew with full knowledge that they were not within the limits of the medical profession, but rather that they were from God. Eloquence had reached the highest level during the era of the Messenger, peace be upon him, and they were proud of it until they hung the seven poems on the door of the Kaaba in defiance of opposing it, as biographical books attest. When the Prophet, peace and blessings of God be upon him, brought forth something that all eloquent people were unable to do, it was known that this was definitely from God.

(The second benefit) The Qur’an was revealed in a form and in parts, and it was not revealed all at once for reasons: (One of them) is that the Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, was not one of the people of reading, so if that had been revealed to him in one sentence, he would not have understood it, and it would have been permissible for him to forget. (Secondly) If the Book had been revealed to him all at once, he might have relied on the Book and been lax in memorizing it. When God sent down an astrologer, he preserved it and it remained the sunnah of memorization in his nation. (And third) in the case of the revelation of the Book all at once, if all the rulings had been revealed at once to the creation, it would have been burdensome for them, and when it was revealed in separate parts, the costs were reduced little by little, so it was easier to bear them, as it was narrated on the authority of some of the companions that he said: God has shown us all goodness. We were polytheists, so if the Messenger of God had come to us with this religion as a whole and with the Qur’an all at once, these costs would have been burdensome for us, so we would not have entered Islam, but he called us to one word, so when we accepted it, we tasted its sweetness. We accepted faith beyond word after word until the religion was fulfilled and the law was perfected. (And fourth) is that if he sees Gabriel time after time, his heart becomes stronger by watching him

He was stronger in carrying out what he carried out, in being patient with the symptoms of prophethood, and in enduring the people’s harm. (And fifth) that when the condition of miraculousness was fulfilled in him despite his being an astrologer, it was proven that he was miraculous. If they had been able to, they would have had to produce someone like him, a separate astrologer. (Sixthly) The Qur’an was revealed according to their questions and the facts that happened to them, so they increased their insight, because informing about faults was due to this being associated with eloquence. (And seventh) is that when the Qur’an was revealed in separate parts and the Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, challenged them from the beginning, it was as if he had challenged them with every one of the stars of the Qur’an, but when they were unable to do so, their inability to oppose all of them was more important, so it was proven in this way that the people were inevitably unable to oppose.

(Eighth) The embassy between God and His prophets and conveying His words to them is a great position. If the Qur’an had been revealed all at once, the removal of this position from Gabriel, peace be upon him, would have been possible. When he descended as a mining agent, that great position remained with him.

(The third benefit) The reason for repeating the statement of monotheism, the state of resurrection, and the stories of the prophets in places is that the Arabs were polytheists and pagans who denied these things, and the non-Arabs

Some of them, like the people of India, China, and the Magians, were like the Arabs in denying, and some of them, like the people of the Trinity, were in excess and negligence in believing these things, so for the sake of confirmation and confirmation, he repeated the statement of these things. There are other reasons for repeating the stories as well, including: The miraculous nature of the Qur’an was also due to the consideration of eloquence, and the challenge was in this regard, so the stories were repeated in different phrases, both briefly and redundantly, while preserving the highest degree of eloquence in each level, so that it is known that the Qur’an is not the speech of humans, because this matter for the eloquent people is beyond human ability. Among them is that they had the right to say that the eloquent words that were appropriate for these stories were used, but the other words remained appropriate for them, and to say that the path of each eloquent person differs from the path of the other, as some of them are able to follow the eloquent path, and some of them are able to summarize, so it does not follow that inability is a type of inability at all. Or they might say that the scope of rhetoric is narrow in explaining stories, and what you once stated is taken into account by divination and agreement, so when you repeated the stories in brevity and redundancy, there was no excuse left of these three excuses.

Among them is that he, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, was distressed by the people’s harm and their evil, as God Almighty told: {And We know that your heart is distressed by what they say.} So God tells a story from the stories of the prophets appropriate to his condition at that time to strengthen his heart, as God Almighty told: {And each of us shall relate to you of the tidings of the messengers that by which we may strengthen your heart and bring you this truth, and an admonition and a reminder to the believers}.

Among them is that Muslims were being harmed by infidels, or that a group of people were converting to Islam, or that the infidels were intended to warn them, so God revealed in each of these stories what was appropriate, because the condition of the predecessors would be an example for the successors. Among them is that a single story may include many things, so sometimes it is mentioned and some things are intended intentionally, and some things are consequential and reflected again (1).

(1) The author of the book said to Al-Shamila: In some copies here is an addition that is not in the printed version, which is: The truth is that it does not have any of the components of a state, so it continues to live on the aid of some foreign countries in constant fear and terror.. And soon the Arabs will expel it from their land in an evil manner, and they will not reunite, and no army will support them, and the crowd will be defeated and turn away. {God’s promise: God does not break His promise}.

sections.heading: Chapter Two: Removing the priests’ suspicions about the Qur’an
content: [Chapter Two: On raising the priests’ suspicions about the Qur’an.]

(The first suspicion) We do not accept that the words of the Qur’an are at the highest level of eloquence that is outside the norm. If we accept that, it would be incomplete evidence of miraculousness, because it only appears to someone who has complete knowledge of the Arabic language. It is necessary that all books found in other tongues, such as Greek, Latin, and others, be at the highest level of eloquence of the word of God, provided that false demands and ugly contents can be presented with eloquent words and eloquent expressions at the highest level.
