He mentioned on page 277 of the ninth volume of the Catholic Harald the sayings of Al-Muqtada Al-Mamduh, so I quote two sayings about them: 1 (Man’s nature is like a horse. If God rides him, he walks as he wants, and if Satan rides him, he walks as Satan walks. He does not choose a rider on his own, but rather the riders strive to ensure that any of them gets him and dominates him.) 2 (If there is a command in the holy books to do this thing, then understand that these books command not to do this good thing because you cannot do it.) End quote. It is clear from his words that he believes in algebra.

On page 33 of his book called The Mirror of Honesty, published in the year 1851, the priest Tames Angelus Katlik said, attacking a Protestant sect thus: (Their ancient preachers taught them these hateful sayings) 1 (that God creates disobedience) 2 (and that man is not chosen to avoid sin) 3 (and that acting on the ten rulings is not possible) 4 (and that major sins, even if they are great, do not lead a person to To imperfection in the eyes of God) 5 (And that faith alone saves a person because we are judged by faith alone, and this teaching is more beneficial and a teaching full of reassurance) 6 (And that the father of religious reform, meaning Lotar, said, “Believe only and know with certainty that you will be saved without the hardship of fasting, without the supplies of piety, without the hardship of confession, and without the hardship of good things, and you will have a precious salvation without suspicion, as Christ Himself has. Sin with complete audacity. Sin and believe only, and He will save you by faith.” In one day you are afflicted a thousand times with adultery or murder. Just believe. I say that your faith will save you. End quote.

It appears that what Protestant scholars said regarding the first matter regarding the Qur’an is rejected without a doubt and is contrary to their holy books, and to the words of their leaders: The creation of evil does not necessitate that God be evil, just as the creation of blackness and whiteness and other symptoms does not necessitate that it be black or white. The wisdom in creating evil is as it is in the creation of Satan, who is the root of evil and the head of corruption, with God’s eternal knowledge that Satan produces such and such, and just as it is in creating lust and greed in human nature. His eternal knowledge of what they entail in every individual human being. Just as God was able not to create or create Satan and not give him the ability to tempt and prevent him from evil, yet He created and did not prevent him from evil due to some wisdom, so He is also able not to create evil, but in His creation He has some wisdom.

(As for the answer to the second matter) it is that there is nothing wrong with the fact that Paradise includes maidens, palaces, and other bliss according to the mind, and the people of Islam do not say that the pleasures of Paradise are limited to physical pleasures only, as Protestant scholars mistakenly say or misrepresent the common people. Rather, they believe in the text of the Qur’an that Paradise includes spiritual and physical pleasures, and the former is better than the latter, and both types occur to believers. God said in Surat Al-Tawbah: {God promised the believing men and believing women Gardens beneath which rivers flow to abide therein, and good dwellings in the Gardens of Eden, and satisfaction from God is greater. That is the greatest victory.} So his saying, and satisfaction from God - the verse - means that satisfaction from God is greater.

It is a rank compared to all the gardens, rivers, and good dwellings mentioned previously. This saying indicates that the best thing God gives in Paradise are spiritual pleasures, even though He gives physical pleasures as well. Therefore, he said that this is the great victory, because man is created from two essences, the gentle upper and the dense lower physical, and joined to them is the occurrence of happiness and misery. If physical good things are achieved and spiritual happiness is joined to them, then the soul will win the happiness that befits it and the body will reach the happiness that befits it. There is no doubt that this is the great victory, even if Protestant scholars say that their meeting in Paradise is also ugly in our minds. I say to them, do not be disturbed, for it will not happen to you, God willing. I learned in the first chapter that the Gospel for us is an expression of what was revealed to Jesus, peace be upon him only. If one of the Christian sayings is found in a Christian saying that contradicts on its surface the ruling of the Qur’an, then it is without regard to the fact that it is narrated by the narration of individual people, and that contradicting their holy books does not harm the Qur’an, as I learned in the answer to the second suspicion.

I say that this statement is absolutely false, and the fact that the people of Paradise are like angels in their claim does not contradict eating and drinking according to the ruling of their books. Do they not see that the three angels who appeared to Abraham and Abraham, peace be upon him, brought to them a fresh calf, fat, and milk, ate these things as stated in the eighteenth chapter of the Book of Genesis, and that

The two kings who came to Lot, peace be upon him, and made them a feast and unleavened bread, ate as he stated in the nineteenth chapter of the Book of Genesis. What is surprising is that when they recognized the physical resurrection, what was the exclusion of physical pleasures? Yes, if they had denied the resurrection at all like the Arab polytheists, or they had denied the physical resurrection and recognized the spiritual resurrection like the followers of Aristotle, their exclusion would have had a basis according to what appears to be the case. According to them, God was incarnated and he did not stop eating, drinking, and other bodily necessities, considering that he was a human being. And since Jesus, peace be upon him, was not as content as Yahya in abstaining from psychological foods and drinking alcohol, the deniers would criticize him for being an eater and drinker, as stated in the eleventh chapter of the Gospel of Matthew.

We have this appeal rejected, but we say that there is no doubt that Jesus, peace be upon him, considering his physical nature, was only a human being. Just as precious foods and drinking wine were not a barrier to spiritual pleasures for him, peace be upon him, despite his being in this worldly abode, but rather spiritual rulings prevailed over his presence, likewise physical pleasures will not be a barrier to the spiritual pleasures of the people of Paradise despite their being in the next life.

(As for the answer to the third matter) it will come in the sixth chapter, God willing, because jihad in the obedience of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, is among the greatest obedience to them, so mention it in the obedience there.

(The fourth suspicion) is that the Qur’an does not contain anything that the soul requires and desires. (And the answer) is that what the spirit requires and desires are two things: complete beliefs and good deeds, and the Qur’an includes an explanation of both types to the fullest extent, as I learned in the answer to the first suspicion. The absence of some matters that are the requirements of the spirit, as claimed by Protestant scholars, does not necessitate the deficiency of the Qur’an, just as the absence of the matter that is required by the spirit does not necessitate the absence of the matter that is necessitated by the spirit, according to the Brahmin scholars of Indian polytheism, as I heard them say that slaughtering animals for the sake of Eating and pleasure are contrary to what the spirit requires and are not recommended by reason at all, and it is inconceivable that he would receive permission for it from God, for the book it contains is not from God.

(The fifth suspicion) There are moral differences in the Qur’an, for example, its saying: {There is no compulsion in religion} and its saying in Surah al-Ghashiya: {So remember, you are only a reminder, and you are not in control over them} and its saying in Surat al-Nour: {Say, “Obey God and obey the Messenger.” But if they turn away, then upon Him is what has been burdened, and upon you is what you have been charged with; and if you obey Him, you will be guided; and the Messenger is not responsible for anything but the clear conveyance.} These verses contradict the verses that contain the command of jihad. In most of the verses, it occurred that Christ was only a human being and a messenger, and in the opposite place it occurred that he was not of the human race, but rather his status was higher than his. The first is his saying in Surah An-Nisa: {The Messiah, Jesus, son of Mary, is only the Messenger of God, and His word which He delivered to Mary, and a spirit from Him} and the second is his saying in Surat al-Tahrim: {And Mary, the daughter of Imran, who guarded her chastity, so We breathed into her of Our spirit} These two differences are among the greatest differences in the claim of the two priests, and so the author of Mizan al-Haqq sufficed with them in the third chapter of the third chapter of it. (And I say) in answer to the first difference that this is not a difference, rather this ruling was before jihad, so when the ruling on jihad was revealed, this ruling was abrogated, and the abrogation is not a moral difference, otherwise there would need to be a moral difference between the Gospel and the Torah in all the abrogated rulings, and likewise in the same rulings of the Torah and likewise in the same rulings of the Gospel, as you have known in the third chapter, without more, provided that

The Almighty’s saying: {There is no compulsion in religion} is not abrogated, and you have learned the answer to the second difference in the seventh matter from the introduction to the book, and it has become apparent to you there that the two aforementioned statements do not indicate that Jesus, son of Mary, is not of the human race, and the understanding of this meaning is pure illusion and corrupt conjecture. What is surprising about these wise people is that they do not see the differences and errors that occurred in their books, as you learned some of them in the third chapter of the first chapter.

sections.heading: Chapter Three: On proving the authenticity of the Prophetic hadiths in the authentic books of the Sunnis and the community
content: [Chapter Three: On proving the authenticity of the Prophetic hadiths in the authentic books of the Sunnis and the community.]
This chapter includes three benefits:

(The first benefit) The majority of the People of the Book, Jews and Christians, considered linguistic narrations as predecessors and successors as the written. Indeed, the majority of Jews considered them with greater consideration than the written, and a group like that considered them equal to it and believed that both were obligatory to submit to and foundations of the faith. The Protestant group of Christians denied it just as the Sadducees of the Jewish group denied it, and these Protestant deniers were forced to deny it, because if they had not denied it, they would not have been able to explain its principles. Their new religion and beliefs, but nevertheless they need it in many places and there is support for it being considered from their holy books, as all these matters will appear to you, God Almighty willing.

Adam Clarke said in explaining the preamble to the Book of Ezra in the second volume of his interpretation, published in 1751: (The Jewish law was divided into two types: written, and they called it the Torah, and unwritten, and they called it the linguistic narrations that reached them through the sheikhs, and they claimed that God had given Moses both...

The two types on Mount Al-Tur, one of them reached us through writing, and the second through the sheikhs, who transmitted it generation after generation, and for this reason they believe that both are equal in rank, on the part of God, and obligatory to be submitted to. Rather, they prefer the second and say that the written law is incomplete and closed in many places, and the origin of faith cannot be complete without taking into account the linguistic narration, and this narration is clear and complete, and explains and completes the written law, and for this reason they reject the meanings of the written law if it contradicts the narrations. Linguistic, and it was known among them that the covenant taken from the children of Israel was not for the sake of the written law, but rather it was for the sake of these linguistic narrations. It is as if by this trick they rejected the written law and made the linguistic narrations the basis of their religion and faith. Likewise, the Roman Catholics in their religion chose this method and interpreted the word of God according to these narrations, even though this narrational meaning was contrary to it in many places, and their situation in the time of our Lord reached the point where the Lord obligated them in this matter to declare them invalid. The word of God for the sake of their Sunnah, and from the covenant of the Lord they went to extremes in it to the point that they glorified these narrations more than what was written. In their books, the words of the sheikhs are more beloved than the words of the Torah, and some of the words of the Torah are good and some are not good, and the words of the sheikhs are all good, and their words are much better than the words of the prophets.
What they mean by the words of the sheikhs are the linguistic narrations that reached them through the sheikhs.

Also in their books is that what is written is like water, Musna, and Talmut, whose narrations are accurate in them, like fine wine. And also in their books, that the written law is like salt, Musna, and Talmut, like pepper and fresh acorns, and other sayings from which it is known that they venerate the linguistic narrations more than the written law, and they understand the word of God according to what is understood to be explained by these narrations, so the written law was to them in the status of a dead body, and the linguistic narrations in the status of the soul. Which has life, and they say that these narrations were originally that when God gave Moses the Torah, He also gave him the meanings of the Torah and commanded that he write the first, memorize the second, and convey to him the linguistic narration only, and this is how it was passed down generation after generation, and therefore they call the first the word “written law” and the second the word “linguistic law,” and the fatwas that are identical to these narrations they call the laws of Moses that were obtained on Mount Sinai, and they claim that Moses obtained the Torah for him in the forty days that was the call between him and God on Mount Sinai. Likewise, these linguistic narrations also occurred to him, and Moses brought them from the mountain and communicated them to the children of Israel. He sought Aaron in the tent after he had returned from the mountain, and he taught him the written law first, then the linguistic narrations, which are the meanings of the written law as he found them from God. And Aaron rose up after he had learned and sat on the right hand of Moses. Eleazar and Itamar, Aaron’s sons, entered and learned as their father had learned, and he said, one of them sat on the left of Moses and the other on the right of Aaron. So the seventy sheikhs came in and learned the two laws and sat in The Tabernacle, then the people who were eager to learn learned, then Moses stood up and Aaron read what he had learned and stood up, then Eleazar and Itamar read and stood up and then the sheikhs read

The Seventy did not learn about the people, so each of these people heard this law four times and memorized it well. Then, after they left, these people told the rest of the children of Israel, and they reported.

The written law was transmitted through writing, and they conveyed its meanings through narration to the second generation. The rulings in the written text were six hundred and thirteen, so they divided the law according to them, and they say that Moses gathered all the children of Israel on the first of the eleventh month of the fortieth year after the Exodus from Egypt and informed them of his death, and he commanded that if anyone forgets a statement of the divine law that he reached through me, he should come to me and ask me. Likewise, if anyone has an objection to a statement of the law, he should come to me so that I may raise that objection, and it was He was preoccupied with teaching for the rest of his life, meaning from the first of the eleventh month to the sixth of the twelfth month, and about the written and unwritten law. He gave the children of Israel thirteen copies of the written law, written by his own hand, by giving each group a copy, a copy, to remain preserved among them, generation after generation. He also gave the children of Levi another copy also, to remain preserved also in the temple. He read the unwritten law, I mean the linguistic narratives, to Joshua.

He ascended Mount Nebo on the seventh day of the month and died there. After the death of Moses, Joshua entrusted these narratives to the sheikhs, and they entrusted them to the prophets. One prophet passed them on to another prophet, until he conveyed Jeremiah to Baruch, and Baruch to Apology and Apology to the council of scholars, the last of whom was Simeon Zedek. He conveyed these narratives to Eneti Konos, who was to Josi the son of Josir, who was to Nathan the Areleite, and Joshua the son of Berechiah, who were to Yehuda ben

Yahya and Shimon the son of Shatah, and they are to Shemaya, and Abu Talion, and they are to Hilal, and he is to his son Shimon, and it is believed that this Simeon is the Simeon whom our Lord the Deliverer took in the hands when Mary brought him to the temple after the days of her purification had been completed, and he passed it on to his son Camliel, and this Camliel is the one from whom Paul learned, and he passed it on to his son Simeon, and he is to his son Camliel, and he is to his son Simeon, and he is to the Lord of Judah, rightly his son Dosh, and this Judah collected these narratives in A book called Old Man is finished.

(Then he said that the Jews hold this book in great esteem and believe that what is in it is all from God, revealed to Moses on Mount Sinai, like the written law, and therefore it is obligatory to submit just like it. Since this book was compiled, it has become completely popular among them through study and teaching, and their great scholars wrote two explanations of it, one in the third century in Jerusalem and the second at the beginning of the sixth century in Babylon. The name of both of these explanations is Kamralan, meaning Kamra in the language, perfection, and complete clarification of the text has been achieved. In these two explanations, in their opinion, if the explanation and the text are combined, this combination is called Talmut, and it is said to distinguish between Talmut Jerusalem and Talmut Babylon, and this was their doctrine.

The entire trend now is included in these two Talmuths, about which the prophets wrote, and since the Talmuth of Jerusalem was closed, therefore now the Talmuth of Babylon is considered by them to be redundant.) End and Horn said in the seventh chapter of the first part of the second volume of his interpretation, printed in 1822: (We have come across a book that contains the various narrations of the Jews and explanations of the texts of the Holy Books, and they believed in his right that when God gave Moses the Torah on Mount Mount Sinai, he also gave him these narrations at that time, and it reached from Moses to Aaron, Eleazar, and Joshua, and from them to the other prophets, and from these prophets to the other sheikhs, and so it reached from generation to generation until it reached Simeon, and this is Shimon, who took our Lord the Deliverer in his hands, and it reached from him to Kamliel, and from him to Yehuda Haqdush. That is, the Holy One, and it was compiled at the end of the second century with difficulty over forty years in a book, and this book has been used from this time part after part by the Jews, and the importance of this book is often greater than the written law.) End quote.

(Then he said upon Musna two explanations, each of which is called Kamra. One of them is Kamra of Jerusalem, which was written in Jerusalem according to the opinion of some scholars in the third century and according to the opinion of Fadermon in the fifth century. The second is Kamra of Babylon, which was written in the sixth century in Babylon. This Kamra is full of weak tales, but among the Jews he is considered great and his study and teaching are popular among them. They return to him in every problem, submitting to him as a guide for them. It is called Kamra because the meaning of Kamra is perfection, and they thought that this explanation was great. The Torah is perfect, and there cannot be a better explanation than it, and there is no need for another explanation, and if the text is joined with the gram of Jerusalem, the combination is called Talmut Jerusalem, and if the gram is joined with it is the gram of Babylon, the combination is called Talmut Babylon.)
Finally, four things emerged from the writings of these two commentators:

(The first) is that the Jews consider the linguistic narration to be like the Torah, and in fact they often venerate it in excess of it and understand that it is in the status of the soul and the Torah is in the status of the body. If the state of the Torah is like this, then what is the status of the other books?

(The second) is that these narrations were collected by Yehuda Haq-Dush at the end of the second century and were preserved in linguistic preservation for one thousand seven hundred years. During this period, great calamities and grave wrongdoings befell the Jews, such as the incident of Bakht Nasr.

Enitochus, Titus, and others, such that the continuity in these incidents ceased and the books were lost, as they were known in the second chapter, and yet they consider them to be more than the Torah.

(And the third) that these narrations in most classes are narrated with one single narration, such as Kalmiel the first and the second, Shimon the second and the third. These were not among the prophets among the Jews, and among the Christians they were among the most staunch infidels who denied Christ. However, for the Jews, these narrations are the basis of faith and the origin of beliefs, and with us the authentic hadith narrated by single narrations is not the basis of beliefs.

(And the fourth) that when Kamra Babel wrote in the sixth century, his weak tales, according to Horn, were preserved in linguistic narration only for a period of more than two thousand. If you knew the condition of the Jews, according to the confession of the investigators of a Protestant faction, then know now the condition of the majority of ancient Christians. Yossi Bess, whose history is considered by Catholic and Protestant scholars, said in the ninth chapter of the second book of his history, published in the year 1848, on page 87, in Statement of the Condition of Jacob the Apostle (that Clemens transmitted a memorized story in his seventh book, Statement of the Condition of Jacob. It is apparent that Clemens transmitted this tale from the linguistic narratives that reached him from fathers and grandfathers).

Then, in Chapter Twenty-Three of the Third Book, 2 quoted Arrhenius’ statement on page 123: (The Church of Ephesus, which Paul built and in which John the Apostle resided until the era of the Sultanate of Tarjan, is a faithful witness to the hadiths of the Apostles.)

Then 3 on that page quoted what Clemens said: (Listen to a story about John the Apostle that is not false, but rather it is true and verified and has remained preserved in the hearts.) Then 4 said in the twenty-fourth chapter of the third book on page 126: (The disciples of Christ, like the twelve apostles, the seventy apostles, and many other people, were not unaware of the cases mentioned). That is, the cases written by the Evangelists (but only Matthew and John wrote them, and it is known from the linguistic narration that their editing was also due to necessity). Then he said 5 in the twenty-eighth chapter of the third book on page 132: (Arrhenius wrote in his third book a situation that he should have written, and this situation reached him from Eulycarp through linguistic narration). Then he said 6 in the fifth chapter of the fourth book on page 147: (I did not see the condition of the bishops of Jerusalem in order in a book, but it has been proven by linguistic narration that they remained for a short period). Then he said 7 in the thirty-sixth chapter of the third book on page 138: (It has reached us through the linguistic narration that when they took Ecnathioth to the Romans...

To kill him by throwing him into the hands of lions because he was a Christian and a Messianic man under the protection of the soldiers. Along the way, he strengthened the various churches with his advice and sayings and told them about the heresies that were widespread in those days or had occurred, and he advised them to adhere strongly to the linguistic narrations. He also recommended, for the sake of increased memorization, that he write these narrations and prove his testimony to them.

Then he said 8 in Chapter Thirty-Nine of the Third Book on page 142: “Bibbs said in the preface to his book: I write for your benefit all the things that came to me from the sheikhs and I preserved them after thorough investigation to prove their further verification by my testimony to them, because since ancient times I have not been satisfied with hearing hadiths from those who gossip a lot and teach other advice as well. Rather, I have heard hadiths from those who only know true advice that is narrated from our truthful Lord, and from those who I have met among His followers. The sheikhs asked him about this: What did he say about Andrew, or Peter, or Philip, or Thomas, or James, or Matthew, or another one of our Lord’s disciples, or Aristion, or the priest John, our Lord’s disciple, because the benefit I gained from the tongues of loved ones is what I gained from the books). Then he said 9 in the eighth chapter of the fourth book on page 151: (Hegesi Bos is a famous church historian and many things have been quoted from his writings.)
He transmitted them from the disciples using linguistic narrations, and this author wrote the issues of the disciples that reached him through linguistic narrations, in easy terms, in five books.

Then 10 in the fourteenth chapter of the fourth book quoted what Arrhenius said in explaining Polycarte’s situation on page 158: (Policarte always taught what he learned from the apostles, and the church conveyed the narration to him, and it was an honest matter.) Then he quoted 11 in the sixth chapter of the fifth book from the words of Arinus, a catalog of the Roman bishops, and said on page 201: (Now to Thyros, its twelfth bishop in the series through which the truthfulness and linguistic narrations from the Apostles have reached us). Then, in Chapter Eleven of Book Five, 12 quoted Clemens’ statement on page 206: (I did not write these books to seek exaltation, but rather out of suspicion of my old age and to be antidotes to my forgetfulness. I collected them on the path of interpretation as if they were explanations of the inspired issues that I became esteemed after I learned them from the blessed, truthful people. Among them was Puni Kos, who was in Greece, and the other who was residing in Mycenaean Crescia. One of them was Syriac and the other was Egyptian, and the rest were residents of the East. One of them was an Assyrian, one of them was a Hebrew from the people of Palestine, and the sheikh who

Another person arrived at his service who had disappeared in Egypt and he was better than all the sheikhs, and I did not ask for another sheikh after him because no one was better than him, and these sheikhs preserved the true narrations that were transmitted from Peter, James, John and Paul, generation after generation.

Then 13 in Chapter 20 of Book Five quoted what Arrhenius said on page 219: (By the grace of God, I heard these hadiths with complete attention and wrote them in my heart, not on paper, and it has been my habit since ancient times to repeat them religiously.) Then he said 14 in the twenty-fourth chapter of the fifth book on page 222: (Policecrates the bishop wrote a narration that reached him via the linguistic narration in his book that he sent to Kathar and the Roman Church). Then he said 15 in the twenty-fifth chapter of the fifth book on page 226: (Narcthus, Theophilus, and Cassius, among the bishops of Palestine, and the bishop of the Church of Assur, and the bishop of Tolmae Clarus, and the other people who came with these bishops presented many things in truth to the story that reached them in the Easter chapter from the Apostles, transmitted by the linguistic narrative, generation after generation. And they wrote at the end of the book that they sent our saying to the churches, so that there would be no place left for those who quickly stray from the straight path. escape). Then he said 16 in the thirteenth chapter of the sixth book, in the statement of the condition of Clemens Alexandrianus, who was a follower of the followers of the Apostles, on page 246: (He said in his book, which was written in the statement of Easter, that the beloved asked me to write for the benefit of future generations, the accounts that I heard from the bishops).

Then he said 17 in Chapter Thirty-One of the Sixth Book on page 263: (Evricatus in his letter, which exists to this day and which he sent to Aristides, explains the application between the statements of Matthew and Luke in the lineage of Christ, considering the narration that reached him from the fathers and grandfathers) His words ended.

It was learned from his seventeen sayings that the ancient Christians held the novel in great regard. Jean Melter Catalc said in his book, which was printed in the country of Derby in the year 1843, in his tenth letter that he sent to James Brune: (I also wrote before that the basis of the faith of Catalc is not only the written word of God, but more generally, whether written or unwritten, meaning the Holy Books and the linguistic narratives as explained by the Catalc Church). Then he said in that letter 2 (Arrhenius said in the fifth chapter of the third volume of his book that there is no easier matter for those seeking the truth than to investigate in every church the linguistic narrations that were transmitted from the Apostles and that they demonstrated throughout the world). Then he said in that letter 3: (Arrhenius said in the third chapter of the first volume of his book that the tongues of the peoples, even if they are different, but the truth of the linguistic narrative in every place are united. The Germanic churches are not different in teaching and doctrine from the churches of France, Spain, the Levant, Egypt, and Libya.)

Then he said in that letter 4: (Arrhenius said in the second chapter of the third volume, and since editing the chains of all the churches leads to lengthening, therefore we return to the narrative and doctrine of the Roman Church, which is ancient, great, and very famous, and was built by Peter and Paul, and all the churches agree with it, because the linguistic narratives transmitted from the Apostles, generation after generation, are all preserved in it.)

Then he said in that letter 5: (Arrhenius said in the sixty-fourth chapter of the fourth book, and if we assume that the Apostles did not leave the books to us, then we say that it was not necessary for us to obey the rulings that were proven by the linguistic narration that was transmitted from the Apostles and they handed it over to the people who handed it over to the church, and these narrations are what the brutalists who believed in Christ worked according to without using letters and ink.)

Then he said in that letter 6: (Tertoline said in his book, which he wrote to refute the people of heresy and was printed in the country of Rahnan, on pages 36 and 37: It is the custom of the people of heresy that they cling to the Holy Books and infer and say that there is nothing other than the written Holy Books capable of making the building of faith, and it is said according to it. With this trick, they incapacitate the strong, throw the weak into their nets, and cause the average to fall into doubt. Therefore, we say, never allow these people to debate. They use the Holy Books as evidence, because the discussion that takes place through the Holy Books does not result in any benefit other than that the brain and stomach become empty. Therefore, the method of referring to the Holy Books is wrong, because there is no separation of a matter from these books, and if something happens, it will be in the incomplete manner, and if this matter were not also the case, then the method of discussion in that form also would be to first verify that the Holy Books have a relationship with which people.

And anyone at any time conveyed the story due to which we became Christians, because the place where the provisions and doctrines of the Christian religion are found is where the truth of the Gospel, its meanings, and all the narratives of the Christian religion that are linguistic are found. Then he said in that letter 7: (Arjun said that it is not appropriate for us to consider people who quote from the Holy Books and then say that the discussion is in your home, so look into it, because it is not appropriate for us to abandon the first narration that is in the church or to believe other than what has been conveyed to us by the churches of God through a serial narration). Then he said in that letter 8: Basil wrote that the many issues preserved in the church that he preaches on were taken from the Holy Books and some from linguistic narrations, and their strength in religion is equal, and whoever has some understanding of the Issawi law does not object to this.

Then he said in that letter: Abu Fanis said in his book that he wrote about interviewing innovators: “Let us use the linguistic narration because all things are not found in the holy books.” Then he said in that Epistle 19: (Chrysostom stated in the explanation of the fourteenth verse 3 of the second chapter of the Second Epistle to the Thessalonians that it clearly appears from this that the Apostles did not communicate all things to us through editing, but rather they communicated many things without editing as well, and both are equal in consideration and therefore
Let us note that the Church’s narration is the source of faith, and if something is proven by the linguistic narration, we do not ask for anything more than that.

Then he said in that letter 11: (Eckstein wrote regarding the person to whom the dyeing occurred from among the innovators that even if there is no editorial support in this section, but let him note that this drawing was taken from the linguistic narration because many things the general church accepts were decided by the disciples and they are not written). Then he said in that letter 12: (The bishop, even if he enacted, said: Let the innovators interpret the sacred books according to the general narrative of the Church.) His words ended. It is learned from his twelve sayings that the linguistic narrations are the basis of the faith of the Katlik sect and were respected by the ancients. On page 64 of the third volume of the Catalak Herald: (Rabb Musa Qudsi cited many evidences that the text of sacred speech cannot be understood without the aid of hadith and linguistic narration, and the sheikhs of Catalak imitated this rule at all times).

[2] (And Tertuline said, “Let him return to understanding the thing that Christ taught the Apostles to the churches that the Apostles built and taught them with their writings and linguistic narrations.” He concluded. He learned from these aforementioned expressions that the Jews’ veneration of narrations and hadiths is greater than their veneration of the Torah, and that the majority of Christian ancients such as Clemens, Arrhenius, Hegesibus, Polycarp, Polycrates, Tarctus, Theophilus, Cassius, Clarus, Clemens Alexandrianus, and Evricanus

Tertuline, Argen, Basilinus, Abu Fannes, Chrysostom, Eccsteine, Saint Bishop, and others glorified and respected linguistic narratives. And Ecnathius had one of his commandments at the end of his life to cling strongly to linguistic narratives. Clemens said in describing his sheikhs that they preserved the true narratives narrated from Peter, James, John, and Paul, generation after generation. And Abu Fannes said, “The benefit I gained from the tongues of the living is what I gained from them.” Books, and Arinus said, I heard the hadiths, thanks to God, with complete attention, and I wrote them down in my heart, not on paper, and it has been my habit since ancient times to always repeat them religiously. He also said that there is nothing easier for those seeking the truth than to investigate in every church the linguistic narrations that were transmitted from the disciples and they showed them in the whole world. He also said, if we assume that the apostles did not leave the books to us, then we say that it was not necessary for us to obey the rulings that were proven by the linguistic narrations that are Quoted from the disciples, Ergen and Tertuline are blamed on the deniers of the hadiths, Basil said the issues taken from the holy books and the hadiths are both equal in strength, and Chrysostom said both are equal in consideration and the church’s narration is the source of faith, and if something is proven by the linguistic narration then we do not ask for anything more than it.
Waxstein stated that many things are given

The general church said that the Apostles decided that it was not written, so it is fair that everyone’s response is not free of fanaticism and ignorance, and their Gospel also belies this matter in the verse.

[1] The thirty-fourth chapter of the fourth chapter of the Gospel of Mark is like this: (He did not speak to them without a parable, or in private, but he explained everything to his disciples.) It is unlikely that all or some of these explanations were narrated, and that the apostles were in need of interpretation, and our contemporaries were not like that.

[2] And the twenty-fifth verse of the twenty-first chapter of the Gospel of John is like this: (And many other things that Jesus did, if they were written down one by one. I do not think that the world itself could contain the written books, and the words of the Gospel, even if they are not devoid of exaggeration and exaggeration, but there is no doubt that what He said and many other things includes all of Christ’s deeds, whether miracles or otherwise, and it is unlikely that any of them will be narrated by linguistic narration).

[3] And the fifteenth verse of the second chapter of the Second Epistle to the Thessalonians is as follows: (Therefore, brothers, stand firm and hold fast to the teachings that you have learned, whether through words or through our letter). His statement, whether it was through words or through our message, clearly indicates that some things reached them through editing and some through oral speech, so both must be considered by Christians, as Chrysostom stated in explaining this topic, as I know.
[4] And in the thirty-fourth verse of the eleventh chapter of the first letter
To the people of Fornithos in the Arabic translation printed in 1844 as follows:

(As for the rest of the things, I will recommend them to you when I come to you.) It is clear that these remaining things he commanded them verbally when he came to them, and these were not written down, and it is unlikely that any of them will be narrated.

[5] And the thirteenth verse of the first chapter of the Second Epistle to Timothy is thus: (Hold fast the form of the sound words which you have heard from me in the faith and love that are in Christ Jesus). What he said from me indicates that he heard some things orally.

[6] And the second verse of the second chapter of the aforementioned letter is thus: And what you heard from me through many witnesses, entrust to faithful people who will be competent to teach others also.) Here their sanctifier commands Timothy to teach faithful people the conversations that he heard from him, and for the faithful to teach other people, so these accounts must be narrated.

(7) And at the end of the second letter to John, it is as follows: (Since I had much to write to you, I did not want it to be on paper and ink; for I hope to come to you and speak with the mouth, so that our joy may be complete.)

[8] And at the end of the third letter, thus: (And I have much to write, but I do not want to write to you with ink and pen, but I hope to see you soon, and we will speak with the mouth). These two verses indicate that John said many things orally.

What is promised and far-fetched is that all or some of these things are not narrated in a narration. It appears from what we have mentioned that whoever from a Protestant sect denies the absolute consideration of hadiths in the Christian religion is either ignorant or arbitrarily stubborn, and his statement contradicts his holy books and the majority of his ancient scholars, and he is included in the group of innovators according to what some of the ancients say. However, he must take them into account in many of his sect’s obsessions, such as that the Son is equal to the Father in essence, that the Holy Spirit is separated from the Father and the Son, that Christ has two natures and one hypostasis, and that He has two natures and one hypostasis. Two divine and human wills, and that after he died he descended into Hell, and other of their obsessions, even though these words are not found specifically in the New Testament, and they believed these matters only from hadiths and traditions, and also he is required to deny many parts of his holy books, such as denying the Gospel of Mark and Luke and nineteen chapters of the Book of Acts of the Apostles, because they were written by linguistic narrations, not by observation or revelation, as was known in the first chapter, and such as denying five chapters from the twenty-fifth to the twenty-ninth of the Book of Proverbs because they were collected during the reign of Hezekiah from the linguistic narratives that were current among them, and between the time of collection and the death of Solomon, peace be upon him, there was a period of two hundred and seventy years.

The first verse of the twenty-fifth chapter of the aforementioned book is thus: These are also the proverbs of Solomon that were written down by the friends of Hezekiah, king of Judah. Adam Clarke, the commentator, said in his commentary printed in the year 1851 at the end of the explanation of this verse: (It is known that at the end of this book there are proverbs collected by order of the Sultan Hezekiah from the linguistic narrations that were current from the time of Solomon, so they collected these proverbs from them and made them an enclosure of this book, and it is possible that what is meant by Hezekiah’s friends is Isaiah, Sheniah, and others. Of the prophets who were in that era.

So that enclosure, like the remaining book, would be a document. Otherwise, how could they have included it in the Holy Book?) End quote. His saying, “I collected authority from the linguistic narrations by Hezekiah’s command,” is clear in what I said, and his saying, “And it could be what is meant,” etc., is rejected because it is merely a possibility that is not fulfilled by the violator without a complete chain of transmission, and he does not have any support. Rather, he says it is a possibility and presumed by the unseen, and his saying, “How did they include it in the Holy Book,” is rejected, because the Jews had more regard for the narratives than for the Torah, so if the Torah becomes a support. According to them, it is considered valid even though it was collected from the narrations of the sheikhs after approximately one thousand seven hundred years. Likewise, the stories of Kamra-Babylon became considered valid even though they were collected after two thousand years. So what prevents them from considering the five chapters that were compiled after two hundred and seventy years? Some of the investigators from Protestant scholars have been fair and admitted that the linguistic narrations are also considered valid, such as what is written on page 63 of the second volume of the Catalan Herald thus: (Indeed, Dr.

Brett, who is one of the distinguished Protestants, said on page 73 of his book that this matter is clear from the holy books, that the Isawi religion became delegated to the early bishops and the followers of the Apostles with the linguistic narration, and they were commanded to preserve it and delegate it to the later generation. It is not proven from a holy book, whether it was the book of Paul or other Apostles, that they wrote together or individually all the things that have anything to do with salvation, and they made a law from which it is understood that there is nothing in it that is necessary and has anything to do with salvation other than What was written, and he said on pages 32 and 33 of the aforementioned book: You see that Paul and the other disciples said that just as they conveyed the hadiths to us by means of editing, so they also conveyed them by means of linguistic narration, and woe to those who do not memorize them, and the Isawiya hadiths in the matter of faith are as reliable as the written ones. End of Dakterpreet’s words.

The Bishop of Mon Neck said: (The hadiths of the Apostles are as reliable as their writings, and no Protestant denies that the linguistic report of the Apostles is more liberating than their liberation.) And Jelnick and Rtah said: (This dispute is that any canonical Gospel and any non-canonical Gospel are eliminated by the linguistic narration, which is the basis of fairness for every dispute.) End of Kathlak Harald’s words. The priest Tames Ankles Katlik said on pages 180 and 181 of his book called The Mirror of Honesty, published in 1851: (The Bishop of Mani Sik, a Protestant scholar, bears witness to the fact that six hundred matters have been decided by God in religion and the Church is commanded to do them, and it is accepted in her right that the Holy Book has stated them in place and what she has done.) End quote. According to the confession of this eminent person, there are six hundred matters that have been proven by linguistic narration and which must be accepted by a group of Protestants.

(Second benefit): This matter is clear from correct experience that a matter that is strange or something that people are interested in is remembered by most people, and otherwise it does not remain preserved in most cases due to lack of interest. Therefore, if you ask people who are not accustomed to eating one specific food or specific foods, “What did you eat yesterday or the day before yesterday?” it will not be remembered by most of them due to interest in this matter and not being wondrous or great. This is the case in most public actions and public sayings, and if you ask about the condition of the star that was one of the tailed stars and appeared in the month of Safar in the year 1259 AH and the month of March 1843 AD. It was visible in the atmosphere for a month and was extremely long. It was preserved for many who saw it, even if it was not the month of its appearance, and its year was preserved for them, and more than twenty-one years had passed since it had passed. This was also the case with great earthquakes, severe wars, and rare events. And since the interest of Muslims in memorizing the Qur’an in every century, there are also more than one hundred thousand memorizers of the Qur’an in this era in all Islamic lands, even if they have passed away. The Sultanate of the people of Islam is one of the largest countries of the kingdoms, and the apathy in religious matters has occurred in the largest of their countries. And whoever doubts this matter among the Christians should try it and enter the Al-Azhar Mosque only, and he will find at any time more than a thousand memorizers of the Qur’an who have memorized it with perfect Tajweed. And if he follows the villages of Egypt, he will not find any of the villages of the people of Islam that is devoid of memorizers of the Qur’an. He finds many mules and donkeys from the people of Egypt who are also memorizers of the Qur’an. If he is fair, he would absolutely admit that these donkeys are memorizers of the Qur’an. In this regard, the oppressors are superior to the Pope, the bishops, and the priests who exist in the East and West in this era, which is the era of widespread knowledge among Christians, not to mention the previous centuries of Christianity from the seventh generation to

The fifteenth generation, in which ignorance was like the slogan of scholars in those centuries, according to the confession of Protestant scholars, and my belief is that there are not in all the lands of Europe ten memorizers of the Bible, the Torah, or both, such that their memorization of one or both of them is equal to the memorization of the Qur’an by these mules and donkeys. I learned, in the first interest, what Arrhenius said that he said: (I heard, by the grace of God, these hadiths with complete attention, and I wrote them in my heart, not on paper, and it has been my habit since ancient times to repeat them. By religion). He also said: (Although the tongues of the peoples are different, the truth of the linguistic narrative is united in every place. The Germanic churches do not differ in teaching and beliefs from the churches of France, Spain, the Levant, Egypt, and Libya).

William Muir said in the third chapter of the History of Clesia, published in 1848: (The ancient Christians did not have a written doctrine of the faith whose belief was necessary for survival and which was taught to children and those who were entering the Christian religion in a linguistic manner. It has been preserved and there is no defect in it over a long period of time. This matter is clear in the Qur’an, and a period of one thousand two hundred has passed.

Eighty years, and just as it is preserved through writing in every century, so it is also preserved in every century through the breasts of thousands of men, and most of the Christian sects are in this time as well, such that if we observe the condition of their major scholars and their elite, as well as their common people, we will find that they do not get to recite their holy books. The teacher, Michael Mashaqa, one of the Protestant scholars, said in the conclusion of his book called The Guide to Obedience to the Bible, printed in the year 1849 on page 316: (One day I asked A priest (one of the priests of Katalak) was to answer me truthfully about reading the Bible and how many times he had read it during his life. He said that he sometimes read, and perhaps a number of books that he had not read, but for twelve years, due to his preoccupation with serving the parish, he did not have the opportunity to read it. It is not without the fact that many of the people know the ignorance of these clergy, but nevertheless they follow their advice in preventing them from reading the useful books that guide them to them.) His words ended with his words.

(The third benefit) The authentic hadith is also considered by the people of Islam in the manner that we will detail, and since the saying of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace (Beware of hadiths on my authority except what you know, whoever lies about me intentionally, let him take his seat in the Fire) is frequently narrated.

Sixty-two companions, including ten missionaries. The people of Islam were interested in the Prophetic hadiths from the first century, and their interest in memorizing the hadiths was greater than that of the Christians, just as their interest in memorizing the Qur’an in every century was greater than the Christians’ interest in memorizing their holy books. But the Companions did not write them down in the books during their time for some excuses, including complete caution so that the words of the Messenger would not be mixed with the words of God. Followers of the Companions such as Al-Zuhri, Al-Rabi’ bin Subaih, Saeed, and others, may God have mercy on them, began to write them down, but they did not write them down in the order of the chapters of jurisprudence. Since this arrangement was good, the followers followed this arrangement

The arrangement. Imam Malik, may God have mercy on him, who was born in the year ninety-five AH, compiled Al-Muwatta’ in Medina, Abu Muhammad Abd al-Malik bin Abd al-Aziz bin Jurayj compiled it in Mecca, Abd al-Rahman bin al-Awza’i in the Levant, and Sufyan al-Thawri.

In Kufa, and Hammad bin Salamah in Basra, then Al-Bukhari and Muslim compiled their Sahihs and confined themselves to mentioning authentic hadiths and leaving out other weak ones. The modern imams exerted great diligence in the matter of hadiths, and he compiled a great art in the names of men, by which he knew the condition of each narrator of the hadith, that is, how his condition was in religion and memorization, and each of the companions of the Sahihs narrated the hadiths with attribution from them to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Some of Al-Bukhari’s hadiths are three-part stories that reach the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, through three means.

The authentic hadith is divided into three categories: mutawatir [1], famous [2], and single narration [3]. Mutawatir is what was transmitted by a group from a group, and it is not permissible for reason to agree with them about lying. An example is the transmission of the numbers of rak’ahs of prayer, the amounts of zakat, and the like. What was famous was what was known in the era of the Companions, such as individual reports, then became famous in the era of the Successors or the era of the Followers, and the nation received it with acceptance in one of the last two eras, so it became as frequent, like stoning in the case of adultery. A single narration is what was reported by one person on the authority of one person, or by one person on the authority of a group, or a group on the authority of one person. The frequent ones necessitate definitive knowledge and denying it is disbelief. The well-known narration necessitates reassuring knowledge and denying it is heresy and immorality. The single narration does not necessitate either of the two sciences mentioned and is considered in the work, not in proving the beliefs and principles of religion. If it contradicts the definitive evidence, whether rational or narrational, it will be interpreted if it is possible to interpret it. Otherwise, it will be abandoned and the rational evidence will not be used. The difference between the authentic hadith and the Qur’an has three aspects: The first is that the entire Qur’an has been transmitted with frequent transmission as it was revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and what has been changed

They conveyed it word for word with another word that is synonymous with it, unlike the authentic hadith because it was also permissible for the trustworthy transmitter who was skilled in the language of the Arabs and the style of their speech to transmit it verbally, unlike the authentic hadith. The second is that since the entire Qur’an is mutawatir, disbelief is required by denying a portion of it as well, unlike the authentic hadith, for it does not require disbelief except by denying a section of it, which is mutawatir rather than the well-known and single narration. The third is that the rulings are related to the words of the Qur’an and its arrangements as well, such as the validity of prayer and the fact that its expression is a miracle, unlike the hadith, in which the rulings are not related. With his words. If you know what I mentioned about the three benefits, you will realize that it does not necessitate that we consider the hadith to be authentic in the aforementioned way with any obscurities or exclusions.

sections.heading: Chapter Four: Refuting the priests’ suspicions based on the hadiths
content: [Chapter Four: Refuting the suspicions of priests mentioned in the hadiths.]
There are five suspicions:

(The first suspicion) is that the narrators of the hadith are the wives of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his relatives and companions, and their testimony against him is not taken into account. (And the answer) is that this suspicion is refuted by them with the slightest change by saying that the narrators of the Christian cases and his sayings included in these Gospels are the mother of Jesus, peace be upon them, and his father, Al-Jaali, Yusuf Al-Najari and his disciples, and their testimony against him is not taken into account. And if they say that it is possible that the faith of Muhammad’s relatives, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions was for the sake of worldly leadership, I say that this possibility is invalid because until the age of thirteen, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, he was in extreme pain from harming the infidels and his companions. May God be pleased with them, they were also afflicted with the utmost harm for the period mentioned, until they left their homelands and migrated to Abyssinia and Medina, and it is inconceivable that any of them could imagine, for this period of time, the greed of this world. However, this possibility exists among the disciples as well, because they were poor fishermen, and they had heard from the Jews that the Messiah would be a great sultan. When Jesus, peace be upon them, claimed that he was the promised Messiah, they believed in him and understood that by following him, they would attain great positions and be saved from sin. The hardship of netting and catching, and when he promised them
Jesus, peace be upon him: (If I sit on the bed, you will also sit on twelve beds, judging the twelve tribes of Israel) as stated in the nineteenth chapter of the Gospel of Matthew.

And he promised them: (Whoever forsakes anything for My sake and for the sake of the Gospel will find it a hundredfold now in this time and will find eternal life in the age to come), as stated in the tenth chapter of the Gospel of Mark, and other things were promised. So they became certain that they would become sultans, each of whom would rule over one of the tribes of Israel, and if any of them missed something for the sake of following him, they would receive in this world a hundredfold of that thing in exchange for it. This matter was firmly established in their minds until Jacob and John requested the son of Zaidi, or I requested. Their mother - despite the differences in the narration of the two Gospels - was the position of great ministry, with one of them sitting on the right of Jesus, peace be upon him, and the other on his left in his kingdom, as stated in the twentieth chapter of the Gospel of Matthew, and the tenth chapter of the Gospel of Mark. But when they saw that they had not attained the imaginary authority nor a hundredfold in this world, nor had anything of the worldly state attained to him either, and he was poor, as he was afraid of the Jews and fleeing from place to place, and they saw that the Jews were about to take him and kill him, they realized that their understanding was wrong. The aforementioned dates are like a mirage that a thirsty person thinks is water. One of them agreed to exchange this imaginary sultanate and these imaginary times for thirty dirhams, which he took from the Jews on the condition that he hand it over to them. The rest of them left it when the Jews took it and fled, and they denied it three times. The most guiding and greatest of the disciples, who had built a church, cursed him.

And the shepherd of his sheep and his successor, I mean, His Eminence Peter, and he swore that I did not know him, and they became completely helpless from their imaginations after he was crucified, according to their claim. Then when they saw him again after the resurrection, their hope returned again, and they thought that they would become sultans this time, so they asked him together at the time of his ascension, saying: Will you restore the kingdom to Israel at this time? (As stated in the first chapter of the Book of Acts) and after the ascension, they fell into another fantasy that is greater than the earthly sultanate that had never been known. You get them to

The time of the ascension, which is that Christ will descend from heaven during their time, and that the Resurrection is near, as I learned in detail from the third and fourth chapters of the first chapter, and that after his descent the Antichrist will be killed and Satan will be imprisoned for a thousand years, and that they will sit on the beds after his descent and live a satisfactory life for the period mentioned in this world, as is understood from the nineteenth and twentieth chapters of the Book of Views, and the second verse of the sixth chapter of the first letter to the people of Corinthians, and then they will obtain permanent happiness in Paradise forever upon the Resurrection. Secondly, because of these matters, they exaggerated in their praise of him and the description of his conditions, as the fourth evangelist said at the end of his Gospel, (There are many other things that Jesus did, and if I wrote them down one by one, I do not think that the world itself could contain books.) There is no doubt that this is a pure lie and an ugly poetic exaggeration, so they exaggerated with proverbs.

These statements are to trap the foolish in their nets until they die without achieving their goal, so their testimony against him is not taken into account, and this report is a matter of obligation, not belief, as I have repeatedly stated. Just as this possibility regarding Jesus and his true disciples, peace be upon them, is invalid, so is their possibility regarding the companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, invalid. In order to confuse the common people, the priests may point to what the Twelver Imami sect says about the Companions, may God be pleased with them all, and the answer to it is obligatory and fulfilled in this way, or it is obligatory, because the historian Musheim said in the first volume of his history: (The Ebionite sect, which was in the first century, believed that Jesus, peace be upon him, was only a human being, born of Mary and Joseph the Najjar like other people, and obedience to the Mosaic law is not limited to the Jews only, but rather It is obligatory for others as well, and working on its provisions is necessary for survival.
Since Paul denied the necessity of this work

He used to quarrel with them in this regard with great intensity, and they used to disparage him severely and despise his writings in a severe manner. Lardner said on page 376 of the second volume of his interpretation: (The ancients told us that this group was rejecting Paul and his letters.) End quote. Bell said in his history in explaining this sect: (This sect accepted only the books of the Old Testament, the Torah, and was alienated from the names of David, Solomon, Jeremiah, and Ezekiel, peace be upon them. The New Testament at its time included only the Gospel of Matthew, but they distorted it in many places and took the first two chapters out of it.) He ended, and he said in his history in explaining the Marcian sect: (This sect believed that God was two gods, one of them the creator of good and the other the creator of evil. The Torah and all the books of the Old Testament said about the second god, all of which contradict the New Testament. Then he said that this sect believed that Jesus descended into Hell after his death and saved the souls of Cain and the people of Sodom from its torment because they came with him and did not obey the God, the Creator of evil. He kept the souls of Abel, Noah, Abraham, and the other righteous people in

Hell, because they were dissing the A-Team. She believed that the Creator of the world was not limited to the God who sent Jesus, and therefore she did not accept that the books of the Old Testament were inspired. She accepted only the Gospel of Luke from the New Testament, but she did not accept the first two chapters of it. She accepted ten letters from Paul’s letters, but she rejected what was contrary to her imagination. End quote.

In the third volume of his interpretation, Lardner quoted Eckstein's statement in the statement of the Mani Kabbaz sect as follows: (This sect says that the God who gave Moses the Torah and spoke to the Israelite prophets is not a god but rather a demon among the devils, and it accepts the books of the New Testament, but it acknowledges the occurrence of annexation to them and takes what it is satisfied with and leaves the rest and prefers some false books to it and says that they are absolutely true.) Then Lardner said in the aforementioned volume: (Historians agree that this entire sect did not accept the books. sacred to the Old Testament at all times).

He wrote in the works of Arklas the doctrine of this sect as follows: (Satan deceived the Jewish prophets, and Satan spoke to Moses and the Jewish prophets, and it adhered to the eighth verse of the tenth chapter of the Gospel of John, that Christ called them thieves and thieves, and it brought forth the New Testament.) End quote. This is the case with the other sects, but I contented myself with quoting the doctrines of the three mentioned sects based on the number of the Trinity, and I say whether the statements of these sects are accepted by Protestant scholars or not, and if they are, then they must believe in these ten matters:
[1] That Jesus, peace be upon him, is only a human being, born from Joseph Al-Najjar.
[2] Working on the provisions of the Torah is necessary for salvation.
[3] Paul is evil and his letters must be answered.
[4] And God is two gods, the Creator of good and the Creator of evil.

[5] The souls of Cain and the people of Sodom were saved from the torment of Hell with the death of Jesus, peace be upon him, and the souls of Abel, Noah, Abraham, and the ancient righteous people were tormented in Hell after his death as well.
[6] And that these people were obedient to Satan.
[7] The Torah and all the other books of the Old Testament are from Satan.
[8] And the one who spoke to Moses and the Israeli prophets is not a god but a devil.
[9] The books of the New Testament were distorted by addition.

[10] And some false books are absolutely true, and if the statements of these sects do not apply to them, then the statements of some Islamic sects do not apply to the majority of the people of Islam, especially if this statement contradicts the Qur’an and the sayings of the pure Imams, may God be pleased with them as well, as you will know. (1)
If you know this, then I say that the Qur’an states that the great companions, may God be pleased with them, did not do anything that would necessitate disbelief and take them away from faith.

1- God Almighty said in Surat Al-Tawbah: {And the first forerunners of the immigrants and the Ansar and those who followed them in righteousness. May God be pleased with them and they will be pleased with Him. And He prepared for them Gardens beneath which rivers flow, to abide therein forever. That is the great victory.} So God said about the first forerunners of the Emigrants and the Ansar four things: (The first) His satisfaction with them (and the second) Their satisfaction with Him.

(1) The author of the book said to Al-Shamila: In some copies here is an addition that is not in the printed version, which is: As for the answer to it in order to verify it, it is because the Glorious Qur’an according to the majority of Twelver Imami Shiite scholars is preserved from change and alteration, and whoever among them says that a deficiency occurred in it, his statement is rejected and not accepted by them. [1] Sheikh Al-Saduq Abu Jaafar Muhammad bin Ali bin Babawayh, who is one of the greatest Twelver Imami Shiite scholars, said in his message of belief: (Our belief in the Qur’an is that the Qur’an that God Almighty revealed to His Prophet is what is between the two covers, and it is what is in the hands of the people, and it is not more than that, and the amount of its surahs among the people is one hundred and fourteen surahs, and with us is Al-Dhuha, and did we not explain one surah, and to Al-Ilaaf, and did you not see how one surah is, and whoever attributes to us that we say that it is more than that is a liar.) End quote. [2] And in the interpretation of Majma’ Al-Bayan, which is an accepted interpretation among the Shiites: (The eminent master, Al-Murtada Alam Al-Huda, the Majestic Abu Al-Qasim Ali bin Al-Hussein Al-Musawi, mentioned that the Qur’an was collected during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, compiled as it is now. He inferred from that that the Qur’an was studied and memorized in its entirety at that time until he appointed a group of companions to memorize them, and that it was presented to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and recited to him, and that a group of companions such as Abdullah bin Masoud, Ubayy bin Ka’b, and others completed the Qur’an before the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Several conclusions, and all of this with the slightest contemplation indicates that it was an organized collection, not published or transmitted, and it was mentioned that whoever disagreed from the Imamis and the Hashawiyyah should not be taken into account, because the disagreement is related to a group of hadith scholars who reported weak reports that they thought were authentic, and the like of them cannot be returned from what is known to be confirmed as authentic.) End quote. [3] Al-Sayyid al-Murtada also said: (Knowledge of the authenticity of the Qur’an is like knowledge of countries, great events, great and well-known events, and the written poetry of the Arabs.
