His meandaka is the Qur’an of Darghaya and the highest degree of transmission of Budh and thousands of companions who memorized and transmitted the history of the Messenger of Khuda, may God bless him and grant him peace, compiled and authored by Budh.” It's over. It has become apparent that the established doctrine among the scholars of the Twelver Imami sect is that the Qur’an that God revealed to His Prophet is what is between the two books and that it is what is in the hands of people and nothing more than that, and that it was a collection and compilation during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and was preserved and transmitted by thousands of companions and a group of companions such as Abdullah bin Masoud, Ubayy bin Ka’b and others sealed the Qur’an with the Prophet several seals and the Qur’an appears and is made public in this order when the twelfth Imam, may God bless him and grant him peace, appeared. God bless him and the few fragments that said the change had occurred. Their statement is rejected and cannot be taken into account among themselves, and some of the weak reports that were narrated in their doctrine cannot be referred to as the same from what is known and is true, because if a single report requires knowledge and there is nothing in the conclusive evidence that indicates it, it must be rejected, as Ibn Al-Mutahhar Al-Hilli stated in his book called (The Principles of Access to the Knowledge of Fundamentals), and God Almighty said: {Indeed, it is We who have sent down the Remembrance, and indeed We will preserve it}. In the interpretation of the straight path, which is an interpretation considered by Shiite scholars (meaning, We will protect it from distortion, alteration, addition, or subtraction). I finish.

(And the third) is their good tidings of Paradise (and the fourth) is the promise of their eternity there. There is no doubt that Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq, Omar Al-Faruq, and Uthman Dhu Al-Nourin, may God be pleased with them, were among the first and foremost among the immigrants, just as the Commander of the Faithful, Ali, may God be pleased with him, was among them, so these four matters were confirmed for them and the validity of their caliphate was confirmed, so the statement of the challenger regarding the three, may God be pleased with them, is rejected, just as the statement of the challenger regarding the fourth, may God be pleased with him, is rejected.

2- God Almighty also said in Surat Al-Tawbah: {Those who believe and emigrate and strive in the cause of God with their wealth and their lives are of the highest rank with God. And those are the winners. Their Lord gives them good tidings of mercy from Him and His satisfaction and gardens for them therein abiding bliss, wherein they will abide forever. Indeed, with God is a great reward.} So God said about the believers who emigrate and strive in the cause of God with their money and their lives four things: (the first) that their rank is greater with God (and the second) that they are winners. What they mean (and the third) is that they are brought good tidings of mercy, contentment, and gardens

(And the fourth) their eternity in Paradise forever. The fourth matter was extremely emphasized with three expressions, I mean his saying “residing,” his saying “they will abide therein forever,” and his saying [a great reward]. There is no doubt that the three caliphs, may God be pleased with them, were among the believers who emigrated and struggled in the cause of God with their money and their lives, just as Ali, may God be pleased with him, was among them, so the four matters were confirmed for them.

3- God Almighty also said in Surat Al-Tawbah: {But the Messenger and those who believed with him struggled with their wealth and their lives, and those are the ones who are good, and those are the successful. God has prepared for them Gardens beneath which rivers flow, in which they will abide. That is the great victory} So God said about the struggling believers four things: (The first) that good things are theirs (and the second) that they are successful.

(And the third) is the promise of gardens (and the fourth) is their eternity therein. There is no doubt that the three, may God be pleased with them, are among the mujahideen believers, so these four matters have been confirmed for them.

4- God Almighty also said in Surat Al-Tawbah: {Indeed, God has purchased from the believers their souls and their wealth that they will have Paradise. They fight in the cause of God, so they kill and are killed, a promise that is binding on Him in the Torah, the Gospel, and the Qur’an. And who is more faithful to His covenant than God? So rejoice in your pledge with which you pledged your pledge. And that is the great victory. The repentant, the worshipers, the praisers, the wanderers, the ones who kneel and prostrate, those who enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, and who keep God’s limits, and give good news to the believers. So God promised Paradise to the striving believers as a confirmed promise and mentioned nine descriptions of them, so it was proven that they were like that and they will win Paradise.

5- And God said in Surat Al-Hajj: {Those who, if We empowered them in the land, established prayer and paid zakat and enjoined what was right and forbade what was wrong, and God is the end of all matters.} So his saying “Who if We empowered them” is a description of those who came before, and His saying “those who were expelled” means what is meant by the emigrants, not the Ansar, because they were not expelled from their homes. So God described the emigrants as saying that if He empowered them in the land and gave them authority, they would do the four things, which are establishing prayer, paying zakat, and commanding. With what is right and forbidding what is wrong, but it has been proven that God empowered the four caliphs, may God be pleased with them, on earth, so it is necessary that they bring the four things, and if they were like that, it is proven that they

On the truth, and in his saying to God is the outcome of matters is an indication that the one mentioned above regarding their empowerment on earth will inevitably come to pass, and then matters will be returned to God Almighty with the outcome, for He is the One whose dominion will never cease.

6- God Almighty said in Surat Al-Hajj: {And strive for the sake of God as He deserves to struggle. He has chosen you and has not placed upon you in religion any hardship to the religion of your father Abraham. He called you Muslims before and in this so that the Messenger may be a witness over you and that you may be witnesses over the people, so establish prayer and pay the poor-rate and hold fast to God. He is your Master. So what a good Master and what a good Helper} So God in this verse called the Companions Muslims.

7- God Almighty said in Surah An-Nur: {God promised those of you who believe and do righteous deeds that He will surely appoint them as successors in the land just as He made those before them successors, and will establish for them their religion which He has chosen for them, and will replace them with security after their fear. They will worship Me, not associating anything with Me. And whoever disbelieves after that - those are the transgressors.} And the word “who” in his saying of you to disdain and how much is the pronoun of the address indicates that what is meant by this address are some of the believers who were present at the time of the revelation of this. The surah is not the whole, and the word succession indicates that the fulfillment of that promise will take place after the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, and it is known that there will be no prophet after him because he is the seal of the prophets. What is meant by this succession is the method of imamate, and the pronouns referring to them in his saying “let them succeed them” to his saying “they do not associate” are all in the plural form, and the plural in reality is not.

It is taken as less than three, so it indicates that these imams promised to them will not be less than three, and his saying, “He will make it possible for them,” etc., is a promise to them of gaining power, strength, and access to the world, which indicates that they will be strong, strong, and effective in the world. They are not in fear and piety, and his saying, “They worship Me and do not associate anything with Me” indicates that during their caliphate they would also be believers, not polytheists.

So the verse indicates the validity of the imamate of the four imams, may God be pleased with them, especially the three caliphs, I mean Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, Omar al-Faruq, and Uthman Dhul-Nurayn, may God be pleased with them, because the great conquests, complete empowerment, the emergence of religion and the security that were during their era were not during the era of the Commander of the Faithful Ali, may God be pleased with him, because he was busy fighting the people of prayer during his honorable era. It is proven that what the Shiites say about the three, may God be pleased with them, or the Kharijites about Uthman and Ali, may God be pleased with them. God has an undeniable statement about them.

8- God Almighty said in Surat Al-Fath regarding the immigrants and Ansar who were with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah: {When those who disbelieved put in their hearts the fever of ignorance, then God sent down His tranquility upon His Messenger and upon the believers and made them obligated to the word of piety and they were more deserving of it and its people. And God is All-Knowing of all things.} So He said about them four things:

(First) They are partners with the Messenger in the descent of tranquility. (The second) They are believers. (Third) The word piety is necessary and indispensable to them. (And fourth) that they were more deserving of the word of piety and its people, and there is no doubt that Abu Bakr and Omar, may God be pleased with them, were among these immigrants, so these four matters were confirmed for them and for the rest of them, and whoever believes in their rights other than these, his belief is invalid and contradicts the Qur’an.

9- God Almighty also said in Surah Al-Fath: {Muhammad is the Messenger of God and those with him are hard against the disbelievers and merciful among themselves. You will see them bowing down and prostrating, seeking the bounty of God and His pleasure. Their marks are on their faces from the effect of prostration.}

He praised the Companions for being tough on the infidels and merciful to each other, and for being kneeling and prostrating, and seeking God’s grace and pleasure. Whoever claims to be an Islamic believer in their regard other than this is mistaken.

10- God Almighty said in Surat Al-Hujurat: {But God has endeared faith to you and beautified it in your hearts, and has made disbelief, immorality and disobedience hateful to you. These are the rightly guided}. He knew that the Companions were lovers of faith and hated disbelief, immorality, and disobedience, and they were mature adults, so believing against these things regarding them is wrong.

11- And God Almighty said in Surat Al-Hashr: {For the poor immigrants who were expelled from their homes and their wealth, seeking God’s bounty and satisfaction, and supporting God and His Messenger - these are the truthful. And those who lived in the abode and the faith before them love those who emigrated to them, and do not find in their hearts any need for what they came to, and prefer to themselves, even if they are in poverty.

So God praised the immigrants and the Ansar in six ways: (The first) that the migration of these immigrants was not for the sake of this world, but rather it was for the sake of seeking God’s pleasure. (The second) is that they were supporters of the religion of God and His Messenger. (And third) that they were honest in word and deed. (And fourth) that the Ansar loved those who migrated to them. (Fifth) They were happy if something happened to the immigrants.

(And sixth) that they used to put them ahead of themselves when they were in need, and these six descriptions indicate the perfection of faith, and whoever believes in their rights other than this is mistaken, and these poor emigrants used to say to Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, O successor of the Messenger of God, and God bears witness to their being truthful, so they must be truthful in this statement as well, and when that is the case, it is necessary to assert the validity of his imamate.
12- God Almighty said in Surat Al Imran: {You are the best nation raised for mankind, enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong and believing in God}.

God praised the Companions with three descriptions: (The first) that they were the best nation. (The second) is that they used to enjoin good and forbid evil. (And third) that they were believers in God, and so are the other verses, but for fear of lengthening, I will suffice with twelve places based on the number of disciples of Jesus, peace be upon him, and the number of the twelve pure imams, may God be pleased with them all.
I quote five sayings from the sayings of the Ahl al-Bayt, peace be upon them, based on the number of the five pure ones, peace be upon them.
-[1] In Nahj al-Balagha, which is a book considered by the Shiites, Ali Radi said

God said about him like this: (To God, so-and-so turned, so he 1: made people of the wicked, 2: healed the wickedness, 3: established the Sunnah, 4: removed innovation, 5: pure gold, 6: few blemishes, 7: achieved its good, 8: preceded its evil, 9: led to obedience to God, 10: and feared Him according to His truth. He departed and left them on ramified paths in which the lost person does not find guidance or gain certainty. Al-Muhtadi) finished.

What is meant by so-and-so is the chosen one of most of the commentators, including Al-Bahrani, Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with him, and the chosen one of some of the commentators, Omar Al-Farouq, may God be pleased with him. Ali, may God be pleased with him, mentioned ten descriptions of the descriptions of Abu Bakr or Omar, may God be pleased with him, so they must exist, and since these descriptions of him were proven after his death by the approval of Ali, may God be pleased with him, there remained no doubt about the validity of his caliphate.
-[2] And in Kashf Al-Ghumma, which is the classification of Ali bin Isa Al-Ardebili Al-Athni

Ashri, who is one of the virtuous people accepted by the Imamis (Imam Ja`far, peace be upon him, was asked about wearing a sword, is it permissible? He said: Yes, Abu Bakr al-Siddiq has adorned his sword. The narrator said: Do you say like this? Then the Imam jumped up from his place and said: Yes, the friend, yes, the friend, yes, the friend - whoever does not say to him al-Siddiq, then God will not make his statement true in this world and the hereafter.) It was proven by Imam Al-Hammam’s statement that Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with him, is a true friend, and those who deny him are liars in this world and the hereafter.

-[3] In some of Ali’s writings, may God be pleased with him, he mentioned what the commentators of Nahj al-Balagha reported regarding Abu Bakr and Omar, may God be pleased with them, like this: (By my life, their position in Islam is great, and their affliction in Islam is severe. May God have mercy on them and may God reward them with the best of what they have done.)

-[4] The author of Al-Fusul, who is one of the leading scholars of the Twelver Imami, reported on the authority of the distinguished Imam Muhammad Al-Baqir, may God be pleased with him, thus: (He said to a group who discussed Abu Bakr, Omar, and Uthman: “Don’t you tell me that you are among the immigrants who were expelled from their homes and their wealth, seeking God’s bounty and approval?”

They support God and His Messenger. They said: No - He said: You are among those who lived in the land and the faith before them loved those who migrated to them. They said: No - He said: As for you, you have been acquitted of being one of these two groups, and I bear witness that you are not among those whom God Almighty said: {And those who came after them say, “Our Lord, forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith, and do not put in our hearts hatred for those who believe. Our Lord, indeed, you are Most Compassionate, Most Merciful.”

Al-Khaydi in Al-Siddiq, Al-Farouq, and Dhu Al-Nourin, may God be pleased with them, is outside the three sects whom God praised with the testimony of Imam Al-Hammam, may God be pleased with him. And in the interpretation attributed to Imam Al-Hammam Al-Hasan Al-Askari, may God be pleased with him and his honorable fathers: (God revealed to Adam to bestow upon every one of the lovers of Muhammad, the family of Muhammad, and the companions of Muhammad, what if God had been divided into every number, from the length of time to the end, and they were disbelievers, He would have led them to a praiseworthy end and faith in God so that they would deserve Paradise. And whoever hates the family of Muhammad and his companions, or one of them, God will punish him with a torment that if it was divided according to the like of God’s creation, he would destroy them. All of them).
Know that love is what is in relation to one’s family and companions, may God be pleased with them, not in relation to one of them, and that hatred for one family and companion is sufficient.

To perish. May God save us from bad belief in the rights of the Companions and their family, may God be pleased with them all, and cause us to die due to their love. In view of the many verses and authentic hadiths, the people of truth agreed that the Companions, may God be pleased with them, must be glorified.

(The second suspicion) is that the authors of the hadith books did not see the Muhammadan cases and the Ahmadi miracles with their own eyes, and they did not hear the sayings of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, from him without intermediary. Rather, they heard them repeatedly one hundred or two hundred years after the death of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they collected them and omitted the amount of half of them for lack of consideration.

(And the answer) I learned in the third chapter that the linguistic narration is considered by the majority of the People of the Book and its consideration is established from this circulated Gospel, and that a Protestant group needs to take it into account in many matters, according to the approval of (Mani Sik) the bishop, in the amount of six hundred, and that five chapters of the Book of Proverbs were collected from the linguistic narrations, during the reign of Hezekiah, two hundred and seventy years after the death of Solomon, peace be upon him, and that the Gospels of Mark and Luke and nineteen chapters of the Book of Acts were written with the linguistic narration and that the matter Whoever is interested in it will be preserved and no defect will be discovered in it over a period of time, and that the Followers had begun to write down the hadiths in books, but they wrote them down in a different order than the chapters of jurisprudence, and that the class of followers of the Followers wrote them down in their order, then Al-Bukhari and the rest of the authors of the Sahih books limited themselves to mentioning the hadiths.

The authentic ones, they left out the weak ones, and each of the companions of the Sahih books narrated the hadiths with their chain of transmission to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. A great art has been written about the names of men, by which the situation of each of the narrators of the hadith is known. Likewise, I have learned that how the people of Islam consider the hadith to be authentic, so nothing is refuted from them. Their statement that they heard it through transmission and dropped the amount of half due to lack of consideration is an error because they did not omit for lack of consideration a hadith from the hadiths that they heard through transmission because the hadith that is frequent is obligatory for them to consider. Yes, they left out the weak ones whose chains of transmission were not complete, and abandoning them does not harm them, as you have known.

In the second chapter, Adam Clarke said: (This matter is certain that the many false Gospels were common in the first centuries of Christianity, and the abundance of these false and incorrect circumstances prompted Luke to edit the Gospel. There is a mention of more than seventy of these false Gospels, and many parts of these Gospels remain, and (Thabari Seuss) collected these false Gospels and printed them in three volumes. End quote.
(The third suspicion) If every rational person abandons fanaticism, he knows that most of the hadiths cannot have true meanings that match what is in the same matter.
(The answer is) There is nothing in the authentic hadiths whose content is impossible to reason with, as for some miracles that are contrary to custom, and some conditions of Paradise.

And hell and the angels that have no counterparts in this world, if their exclusion of them is because they are impossible with proof, then they must mention this proof and we must answer it, and if it is because they are contrary to the norm or there are no counterparts to them in this world, then it does not harm us, because if the miracle were according to the norm, it would not be a miracle. Isn’t it the fact that the stick became a snake and swallowed all the dragons of the magicians and then became as it was without increasing in size? And so all the miracles of Moses, peace be upon him, are unlike The course of custom, and the analogy of the other world to this world is an analogy with a difference. Yes, if there is definitive proof of the abstention of something, it is certain that it is abstained in the other world as well, and without the proof being established, no one dares to deny it in the other world. Do they not see the difference in the conditions of the regions, for some things are found in some and not in others? Whoever is from a region and hears the state of some wondrous things specific to another region will rule it out, and will often deny it on the condition that hearing it is not frequent.

Some things may be excluded at times and not at others, just as crossing this distance by sea at such a speed that is traveled by smokeboats, or by land that is traveled by smokemobiles, was among the things that were unlikely for people before the creation of smokeboats and smokemobiles, as well as the arrival of news in a minute or two over a long distance by means of a known wire, was among the things that were unlikely before its creation, and remained unlikely after these things were invented and tested.

However, in fairness, the habit of deniers is that they turn a blind eye to fairness and judge everything deemed unlikely in their opinions to be impossible, and Protestant scholars learned this habit from their kind, whom they call atheists. But what is strange about these scholars is that they do not see that their books are full of clear errors, as I quoted some of them as an example in the third chapter of the first chapter, and that they were not aware of the exclusions of their kind and treated the Muslims accordingly.

I treated them as members of their class, and the exclusions of members of their class were often stronger than their incomplete exclusions, and I quote some of the places in which they mock and exclude... for example:

[1] It occurred in the twenty-second chapter of the Book of Numbers as follows: 28: (Then the Lord opened the mouth of the donkey and she said to Balaam: What have I done to you? This has smitten me three times.) 29: (And Balaam said to the donkey: Because you deserved that from me, etc.) 30: (Then the donkey said to Balaam: I am not your donkey that has been riding since you were a boy until this day of yours. Have I done the same to you? And he said: No.)
Horne said on page 636 of the second volume of his Tafsir, printed in 1822: (The infidels have for a short time mocked the speech of Balaam’s donkey.) End quote.
[2] It was mentioned in the seventeenth chapter of the First Book of Kings that there were 2 ravens

Meat and bread were provided to the Messenger for a period of time, and this matter was a laughing matter among people of their class, until their famous investigator, Horne, leaned in to their opinion and criticized the foolishness of their interpreters and translators in three ways, as I learned about it in the third chapter of the first chapter.

[3] He signed the fourth chapter of the Book of Ezekiel like this, and his phrase was quoted from the Arabic translation printed in the year 1844: [4]: (And you shall sleep on your left side, and you shall put the iniquities of the house of Israel on it according to the number of days that you shall lie on it, and you shall take their iniquity. [5] But I have given you the years of their iniquities, according to the number of days, three hundred and ninety days, and you shall bear the iniquity of the family of Israel) 6: (Then, when you have completed this, you shall sleep on your right side again, and you shall take the iniquity of the family of Judah for forty days. One day, instead of a year, I have given it to you.) 7: (And you shall turn your face toward besieging Jerusalem, and your arm shall be strong, and you shall build upon it.) 8: (Behold, I have strengthened you with bonds, and you shall not turn from your side to the other until the days of your besiegements are completed.) 9: (And you shall take for yourself wheat, and barley, and beans, and lentils, and millet, and rye, and put them in one vessel, and bake for yourself bread according to the number of days that you shall lie on your side, three hundred. And for ninety days you shall eat.) 10: (And the food you shall eat shall be twenty mithqals by weight. Every day from time to time you shall eat.) 11: (And you shall drink water in proportion to one-sixth of the amount from time to time that you drink it.) 12: (And you shall eat like flatbread of barley and smear it with the dung that comes out of a person in their eyes.)
So God commanded Ezekiel, peace be upon him, with three rulings:

(The first) is that he lies on his left side for three hundred and ninety days and bears the sin of the family of Israel, then lies on his right side for forty days and bears the sin of the family of Judah.
(The second) is that he faces the besiegement of Jerusalem, with his arm tied, and not turning from one side to the other until the days of the besiegement are completed.

(And the third) is that he eats bread stained with human excrement for three hundred and ninety days. People of their kind mock these rulings and rule out that they are from God, and say that they are weak and far from reason. God does not command that His holy prophet should eat bread stained with human excrement for three hundred and ninety days. Was the perpetuity other than this, unless it is said that excrement in the case of the pure is pure, as is understood from the apparent meaning of the words of their saint, Paul, in the verse? The fifteenth of the first chapter of his letter to Titus, given that God had declared through him (The soul that sins will die, and the son will not bear the iniquity of the father, and the father will not bear the iniquity of the son. The righteousness of the just will be upon him, and the hypocrisy of the hypocrite will be upon him) as stated in the twentieth verse of the eighteenth chapter of his book. So how did He command him to bear the sins of Israel and Judah for four hundred and thirty days?

[4] It occurred in the twentieth chapter of the Book of Isaiah that God commanded him to be naked and barefoot for three years and to walk in this state, and his kind mocked this ruling and said mockingly, God commands his prophet who is within the bounds of reason.
He is not crazy if he walks with his private parts exposed between men and women for three years.

[5] It occurred in the first chapter of the Book of Hosea that God commanded him to take for himself an adulterous wife and the children of adultery. Then it occurred in the third chapter of the aforementioned book that he should fall in love with an immoral woman beloved of her husband, and it occurred in the thirteenth verse of the twenty-first chapter of the Book of the Rabbis as follows: (A priest shall not marry anyone but a virgin woman, nor shall he marry a widow, nor a divorced woman, nor one defiled by fornication. He shall not marry any of these at all, but he shall marry a virgin from his people.)

And in the fifth chapter of the Gospel of Matthew, it is as follows: (Everyone who looks at a woman to lust after her has committed adultery with her in his heart.) So how did God command His Prophet to do what he mentioned, and so on with other exclusions? So whoever wishes, let him return to the books of his kind.

(The fourth suspicion) Many hadiths contradict the Qur’an because it was mentioned in the Qur’an that Muhammad, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, did not appear to be a miracle. In the hadiths, many miracles were performed by him, and it was mentioned in the Qur’an that Muhammad, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, was guilty. In most of the hadiths, it was infallible, and it was written in the Qur’an that Muhammad, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, was initially in ignorance and misguidance, as in his saying in Surah Ad-Dhuha: {And He found you astray. So he guided}

Such as his saying in Surat Al-Shura: {You did not know what the Book or faith is, but We made it a light by which We guide whomsoever We will of Our servants} and in the hadiths that he was born in faith and for this reason many miracles appeared from him. This is the goal of their effort to prove the contradiction between the Qur’an and the Hadiths.

(And the answer) is that the first two matters, since they were among the greatest attacks on the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, I wanted to address them in the sixth chapter on attacks and answer them there, so wait.

(And the answer to the third) is that what is meant by the lost in the first verse is not the one who strays from the faith, to mean the unbeliever, thus rejecting their objection. Rather, there are several aspects to the interpretation of this verse:

(The first) is what was narrated with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him. He said, “I strayed from my grandfather, Abdul Muttalib, and I was a lost boy, and hunger almost killed me, so God guided me.”

(The second) is that its meaning is that he found you straying from your law, that is, you do not know it except through inspiration or revelation, so he guided you to it sometimes through clear revelation and at other times through hidden meaning, and this is chosen by Al-Baydawi, Al-Kashshaf, and Al-Jalalayn. In Al-Baydawi, he found you straying from the knowledge of wisdom and rulings, so he guided you, so he taught you revelation, inspiration, and guidance for consideration, and he brought this meaning in relation to Moses, peace be upon him, also in the Almighty’s saying: {I did it then, and I was among those who went astray}.

(Third) It is said that the water remained in the milk when it became immersed, so the meaning of the verse is: You were immersed among the infidels in Mecca, so God Almighty strengthened you until you demonstrated His religion. This meaning was stated in the Almighty’s saying: {When We stray into the earth, shall we surely be in a new creation}.

(And the fourth) is that its meaning is: You were astray from prophecy, and you did not aspire to it, and nothing of it occurred to your heart. The Jews and Christians used to claim that prophecy was among the Children of Israel, so I guided you to prophecy, which you did not aspire to at all.

Verse thirty-one of chapter twenty-nine is thus: “And when the Lord saw that Leah was hated, he opened her womb, but Rachel was barren.” The twenty-second verse of the thirtieth chapter of the aforementioned book is as follows: (Then the Lord remembered Rachel and responded to her and opened her womb.) Look at his aversion to exposing the private parts of men and his desire to remove the private parts of women and open and close their wombs.
(29) In the twenty-fourth verse of the ninth chapter of the Book of Jeremiah, it says: (I am the Lord who exercises mercy, judgment, and justice on earth.)

And I have known the state of his satisfaction with mercy and truthfulness, so I know the state of his justice in the twenty-first chapter of the Book of Ezekiel thus: [3] (And you shall say to the land of Israel thus: (Says the Lord God, Behold, I come to you, and I will draw out my sword from its sheath, and I will kill for you the righteous and the hypocrite) [4] And because I have killed for you the righteous and the hypocrite, for this purpose shall it come forth.)

My sword from its sheath to every body from the right to the left. If it is accepted that killing the hypocrite is fair according to Protestant scholars, but how can killing the righteous be fair according to them? And in the thirteenth chapter of the Book of Jeremiah: 13 (And we will say to them, Thus says the Lord, Behold, I am going to make drunken all the inhabitants of this land, and the kings who sit of the seed of David on his throne, and the priests, and the prophets, and all the inhabitants of Jerusalem. 14 And I will scatter them man for his brother, and fathers and children all together. Says the Lord, I will not have mercy, nor will I spare, nor will I be gracious, until I destroy them.) So I will fill all the inhabitants of this land with drunkenness, and then he killed them, that is, justice.

Verse twenty-nine of the twelfth chapter of the Book of Exodus is thus: (And when the middle of the night the Lord killed all the firstborn of the people of Egypt, from the firstborn of Pharaoh who sat on his throne, even to the firstborn of the captives who were in the prison, and all the firstborn of the livestock.) So he killed all the firstborn of the people of Egypt and the firstborn of livestock, meaning justice, because the faithful among the firstborn of the people of Egypt were innocent children, and the firstborn of livestock were also not guilty.

(30) The twenty-third verse of the eighteenth chapter of the Book of Ezekiel is thus: (My good pleasure is the death of the hypocrite, says the Lord God, unless he repents of his ways and lives.) And the eleventh verse of the thirty-third chapter is as follows: (Then say to them, “Even I, says the Lord God, do not want the death of the hypocrite, but that the hypocrite repent from his way and live,” etc.).

He learned from these two verses that God does not like the death of the evil person, but rather he loves the evil person to repent and be saved. The twentieth verse of the eleventh chapter of the Book of Joshua is thus: (So the Lord hardened their hearts and destroyed them.)
(31) The fourth verse of the second chapter of the first letter to Timothy is thus: (Who wants all people to be saved and to come to the knowledge of the truth).

And in the second chapter of the Second Epistle to the Thessalonians, it is as follows: 11 And for this reason God will send them a work of error, so that they will believe a lie, 12 so that all who did not believe the truth but had pleasure in unrighteousness would be damned.
(32) The eighteenth verse of the twenty-first chapter of the Book of Proverbs is thus: (Instead of the righteous, the hypocrite will be safe, but instead of the upright, the unrighteous.)
The second verse of the second chapter of the first letter to John is thus: (And He is the propitiation for our sins, and not for our sins only but also for the sins of the whole world).

From the first verse, he understood that the wicked are expiations for the righteous, and from the second, that Christ, peace be upon him, who is infallible according to Christians, became an expiation for the wicked.

(Benefit) What some priests claimed that Muslims do not have good atonement is wrong, because if we ponder the ruling on the expression of proverbs and look at the sects of the sons of Adam, we will find that the multiple expiations from those who deny Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, exist for every individual Muslim, although Christ, peace be upon him, was not an atonement for the sins of the whole world, as John acknowledged, so how can he not be an atonement for Muslims who acknowledge the monotheism of God?

And his prophecy, his honesty, and the fact that his mother was honest and innocent. Indeed, if anyone was fair, he would know that the people of eternal life are these Muslims and not others, as I learned in the fourth chapter.

(33) It occurred in the twentieth chapter of the Book of Exodus. You shall not murder, nor commit adultery. The second verse of the fourteenth chapter of the Book of Zechariah is thus: (And I will gather all the nations to Jerusalem to fight, and the city will be taken, and the houses will be destroyed, and the women will be exposed.) The Lord promised to gather the nations to kill his own people and expose their women and commit adultery with them.
(34) In the thirteenth verse of the first chapter of the Book of Hakkuk, this is how: (You have slit your eyes so that you may not see evil and be unable to look at iniquity.)
And the seventh verse of the forty-fifth chapter of the Book of Isaiah: (I form [p. 165] the light, and I create darkness, I make peace, and I create evil. I am the Lord, who creates all of them.)

(35) In the Thirty-Fourth Psalms it is as follows: 15 (For the eyes of the Lord are upon the righteous, and His ears are toward their cry) 17 (For those who cried out, He responded to them and delivered them from all their harms) 18 (For the Lord is close to the brokenhearted and a Savior of the humble in spirit). And in the twenty-second Psalms it is as follows: 1: (My God, my God, why have you forsaken me far from my salvation and the words of my cry) 2: (My God, my God, I pray during the day and you do not answer, and at night there is no silence for me).
And the forty-sixth verse of the twenty-seventh chapter of the Gospel of Matthew

Thus: (And about the ninth hour Jesus cried out with a loud voice, saying, “Eli, Eli, lama sabachthani,” that is, “My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?”) Were not David and Jesus, peace be upon them, righteous and brokenhearted and humble in spirit? Why did he leave them or hear their cries?
(36) The thirteenth verse of the twenty-ninth chapter of the Book of Jeremiah is thus: (You will seek Me and find Me if you seek Me with all your heart.)
The third verse of the twenty-third chapter of the Book of Job is thus: (Who will grant me knowledge so that I may find him and be able to reach his gathering?)

God has testified against Job that he is righteous and upright, fearful of God, and far from evil, as stated in the first and second chapters of his book. This holy person has no knowledge of the way of God’s presence, let alone his own.

(37) In the fourth verse of the twentieth chapter of the Book of Exodus, it is as follows: (We make for you no image or representation of anything that is in heaven or that is in the earth or that is in the waters under the earth). The eighteenth verse of the twenty-fifth chapter of the aforementioned book is as follows: (And make a card and a pen of gold, and put a covering on both sides of it.)
(38) The sixth verse of the Epistle of Jude is thus: (And the angels who did not observe

Their leadership, but they left their dwelling place. He preserved them until the judgment of the great day in eternal chains under darkness.) He learned from her that the devils are bound with great chains until the Day of Resurrection. It is known from the first and second chapters of the Book of Job that Satan is not restricted, but rather he is free and present with God.

(39) In the fourth verse of the second chapter of the Second Epistle to Peter, it is as follows: (God did not spare the angels who had sinned, but rather cast them into chains of darkness and handed them over to be kept for judgment.) In the fourth chapter of the Gospel of Matthew, Satan tempted Jesus, peace be upon him.

(40) The fourth verse in the ninetieth Psalms is like this: (For a thousand years to you are like a bygone yesterday and like a deep night). And the eighth verse of the third chapter of the Second Epistle to Peter is like this: (For with the Lord one day is like a thousand years, and a thousand years are like one day). However, he said in the sixteenth verse of the ninth chapter of the Book of Genesis like this: (And the bow will be in the clouds, and I will see it, and I will remember the eternal covenant that has been established between God and every living soul of all flesh on the earth.) However, the fact that the bow is a sign of the covenant is not good, because the bow is not in every cloud, but rather in a few times of clouds, which is often the time when the clouds are thin, and this time does not lead to abundant rain from which there is a fear of a flood, so the sign does not occur at the time of need for it, but rather at the time of dispensing with it.

(41) In the twentieth verse of the thirty-third chapter of the Book of Exodus, God says in a speech to Moses, peace be upon him, like this: (You are not able to look at my face, because no human being can see me and live). And in the thirtieth verse of the thirty-second chapter of the Book of Genesis, Jacob, peace be upon him, said thus: (I saw God face to face, and my soul was saved). Jacob, peace be upon him, saw God face to face and remained alive, and in the story in which this saying occurred there are other things as well that are not appropriate. The first: mentioning the wrestling between God and Jacob. The second: It extends until dawn. Third: that one does not strengthen the other. Fourth: God was not able to let me go by himself, so he said, let me go. Fifth: Jacob did not divorce him except as compensation, which was to bless him. Sixth: God asked him about his name and he knew that he did not know his name.

(42) The twelfth verse of the fourth chapter of the first letter to John is thus: (No one has ever seen God.) And in the twenty-fourth chapter of the Book of Exodus it is as follows: 9 “And Moses and Aaron went up and called Ab and Abihu and seventy men of the elders of Israel 10 and they saw

To the God of Israel, and under His feet are like a blue stone and like the color of the sky and a light that appears.) 11 (And he did not extend his hand to the elders of Israel, and they saw God and ate and drank.) So Moses [p. 168] and Aaron and the seventy sheikhs, peace be upon them, saw God and ate and drank with Him. I say first: that the last sentence, according to its apparent meaning, indicates that they ate and drank God, but what is meant is perhaps what the objectors understood. Secondly: The God of the Children of Israel (God forbid) was in the image of the gods of the Indian polytheists, such as Ramjand Rukrishna, because their colors, as stated in their books, were the color of the sky.
(43) In the sixteenth verse of the sixth chapter of the first letter to Timothy, it says: “Whom no man has seen nor is able to see.”
In the fourth chapter of sightings, John saw him sitting on the throne
He who sits in the scene looks like a stone of jasper and agate.

(44) The thirty-seventh verse of the fifth chapter of the Gospel of John, Jesus’ statement in his speech to the Jews is thus: (You have never heard his voice, nor seen his appearance.) You learned about seeing God in the previous example. As soon as I heard his voice. In the twenty-fourth verse of the fifth chapter of the Book of Exceptions, it says: “The Lord our God has shown us his glory and his greatness, and we have heard his voice in the middle of the day.”

(45) In the twenty-fourth verse of the fourth chapter of the Gospel of John, this is how: (God is a Spirit). And in the thirty-ninth verse of the twenty-fourth chapter of the Gospel of Luke, it is as follows: (The spirit does not have flesh and bones). It is known from these two phrases that God does not have flesh and bones. Every member of God from the head to the leg was confirmed to him in their books, and they quoted examples to prove these members, and I identified them in the introduction to the fourth chapter. Then they said sarcastically: “He has not yet known that he is a gardener, a builder, a potter, a tailor, a surgeon, a barber, a midwife, a butcher, or a farmer.”
Or a merchant or someone else, because the words of their books are confused.”
In the eighth verse of the eighth chapter of the Book of Genesis, this is the following: (And the Lord God planted the Paradise of Bliss from the beginning), so it is known that he is a gardener.

It is also known from the nineteenth verse of the forty-first book of the Book of Isaiah, and in the thirty-fifth verse of the second chapter of the first book of Samuel, thus: (And he built him a faithful house), and so in verse 11 and 27 of the seventh chapter of the second book of Samuel, and verse 38 of the eleventh chapter of the first book of Kings, and verse 1 of the Psalms 127, and it is known from these verses that he is a builder. The eighth verse of the sixty-fourth chapter of the Book of Isaiah is thus: (And now, O Lord, you are our father and we are the clay and you are the one who formed us and we are all the works of your hands) so it is known from it that he is a potter. Verse twenty-one of the third chapter of the Book of Genesis is thus: (And the Lord God made garments of skins for Adam and his wife and clothed them) so it is known that he is a tailor. And in verse 17 of the thirtieth chapter of the Book of Isaiah, it says: (I will heal your wound).

He knows that he is a surgeon. And the twentieth verse of the seventh chapter of the Book of Isaiah is as follows: (On that day the Lord will shave Moses, denouncing those who crossed the river with the king of the Athorians, the head, the fur of the feet, and the whole beard), so it will be known that he is a barber. It is known from verse 31 of chapter twenty-nine and verse 22 of chapter thirtieth of the Book of Genesis that he is a midwife. They were quoted shortly in the twenty-eighth statement of difference. The sixth verse of the thirty-fourth chapter of the Book of Isaiah is thus: (The sword of the Lord was filled with blood, fat from the fat of the lambs and goats from the blood of fattened rams), so it is known that he is a butcher. And the fifteenth verse of the forty-first chapter of the Book of Isaiah is thus: (Behold, I have made you like new wheels of a wheel, like saws that trample and trample the mountains, and crush the hills, and make them like dust.) So he knows that he is a farmer. And in the eighth verse of the third chapter of the Book of Joel, this is how: (And I will sell your sons and daughters into the hands of the children of Judah) so he knows that he is a merchant.

And in the thirteenth verse of the fifty-fourth chapter of the Book of Isaiah, it says this: (All your children will learn from the Lord) and he will know that he is a teacher. It is known from Chapter Thirty-Two of the Book of Genesis that he is a wrestler.

(46) The ninth verse of the twenty-second chapter of the Second Book of Samuel is thus: (Smoke rose from his nostrils, and fire blazed from his mouth to consume, and coals ignited from them.) The tenth verse of the thirty-seventh chapter of the Book of Job is thus: (Snow is from the breath of God and He freezes liquid water).
(47) The twelfth verse of the fifth chapter of the Book of Hosea is thus: (And I am like a mite to Ephraim, and like a worm to the house of Judah.)

The seventh verse of the thirteenth chapter of the aforementioned book is thus: (And I will be to them like a lion, like a tiger, in the way of the Assyrians), sometimes like a mite and a worm, and sometimes like a lion and a tiger.

(48) The tenth verse of the third chapter of Jeremiah’s Lamentations is thus: (A rusty monster has become a lion to me in secret.) The eleventh verse of the fortieth chapter of the Book of Isaiah is thus: (Like a shepherd, he feeds his flock) etc. Sometimes like a bear and a lion, and sometimes like a shepherd.

(49) In the third verse of the fifteenth chapter of the Book of Exodus, this is the following: (The Lord is like a fighting man). And in the twentieth verse of the thirteenth chapter of the Hebrew Epistle, it says: (And the God of peace).

(50) In the eighth verse of the fourth chapter of John, it says this: (God is love). The fifth verse of the twenty-first chapter of the Book of Jeremiah is thus: (And I will attack you with an outstretched hand and with a strong arm and with rebuke and with anger and intense indignation.) When Nubia reached the age of fifty, I contented myself with quoting these differences to this extent for fear of lengthening. Whoever wants more, let him browse the books of the aforementioned objectors and find other differences in them. The fifteenth verse of the twenty-first chapter of the Book of Exceptions is thus: (And if a man has two wives, one beloved and the other hated) etc. The twenty-seventh verse of the ninth chapter of the Book of Joshua is as follows: (And it was imposed on them), meaning the people of Gibeon today, that they should serve the entire people and serve

At the altar of the Lord, they cut wood and draw water in the place that the Lord chooses. And in the fifty-sixth chapter of the Book of Isaiah, this is the following: (The Lord says to the eunuchs who keep My Sabbaths and choose what I will and keep My covenant. I will give them in My House and within My walls a place and a name better than that of sons and daughters. I will give them an everlasting name that will not perish.) It is known from these verses that God is permitted to marry two wives. One of the people is in slavery and slavery and is satisfied with the eunuchs. (And these) things are all reprehensible to the English, whether legally or rationally, and the twenty-fifth verse of the first chapter of the first letter to the Corinthians is thus: (For the foolishness of God is wiser than people, and the weakness of God is stronger than people). The ninth verse of the fourteenth chapter of the Book of Ezekiel is thus: (And if the prophet goes astray and speaks a word, then I, the Lord, have led that prophet astray) etc. From these two verses it is known that God is ignorant and misguided by His prophets (God forbid). Atheist Jean Clark said after quoting some of the previously mentioned sayings: (This God of the children of Israel is not only a murderer, an unjust, a liar, a fool, and a deceiver, but he is also a burning fire.)

As Paul said in the twenty-ninth verse of the twelfth chapter of the Hebrew Epistle, our God is a consuming fire, and falling into the hands of this God is terrifying. As Paul said in verse thirty-one of chapter ten of the Hebrew Epistle: “It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God.” Obtaining freedom from Ruqyah is like this god

He is better with haste, because if his only son does not survive, who can hope for mercy and kindness from him? And this God, whom these books state, is not a God that can be relied upon. Rather, he is an unrealized thing that gathers opposites and illusions, misleading His prophets.) End quote. So look at the members of the class of priests, to what extent their shift has reached, and it will be known that their objections to what occurred in their English and other translations. If the observer finds in the statement of the number of verses or in some of the contents something that contradicts the Arabic translation, then it is due to the difference in translations.

sections.heading: Chapter One: (On proving the prophethood of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and it contains six paths)
content: Chapter One: (On Proving the Prophethood of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace
It contains six paths.)
[Miracles of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace]

(The first path) is that many miracles appeared at his hand, may God bless him and grant him peace, and I mention a summary of them in this path from the Qur’an and authentic hadiths by deleting the chain of transmission and presenting them in two types.

In the third chapter of Chapter Five, I learned in full detail that there is nothing objectionable, logically or narrated, in considering linguistic narrations that include the conditions of narration that are considered by our scholars, may God Almighty have mercy on them.

There are two types (as for the first type), it is in explaining its news about the unseen, past and future. As for the past, it is the stories of the prophets, peace be upon them, and the stories of the decreed nations without hearing from anyone and not being taught from a book, as you learned in the fourth command of the first chapter of the fifth chapter, and it was referred to in the Almighty’s saying: {These are of the news of the unseen that We reveal to you, neither you nor your people knew them before this}.

The discrepancy that occurred between the Qur’an and the books of the People of the Book in explaining some of these stories was explained in the second chapter of Chapter Five in the answer to the second suspicion. As for the future, it is many. On the authority of Hudhayfah, may God be pleased with him, that he said: (He stood among us, and he did not leave anything that would be in his position until the Hour of Judgment, except that he told it, and he who memorized it preserved it, and he who forgot it forgot it. These companions of mine have taught him, and that there will be something from him, so I recognize it and remember it just as a man remembers a man’s face when he is absent from him, and then when he sees him, he recognizes him.) Narrated by Al-Bukhari and Muslim.

In the third matter of the first chapter of the fifth chapter, I learned twenty-two stories from the news included in the Qur’an, and God Almighty said: {Or did you think that you would enter Paradise, and when the like of those who passed before you came to you, misfortune and adversity befell them, and they were shaken until the Messenger and those who believed with him said, “When will God give victory? Indeed, God’s victory is near.”

God promised the Muslims in this statement that they would shake him until they vomited him and sought his help. The Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, said to his companions: “The matter will become severe when the parties come together against you, and the consequences will be for you over them.” He also said: (The parties will march to you in nine or ten days). Then the parties came as God and His Messenger had promised, and they were ten thousand. They besieged the Muslims and fought them fiercely for a period of a month. The Muslims were in extreme distress, distress, and terror. They said, “This is what God and His Messenger promised us,” and they were certain of Paradise and victory. As God Almighty told us, saying: {And when the believers saw the parties, they said: This is what God and His Messenger promised us, and God and His Messenger have spoken the truth, and it only increased them in faith and submission}. The imams of hadith, may God be pleased with them, came out:
1- The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, informed the Companions of the conquest of Mecca, Jerusalem, Yemen, the Levant, and Iraq.
2- And security appears until the woman travels from Al-Hira to Mecca without fear
Except God.
3- Khaybar will be conquered by Ali, may God be pleased with him, the next day.
4- And they divide the treasures of the King of Persia and the King of Rome.
5- And the daughters of Persia serve them. All of these matters occurred during the time of the Companions, may God be pleased with them, as he told us.
6- And his nation will split into seventy-three sects.

7- A knight will go head-to-head or two, and then there will be no knight after that, and the Romans will have horns. Whenever a century dies, the horn of the people of Sakhr and Bahr Farahat will be left behind in its place at the end of time. What is meant by the Romans is the Franks and the Christians, and as was told, what remained of the Persian Sultanate had a trace other than the Romans. Even though their Sultanate disappeared from the Levant during the caliphate of Omar, may God be pleased with him, and Heraclius was defeated from the Levant to the farthest part of his country, their Sultanate did not disappear completely, but rather, whenever a century perished, another century succeeded it.
8- And that God planted the earth for me, so I saw its easts and its wests, and He will reach the dominion of my nation

What did he give me of it?) The meaning is that God gathered the earth for me once by bringing its farthest to the closest until I saw what was in it, and my nation will open it part by part until it possesses all its parts, and in order to limit it to its easts and wests, his religion spread in the easts and the wests, from the land of India, which is the farthest part of the east, to the Sea of Tangier, which is the farthest west, and it did not spread to the south and the north like it spread in the east and the west. Perhaps in their use of the plural word, and in the introduction of the easts, is a nod to What is there is the appearance of a large number of scholars from them compared to others, and that the scholars of the East are more and more prominent than the scholars of the Maghreb.

9- And that the people of the West will continue to prevail upon the truth until the Hour comes.) In another hadith, Abu Umamah narrated: (A group of my nation will continue to adhere to the truth until the command of God comes to them, and they are like that. It was said: O Messenger of God, and where are they? He said: By the Holy House.) What is meant by the majority of scholars by the people of the West is the people of the Levant because
West of Hijaz, according to the novel “Illusion in the Levant”.
10- And that temptations do not appear as long as Omar is alive and he was as he told, and Omar, may God be pleased with him, closed the door to temptation.
11- And the Mahdi, may God be pleased with him, will appear.
12- And that Jesus, peace be upon him, will descend.
13- And the Antichrist will emerge.
These three matters will appear, God willing, and God knows best.
14- Othman was killed while reading the Qur’an.

15 - The most miserable of others is the one who dyes one of these. It means that Ali’s beard is from the blood from his head, meaning he kills him, and they, may God be pleased with them, were martyred as he was told.
16- Ammar was killed by the oppressive faction, so he was killed by Muawiyah’s companions.

17- And the caliphate after me in my nation will last for thirty years, then it will become a solid kingdom after that.) So the true caliphate was like that with the passage of the period of the caliphate of Al-Hasan bin Ali, may God be pleased with them, because the caliphate of Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, was two years, three months and twenty days, the caliphate of Omar, may God be pleased with him, was ten years, six months and four days, the caliphate of Othman, may God be pleased with him, was eleven years, eleven months and eighteen days, and the caliphate of Ali, may God be pleased with him, was four years. And ten months and nine days, in full, the caliphate of Al-Hasan, may God be pleased with him.
18- And the destruction of my nation was at the hands of Aghilaim from Quraysh, and Al-Murad Yazid and his sons
Marwan.
19- The Ansar diminished until they were like salt in food, and their affairs continued to disperse until there was no group left for them. And it happened as he told me.
20- And there will be a liar and a liar in Thaqif, i.e. a destroyer, so they saw them
Al-Mukhtar and Al-Hajjaj.

20- And the two deaths, i.e. the epidemic and the plague, occur after the conquest of Jerusalem, and this epidemic occurred during the caliphate of Omar, may God be pleased with him, in Emmaus, one of the villages of Jerusalem, and there his army was located. It was the first plague that occurred in Islam, in which seventy thousand died in it.
Three days.

22- And that they raid in the sea like kings on beds. In the two Sahih books: (The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to go to Umm Haram bint Milhan, one of the breastfeeding aunts of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and she was under the care of Ubadah ibn al-Samit. He went in to her one day and she fed him, then she sat down to rub his head and he fell asleep. Then he woke up laughing and she said: Why are you laughing? He said: People from my nation were presented to raiders in the path of God riding on this sea, 2 kings on beds. Or like kings over the family. She said: I pray to God to make me one of them. 3 And he said: You are among the first. So she rode on the sea in the time of Muawiyah and fell off her animal after she got out of it and died.)
23- If faith were linked to the Pleiades, men from Persia would have attained it, and it contains a reference to the greatest Imam Abu Hanifa al-Kufi, may God Almighty also have mercy on him.
24- Fatima was the first of his family to join him, so she died, may God be pleased with her, after six years
Months after his death, may God bless him and grant him peace.

25- (And this son of mine), meaning Al-Hassan Ibn Ali, may God be pleased with them both, is a master, and God will reconcile two great groups through him. It happened as he was told, and God reconciled through him his followers and the people of the Levant.
26- And Abu Dharr lives alone and dies. It was as he told.

27- (And the quickest of his wives to catch up with him are the ones with the longest hands.) Zainab bint Jahsh, may God be pleased with her, was the quickest of them to catch up with him because of her long hand in charity.

28- (And that Al-Hussein bin Ali, may God be pleased with them both, was killed at At-Taf) and it is with a fatha ta’ and a stressed fa’ in a place in the area of ​​Kufa on the shore of the Euphrates River, and now it is famous for Karbala, so Al-Hussein, may God be pleased with him, was martyred at Al-Taf as he was told.
29- He said to Suraqa bin Jasham: How will you do if you wear Khosrau’s bracelets?
When Omar, may God be pleased with him, brought them, he clothed them with him and said: Praise be to God who robbed Chosroes of them and clothed them with Suraqah.
30- He said to Khaled, may God be pleased with him, when he directed him to Lakider: You find him hunting cows. It was as he told.

In the hadith of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, according to the two sheikhs: (The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The Hour will not come until a fire emerges from the land of Hijaz, illuminating the necks of camels in Busra).
