As for (the first), if a past tense is split, and it is interpreted as a meaning, it will become a metaphor and will not turn into a metaphor unless it is impossible to interpret the truth, and here it is not impossible, but rather it is necessary to interpret it according to its real meaning, as I knew previously.

As for (the second), it is because it is a slander that was inflected according to Al-Baydawi, which is what was interpreted as split and split, and rather it was interpreted in its past meaning, but after he interpreted it according to his chosen one, he quoted the saying of some people in the form of nursing, then he rejected his statement, so this saying is rejected by him.

When the author of the inquiry objected to the author of Al-Mizan on the aforementioned statement and said: (The priest is either mistaken or misleading the common people). The aforementioned author took notice and changed this phrase in the new Persian version printed in 1849, and the Urdu version printed in 1850, and said: (The word “hour,” which is known as “lam” in the case of individuals, appears in every place in the Qur’an meaning the Day of Resurrection, and the sentence “the moon was split open” due to the conjunction “waw”” was attached to the sentence “the Hour has approached,” and the past tense is present in both sentences. Just as the first verb “closed” means the future, meaning the Day of Resurrection will come, so the second verb “is split” also means “it will be split,” meaning “if the Day of Resurrection” comes.” On the Day of Resurrection, the moon will be split open, and some commentator scholars also interpreted it like this, such as Al-Zamakhshari and Al-Baydawi, even though they believed in their interpretation that this verse is a miracle of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, but they also stated like this, and on the authority of some people, that its meaning is that it will be split open on the Day of Resurrection, and in Hudhayfah’s reading, “the moon will be split open,” meaning the Hour has approached, and it has come
One of the signs of its approach was that the moon was split. Al-Baydawi said: It was said that it means it will split on the Day of Resurrection. End quote.

The author of Al-Mizan was alerted and changed the phrase, but he was impressed by the summary of Al-Kashshaf’s phrase, as he dropped some of the phrase, claiming that it was not useful, and quoted his saying: And in the reading of Hudhayfah, and the moon was split, etc. This statement does not fit its purpose because it is stated in proving the aforementioned miracle that it was said: This saying was transmitted completely. I said, then there is no reason to omit some of the phrase, and the phrase of the scout is like this: (And some people say that its meaning is to be split open on the Day of Resurrection. And his saying: And if they see a sign, they turn away and say continuous magic, it will turn it back, and that is enough of a response. Hudhayfah’s reading is that the moon has been split open, that is, the Hour has approached, and it has come from the signs of its approach that the moon has split as you say. The prince has come and the good tidings of his arrival have come. Hudhayfah said that he delivered a speech in al-Mada'in and then said: Indeed, the Hour has approached and the moon has split during the time of your Prophet.) His words ended with his words.

His saying: The word “Hour” known as “Lam” etc. The same applies to his saying in a sentence: The moon split because of the conjunction “waw,” etc. He does not achieve what he intended from them. Perhaps he understood that the word “Hour” meant the resurrection and the splitting of the moon were among its signs, so it must be

He is connected to it and is in it, and this is a mistake that arises from lack of contemplation. God Almighty said in Surah Muhammad: {So do they wait except for the Hour to come upon them suddenly? Its signs have come.} His saying: Its signs have come indicates that its signs have been fulfilled, because if the word “may” enters into the past, it indicates the presence of the action in the past time close to the situation, so the commentators interpreted this saying thus in Al-Baydawi (because its signs have appeared, such as the sending of the Prophet and the splitting of the moon).

In Al-Tafsir Al-Kabir (the Signs, the signs, the commentators said: They are like the splitting of the moon and the message of Muhammad, peace be upon him, and in Al-Jalalayn, that is, their signs, including the sending of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the splitting of the moon and smoke).

Al-Husseini’s phrase, like Al-Baydawi’s, is his saying: Just as the first verb was approached in the sense of the future, it is wrong because it is in its past sense, and translating it in Persian to mean (razu qiyamat khawahid amad) is not correct, and what was narrated from some people is rejected by the commentators.

Then he said: (Even if we accept that the moon split occurred, it would not be a miracle of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, because it is not stated in this verse nor in another verse that this miracle appeared at the hands of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace.) End quote.

I say: It indicates that it is a miracle, the second verse and the authentic hadiths that are authentic according to rational control are in addition to the authenticity of these distorted Gospels that are full of errors, and the differences narrated by single narrations whose connected chains are missing, as I learned in the first and second chapters.

Then he said: (The relationship of the second verse to the first verse is that the deniers see signs of the Resurrection at the end of time and do not believe in them. Rather, they say, as is the custom of the infidels of the predecessors, that it is obscene magic and nothing else.) His words ended.
This is also wrong in two ways:

The first: The denier does not deny it out of obstinacy, and the unbeliever does not attribute the supernatural matter to magic unless someone claims that this extraordinary matter is one of My miracles or miracles. If signs of the Resurrection appear at the end of time without claiming, how can the deniers deny them, and how can they say: It is obscene magic and nothing else?

The second: The splitting of the moon in the future will only happen on the Day of Resurrection, especially on this day. The infidels do not say that it is continuous magic because the command of the Resurrection will appear on this day for everyone. Unless one of them is sane and opposes such a directive, then perhaps he will say what he claims, or utter this saying of this directive himself or other Protestant scholars like him, after they emerged from their events due to the stubbornness of the Muhammadan religion being deeply rooted in their hearts.

Then he said: (If this miracle had appeared at the hands of Muhammad, he would have told the stubborn people who were asking him for a miracle that I split the moon at such-and-such a time, so do not disbelieve.) You will see his answer in the second chapter in its most complete manner, God willing.

The author of the Way of Faith said, denying this miracle: (Several commentators, such as Al-Zamakhshari and Al-Baydawi, interpreted this position as meaning that the moon would split on the Day of Resurrection, and if it had happened, it would have become famous throughout the world, and there is no meaning to its fame in one region.) He ended his words with a summary.

It has become clear to you from what we have mentioned that both of these matters are definitely not correct, and this priest surpassed the author of Al-Mizan, as he cited the narrational and rational evidence, and stated the name Al-Kashshaf. Also, perhaps he saw in the old version of Al-Mizan a word like Al-Baydawi and others, and he thought that what was meant by “other than Al-Kashshaf,” because Al-Baydawi has many similarities with Al-Kashshaf in relation to the other interpretations, so he declared the name Al-Kashshaf so that he could get credit for the author of Al-Mizan.
The author of Al-Kashshaf said about the principle of interpretation of this
Surah: (The splitting of the moon is one of the signs of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and one of his luminous miracles) His words ended.

The author of the treatise that he wrote in response to Maktoob, Al-Fadil Nimat Ali Hind, objecting to this miracle, said: (It is not proven from this verse that this miracle came from Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and this matter is not proven from the interpretations.) End quote.

This third one is more good emanating from the first two than both of them, as he said: This matter is not proven from the interpretations. Perhaps he thought that the first priest was truthful in his words, like Al-Baydawi and others, and the second priest was truthful in his words, like Al-Zamakhshari and Al-Baydawi. Then he compared the situation of the rest of the interpretations based on these two interpretations, and said: This matter is not proven from the interpretations, so that he gets credit over the first two priests, and his insight appears to his people in that he read all of the interpretations, so it appears that each of the following three of these interpretations is correct. The previous one, and this is not surprising, because such a matter was widespread among Christians in the first century, as appears from the letters of the disciples, and it became a religious recommendation in the second century of Christianity, as the historian Musheim said in explaining the situation of scholars of the second century of Christianity on page 65 of the first volume of his history printed in the year 1832: (Among those who followed the opinion of Plato and Pythagoras there was a famous saying that lying and deception in order to increase honesty and the worship of God are not only permissible, but also subject to improvement. The Jews of Egypt first learned this saying from them before Christ, as this clearly appears from many ancient books. Then he influenced
The epidemic of this mistake is bad among Christians, as this matter appears from the many books that have been falsely attributed to the elders.) End of his speech.
Adam Clarke said in the sixth volume of his interpretation, explaining the first chapter of Paul’s letter to the Galatians:

(This matter is certain that the many false Gospels were common in the first centuries of Christianity, and the abundance of these false and incorrect circumstances prompted Luke to edit the Gospel. There is a mention of more than seventy of these false Gospels, and many parts of these Gospels remain.) End quote.

If their ancestors attributed more than seventy Gospels to Christ, the disciples, and Mary, peace be upon them, what wonder would it be if these priests, in order to mislead the common people of Islam, attributed some matters to interpretations of the Qur’an?

Know that the last letter was famous in India, and the priests shared it often in his country, but when several Islamic scholars wrote a response to it and what they wrote became known, they abandoned it and printed three books of the response to it. The first: “The Christian Masterpiece” by Sayyid al-Din al-Hashimi. The second: “Muslim support” for some relatives of a Shiite mujtahid, but they are not. The third: “Khalisat Saif Al-Muslimeen” by Mr. Haider Ali Al-Qurashi.

3- In Al-Baydawi: (It was narrated that when the Quraysh emerged from Al-Aqanqal, peace and blessings of God be upon him said: This is the Quraysh who came with their arrogance and pride, denying your Messenger. Oh God, I ask you for what you promised me. Then Gabriel, peace be upon him, came to him and said to him: Take a handful of dirt and throw it at them. When the two groups met, he took a handful of pebbles and threw it in their faces. And he said:

The faces were astonished, and no polytheist remained except a specific occupation, so they were defeated and the believers sent them back, killing them and taking them prisoner. Then when they left, they began to boast, and the man said, “I was killed and captured.” End quote.

And God Almighty said: {And you did not throw when you threw, but God threw} meaning {And you did not throw}, O Muhammad, a throw that reached their eyes but you were not able to do it {when you threw} i.e. you brought the form of throwing {but God threw} He brought what was the purpose of the throwing, so He brought it to their eyes all the way until they were defeated, and you were able to cut off their traces.

Al-Fakhr Al-Razi, may God have mercy on him, said: (What is more correct) is that this verse was revealed on the day of Badr, otherwise foreign words about it would have been included during the story, and this is not appropriate, and it is not far-fetched for all other incidents to be included because what matters is the generality of the word, not the specific reason.) His words ended.
I learned in the introduction what the author of Mizan al-Haqq said about this miracle, so I will not repeat it.

4- Water sprung from between the fingers of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in multiple places. This miracle is greater than water gushing out of a stone, as happened to Moses, peace be upon him, for that is the habit of stone in general, and as for flesh and blood, he did not know anyone else, may God bless him and grant him peace. On the authority of Anas bin Malik, may God be pleased with him, he said: (I saw the Messenger of God, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, and it was time for the afternoon prayer. The people looked for ablution but did not find it, so the Messenger of God, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, brought an ablution. The Messenger of God, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, put his hand in that vessel and ordered the people to perform ablution from it. He said: I saw water springing from between his fingers, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, and the people performed ablution until the last of them had performed ablution.) And this is the miracle. It was issued by Zawraa at the city market.

5- On the authority of Jabir, may God be pleased with him: (The people were thirsty on the day of Al-Hudaybiyyah, and the Messenger of God, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, had a bowl in front of him, so he performed ablution from it. The people came towards him and said: We have no water except what is in your bowl. So the Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, put his hand in the bowl, and the water began to bubble from between his fingers like springs.) The people were one thousand and four hundred.

6- On the authority of Jabir, may God be pleased with him (he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to me: O Jabir, call for ablution and mentioned the hadith in its length and that we found only a drop in the defenseless, denouncing

So he brought him to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he immersed him and said something, I do not know what it was, and said: He called for the kneecap, so I brought it and placed it in his hands. He mentioned that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, extended his hand into the jar, separated his fingers, and poured Jabir on it and said: In the name of God. He said: I saw the water boiling from between his fingers, then the bowl escaped and turned around until it was full. He ordered the people to draw water, so they drew water until they quenched their thirst. I said: Is there anyone left in need? Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, raised his hand from the pot while it was full. This miracle occurred during the Battle of Bawat.
7- On the authority of Moaz bin Jabal in the story of the Battle of Tabuk, and that they returned the spring while it was

It filled with some water like a trap, so they scooped it out of the spring with their hands until it gathered into something, then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, washed his face and hands in it, then put it back in it, and it gushed out with a lot of water, so the people drew water. He said in the hadith of Ibn Ishaq: Then a stream of water poured out that had a sensation like the sensation of lightning bolts. Then he said: O Muadh, if your life is long, you will soon see what is here filled with heavens.

8- On the authority of Imran bin Al-Husayn, may God be pleased with them both, that he said: (When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions became thirsty during some of their travels, he directed two men from his companions to

He informed them that they would find a woman in such-and-such a place with a camel with two hadiths on it. They found her and brought her to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. He put it in a vessel from her matadah and said to it, “What God wills.” Then he put the water back in the two jugs. Then she opened her covers and ordered the people to fill their watering cans until they did not leave anything except to fill it. Imran said: It seems to me that they have only become fuller. Then he ordered that some of the provisions be gathered for the woman until they filled her dress, and he said: Go, for we did not take anything from your water, but God gave us something to drink.

9- In the hadith of Omar, may God be pleased with him, about the army of hardship, he mentioned the thirst that afflicted them, to the point that a man would slaughter his camel, squeeze out its dung and drink it, so Abu Bakr wanted to pray to the Prophet, so he raised his hands and did not return them until the sky said, “And it poured out,” so they filled what vessels they had with them, and it did not go beyond the army.

10- On the authority of Jabir, may God be pleased with him, that a man came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to feed him. He asked him to feed him half a wasq of barley, and he, his wife, and his guest continued to eat from it until he ate it, so he came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and informed him. He said: If you had not eaten it, you would have eaten from it and he would have eaten it with you.

11- On the authority of Anas, may God be pleased with him, that the Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, fed eighty men with disks of barley, which Anas brought under his hand, that is, his armpit.

12- On the authority of Jabir, may God be pleased with him, that the Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, fed a thousand men on the Day of the Trench with a saa of barley and one bunch of grapes. 3 Jabir, may God be pleased with him, said: So he swore by God that they would eat until they left him and went astray, and that our wheat would be covered as it is and that our dough would be baked, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, spat in the dough and the wheat and blessed it.

13- On the authority of Abu Ayyub, may God be pleased with him, that he made for the Messenger of God, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, and for Abu Bakr about what was sufficient for them. Then the Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, said to him: Call thirty of the nobles of the Ansar. So he called them, and they ate until they left. Then he said: Call for sixty, and it was like that. Then he said: Call for seventy, and they ate until they left him. Not one of them left until he converted to Islam and pledged allegiance. Abu Ayoub, may God be pleased with him, said: One hundred and eighty men ate from my food.
14- On the authority of Samra bin Jundub, a bowl containing meat was brought to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace
They followed it from morning until night, some people getting up and others sitting.

15- On the authority of Abdul Rahman bin Abi Bakr, may God be pleased with them both, he said: We were with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, one hundred and thirty. It was mentioned in the hadith that he kneaded a saa’ of food and made a sheep and roasted the blackness of its stomach. He said: By God, there is not a hundred and thirty pieces of it except that he had a portion of it, then he made two bowls of it, so we all ate, and there was leftover in the two bowls, so I carried it on the camel.
16- On the authority of Salamah bin Al-Akwa’, Abu Hurairah, and Omar bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him

On their authority, they mentioned a fermentation that afflicted the people with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in some of his battles. So he called for the rest of the supplies, and the man brought the Hathiya 4 of food and more than that, and the highest of them was the one who brought a saa’ of dates, so he combined it with nata’ and Salamah said: So I scored it like the calf of a goat. Then he called the people for their containers, and there was not a container left in the army except its filling and what remained of it.

17- On the authority of Anas bin Malik that when the Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, built a house in Zainab, he ordered him to invite a people for him that he named until the house and the room were filled, so he presented to them a tower containing an amount of dates.
Feeling anxious, he put it down, dipped three fingers, and started the people to have lunch and go out, and the tor remained as it was.

18- On the authority of Ali bin Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, that Fatima cooked a pot for their lunch, and directed Ali to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to eat with them, so he ordered her to scoop for all his wives, one by one, then for him, peace be upon him, then for Ali, then for her, then she lifted the pot and it was overflowing. She said: So we ate from it as much as God wished.

19- On the authority of Jabir, may God be pleased with him, regarding his father’s debt after his death. He had given his father’s creditors the original amount of his money, but they did not accept it, and its fruits were not enough to support their debt. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to him after ordering him to mow it and make it a plow on its roots, so he walked in it and prayed. So Jabir paid back his debts and gave him what they used to get every year.

20- Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, said: People were afflicted with starvation, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to me: Is there anything? I said: Yes, some dates in the manger. He said: So he brought it. So he put his hand in and took out a fist, then extended it and called for blessing. Then he said: Call ten, and they ate until they were full, then ten again until the whole army was fed and they were full. He said: Take what you brought, put your hand in it and take some of it and do not throw it up. So I took most of what I brought and ate from it and fed the lives of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Abu Bakr and Omar until he killed Uthman, so he plundered from me and went away.

The miracle of the multiplication of food due to the blessing of his supplication is narrated on the authority of a few dozen companions, and many times more of them were narrated by the Successors, then by countless number of people after them. Most of it was mentioned in famous stories and famous councils, and it is not possible to talk about it except in accordance with the truthfulness and with caution against falsehood. Rather, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, first obtained little water or little food and then increased it, and he did not invent from the beginning of the matter from nothingness to existence much water or much food, out of observance of etiquette according to what appears to be known that what exists is God. The blessing occurred because of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Although multiplication is also in reality on the part of God, like creation. This is what the prophets did, as is evident from the miracle of Elijah, peace be upon him, in multiplying flour and oil in the house of a widow woman, as stated in the seventeenth chapter of the First Book of Kings.

And from the miracle of Elisha, peace be upon him, in multiplying twenty loaves of barley and ears of corn rubbed in a napkin until a hundred men and leftovers ate, as stated in the fourth chapter of the Second Book of Kings, and from the miracle of Jesus, peace be upon him, in multiplying five loaves of bread and two fish, as stated in the fourteenth chapter of the Gospel of Matthew.

21- On the authority of Ibn Omar, may God be pleased with them both, he said: We were with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on a journey, and a Bedouin came to him, and he said: O Bedouin, where do you want? He said: My family. He said: Is there anything good for you? He said: What is it? He said: To bear witness that there is no god but God alone, with no partner, and that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger. He said: Who will bear witness for you on what you say? He said: This is the brown tree, which is on the shore of the valley. So it came to cover the ground until it stood in front of him, so he testified for it three times. She testified that it was as he said, then she returned to her place.

Then he saw two trees on the shore of the valley. The Messenger of God, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, went to one of them and took one of its branches and said: “Follow me, God willing.” So I was led along with him like a scratched camel that fights with its leader. Jabir mentioned that he did the same to the other, until when he was fair between them, he said: They came together on me, God willing, so they did, so he sat behind them and I came out green. I sat talking to myself, then I turned around and saw the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, coming, and the two trees had separated and each one of them stood on a stalk.
23- On the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, he said to a Bedouin: Have you seen?

If I call this bud from this palm tree, will you bear witness that I am the Messenger of God? He said: Yes. So he called him and he started to criticize until he came to him and said: Go back. So he returned to his place.

24- On the authority of Jabir, may God be pleased with him, the mosque was roofed over the trunks of palm trees, and when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, would deliver a sermon, he would stand on a trunk of them, and when the pulpit was made for him, we heard that trunk sound like the voice of a tax collector. In the narration of Anas: until the mosque shook at his bellowing, and in the narration of Sahl: and the people’s crying increased when they saw it, and in the narration of Al-Muttalib: until it cracked and split until the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came and put his hand on it and it remained silent.

The report about the trunk’s groaning and yearning, given its origin, is well-known among the predecessors and successors, and given its meaning is frequent, it supports definitive knowledge. It was narrated by a few dozen companions, including Ubayy bin Ka’b, Anas bin Malik, Abdullah bin Omar, Abdullah bin Abbas, Sahl bin Saad Al-Saadi, Abu Saeed Al-Khudri, Buraydah, and Umm Salamah.

Al-Muttalib bin Abi Wada’ah, may God be pleased with them, all narrate the meaning of this hadith, even if their wording is different in the matter of narration, there is no doubt about the occurrence of moral continuity.

When the Messenger of God, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, entered the mosque in the year of the conquest, he began pointing with a rod in his hand at them without touching them and saying: Truth has come and falsehood has perished.
