If Pharklet had been an expression of the spirit descending on the day of the final, then there would have been no need for this paragraph, because it would not have been thought that the disciples would rule out the Spirit descending upon them again, because they had exhausted it before as well. Indeed, there is no room for exclusion either, because if It descended on someone's heart and settled in it, and its effect will inevitably appear clearly. It is inconceivable to deny the one affected by it, and it is not possible for it to appear to them in a form in which there is a suspicion that would be exclusion. It is a description of the prophet who was given good tidings. The truth of the matter is that when Christ, peace be upon him, learned from experience and in the light of prophecy that many of his nation would deny the prophet who was heralded when he appeared, he first confirmed this paragraph and then told about his coming.

[2] This spirit is united with the Father absolutely and with the Son, given his true divinity, so it is not true about him (another Pharaclitus), unlike the prophet who was preached about, for he believed this saying about him without affectation.

[3] Agency and intercession are among the properties of prophecy, not among the properties of this spirit united with God, so they do not apply to the spirit and they do not apply to the prophet who was given good tidings about him without affectation.

[4] That Jesus, peace be upon him, said: (He will remind you of everything I said to you). It is not proven from any of the New Testament letters that the disciples had forgotten what Jesus, peace be upon him, said, and that this spirit descending on the day of the final day reminded them of it.

[5] That Jesus, peace be upon him, said: (And now I have told you before it happens, so that when it happens you will believe.) This indicates that what is meant by it is not the spirit, because you have known in the first matter that lack of faith was not suspected among them at the time of its revelation, but there is no room for exclusion either, so there is no need for this statement, and it is not the business of a wise and rational person to speak insipid words, let alone the status of the great prophet. If we mean by it the prophet who was given good tidings, then this speech is in its place and highly desirable for the sake of confirmation once again.

[6] That Jesus, peace be upon him, said: (He bears witness for me). This spirit did not testify for it in the hands of anyone, because his disciples to whom it descended did not need testimony, because they knew Christ well before his descending as well, so there is no benefit in testifying before them, and the deniers who were in need of testimony, this spirit did not testify in their hands, unlike Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, for he testified for the sake of Christ, peace be upon him, and he told the truth and absolved him of the claim of divinity, which is the worst type.
Disbelief and misguidance, and he acquitted his mother of the accusation of adultery, and their innocence was mentioned in the Qur’an in multiple places, and in hadiths in countless places.

[7] That Jesus, peace be upon him, said: (And you bear witness because you have been with me from the beginning, and this verse in the Arabic translation printed in 1816 is like this: (And you also bear witness because you were with me from the beginning). And in the Arabic translation printed in 1860 it is like this: (And you also bear witness because you have been with me from the beginning). There is also a word in these three translations, and the same is found in the Persian translations printed in 1816, 1828, and 1860. 1841 And in the Urdu translation printed in 1814, there is also a translation of the word. The word also was omitted from the translations from which the phrase John was quoted, inadvertently or intentionally. This statement clearly indicates that the testimony of the disciples is different from the testimony of Pharaclit. If what is meant by it is the spirit descending on the Day of

The abode, so there is no difference between the two testimonies, because the aforementioned spirit did not witness an independent testimony other than the testimony of the disciples. Rather, the testimony of the disciples is his own testimony, because this spirit, despite being a god united with God in a true union free from descent, abode, stability, and form, which are symptoms of the body and corporeality, descended like a stormy wind and appeared in the forms of divided tongues as if of fire, and settled on each one of them on the day of the abode, so their condition was like the state of one who bears the effects of the jinn, as The statement of the jinn is his statement in that case, and likewise the testimony of the spirit was the testimony of the disciples, so this saying is not valid other than if what is meant by it is the prophet who was given good tidings, for his testimony is different from the testimony of the disciples.

[8] That Jesus, peace be upon him, said: (If I do not go, Al-Farqalit will not come to you, but if I go, I will send him to you). So his coming was linked to his going, and this spirit, according to them, descended on the disciples in his presence when he sent them to the country of Israel. His coming was not conditional on his going, so it is not meant by Farqalit. Rather, what was meant by him was a person about whom none of the disciples had inquired further before the time of his ascension, and his coming was dependent on the going of Jesus, peace be upon him, and Muhammad, peace be upon him, was like that, because he came after the going of Jesus, peace be upon him, and his coming was contingent on the going of Jesus, peace be upon him. Peace be upon him, because the existence of two messengers with two independent laws in one time is not permissible, other than if the other follows the law of the first or if each of the messengers follows one law, because in this case it is permissible for there to be two or more in one time and one place, as their existence was proven between the time of Moses, peace be upon him, and Jesus, peace be upon him.

[9] That Jesus, peace be upon him, said: (He rebukes the world). This statement is like the clear text of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, because he rebuked the world, especially the Jews, for their lack of belief in Jesus, peace be upon him, in a rebuke that only a stubborn stubborn person would doubt, and his rational son, Muhammad al-Mahdi, will be a companion of Jesus, peace be upon him, in the time of killing the one-eyed Antichrist and his followers, unlike the Spirit descending on the Day of Resurrection, for his rebuke is not valid on anyone’s principles, and rebuke was not the position of the disciples after his revelation either, because they were calling to the religion with encouragement. And preaching, and what Rankin said in his book called the Motif of Falsehood, which is in the Urdu language, in his response to the conclusion of Sawlat al-Dhigham: (The word “rebuke” is not found in the Bible or in any of the translations of the Bible, and this inferred person cited this word to express clear truth about Muhammad because Muhammad, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, rebuked and threatened many times, but such confusion is not the business of believers and those who fear God.) His words ended, so it is rejected. This priest is either ignorant, mistaken, or mistaken, having neither faith nor fear of God, because this word is found in the aforementioned Arabic translations from which John’s phrase was quoted, and in the translation printed in 1671 in the Great Romans, and the phrase in the Arabic translation printed in Beirut in the year 1860 is thus: (And when He comes, He will convict the world of sin, etc.).

In the Arabic translations printed in 1816 and 1825, and in the Persian translations printed in 1816, 1828, and 1841, there is the word “obligation,” and the words “rebuke” and “obligation” are also close to rebuke, but there is no complaint about it, because such a matter is the custom of Protestant scholars, and therefore you see that the translators

Persian and Urdu left the word Faraklet due to its fame among Muslims regarding Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the translator of the Urdu translation published in 1839, these are his predecessors as well, as he referred to the spirit of feminine pronouns so that the common people would suspect that the meaning of this word is feminine and not masculine.

[10] Jesus, peace be upon him, said: (As for sin, it is because they did not believe in me.) This indicates that Paraclete would be visible to the deniers of Jesus, peace be upon him, rebuking them for not believing in him, and the Spirit descending on the Day of Resurrection was not apparent to the people, rebuking them.

[11] Jesus, peace be upon him, said: (I have many words to say to you, but you are not able to carry them now). This contradicts the will of the Spirit descending on the Day of Resurrection, because it does not add any ruling to the rulings of Jesus, peace be upon him, because, according to the claim of the people of the Trinity, the command of the disciples was to adhere to the doctrine of the Trinity and to call upon the people of the entire world, so any matter that happened to them is greater than the words he said to them until the time of his ascension. Yes, after the descent of this spirit, they dropped all the provisions of the Torah, which are except for some of the ten provisions mentioned in the twentieth chapter of the Book of Exodus, and they permitted all the prohibitions, and this matter cannot be said in its right to be said that they were not able to carry it, because they were able to carry the dropping of the ruling of glorifying the Sabbath, which is the greatest of the rulings of the Torah, which the Jews denied that Jesus, peace be upon him, was the promised Messiah due to his failure to observe this ruling, so accepting the dropping of all the rulings was easier for them. Yes, accepting the increase of the rulings due to weakness of faith, and weakness. Power until the time of his rise, as recognized by Protestant scholars,

It was beyond their ability. It appears that what is meant by Farqalit is a prophet whose law will be increased in relation to the Isawi law, and whose burden will be burdened on the weak accountable ones, namely Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace.
[12] That Jesus, peace be upon him, said: (He does not speak on his own initiative, but rather he speaks with everything he hears).

This indicates that Paraclete would be such that the children of Israel would disbelieve him, so Jesus, peace be upon him, needed to confirm his truthfulness, so he said this statement, and there is no room for suspicion of disbelief regarding the spirit descending on the Day of Resurrection, given that this spirit is with them as the eye of God, so his statement has no meaning, but rather speaks what it hears. His credibility is Muhammad, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, for there was a suspicion of disbelief against him, and he was not the essence of God, and he was speaking what was revealed to him, as God Almighty said: {And he does not speak out of inclination. Indeed, it is only a revelation revealed to me} and He said: {I follow only what is revealed to me}.

[13] That Jesus, peace be upon him, said: (He takes from what is mine). This does not apply to the spirit, because according to the people of the Trinity, it is eternal, uncreated, and absolutely omnipotent, and does not have an awaited perfection. Rather, every one of its perfections is attained by action, so the promised one must be of the kind that has an awaited perfection. Since this statement was misleading that this prophet was obedient to His law, he refuted it by saying later:

(All that the Father has is mine. For this reason I said, “He will take of what is mine.”) This means that everything that happens to Pharaclitus from God is as if it happens from me, just as it is well-known that whoever is for God, God is for him. For this reason, I said that he takes from what is mine.
As for the second, I mean the suspicions mentioned by Protestant scholars, there are five:
[The suspicion regarding the eighteenth gospel:]

(The first suspicion) This phrase was interpreted by Faraklit as the Holy Spirit and the Spirit of Truth, and they are two expressions of the third Avnom. So how is it correct for Faraklet to mean Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace? I say in the answer: The author of Mizan al-Haqq claims in his writings that the words Spirit of God, Holy Spirit, Spirit of Truth, Spirit of Truth, Spirit of the Mouth of God have one meaning, and he said in the first chapter of the second chapter of Miftah al-Asrar on page 53 of the Persian version printed in the year 1850: (The word Spirit of God The word “Holy Spirit” in the Torah and the Gospel has one meaning.) End quote. He claimed that these two words are used in the same meaning in the two Testaments, and he said in solving the problem in the answer to unveiling: (Whoever has some sense of the Torah and the Gospel knows that the words Holy Spirit, Spirit of Truth, Spirit of the Mouth of God, and others mean the Spirit of God, so I did not consider it necessary to prove it.) End quote. If you know this statement, we would ignore the validity of his claim or its incorrectness here, and we accept the synonymy of these words according to his claim, but we would deny that their use in every place in the two Testaments means the third hypostasis, and we would say an identical statement.

Because he said, “Whoever has any feeling for the books of the Two Testaments knows that these words are often used in terms other than the hypostasis.” In the fourteenth verse of the thirty-seventh chapter of the Book of Ezekiel, God Almighty said in a speech to thousands of people whom He revived through the miracle of Ezekiel, peace be upon him, like this: (And I will put my spirit in you.)

In this saying, the Spirit of God means the human speaking soul, not in the sense of the third hypostasis, which is the eye of God, according to their claim. In the fourth chapter of the First Epistle to John, this is an Arabic translation in the year 1760: 1 (Beloved, do not believe every spirit, but test the spirits as to whether they are from God, for many false prophets have gone out into the world) 2 (By this you will know the Spirit of God. Every spirit that confesses that Jesus Christ has come in the flesh is from God) 6 (We are from God, so who knows God?) He hears us, and he who is not of God does not hear us. From this we know the spirit of truth and the spirit of error. This is the sentence in the second verse: (By this you will know the Spirit of God).

In other translations, this is an Arabic translation in 1821, 1831, and 1844: (And by this the Spirit of God is known). Arabic translation in 1825: (You distinguish the Spirit of God and the word “Spirit of God” in the second verse, and the word “Spirit of Truth” in the sixth verse, meaning the true preacher, not in the sense of the third hypostasis. Therefore, the translator of the Urdu translation printed in the year 1845 translated the word “every spirit” with “every preacher,” and the word “souls”

With the preachers in the first verse, and the word “spirit” in the second verse means the preacher on the part of God, and the word “spirit of truth” in the sixth verse means “the truthful preacher,” and the word “spirit of error” was translated as “the misleading preacher,” and what is meant is “the Spirit of God” and “the Spirit of Truth,” the third hypostasis, which is the eye of God, according to their claim, and it is apparent, so Pharaclet’s interpretation of the Holy Spirit and the Spirit of Truth does not harm us because they mean the true preacher, just as the word “Spirit of Truth” and “Spirit of God” in this sense is in the first letter of John, so it is correct. They were named after Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, without a doubt.

(The second suspicion) is that those who are addressed by their pronouns are the dialogues, so Pharklet must appear during their era, and Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not appear during their era. I also say this is nothing, because its origin is that those present at the time of the speech must be satisfied with the pronoun of the address, and it is not necessary in every situation. Do you not see that what Jesus, peace be upon him, said in the sixty-fourth verse of the twenty-sixth chapter of the Gospel of Matthew in the speech of the chief priests, the elders, and the council is like this: (And again I say to you, from now on you will see the Son of Man sitting at the right hand of Power and coming on the clouds of heaven.) These people who were being addressed have died, and more than one thousand eight hundred years have passed since their death, and they did not see him coming on the clouds of the sky. Just as what is meant by those being addressed here are those who were present among their people at the time of his descent from heaven, so in what we are talking about, what is meant is those who are present at the time of the appearance of Pharklet.

(The third suspicion) is that it occurred to Pharaclitus that the world does not see him or know him, and you know him, and he does not believe in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, because people saw him and knew him.

I also say this is nothing, and they are the people most in need of an interpretation in this statement for us, because the Holy Spirit is the eye of God to them and the world knows God more than knowing Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. So we must say that what is meant by knowledge is true and complete knowledge. In the form of interpretation, there is no doubt about the truth of this statement about Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. What is meant is that the world does not know him with true and complete knowledge, and you know him with true and complete knowledge. What is meant by seeing is knowledge, and therefore Jesus, peace be upon him, no longer used the word “vision” after pronouncing it. You, he said, and you know him.

If we attribute vision to visual vision, then the negation of vision would be interpreted as what is meant by the statement of the first evangelist in the thirteenth chapter of his Gospel, and I quote his phrase from the Arabic translation printed in the years 1816 and 1825: 13 (Therefore I give them parables, because they see and do not see, and they hear but do not listen and do not understand) 14 (And Isaiah’s prophecy was completed regarding them, where he said, “You listen by hearing and do not understand, and you look by sight and do not see.”) There is also no problem with things like these two, even if they have metaphorical meanings, they are in the status of conventional truth. I came across the words of Jesus, peace be upon him, many times: in the twenty-seventh verse of the eleventh chapter of the Gospel of Matthew, like this: (And no one knows the Son except the Father, and no one knows the Father except the Son and whomever the Son wants to reveal to him).
And in the twenty-eighth verse of the seventh chapter of the Gospel of John, it says: (He who sent me is true, whom you do not know).

And in the eighth chapter of the Gospel of John, this is the following: (You do not know me or my Father. If you had known me, you would have known my Father also) 55 (and you do not know him, that is, God) etc.
And in the twenty-fifth verse of the seventeenth chapter of the Gospel of John, it says: (O Father, the world has not known you, but I have known you).

And in the fourteenth chapter of the Gospel of John, it is as follows: 7 (If you had known me, you would have known my Father also, and from now on you know him and have seen him) 8 (Philip said to him, “Lord, show us the Father, and it is enough for us”) 9 (Jesus said to him, “I have been with you this long time, and you have not known me. O Philip, he who has seen me has seen the Father. How can you say, ‘Show us the Father’?”)

What is meant in these sayings by knowledge is complete knowledge and by vision is knowledge. Otherwise, these statements are not definitely correct, because the common people knew Jesus, peace be upon him, in addition to the Jewish leaders, priests, sheikhs, and disciples, and seeing God with sight in this world is impossible for the people of the Trinity as well.

(The fourth suspicion) is that it occurred against Pharaclitus: (He resides with you and abides among you). It appears from this statement that Pharaclitus was at the time of the speech residing with the disciples, and a constant among them, so how can this be true of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace?
I say: This saying in other translations is a Sunnah Arabic translation

1816, and 1825: (For he abides with you, and will be in you.) Persian translations printed in 1816, 1828, and 1841. The Urdu translation printed in 1814 and 1839 are all identical to these two translations, and in the Arabic translation printed in 1860 it reads like this: (He will abide with you, and he will be in you). So it appears that what is meant by his saying “remains in you” is future stability with certainty, so there is no objection to it in any way, and his saying remains “remaining with you,” so I say: It is not correct to take this saying to the meaning that is “remaining with you now,” because it contradicts his saying: (I will ask the Father, and he will give you another Faraklet), and his saying: (I have told you before it happens, so that if it happens you will believe), and his saying: (If I do not go, the Faraklet will not come to you), and if it is interpreted, we say that it means Reception, just as the saying after it means reception, and its meaning is residing with you in reception, so there is no scratch on its truthfulness also regarding Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. The expression of reception in the present, or rather in the past, in certain matters is abundant in the two Testaments. Don’t you see that Ezekiel, peace be upon him, first told about the emergence of Gog and Magog, in the future time, and their destruction when they reached the mountains of Israel?

Then he said in the eighth verse of the thirty-ninth chapter of his book thus: (Behold, he has come, and the Lord God says, “This is the day of which I spoke.”) So look at his saying, “Here he came and he has come.” This saying in the Persian translation printed in the year 1839 is like this: (Your son is Rasid and with the arrival of Jabust), so he expressed the future state in the past because it is certain and beyond doubt, and a period of more than two thousand has passed.
Four hundred and fifty years and their exit did not appear.

And in the twenty-fifth verse of the fifth chapter of the Gospel of John, it is as follows: (Verily, truly, I say to you, an hour is coming, and now is, when the dead will hear the voice of the Son of God, and those who hear them will live.) So look at his saying, and it is now, and a period of more than one thousand eight hundred has passed, and this hour has not come, and even now it is unknown, and no one knows when it will come.

(The fifth suspicion) in the first chapter of the Book of Acts is thus: 4 (And while he was meeting with them, he commanded them not to depart from Jerusalem, but to wait for the promise of the Father, which you heard from me) 5 (For John baptized with water, but you will be baptized with the Holy Spirit not many days later.) This indicates that Pharklet is the spirit descending on the Day of Resurrection. Because what is meant by the promise of the father is Pharklet, I say the claim that what is meant by the promise of the father is Pharklet, is a pure claim. In fact, it is wrong in thirteen ways, and I have known them. Rather, the truth is that informing about Pharklet is one thing, and promising to send down the spirit upon him again is another thing, and God has fulfilled both promises. He expressed the first promise with the coming of Pharklet, and here with the promise of the father. The point of the matter is that John conveyed the good news of Paraclete, and the rest of the evangelists did not transmit it, and Luke transmitted the date of the descent of the Spirit that descended on the day of the final, but John did not transmit it.
And there is nothing wrong with it, for they may agree on conveying vile statements, such as Jesus, peace be upon him, riding a donkey while going to the mosque.

Jerusalem, the four agreed upon his narration, and they may differ in narrating the great cases. Do you not see that Luke was alone in mentioning the resurrection of the widow’s son from the dead in Nabin, and by mentioning the sending of Jesus, peace be upon him, seventy disciples, and by mentioning the healing of ten lepers, and none of the evangelists mentioned these cases even though they were among the great cases, and that John was alone in mentioning the wedding feast in Cana of Galilee, and the miracle of turning water into wine appeared from Jesus, and this miracle is the first of his miracles, and the reason for the manifestation of his glory. And the disciples’ faith in him, and by mentioning the healing of the sick man in Bethsaida in Jerusalem, and this is also a great miracle, and the sick person had been sick for thirty-eight years, and by mentioning the story of a woman caught in adultery, and by mentioning the healing of the blind man, and this is also one of his greatest miracles, and they are stated in Chapter Nine, and by mentioning the revival

The excuses are from the dead, and none of the evangelists mentioned them, even though they are great cases. This is the case with Matthew and Mark, as they alone mentioned some miracles and cases that no one else mentioned.

Since the research on this matter has been lengthy, let us limit ourselves to this amount of good news that I quoted from their books that are considered by them in our time. As for the good news that is found in other books that are not considered by them in our time, I did not quote them. After I finished, I will also quote one piece of good news from her as an example.

So I say: Priest Seal conveyed in the introduction to his translation of the Glorious Qur’an from the Gospel of Barnaya the good news of Muhammadiyah thus: (Know, O Barnabas, that the sin, even if it is small, God will reward for it because God is not satisfied with the sin, and when He spared my mother and my disciples for the sake of this world, God was displeased with this matter, and He wanted, by virtue of His justice, to reward them in this world for this inappropriate belief so that they would be saved from the torment of Hell, and they would not be harmed. There, even though I was innocent, when some people said about me that he is God and the Son of God, God hated this saying and His will required that the devils not laugh at me on the Day of Resurrection and not mock me. So, due to His kindness and mercy, it was deemed appropriate for there to be laughter and mockery in this world because of the death of Judas, and every person thinks that I was crucified, but this insult and mockery will remain until Muhammad, the Messenger of God, comes. When he comes in this world, he will alert every believer of this mistake. This suspicion rises from the hearts of the people.) End translation of his words.

(I say) This is great news, and if they object that this Gospel was rejected by the councils of our predecessor scholars (I say) there is no consideration for their rejection and acceptance, as I learned from what is mentioned in the first chapter, and this Gospel is one of the ancient Gospels and it is mentioned in the books of the second and third centuries. Accordingly, this Gospel was written two hundred years before the appearance of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and no one can tell without inspiration about such a matter two hundred years before it occurred, so this must be the saying of Jesus, peace be upon him, and if they say that Did any of the Muslims distort this Gospel after the appearance of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace? I said: This possibility is very remote because the Muslims did not pay attention to these four Gospels either, so how about the Gospel of Barnabas? It is unlikely that any Muslim’s distortion of the Gospel of Barnabas would have an effect that would change the existing versions among Christians as well, and they claim that the scholars of the People of the Book, Jews and Christians who converted to Islam, transmitted

Regarding the books of the two Testaments, the Gospels of Muhammad, and their distortion, based on their claim, I say that these great scholars distorted what they claimed, and their distortion did not affect the places of these Gospels in their books that were present with them. So how did the distortion of some Muslims in the Gospel of Barnabas affect the copies that they had? This possibility is very weak and must be rejected.

(Warning) We first reported this news in the book Al-Ijaz Al-Isawi, from the translation printed in the year 1850 AD, and this book was printed in the year 1271 AH and 1854 AD and became famous throughout India and their translations, and their books change somewhat in the later printing in relation to the earlier printing, as I also pointed out in the introduction to the book. If the viewer does not find this good news in some copies of the aforementioned translation printed in a year other than the aforementioned year, he will not fall into doubt, especially if these are some of the copies printed in the year It is later than one thousand eight hundred and fifty-four AD, because if Protestant scholars naturally dropped this good news from the aforementioned translation, it would not be excluded from their habit, which has become a natural matter for them.

The Honorable Haider Ali Al-Qurashi said in his book called Khulasat Saif al-Muslimeen, which is in the Urdu language, on pages 63 and 64: (The priest or the Armenian resident translated the book of Isaiah into the Armenian language in the year one thousand six hundred and six.

Sixty years, and this translation was printed in the year one thousand seven hundred and thirty-three in the Anthony Bortoli printing press. In this translation, in the forty-second chapter, there is this paragraph: (Praise God with a new praise, with the sign of Sultanate on his back, and his name is Ahmed) ended. This translation is available among the Armenians, so look into it.) End of his speech.

(I say) This translation did not reach me and I did not see it, but this honorable man may have seen it and looked at it, and there is no doubt that this paragraph is of great benefit, even if this translation is not considered by Protestant scholars, and who among the more Muslim Jewish and Christian scholars in the first century testified to the presence of the Muhammadan gospels in the books of the two Testaments, such as Abdullah bin Salam and the sons of Sa`yah.
Benjamin, Mukhayriq, Ka'b Al-Ahbar and others were Jewish scholars, as was Buhair

Onestor al-Habashi and Dhaftar, who was the Roman bishop who converted to Islam at the hands of Dihya al-Kalbi at the time of the message, and they killed him, and al-Jaroud, al-Najashi, al-Sus, and the monks who came with Jaafar bin Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, and other Christian scholars. He acknowledged the validity of his prophecy and the generality of his message. Heraclius, Caesar of the Romans, Muqawqis, ruler of Egypt, Ibn Surya, Hayy bin Akhtab, Abu Yasser bin Akhtab, and others who carried them. Envy of misery, but they were not spared.

It was narrated that when he, peace be upon him, wanted evidence against the Christians of Najran, then they insisted on their ignorance, so he, peace be upon him, said: God has commanded me, if you do not accept the proof, to discredit it to you. So they said: O Abu al-Qasim, rather, we will return and look into our matter, then we will come to you. When they returned, they said to Al-Aqib, and he was of their opinion: What do you think? He said: By God, you have known his prophethood, and he has come to you with a decision on the matter of your friend. By God, no people gives a prophet except that they will perish, even if you refuse except for the benefit of your religion. So they bid farewell to the man and left, and they came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he had begun embracing Al-Hussein and holding the hand of Al-Hassan, with Fatima walking behind him, and Ali, may God be pleased with him, behind her, and he was saying: If I pray, then believe. Their bishop said: O Christians, I see faces. If they had asked God to remove a mountain from its place, He would have removed it, so do not be frivolous or you will perish. So they submitted to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and paid him a tribute of two thousand red robes and thirty iron shields. He, peace and blessings be upon him, said: If they had tried, they would have been turned into monkeys and pigs, and the valley would have burned down with fire, and God would have eradicated Najran and its people, even the birds in the trees.
This incident demonstrated his prophecy in two ways:

(The first) is that he, peace and blessings be upon him, frightened them with the infliction of torment on them, and if he had not been confident of that, it would have been an effort on his part to show that he lied to himself, because if he had failed and the torment had not been inflicted on him, his lie would have become apparent, and it is known that he was one of the wisest of people, so it was not appropriate for him to do an act that would lead to his lying being revealed, so when he insisted on that, we know that he only insisted on it because he was confident in God’s promise.

(The second) is that the people were spending their souls and money in disputes with the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace. If they had not known that he was a prophet, they would not have abandoned his challenge.

sections.heading: Chapter Two: (On Defending Appeals)
content: [Chapter Two: (On Defending Appeals).]

Know, may God Almighty guide you in both worlds, that Christians claim that prophets are infallible only in conveying revelation, whether it is a report or a text. As for matters other than conveying the message, they are not infallible, neither before nor after the prophecy. After that, all sins will come from them intentionally, in addition to mistakes and forgetfulness. They will start committing adultery with incestuous women, not to mention foreign women. They will start worshiping idols and building temples for them. And no prophet will emerge from them from Abraham to Yahya, peace be upon them, who is not an adulterer or one of the children of adultery. May God protect us from such corrupt beliefs against the prophets, peace be upon them.

I learned in the seventh matter of the introduction to the book, in the third and fourth chapters of the first chapter, and in the first purpose of the second chapter that their claim of infallibility in reporting is also false and has no basis in their principles. This claim is made by them to mislead the common people. Their attacks on Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, in some matters that they understand as sins in their corrupt claim, do not discredit his prophecy based on their origins. And even though I detest it to transfer the sins of the prophets and the slanderous infidelities from their books, even if it is necessary, I do not believe in the presence of the prophets to do justice to them with these sins and infidelities, forbid and no. But when I saw that Protestant scholars had been excessive in their language against Muhammad, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, regarding light matters, and had turned mustard into a mountain to confuse the common people who did not pay attention to their books, and I suspected that the naive would fall under suspicion of their false camouflage, I quoted some of them obligatorily, and I disavowed their belief in a thousand.

A tongue, and its transmission is only like the transmission of words of disbelief, and the transmission of disbelief is not disbelief, and its transmission was preceded by the transmission of their attacks on Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the answer to it. The priest William Asmt, one of the Protestant scholars, wrote a book in the Urdu language and printed it in the country of Mirzapur in the country of India in the year 1848 AD, and he called it the Path of the Saints, and he wrote in it the state of the prophets from Adam to Jacob, peace be upon them, quoting the Book of Genesis and its interpretations that are considered by scholars. Protestant, so I quote in some places from this book as well.

[1] The story of Adam, peace be upon him, is famous among them, and in the third chapter of the Book of Genesis, it is written. They acknowledge that he sinned intentionally and did not confess his sin to what God asked for, and his repentance was not proven by them until the end of his life on page 23 of the Path of the Saints: (Oh my regret that his repentance was not proven and that he did not ask forgiveness of God for his sin once again) End.

[2] In the ninth chapter of the Book of Genesis, this is the following: 18 (And the sons of Noah who came out of the ark were Shem, and Ham, and Japheth, and Ham the father of Canaan) 20 (And they began

Noah was a farmer plowing the land and planted a vineyard. (21) And he drank wine, and became drunk, and uncovered himself in a tent. (22) And when Ham, the father of Canaan, saw that his father’s private parts were uncovered, he told his brothers outside. (24) And when Noah woke up from the wine, and learned what his youngest son had done to him. (25) Then he said, “Cursed be Canaan; he will be his brothers’ servant.” It contains a statement that Noah drank wine, got drunk, and became naked. What is surprising is that the guilty person by looking at his father’s nakedness was Ham, the father of Canaan, and his son Canaan was punished with a curse, and the son took the father’s sin against him, contrary to justice. Ezekiel said in the twentieth verse of the eighteenth chapter of his book: (The soul that sins will die, and the son will not bear the iniquity of the father, and the father will not bear the iniquity of the son. The righteousness of the just will be upon him, and the hypocrisy of the hypocrite will be upon him.)

Even if we assume that he blamed the father's sin on the son, contrary to justice. What was the reason for singling out Canaan, because Ham’s sons were four: Cush, Mizraim, Put, and Canaan, as stated in Chapter Ten?

[3] On page 74 of the Path of the Saints, regarding the situation of Abraham, it is as follows: (His condition is not known until seventy years of age. He was raised among the pagans, and spent most of his life among them, and he knew that his parents did not know the true God. It is possible that Abraham also

He used to worship idols unless God appeared over him, then He appeared over him and chose him from among the people of the world, and made him a special servant.) End quote. It appeared that Christians believed that Abraham, up to seventy years of age, was worshiping idols. I say that he worshiped idols until he was seventy years old, which is almost certain, given their origins. Because the people of the world at this time were pagans, and he was raised among them, and his parents were also among them. The Lord did not appear to him until that time, and infallibility from worshiping idols is not a condition after prophecy, let alone being a condition before prophecy. If the condition of this father of the prophets appears to be seventy years of his age before the prophecy, then convey his condition after the prophecy.

[4] In the twelfth chapter of the Book of Genesis, this is the following: 11 (And when he was about to enter Egypt, he said to Sarah his wife, ‘I know that you are a fine woman.’) 12 (And it shall come to pass, when the Egyptians see you, that they will say that she is his wife, and they will kill me and spare you.) 13 (And now I desire of you, so say that you are my sister, so that it may go well with me because of you, and that a soul may be spared for your sake.) The reason for lying was not just fear, but also the hope that good would happen. Rather, the good was stronger. Therefore he brought him forward and said that it may be well with me because of you, and that my soul may be kept alive for your sake. Goodness also happened to him, as stated in verse sixteen. However, his fear of being killed is just an illusion, especially if he was content to leave her, because there is no basis for his fear after that at all. How is it permissible for reason that Abraham was satisfied with leaving his harem and handing her over and not defending her, and he would not be satisfied with someone like him who had some jealousy, so how could he be satisfied like the jealous Abraham?

[5] In the twentieth chapter of the Book of Genesis, it is as follows: 1 (And Abraham journeyed from there to the land of the South, and dwelt between Cadiz and Sur, and El-Tahah in Gerara) 2 (He said of Sarah his wife, “She is my sister.” And Abu Malek, the king of Gerara, directed him and took her) 3 (And God came to Abu Malek in a dream at night, and said to him: Behold, you are dying for the wife whom you have taken, because she has a husband.) 4 (And Abu Malek was not near her, and he said: O Lord, will I destroy a righteous people? He taught him) 5 (Isn’t he the one who said that she is my sister, and she said that he is my brother). Abraham and Sarah lied there again, and perhaps the reason here, in addition to fear as well, was to obtain the benefit, and it occurred as stated in the fourteenth verse, although there was no reason for fear if he was satisfied with handing her over without the fighter on page 99 of the saints’ path, like this: (Perhaps when Abraham denied that Sarah was his wife the first time, he resolved in his heart that he would not commit such a sin, but he fell into the previous network of Satan again due to negligence.) End quote.
[6] On pages 92 and 93 of the Path of the Saints: (Abraham could not have been not guilty of marrying Hagar, because he knew well the words of Christ written in

The Gospel, that He who created them from the beginning created them male and female, and said, “For this reason a man will leave his father and mother and cling to his wife, and the two will become one flesh.” End quote. I say just as this is not possible, so it is not possible for him to be not guilty of marrying Sarah, because he knew very well the words of Moses written in the Torah: (You shall not uncover your sister, whether by your father or by your mother who was born in the house or outside the house. Likewise his saying: (Any man who marries his sister, his father’s daughter, or his sister, his mother’s daughter, and sees her nakedness and she sees his nakedness, this is a severe disgrace, and they will be killed in front of their people. This is because he uncovered his sister’s nakedness, and their sin will be on their heads.) The same applies to his saying: (He who has intercourse with his sister through his father or his mother will be cursed), as I learned in the third chapter of this book. Such sexual intercourse is equivalent to adultery according to Protestant scholars. It is necessary for Abraham, peace be upon him, to have been an adulterer before and after his prophecy, and all of his children from Sarah were the children of adultery. If it was permissible for him to marry a sister in his law, they would also have to have multiple marriages permissible in that law. There is no objection with regard to Hagar or with regard to Sarah, which is the truth with us, but it is necessary, based on their corrupt origin, that this Prophet
The father of the prophets, just as he was a liar, so he was an adulterer from the beginning of his life to the end, and yet he was God’s friend. Could God’s friend be like him?

[7] In the nineteenth chapter of the Book of Genesis, this is the following: 30 (So Lot went up from Zero and dwelt in the mountains, and his two daughters with him, and he feared that Zehar would dwell and took refuge in a cave, he and his two daughters with him) 31 (Then the older of them said to the younger, ‘Our father is old, and there is no man on earth who can come in to us as he decreed for all the earth.’) 32 (Come, let us make him drink wine, and we will lie with him, and we will appoint a successor to our father.) 33 (So they committed adultery with their father.) (34) So they made their father drink wine that night also, and the younger went in and lay with her father, and he did not know when Her laying down and not her rising up) 36 (So Lot’s daughters became pregnant by their father) 37 (And the eldest bore a son and called his name Moab, and he is the father of the Moabites.
To this day) 38 (And the youngest also bore a son and called his name Oman, meaning a son of my kind, for he is the father of the Omanis to this day).

And on page 128 of the Saints, after narrating this situation, it is as follows: (His situation is worthy of being cried over, and we, after regretting, fearing, and fearing for ourselves, marvel at him. Is he the one who remained pure in robes from all the evils of Sodom, and who was strong in walking on the path of God, and far from all the impurities of that town, and who was overcome by immorality after he went out to the land? Any person would be safe in a country, a land, or a cave) his words ended. When [p. 304] the priests cried over his condition, we do not need to prolong it, and their crying is sufficient, except that I say that God did not kill the Moab and Amman that were born through adultery, and the boy who was born through the adultery of David, peace be upon him, with Uriah’s wife, was killed. Perhaps adultery with someone else’s wife is more severe than adultery with girls according to them. Rather, they were among those acceptable to God. As for Moab, because Obed was the grandfather of David, peace be upon him, his mother’s name was Ruth, as stated in the first chapter of the Gospel of Matthew. This Ruth was a Moabite, one of the children of Moab. She is one of the grandmothers of David, Solomon, and Jesus, peace be upon them. David is the firstborn son of God, and Solomon is also the son of God, and Jesus is the only son of God, and even God, according to the Christians’ claim.

As for Oman, this is because Rehoboam, son of Solomon, is one of the grandfathers of Jesus, peace be upon him, as stated in the first chapter of the Gospel of Matthew as well, and his mother was an Omani woman, one of the children of Oman, as stated in the fourteenth chapter of the First Book of Kings. She is also one of the grandmothers of the only Son of God, or even God, according to their claim.

The nineteenth verse of the second chapter of the Book of Exceptions is as follows: “And you shall approach the vicinity of the children of Oman. Beware of fighting them, and do not move to fight them, for I will not give you anything of the land of the children of Oman. I have given it to the children of Lot as an inheritance.” What more honor does Moab and Oman have, the two sons of adultery, than that some of the daughters of the first have become great-grandmothers to the sons of God, or even God, according to their claim? Some of the daughters of the second became the grandmother of God’s only son, or even God, according to their claim. And God prevented the children of Israel, who were children of God, according to the text of the Torah, from inheriting the land of his children, but a scratch remained, which is that if the lineage of Jesus, peace be upon him, considering these two great ancestors, reached Moab and Oman, he would become Moabite and Omani, and the Omanis and Moabites would not have entered the community of the Lord forever.
The third verse of Chapter Twenty-Three of the Book of Exceptions is as follows:
(And the Omanites and the Moabites after ten years also will not enter the assembly of the Lord forever.)

So how did Jesus, peace be upon him, enter the community of the Lord? Rather, he became their leader, and even the son of God, according to their claim. And if it is said that lineage is considered through fathers, not through mothers, then Jesus, peace be upon him, would not be an Omani or a Moabite. I said that if such were the case, then it would be necessary for him not to be an Israeli Jew or a Davidic Solomonic either, since these descriptions also occurred to him from the mother’s side, not the father’s side, so he would not be a promised Messiah, and considering these descriptions based on the mother and not considering his being an Omani and a Moabite from the side of the grandmothers. Preference without probability, and this also occurred in David and Solomon, peace be upon them, considering Ruth, but I will not dwell on this at length and return to the origin of the story, and I say: This Lot, peace be upon him, who is in a state, should have been wept by the priests. There is no doubt that, according to the Gospel, he is righteous and holy. There was no weakness among them in his sanctity after this heinous movement, the likes of which has not been heard in the vile people who are drunk most of the time, because they also distinguish their daughters from foreign women in the state of alcohol, and since the privilege between girls and others is lost due to the intensity of the alcohol, the drunk at this time is no longer capable of intercourse, as testified by those who are fond of drinking alcohol, and what we have heard until... Now in India, one of the vile people did this thing with alcohol to his daughter or his mother. If the alcohol leads to this level, then how sorry I am for the condition of the Christian people of Europe. How can they hope that their mothers, daughters, and sisters will be saved from the hands of their sons, fathers, and brothers, because most of the time they are drunk with their husbands?
And their women, especially if we measure the situation with regard to their weak ones.

The astonishment is that this saint, just as he was tested on the first night, was also tested on the second night, unless it is said that this matter was a decree so that the sons of God, or rather God, would be born from some of his daughters, and he would be included in the lineage of the only Son of God. If such a thing happened to some individual people, the earth would feel distressed and distressed for him as wide as it was, so what is astonishing is Lot. I seek refuge in God from these myths, and I say that this false story is one of the slanders: In the second chapter of the Second Epistle to Peter, it is as follows: 7 (And he saved the righteous Lot, defeated, from the wicked’s life of promiscuity) 8 (If the righteous by sight and hearing, while he lived among them, day after day torments his righteous soul with sinful deeds). So Peter called Lot, peace be upon him, the righteous, and praised him. I also bear witness that he was righteous and free from what they attributed to him.

[8] In the twenty-sixth chapter of the Book of Genesis, this is the following: 6 (So Isaac stayed in Gerara) 7 (And the men of that place asked him about his wife, and he said, “She is my sister,” because he was afraid to say that she was his wife, lest they kill him for her beauty.) Ishaq also deliberately lied, like his father, and told his wife that she was his sister. On page 168 of the Path of the Saints: (Ishaq’s faith slipped because he told his wife that she was his sister). Then on page 169 (Oh my regret, there is no perfection in any of the sons of Adam other than the peerless one. What is surprising is that the net of Satan into which Abraham fell, Isaac also fell into, and he said of his wife that she was his sister. What a regret that people like these who are close to God are in need of admonition) he ended his words. When the priests deeply regretted the misstep of his faith and the lack of perfection in it
And his falling into the network of Satan, which Abraham, peace be upon him, fell into, and his need for exhortation, so we will not dwell on it.

[9] In the twenty-fifth chapter of the Book of Genesis, this is the following: 29 (And Jacob cooked stew, and when Esau came to him weary from the field) 30 (And he said to him, Feed me with this red stew, for I am very tired, and for this reason he called his name Edom) 31 (And Jacob said to him, Sell me your birthright.) 32 (And he answered and said, Behold, I die, and what use will that birthright be for me?) 33 (And Jacob said to him, Swear to me, and he swore to him Esau and sold the birthright.) 34 (So Jacob brought bread and a meal of lentils to Esau, and he ate and drank and went away, and was negligent about the fact that he had sold the birthright.) So look at the religion of Esau, who was the eldest son of Isaac, peace be upon him, that he sold the birthright, which meant entitlement to the position of prophecy and blessing to him, which were in the rank of this bread and the edamame of lentils. Likewise, look at the love of Jacob, peace be upon him, and his goodness, that he did not give this edible item to the hungry, tired older brother except by sale, and he did not take into account brotherly love and benevolence without compensation.

[10] Whoever reads the twenty-seventh chapter of the Book of Genesis will know with certainty that Jacob, peace be upon him, lied three times and deceived his father, and his deception, as it affected Isaac, peace be upon him, also affected God, because Isaac, peace be upon him, was from the bottom of his heart and his belief calling for Esau, not for Jacob, peace be upon him. Just as Isaac did not distinguish between...

Two brothers in supplication, so God did not distinguish between them when answering the supplication. What is surprising is that God’s guardianship, prophecy, and righteousness are achieved by the impossible. And I remembered a story that is appropriate for this situation, which is: An immoral man from the Banu group asked for hashish from a donkey for his horse, and the donkey did not give him. He said, “If you do not give me, I will pray for your donkey, and it will die tonight.” He went away and his horse died that night. When he woke up and found his horse dead, he moved his head in amazement and said: “Wow, what a wonder. It has been millions of years since the divinity of our God has passed and the horse cannot be distinguished from the donkey until now. I prayed for the donkey and destroyed my horse. This was the state of the religion of the father of the Israelite prophets, or the state of God’s knowledge, so the denier may say: It is possible that the dealings of the Israeli prophets with God were also based on deception, like their Supreme Father, and it is possible that Jesus, peace be upon him, promised God that you would give me the power of miracles, call upon creation to your monotheism and your lordship, but God did not distinguish truth from lying and gave him the power, so he called for the lordship of himself and transgressed against God. I seek refuge in God from these flimsy matters.

I quote some passages from the Path of the Saints from page 179, 180 and 181. He said firstly: (This is a place of extreme fear that such a person uttered lie after lie and included the name of God in his deception), then he said secondly: (Jacob said a word that is the end of disbelief. God’s will was that I quickly found the catch),

Then he said thirdly: (We do not apologize on the part of Jacob in this matter with any excuse, and let every righteous person refrain from such a matter), then he said fourthly: (The bottom line of the speech is that he did wrong in order to achieve goodness, and in the Gospel he must be punished for the same), then he said fifthly: (Just as Jacob sinned, so did his mother sin more than him, because she was the one who created this corruption and she ordered Jacob to do these deceptive things.) End.

[11] In the twenty-ninth chapter of Genesis, this is how: 15 (Then he said to Jacob, “Perhaps you are my brother for free, and you will serve me for what I have paid you.” 16 (And he had two daughters. The name of the eldest was Leah, and the name of the younger was Rachel.) 17 (And Leah was at ease in my eyes, and Rachel had a beautiful face and a beautiful appearance.) 18 (So Jacob loved Rachel and said, “I will worship you with your younger daughter Rachel for seven years.” 19 (And Laban said to him, “You are more worthy of her than anyone else, so stay with me.” 20 (And Jacob will worship Rachel for seven years. (21) And he said to Laban, “Give me my wife, for I have completed the days to go in to her.” 32 (So Laban gathered a large crowd of lovers and arranged a wedding.) 23 (And when evening came, he brought his daughter Leah to Jacob.) 34 (And Laban gave a maid named Zilpah to his daughter, and Jacob went in to her as usual. And when the morning came, he saw that it was Leah.) 25 (And he said to Laban, “What is this?” What have you done to me? Did I not worship you, Rachel, and why did you deceive me?) 26 (Laban answered, “There is no custom in our land to marry the younger before the older.” 27 (So complete this week, and I will give you the other in return for the work that you do for me for another seven years.) 28 (And Jacob did so, and after the week had begun,

He married Rachel (29) and Laban gave to his daughter Rachel a slave named Bilha (30) (So he went in to Rachel and loved her more than Leah, and she worshiped him and served him for another seven years). He responds to three objections:

(The first) is that Jacob, peace be upon him, was staying in Laban’s house, and he saw his two daughters and knew them well, considering their faces, bodies, and voices, and there was a clear sign in Leah, which was the relaxation of the eyes. So it is very surprising that Leah was in his bed all night and he saw her, had sex with her, and touched her, and did not know her, except for them to say that he was drunk like Lot, peace be upon him. Just as Lot, peace be upon him, did not recognize it, so he is.

(The second) is that he loved Rachel and served her father for her first for seven years, and she was with him for a few days because of her love and excessive love. Then, when Laban deceived him and married off his eldest daughter, Jacob argued with him and made Rachel serve another seven years. These matters, according to the Christians’ claim, are not appropriate for the rank of prophethood, and just as he deceived his father, he was deceived by his son-in-law.
(Third) He is not satisfied with one wife, and it is not permissible to marry two women, especially two sisters, according to their corrupt claim.

The author of the Path of the Saints apologized on page 189 of his book as follows: (It appears that if Jacob had not been deceived by Laban, he would not have married anyone other than Rachel, and this does not serve as evidence for the permissibility of polygamy, because it was not by God’s command nor with Jacob’s consent.) End quote.

I say: This is a cold excuse that does not make him fat, does not make him rich, and does not save Jacob, peace be upon him, from being inviolable, because he was not forced or coerced into a second marriage, and he had to be content with one wife.

And I say: As this apologist said in his attack on Abraham, peace be upon him, that Jacob, peace be upon him, knew well the words of Christ written in the Gospel, that He who created them from the beginning created them male and female, etc. He also knew well what Moses, peace be upon him, said that bringing two sisters together is absolutely forbidden, as I learned in the third chapter. One of the two marriages is invalid, and the woman whose marriage was invalid must have her children and her children’s children as children of adultery. According to both assessments, it is necessary that many of the Israeli prophets were like that, God forbid. So look at the religion of Christians. In order to preserve their corrupt origins, they accuse the prophets and attribute evil things to them. However, this lame excuse does not apply to Zilpah and Bilha, whom Jacob married with reference to Leah and Rachel, as stated in Chapter Thirty of the Book of Genesis, and all of their children are the children of adultery according to their origins.

[12] In the thirty-first chapter of the Book of Genesis, this is the following: 19 (And Laban had gone to shear his sheep, and Rachel had stolen her father’s idols) 20 (So Jacob, peace be upon him, concealed his matter from his father-in-law, and did not let him know that he was a fugitive.) 21 (And he fled, and all that he had, and crossed the river, and headed toward Mount Gilead.) 22 (And it came to Laban on the third day that Jacob had fled.) 23 (So Laban took his brothers, And he followed him seven days' journey, and overtook him at Mount Gilead. (29) And he said to Jacob: Why have you done this, and given my daughters to drink hidden from me, like someone who has

Captivity by the sword) 30 (And now you have set out, but your desire was to go to your father’s house, so why did you steal my gods) 31 (Jacob answered, etc.) 32 (And as for what you rebuke me with for stealing, whoever you find your gods with shall be put to death in the presence of our brothers, etc.) 33 (So Laban went into Jacob’s tent as a guardian and of the two nations, but he did not find them, and when he entered Rachel’s tent) 34 (they are She hastened, and hid the idols under a camel’s spoke, and sat on it. Laban searched the whole tent, but did not find anything. (35) “And she said, ‘Do not rebuke me, my lord, for I cannot get up to you, for I am in a state of women’s distress.’” Laban searched everything in the house, but he did not find anything.

So look at Rachel, how she stole her father’s idols, and how she lied. It is apparent that she stole for her own purposes of worship, as indicated by the apparent meaning of the phrase in the thirty-fifth chapter of the Book of Genesis, as you will know in the following witness, and because she was from the house of the pagans and that her father was a pagan who worshiped idols, as indicated by verse thirty and thirty-two. It is apparent that she was following the religion of her father, so this beloved wife of Jacob, peace be upon him, was a thief and a liar. And a worshiper of idols.

[13] In the thirty-fifth chapter of the Book of Genesis, this is the following: 2 (And Jacob said to his family, and to all who were with him, Put away the strange gods from among you, and purify yourself, and change your clothes.) 4 (And they gave him all the strange gods that were in their hands, and the earrings that were in their ears, and he buried them under the oak that was at Shechem.)

What is clear from this statement is that the people of the house of Jacob, peace be upon him, and those with him up to this point were worshiping idols, and this matter, considering his house, was very heinous. But he forbade them.

Before this, about idolatry, and if they gave him all the foreign gods, it seems that Rachel also paid the stolen gods as well, so Jacob, peace be upon him, should have sent them to Laban, not buried them under the oak that Shechem had, and excused Rachel for stealing them.

[14] In the thirty-fourth chapter of the Book of Genesis, this is how: 1 (And Dina, the daughter of Leah, went out to look at the daughters of that country) 2 (And Shechem the son of Hamor the Havite, the ruler of the land, saw her and loved her, so he took her and lay with her and humiliated her) 3 (And his soul became attached to her, and he loved her and spoke to her in a way that pleased her, and it fell to her heart) 4 (And Shechem said to his father Hamor, Take this maid to me as a wife) 8 (So Hamor spoke to them) etc. 13 (And the sons of Jacob etc. answered) 14 (No We can do what you ask, and we cannot give our sister to an uncircumcised man, for that is a disgrace to us.) 15 (In this we will resemble you if you become like us in order to circumcise all your males.) 24 (So they all consented, and every one of them who was male was circumcised.) 25 (And when the third day came, and they were in great pain, the two sons of Jacob, Simeon and Levi, each of them, took his sword, and they entered the city in peace, and killed every male.) 26 (And Hamor, and Shechem his son, and they took Dina [p. 312] their sister from Beth Shechem) 27 (And they went out, and the sons of Jacob came in upon the slain, and plundered the city where Dina had exposed their sister.) 28 (And they took their flocks, and their herds, and their donkeys, and all that was in the houses, and all that was in the field, and took captive their children and their women.)

So look at Ismat Dina, the daughter of Jacob, that she committed adultery and fell in love with Sheshim, as indicated by his saying: and he fell in love with her heart. And look at the injustice of Jacob’s sons, that they killed males

All the townspeople took their women and children captive, and plundered all their money. Their mistake and injustice are clear, and the mistake of Jacob, peace be upon him, is that he did not prevent them from this heinous movement before it occurred, and he did not take retribution from them, nor did he return the women, children, and the stolen money, and even if he was unable to prevent them, he returned these things, and took retribution, so he had to leave the company of this injustice, although it is very unlikely that two men would kill all the people of the town, even if we assume that they were in the agony of circumcision.
[15] In the thirty-fifth chapter of the Book of Genesis, this is the following: (Rubel went and slept with Bilhah, his father’s concubine, and Israel heard it.)

So look at Rubel, the eldest son of Jacob, peace be upon him, that he committed adultery with his father’s wife, and at Jacob that he did not carry out the punishment or punishment, neither on his son, nor on this wife.
